title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text: SFW-16 Overstated Medium-high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Statement
MBNMAdose fits model-based dose-response network meta-analysis, and in a truly disconnected network the assumed dose-response form is not identified by the data being combined, so results can be highly sensitive when dose support is sparse or non-overlapping. That form is not beyond checking, however: randomized dose-level evidence still estimates the curve parameters and supports goodness-of-fit checks and comparison among curve families, and Pedder et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315) ran the deletion experiment, finding MBNMA estimates on disconnected networks consistent with NMA on augmented networks in 15 of 18 datasets, with the three failures needing a richer dose-response form. crossnma is also broader than the source described: its CRAN title is Cross-Design and Cross-Format Network Meta-Analysis and Regression and it handles individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both with meta-regression on up to three covariates, while its cross-design bias-adjustment parameter remains unidentified by the outcomes being combined. Neither package standardizes to an external target covariate distribution.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Why it is open
In a disconnected network the shared dose-response or class structure supplies the identification that randomization does not, so the comparison depends on a functional form the analyst chose, and a fitted curve returns a smooth plausible estimate at any dose without showing how much of the comparison the curve contributed. Deletion validation shows the assumption can hold in practice, but it was run on datasets where the connected answer was known, which is exactly what a genuinely disconnected application lacks. For crossnma, the parameter expressing how far nonrandomized evidence is down-weighted is not identified by the outcomes being combined, so residual confounding passes into the pooled estimate scaled by an assumed factor. Neither package carries a target covariate distribution, so combining doses or designs does not address who the estimate applies to.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




MBNMAdose (CRAN)
fits model-based dose-response network meta-analysis linking treatments and doses through a shared dose axis, which can connect otherwise disconnected networks under the assumed curve and class structure


crossnma (CRAN)
cross-design and cross-format network meta-analysis and regression for individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both using a three-level hierarchical model, with meta-regression on up to three covariates and explicit modeling of design bias; performs no standardization to an external target population


Pedder, Dias, Bennetts, Boucher and Welton 2021
deletes studies and treatments from a triptans network and compares MBNMA estimates on the resulting disconnected networks against NMA on augmented networks, agreeing in 15 of 18 datasets with the remaining 3 needing a more complex dose-response relationship; the validation evidence the entry omitted

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Probable solution or research direction
When dose-response models bridge disconnected evidence, report how much of the comparison is driven by the curve and class assumptions, and check them the way they can be checked: alternative curve families, goodness of fit against the dose-level randomized evidence, and deletion validation of the kind Pedder et al. performed. When designs are combined, treat cross-design exchangeability and residual confounding as explicit sensitivity parameters rather than fixed inputs, and exploit overlapping designs where they exist. In both cases obtain population adjustment and target transport from separate tooling rather than assuming the synthesis has supplied it.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. MBNMAdose can bridge otherwise disconnected treatments through an assumed dose-response form, and in a truly disconnected network that form is not identified by the data being combined, although Pedder et al. (2021) validated it by deletion in 15 of 18 semi-synthetic datasets; crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence and individual with aggregate data, and its cross-design bias-adjustment parameter is not identified by the data being combined. Neither package standardises to an external target covariate distribution.
The source titled this. “MBNMAdose and crossnma bridge on assumptions data cannot check” The title says the bridging assumptions cannot be checked, but randomized dose-level evidence supports fit and curve-family comparison and MBNMA was validated by deletion in 15 of 18 datasets.
The source said. “MBNMAdose is an active dose-response NMA ecosystem that connects treatments and doses mechanistically, and crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence with bias considerations. In both, the assumption that creates the link (the dose-response curve and class structure; cross-design exchangeability) can dominate the resulting comparison, and neither performs population adjustment or automatic target transport.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors called the title claim too strong. The literature auditor supplied the paper the entry omitted, Pedder et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315), which validated MBNMA by deletion in 15 of 18 semi-synthetic datasets, and corrected the description of crossnma, which handles individual, aggregate and mixed-format data rather than only randomized plus nonrandomized evidence; GPT-5.6 Sol added that curve assumptions are partly checkable through fit and curve-family comparison and that mechanistic overstates what is model-based or semi-mechanistic dose-response modeling.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. The title claim ‘assumptions data cannot check’ is too strong for MBNMAdose, and the entry omits the paper that shows why. Pedder, Dias, Bennetts, Boucher and Welton (2021) ran exactly the bridge-deletion experiment the agenda asks for elsewhere: they deleted studies and treatments from a triptans NMA and compared MBNMA estimates on the resulting disconnected networks against NMA on augmented networks, finding agreement in 15 of 18 datasets and identifying the three failures as needing a richer dose-response form. That paper sits in the catalog’s own documentation/refs folder yet SFW-16 cites only the CRAN page. Separately, crossnma is described too narrowly. Its CRAN title is ‘Cross-Design & Cross-Format Network Meta-Analysis and Regression’ and it handles individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both with meta-regression on up to three covariates, so it is not merely an RCT-plus-observational combiner; the accurate residual claim is that it performs no standardisation to an external target population.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C3, C4, and C6 are sound: MBNMAdose is not general population-adjustment software, crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence with bias modeling, and neither automatically standardizes to an external target population. C2 is sound only conditionally: in a disconnected comparison, shared curve or class structure can supply the otherwise missing identification. But randomized dose-level evidence still estimates the curve parameters and can support goodness-of-fit checks, comparisons among curve families, and bridge-deletion validation. The statements that the comparison is determined by functional form rather than randomized evidence and that the curve contribution cannot be seen are therefore too strong. C1 also uses ‘mechanistic’ too broadly for what is generally model-based or semi-mechanistic dose-response modeling. C5 is correct only as a causal-identification limitation: cross-design exchangeability and absence of residual confounding cannot be established from the combined outcomes alone, although crossnma can explicitly model design bias and exploit overlapping designs. The remaining transport and sensitivity-analysis gaps are open, but they are decision-critical only when disconnected or nonrandomized evidence is load-bearing; otherwise they are roadmap items.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text: SFW-14 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Implementation-specific

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Statement
drMAIC 0.1.0 appeared on CRAN on 29 March 2026 as Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA, sole author Anupama Singh, implementing entropy balancing with augmented, doubly robust MAIC, diagnostics and bootstrap confidence intervals for binary and time-to-event outcomes, with one vignette and a single test file; its repository was created on 23 March 2026 and last pushed the next day. No accompanying methods publication and no independent evaluation were found, so treating it as a reference implementation is premature. What such an audit can settle needs separating from what it cannot: double robustness is an analytical property holding under identification, positivity, regularity and correct specification of at least one nuisance model, so simulation tests the implementation and its finite-sample behavior rather than the theorem. Augmented weighting for PAIC is also not new with drMAIC, since Gao, Heath and Baio (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10021) published G-MAIC, which combines outcome regression with weighting adjustment and was evaluated across 18 scenarios against MAIC and parametric G-computation.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Why it is open
A doubly robust weighting package makes a claim about behavior under misspecification that a user cannot check from their own data, so only review of the estimating equations plus finite-sample simulation can show whether the implementation delivers what the theory promises. Simulation evidence shipped with a method is generated under that method’s own assumptions, and here there is no shipped simulation and no methods paper at all, only one vignette and one test file. The field has no neutral benchmark suite, so a new package’s operating characteristics cannot be checked by anyone except its author. A CRAN release confers apparent legitimacy in HTA submissions faster than independent evaluation can be produced, so the validation gap widens with each new package.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




drMAIC 0.1.0 (CRAN, published 29 Mar 2026; Anupama Singh)
implements entropy balancing with standard and augmented, doubly robust MAIC, diagnostics, sensitivity tools and bootstrap confidence intervals for binary and time-to-event outcomes; one vignette, a single test file, and no accompanying methods publication found


Gao, Heath and Baio 2025, Regression augmented weighting adjustment for indirect comparisons in health decision modelling (G-MAIC)
combines outcome regression with weighting adjustment and uses a Bayesian bootstrap to propagate the uncertainty of population-adjusted estimates, evaluated against non-adjusted methods, MAIC and parametric G-computation across 18 scenarios; the published comparator any drMAIC benchmark should include

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Subject drMAIC to independent review of its code and estimating equations, then to finite-sample comparison under one nuisance model correct, both models wrong and weak overlap, reporting failed fits rather than only successful ones. Include the published comparators, G-MAIC and parametric G-computation, so the exercise places drMAIC against methods that already carry simulation evidence. Keep the claims separated in reporting: the double-robustness property needs a proof under stated identification and regularity conditions, while omitted-modifier scenarios test violation of exchangeability and belong in a sensitivity analysis. Component drift belongs only in a component-PAIC extension, not in this package’s benchmark.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “drMAIC’s doubly robust claims lack independent adversarial audit” The title demands an adversarial audit of the double-robustness claim, a standard the audit rejected since simulation tests the implementation rather than the theorem.
The source said. “drMAIC appeared on CRAN in March 2026 as an early implementation of standard and augmented, doubly robust MAIC with diagnostics and sensitivity tools. The report holds that its methodological and software claims require independent audit, adversarial simulation and head-to-head comparison with established transport estimators before it is treated as a reference implementation, because package availability is evidence of implementation and not of methodological superiority.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol judged the proposed proof standard wrong: adversarial simulation checks implementation and operating characteristics but cannot establish or refute the double-robustness theorem, both nuisance models being wrong is an expected failure condition rather than a test of the property, an omitted modifier violates exchangeability rather than misspecifying a nuisance model, and component drift is irrelevant unless drMAIC is extended to component models. The literature auditor added that augmented weighting for PAIC already has a published comparator, G-MAIC (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10021), which any benchmark should include.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. CRAN confirms drMAIC 0.1.0 published 2026-03-29, ‘Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA’, sole author Anupama Singh, entropy balancing plus augmented/DR MAIC with diagnostics, bootstrap CIs, binary and time-to-event outcomes, one vignette. Source line 1044 matches the entry’s wording verbatim. The repository corroborates the immaturity concern harder than the entry does: created 2026-03-23, last pushed 2026-03-24, two stars, and tests/testthat contains a single file, test_core.R. I found no accompanying methods publication and no independent evaluation, though per calibration an absence I found by searching is not proof. One correction of emphasis: augmented weighting for PAIC is not new with drMAIC. Gao, Heath and Baio (2025) published G-MAIC, combining outcome regression with weighting and evaluated over 18 scenarios against MAIC and parametric G-computation, so the benchmark the entry asks for has a published comparator to include.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Independent implementation audit and finite-sample benchmarking are prudent before treating drMAIC as a reference implementation. The report’s proof standard is nevertheless wrong: double robustness is an analytical property under identification, consistency, positivity, regularity, and correct specification of at least one nuisance model; simulation checks implementation and finite-sample behavior but cannot establish the theorem by itself. Both nuisance models being wrong is an expected failure condition, poor overlap targets positivity and numerical behavior, and an omitted modifier violates exchangeability rather than merely misspecifying a nuisance model. Component drift is not a relevant benchmark unless drMAIC is extended to component models. No local drMAIC source was available to verify C1-C3, while absence of prior audits and field-wide benchmarks are literature-status claims outside this lens.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text: SFW-12 Confirmed open High priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Statement
outstandR reached CRAN as version 2.0.0 on 10 June 2026, titled Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data (Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar), implementing the parametric G-computation approach of Remiro-Azocar, Heath and Baio (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565). Its CRAN description is framed entirely around the two-trial limited-IPD problem with no mention of networks, so the pairwise focus holds, and no published validation covers its behavior in networks or across disconnected evidence. Dependence on the target covariate distribution is partly definitional rather than a defect, since standardization is defined relative to a declared target, and the package ships custom-copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes that acknowledge the sensitivity rather than hiding it. Dependence on the outcome model is a genuine robustness concern, and any disconnected-network use would additionally require structural bridge assumptions that standardization cannot identify.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Why it is open
Outcome standardization was developed for the two-trial indirect comparison, so extending it to a network requires deciding how standardized arm-level quantities from different studies combine while preserving within-study randomization, which is not a mechanical generalization. Reconstructing the target covariate distribution from limited published moments makes the result sensitive to the reconstruction, which the copula vignette exposes but cannot resolve. Nothing published characterizes the package’s behavior in networks or across disconnected evidence, and in the disconnected case standardization would need a bridge assumption it cannot identify from the data. The 2.0.0 separation of outcome model from balance model prepares the way for doubly robust variants that are not there yet.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




outstandR (project site)
computes compatible marginal effects by model-based standardization and covariate simulation as an alternative to conventional STC; documentation site including the custom-copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes


outstandR 2.0.0 (CRAN, published 10 Jun 2026; Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar)
released package titled Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data, framed around the two-trial limited-IPD problem; its 2.0.0 release notes separate outcome_model from balance_model to accommodate forthcoming doubly robust methods


Remiro-Azocar, Heath and Baio 2022, Parametric G-computation for compatible indirect treatment comparisons with limited individual patient data, Research Synthesis Methods
standardizes a GLM or Cox outcome model over the target covariate distribution to recover a marginal effect compatible with the aggregate-data trial; the method outstandR implements

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Characterize rather than rebuild: run outstandR against alternative reconstructions of the target distribution and alternative outcome models to map where the estimate moves, using the copula machinery the package already exposes. Extend the standardization from the pairwise case to networks by specifying how standardized arm-level quantities combine while preserving within-study randomization, and state explicitly which bridge assumption any disconnected-network extension would rely on. Use the 2.0.0 outcome-model and balance-model split as the hook for doubly robust variants, and publish the network validation that does not currently exist.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “outstandR is pairwise only and sensitive to the simulated target” The title treats sensitivity to the target distribution as a defect, but the audit found it partly definitional and found shipped vignettes that acknowledge it.
The source said. “outstandR is an active outcome-standardization package producing compatible marginal effects through model-based standardization and covariate simulation, and a useful alternative to conventional STC, but it is focused on pairwise comparisons, is sensitive to the target distribution and outcome model, and needs broader network and disconnected-network validation.”
What was wrong with it. The source cited only the pkgdown site; the literature auditor found outstandR is now on CRAN at version 2.0.0 (10 June 2026) with the underlying method published (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565), and that the package already ships copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes addressing the target-distribution sensitivity the entry treats as unexamined. GPT-5.6 Sol added that sensitivity to the target distribution is partly definitional and that disconnected-network use would need bridge assumptions standardization cannot supply, making this a roadmap limitation rather than a defect in pairwise use.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The characterisation is accurate but the citation is stale. outstandR is no longer only a pkgdown site: version 2.0.0 is on CRAN, published 2026-06-10, titled ‘Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data’, authored by Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar and built on the parametric G-computation paper (doi 10.1002/jrsm.1565). The CRAN description is framed entirely around the two-trial limited-IPD problem with no mention of networks, which supports ‘focused on pairwise comparisons’. Sensitivity to the reconstructed target is real enough that the package ships a custom-copula vignette and a diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignette, so the package acknowledges rather than hides it. The 2.0.0 NEWS separates outcome_model from balance_model explicitly to ‘future-proof the package for upcoming doubly-robust methods’. I found no published validation of outstandR in networks or disconnected evidence, so that claim stands, though absence of validation is not something I can positively verify.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Standardizing arm-specific outcome predictions over the same target joint covariate distribution yields compatible marginal effects and is technically preferable to conventional mean-covariate STC for nonlinear or non-collapsible models. Pairwise focus and broader network validation are reasonable open scope questions. Dependence on the target population is partly definitional rather than a defect, while dependence on the outcome model is a genuine robustness concern. Disconnected-network use would additionally require structural bridge assumptions that standardization cannot identify. This is a roadmap-level limitation for network use, not a critical defect for an explicitly pairwise analysis. No local outstandR source was available for code-level confirmation of package capabilities.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text: SFW-10 Partially addressed Very high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Statement
maicplus 0.1.2 still needs a joint sandwich estimator covering the outcome and weight-estimation equations (#111), parallel bootstrap (#148), explicit estimand metadata and ATT reporting (#142), alternative weight scaling (#178), reporting expansion (#154) and principled trimming or truncation that discloses the lost calibration and changed target (#141). Several disclosures the source asked for already exist in the release: the bootstrap re-estimates weights inside each IPD resample, the anchored path perturbs the published comparator effect by its standard error, scaled and unscaled weights are exposed, the survival effect is labeled as a hazard ratio, and the unanchored bootstrap documents that it assumes no uncertainty in the comparator trial population. The claim about propagating aggregate-data uncertainty in the bootstrap has no matching open issue, the nearest being #143 on pinning down the anchored bootstrap, although target covariate summaries do remain fixed. Treating estimated weights as fixed also does not invariably understate variance, and simple trimming changes calibration and the effective target without producing a clean ATT estimand.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Why it is open
MAIC weights are estimated, so a variance that ignores the weight-estimation step is wrong in a direction that depends on the design rather than always downward, and no released estimator stacks the outcome and weighting estimating equations even though the comparative evidence on which variance families behave well is published. Trimming or truncating weights changes the calibration and the population actually being estimated, and no agreed rule exists to implement, so an actively maintained package has nothing to adopt. Whether the published target summaries should carry uncertainty depends on the inferential framework, and the package conditions on them without saying that this is a choice. The remaining disclosure gaps are structural rather than technical: defaults produce valid-looking output, so an omitted estimand declaration is invisible downstream, which is how such errors reach submissions.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




maicplus 0.1.2 (CRAN, published 21 Feb 2025)
implements MAIC weighting, variance and reporting utilities whose open issues include weight-estimation-aware variance, trimming and estimand metadata; the report proposes it should evolve into a reference implementation


hta-pharma/maicplus (GitHub)
maintained open MAIC workflow repository, successor to older Roche MAIC tooling; open issues verified in the audit are #111 sandwich estimator for derived weights, #141 trimming and truncation, #142 ATT reporting, #148 parallel bootstrap, #178 alternative weight scaling, #154 reporting functions and #143 on pinning down the anchored bootstrap


maicplus 0.1.2 bootstrap and reporting implementation, hta-pharma/maicplus@aabcaf8
shows the bootstrap re-estimates weights within each IPD resample rather than treating them as fixed, the anchored path perturbs the published comparator effect by its standard error, scaled and unscaled weights are exposed, and the unanchored bootstrap documents its assumption of no uncertainty in the comparator trial population


Chandler and Proskorovsky 2024, Uncertain about uncertainty in matching-adjusted indirect comparisons? A simulation study to compare methods for variance estimation, Res Synth Methods 15(6):1094-1110
compares conventional raw-weight, ESS-rescaled, sandwich and bootstrap variance estimators across 108 scenarios and finds sandwich estimators downward-biased at small ESS with finite-sample adjustment markedly improving them; concrete guidance the variance work can be calibrated against


Remiro-Azocar 2022 (two-stage MAIC)
quantifies the trade-off from weight truncation, finding substantial precision and efficiency gains but considerable induced bias, and states that truncation shifts the target population or estimand definition; the evidence a trimming implementation should surface


Jiang et al. 2025 (the MAIC paradox)
shows with synthetic data that different entities can reach opposing conclusions from the same data when the target population is not clearly defined, sourcing the estimand-disclosure argument this entry makes


Ishak et al. 2025, A Framework for Reliable, Transparent, and Reproducible Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons, PharmacoEconomics
published PAIC reporting and risk-of-bias framework whose elements a reference MAIC workflow can implement structurally instead of designing disclosure requirements from scratch

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Implement the joint sandwich estimator over the outcome and weight-estimation equations, calibrated against the published comparison of variance families rather than derived in isolation, and add parallel bootstrap so the recommended sensitivity analyses fit submission timelines. Add trimming and truncation that report the calibration lost and the target actually estimated, using the published quantification of the bias and precision trade-off as the default warning. Attach explicit estimand metadata to the fitted object and expand reporting against the existing PAIC reporting framework (Ishak et al., doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) so the estimand, weight construction, variance method, any trimming-induced change of target and the survival effect measure are structurally disclosed. Decide separately whether target-summary uncertainty is propagated, and state which inferential framework the package assumes.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Open maicplus issues include sandwich variance accounting for estimated weights, propagating aggregate-data uncertainty in the bootstrap, parallel bootstrap, alternative weight scaling, weight trimming and truncation, explicit ATT reporting and reporting expansion. The report argues a reference MAIC workflow should eventually make the estimand, the weight construction, the variance method, the trimming-induced target change and the survival measure impossible to overlook.”
What was wrong with it. The literature auditor verified issues #111, #141, #142, #148, #178 and #154 but found no issue on propagating aggregate-data uncertainty in the bootstrap, and GPT-5.6 Sol found in the 0.1.2 source (hta-pharma/maicplus@aabcaf8) that the bootstrap already re-estimates weights, the anchored path already propagates comparator-effect uncertainty, and several scaling and effect-measure disclosures already exist. The premise that these gaps persist because the methods are unsettled fails for variance and trimming, where Chandler and Proskorovsky (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1759) give concrete guidance across 108 scenarios and Remiro-Azocar (doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01692-9) quantifies the bias cost of truncation; the claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced, with Jiang et al. (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10) supplying the MAIC paradox evidence behind the estimand-disclosure argument.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): Nearly every issue claim verifies verbatim in the open maicplus tracker: #111 sandwich estimator accounting for derived weights, #141 trimming and truncation, #142 ATT reporting, #148 parallel bootstrap, #178 alternative weight scaling, #154 reporting functions. One claim I could not confirm: ‘propagating aggregate-data uncertainty in the bootstrap’ has no matching issue; the nearest open item is #143 ‘pin down the implementation of bootstrap in anchored case’, and #182/#28 on bootstrapping are closed. The why_open framing that these gaps persist because the methods are unsettled is too strong for variance: Chandler & Proskorovsky (2024) evaluated four variance families over 108 scenarios and give concrete guidance, and Remiro-Azocar (2022) quantified the bias cost of truncation. The estimand-disclosure argument gains a real citation from Jiang et al. (2025) on the MAIC paradox and target-population definition, which the entry does not cite. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is an empty placeholder. Version 0.1.2 lacks a joint sandwich estimator for outcome and weight-estimation equations, parallel bootstrap, trimming or truncation controls, and explicit estimand metadata. However, its bootstrap re-estimates weights within IPD resamples, and the anchored bootstrap perturbs the published comparator effect using its standard error. Target covariate summaries remain fixed. The package already exposes scaled and unscaled weights, labels the survival effect as HR, and explicitly discloses the unanchored bootstrap’s conditioning assumption. Treating estimated weights as fixed can increase or decrease variance error, not invariably understate variance. Simple trimming changes calibration and the effective target but does not necessarily create a clean ATT estimand.

The why_open framing that these gaps persist because the methods are unsettled is too strong for variance: Chandler & Proskorovsky (2024) evaluated four variance families over 108 scenarios and give concrete guidance, and Remiro-Azocar (2022) quantified the bias cost of truncation. The estimand-disclosure argument gains a real citation from Jiang et al. (2025) on the MAIC paradox and target-population definition, which the entry does not cite.

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is an empty placeholder. Version 0.1.2 lacks a joint sandwich estimator for outcome and weight-estimation equations, parallel bootstrap, trimming or truncation controls, and explicit estimand metadata. However, its bootstrap re-estimates weights within IPD resamples, and the anchored bootstrap perturbs the published comparator effect using its standard error. Target covariate summaries remain fixed. The package already exposes scaled and unscaled weights, labels the survival effect as HR, and explicitly discloses the unanchored bootstrap’s conditioning assumption. Treating estimated weights as fixed can increase or decrease variance error, not invariably understate variance. Simple trimming changes calibration and the effective target but does not necessarily create a clean ATT estimand. title: No agreed leave-one-out unit for mixed IPD and aggregate likelihoods
text:
Statement
Open multinma issues record poor Pareto-k behavior together with ambiguity over the unit of leave-one-out prediction (#60), absent prior-sensitivity tooling (#32) and uncertainty around rankings and SUCRA (#17). Two of these are implementation gaps with published prescriptions rather than missing methods: #32 asks multinma to expose log-prior evaluations so the existing power-scaling method in priorsense can be used, and #17 asks for SUCRA credible intervals following Trinquart et al., which is arithmetic on the mean-rank posterior. multinma 0.9.1 already reports posterior rank distributions with credible intervals through posterior_ranks() and shows prior-to-posterior movement through plot_prior_posterior(), so the ranking and prior-dependence gaps are narrower than stated. What is genuinely unsettled is the held-out unit: loo.stan_nma delegates to rstan::loo while the log-likelihood mixes patient-level IPD, arm-level aggregate and study-level contrast contributions, so the unit is heterogeneous, no unit selection or exact-refit fallback is exposed, and no field convention fixes which unit answers which predictive question.

title: No agreed leave-one-out unit for mixed IPD and aggregate likelihoods
text:
Why it is open
In a hierarchical evidence-synthesis model there is no single natural held-out unit, and multinma’s log-likelihood mixes patients, arms and study-level contrasts, so a reported leave-one-out number aggregates over units that answer different predictive questions and is not comparable across analyses. No convention fixes the unit and no exact-refit or grouped fallback is exposed for when the importance-sampling approximation degrades, which is precisely when the model is complex enough for the comparison to matter. Prior dependence in sparse or partially disconnected networks is visible only if the analyst chooses to look, since power-scaling needs a log-prior the package does not expose and the prior-versus-posterior plot is qualitative. Rankings compound this because SUCRA is a nonlinear functional of the posterior reported without an interval, even though the mean-rank interval it would be derived from is already available.

title: No agreed leave-one-out unit for mixed IPD and aggregate likelihoods
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Settle the held-out unit first, because it is the only item with no published answer: define what leaving out a patient, an arm, a study or a treatment means in hierarchical NMA and ML-NMR, implement a diagnostic for each, and provide an exact-refit or grouped fallback when Pareto-k diagnostics fail. The other three are plumbing against known prescriptions: expose log-prior evaluations so priorsense power-scaling works, derive SUCRA intervals from the mean-rank posterior as Trinquart et al. specify, and surface both by default rather than as optional extra analysis. Report Pareto-k failure as a statement about the approximation rather than about the model, so users do not discard a valid fit.

title: ML-NMR runtime can constrain repeated sensitivity analyses at scale
text: SFW-06 Unverifiable High priority Established Implementation-specific

title: ML-NMR runtime can constrain repeated sensitivity analyses at scale
text:
Statement
multinma ML-NMR can become computationally expensive as aggregate-data integration rows and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo gradient evaluations grow, which can constrain repeated sensitivity analyses in large models. Open issue #66 (raised 17 March 2026) reports 24 hours or more for 16000 iterations with 200-plus integration points in a random-effects model over many studies, and open issue #29 (14 January 2024) requests a cmdstanr backend, which may improve compilation and execution but does not remove the model’s integration arithmetic. The auditors disagreed on how far this generalizes and both readings stand: the literature auditor verified every claim as stated and read the tracker as evidence that users hit prohibitive runtimes, while GPT-5.6 Sol found that release 0.9.1 already reduced the default integration burden and added integration checking, so the evidence supports a material caution at larger scales rather than a general block on routine sensitivity analysis.

title: ML-NMR runtime can constrain repeated sensitivity analyses at scale
text:
Why it is open
ML-NMR requires numerical integration over the covariate distribution inside every likelihood and gradient evaluation, and while integration nodes and design data can be reused, the parameter-dependent likelihood terms cannot, so cost grows with total integration rows and is not amortizable across iterations. At large scale that turns computation into a methodological constraint, because the sensitivity analyses, prior checks and simulation studies the rest of the agenda demands multiply the cost. How large is large enough to matter has never been characterized, which is exactly why two auditors read the same tracker differently. The backend request reflects the same pressure but addresses compilation and execution rather than the integration arithmetic itself.

title: No neutral cross-package benchmark suite for PAIC implementations
text: SFW-04 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging Tractability 5/5

title: No neutral cross-package benchmark suite for PAIC implementations
text:
Statement
No neutral field-wide benchmark exists that compares baseline connection, CNMA, component PAIC, reference prediction, dose-response models, class effects and partial identification under shared disconnected-network data-generating mechanisms, with public seeds, versioned expected outputs and analytic-truth unit tests. Package-local infrastructure of that kind does exist: at commit 9d150e9 cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, ships seeded disconnected-network fixtures with known truth, analytic estimability and likelihood tests, deliberate non-estimability tests, multi-arm tests and cross-package equivalence checks against maicplus. Independent comparative simulation also exists for parts of the field: Chandler and Proskorovsky (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1759) compared four families of MAIC variance estimator across 108 scenarios, and Liu et al. (doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1) ran a 729-scenario full-factorial comparison of unanchored MAIC against naive indirect comparison, neither promoting a method of its own. What is missing is the neutral, maintained, cross-package suite that any implementation can be run against.

title: No neutral cross-package benchmark suite for PAIC implementations
text:
Why it is open
Cross-package validation needs an agreed estimand and input format, neither of which exists, so outside a single package’s own fixtures there is nothing for expected outputs to be expected against. The independent simulation studies that do exist each answer one question and were not built to be re-run by others, so they are evidence rather than infrastructure: no seeds, manifests or reference implementations survive for the next comparison. The mechanisms that would actually discriminate between bridges, namely bridge violation, component drift, unmeasured modifiers and design differences, are still rarely simulated by anyone. Benchmarks are maintenance work with no publication reward and need cross-group coordination nobody owns, so discrepancies surface only in appraisals, where they are attributed to analyst choice rather than to software behavior.

title: No neutral cross-package benchmark suite for PAIC implementations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Generalize what already exists rather than starting over: promote cpaic’s seeded known-truth fixtures and cross-package equivalence tests into a package-independent repository, and re-express the published author-neutral simulations as re-runnable scenarios with seeds and manifests. Add the adversarial data-generating mechanisms nobody currently simulates, including bridge violation, component drift, unmeasured modifiers and design difference, and declare an estimand and decision-relevant performance measures for each. Ship versioned expected outputs, analytic-truth unit tests and reference implementations with containerized workflows so any ITC or PAIC package can be run against them and discrepancies are attributable to software rather than to analyst choice.

title: No neutral cross-package benchmark suite for PAIC implementations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “No neutral benchmark suite or analytic-truth tests for PAIC code” The title says analytic-truth tests do not exist, but seeded known-truth fixtures, analytic and non-estimability tests and cross-package equivalence checks were found.
The source said. “There is no open benchmark suite for ITC, PAIC, disconnected-network, component and QBA methods with synthetic and real exemplars, public seeds, expected outputs, analytic-truth unit tests and cross-package validation, and no shared set of disconnected-network data-generating mechanisms under which baseline connection, CNMA, cpaic, reference prediction, dose-response models, class effects and partial identification can be compared. The report argues such a neutral comparison is a publication in its own right and may have more practical influence than another estimator paper.”
What was wrong with it. The source claimed PAIC software is not routinely unit tested against analytic truth and that no benchmark datasets or cross-package tests exist; GPT-5.6 Sol found seeded known-truth fixtures, analytic and deliberate non-estimability tests and cross-package equivalence checks already in cpaic at commit 9d150e9, and the literature auditor rejected the premise that comparative evidence comes mostly from the authors of the method being promoted, naming two author-neutral simulation studies (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1759, doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1). title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text: SFW-02 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text:
Statement
The report proposes a cross-package machine-readable object, illustrated as a YAML specification, recording the estimand (population, outcome, contrast, intercurrent-event strategy), the evidence structure, the bridge, the adjustment, the quantitative bias analysis configuration and the requested output, and the literature auditor confirmed every field verbatim in the source at section 16.6. No such schema was found, but that is an exhaustive software-landscape negative neither auditor could verify rather than an established fact. Prose-level reporting structure for PAIC does exist: Ishak et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) publishes a framework for reliable, transparent and reproducible population-adjusted indirect comparisons, but it governs what an analyst reports and does not define a machine-readable object that packages read and emit. A schema would also make analyses portable and auditable only if it carried controlled definitions, versioning, validation rules, provenance and explicit mappings to package-specific estimands, so serializing labels into YAML is necessary rather than sufficient.

title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text:
Why it is open
Every package encodes these choices implicitly in its own arguments and defaults, so moving an analysis between tools means re-deriving the specification from code, and the published reporting framework is a prose checklist a reviewer reads rather than an artifact a program can validate. Standardizing function names would not help, because the packages implement genuinely different models; what is shared is the scientific specification, not the API. Current packages lead with the estimate and keep assumptions in model code and prior specifications, so there is nothing to serialize without new work. Adoption further requires controlled vocabularies and estimand mappings agreed among independently maintained packages that have no incentive structure for that coordination.

title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ishak et al. 2025, A Framework for Reliable, Transparent, and Reproducible Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons, PharmacoEconomics
publishes a reporting and risk-of-bias framework for population-adjusted indirect comparisons, the closest existing thing to a PAIC reporting standard; it is prose for analysts rather than a machine-readable specification that packages can read, emit or validate

title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the schema on top of the reporting framework that already exists rather than beside it: take the elements Ishak et al. 2025 asks analysts to report and give them controlled definitions, a version, validation rules, provenance fields and explicit mappings to each package’s estimand conventions. Have synthesis packages read and emit it, and generate the assumptions map, bridge ledger and bias ledger from it, printed before the estimate rather than after. Make round-tripping the acceptance test: the same specification loaded into two packages should yield the same declared estimand and target, not merely the same field names.

title: No machine-readable specification standard for ITC analyses
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The report proposes a cross-package machine-readable object, illustrated as a YAML specification, recording the estimand (population, outcome, contrast, intercurrent-event strategy), the evidence structure (connectedness, number of randomized subnetworks, which studies have IPD), the bridge (type, components, drift sensitivity), the adjustment (modifiers, prognostics, target distribution), the QBA configuration and the output requested, and argues the bridge ledger itself should be machine-readable so that assumption and sensitivity summaries can be generated automatically. No such schema or package-generated ledger exists.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated as fact that no machine-readable bridge-ledger schema exists and that no package generates assumption and sensitivity summaries automatically; both auditors classed these as exhaustive negatives they could not confirm, and GPT-5.6 Sol added that a schema is enabling infrastructure rather than a condition for a valid analysis. The reporting side is not empty either: Ishak et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) already publishes a PAIC reporting and risk-of-bias framework in prose.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I retrieved the source document (documentation/open_problems_itc_paic_cpaic_qba_2026.md, section 16.6, lines 2324-2359) and every self-referential claim checks out verbatim: the YAML block contains estimand (population, outcome, contrast, strategy: ‘treatment policy’), evidence (connected, randomized_subnetworks, ipd_studies), bridge (type, components, drift_sensitivity), adjustment (modifiers, prognostics, target_distribution), qba (mode, omitted_variables, selection_bias, outcome_misclassification, component_drift, parameter_sources) and output (marginal, conditional, partial_identification), followed by ‘This is more valuable than forcing all packages to share the same function names. It makes the scientific specification portable and auditable.’ The two existence claims (‘no machine-readable schema for a disconnected-network bridge ledger currently exists’; ‘no current package automatically generates assumption and sensitivity summaries’) are negatives I searched for and could not confirm from any source that itself asserts the absence; per calibration they are unverifiable, not supported. Adjacent prior art exists on machine-readable evidence-synthesis databases but it concerns extraction databases, not estimand/bridge specification.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 and C4-C8 describe a technically feasible schema, and scientific semantics are more important than standardized function names as claimed in C2. C3 holds only if the schema also has controlled definitions, versioning, validation rules, provenance, and explicit mappings to package-specific estimands; serializing labels into YAML alone does not make analyses portable or auditable. The illustrated fields are proposed requirements, not an implemented or enforced standard. The interoperability and auditability problem is real, but a machine-readable schema is enabling infrastructure rather than an identification condition or a universal prerequisite for a valid decision-grade analysis.

title: No agreed parameterization or format for unanchored PAIC sensitivity
text: QBA-29 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: No agreed parameterization or format for unanchored PAIC sensitivity
text:
Statement
Unanchored PAICs depend on cross-study exchangeability and transportability assumptions that are strong and partly untestable: Phillippo et al. 2017 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740), the peer-reviewed account of NICE DSU TSD 18, state that unanchored comparisons make much stronger assumptions, which are widely regarded as infeasible. The report’s rule, that no unanchored PAIC receives a strong causal interpretation without a formal QBA or partial-identification analysis or an explicit exploratory label, is a reporting safeguard rather than a condition for identification: QBA is neither mathematically necessary when the identifying assumptions hold nor sufficient to justify a causal claim, and it never establishes the absence of bias outside the specified model or range. Residual bias is unestimable from the usual observed data law without auxiliary information, so negative controls, proxies, validation data or additional structural restrictions are what would change that, and there is still no agreed parameterization, threshold or reporting format for the sensitivity analysis the rule would require.

title: No agreed parameterization or format for unanchored PAIC sensitivity
text:
Why it is open
Residual bias in an unanchored comparison is a function of unmeasured prognostic structure, so within the usual data law it can only be bounded by assumption, and there is no agreed parameterization, prior or reporting format for that bias in the ITC setting, so even a willing analyst has no standard instrument. Enforcement depends on journals and appraisal bodies while unanchored PAICs continue to be submitted as primary comparative evidence with no quantification of residual bias, often where no alternative exists, so the pressure is toward a point estimate rather than a bias range. There is no agreed threshold for what counts as a formal QBA, so a token one-parameter analysis could satisfy the letter of the rule. Labeling a result exploratory also removes the basis for a reimbursement decision that still has to be made, which creates pressure against applying the rule exactly where it matters most.

title: No agreed parameterization or format for unanchored PAIC sensitivity
text:

Work
What it contributes




NICE Decision Support Unit, Technical Support Document 18: Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Submissions to NICE
Long-standing guidance treating the unanchored population-adjustment assumption set as unusually demanding. The entry cited it with no locator; this is the document it referred to.


Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2017, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (peer-reviewed account of NICE DSU TSD 18)
States that unanchored comparisons make much stronger assumptions, which are widely regarded as infeasible, and that the accuracy of unanchored estimates is unknown because residual bias from unobserved factors cannot be quantified. Supplies the real citation for the entry’s unsourced NICE claims.


Ren et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Motivated by the observation that robustness of unanchored results with regard to model assumptions is often only qualitatively discussed, corroborating the absence of a routine residual-bias sensitivity analysis.


Leahy et al. 2023, International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
HTA workshop recommendations whose ninth item is that QBA should generally be considered a sensitivity analysis, supporting the claim that no standard residual-bias analysis routinely accompanies unanchored PAIC.

title: No agreed parameterization or format for unanchored PAIC sensitivity
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adopt the rule as a reporting safeguard rather than as an identification criterion: require unanchored submissions to state the exchangeability and transportability assumptions explicitly and, for decision-grade use, to accompany the estimate with QBA or partial identification over substantively justified departures, qualifying the causal interpretation as exploratory where adequate sensitivity analysis is unavailable. Define a minimum standard for what qualifies, so a token one-parameter analysis does not satisfy it, and state in the output that the analysis characterizes robustness under its own assumptions rather than establishing the absence of bias. Pair the exploratory label with decision procedures that can act on bounds, and where auxiliary information exists, whether negative controls, proxies, validation data or defensible structural restrictions, use it rather than treating residual bias as unaddressable in principle.

title: Prespecification and outcome-driven choice of sensitivity ranges
text: QBA-27 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Prespecification and outcome-driven choice of sensitivity ranges
text:
Statement
Sensitivity parameters, their scales, ranges, distributions and dependence assumptions should be prespecified where feasible, and this is already published HTA guidance rather than a new proposal: Leahy et al. 2023 (doi:10.1017/S0266462323002702) recommend that input parameters be identified through a systematic and transparent approach and specified a priori in a protocol or analysis plan, with code and data shared with HTA bodies and early engagement on the nature of the QBA. Ranges tuned after seeing which values preserve statistical significance or cost-effectiveness must not be presented as prespecified, although a disclosed post hoc tipping search is a legitimate exploratory analysis. What is missing is enforcement rather than the principle: no dedicated registration or auditable tooling makes a post hoc range change visible in the record, and no QBA-specific correction repairs undisclosed data-dependent selection over models and ranges, even though a specification can already be time-stamped in an ordinary protocol or registry and general selective-inference, multiverse and worst-case methods exist.

title: Prespecification and outcome-driven choice of sensitivity ranges
text:
Why it is open
QBA multiplies analyst degrees of freedom because every bias parameter has a scale, a range, a distribution and a dependence structure that are chosen rather than estimated, and the analysis is typically performed by the sponsor after the primary result is known. A reviewer reading the submission cannot distinguish a prespecified range from one tuned until the conclusion survived, because the tuning leaves no trace in the output and nothing in the record time-stamps the specification unless the analyst volunteers it. No statistical correction can repair an undisclosed choice of bias model and range, so the guarantee has to come from governance and auditable tooling rather than from inference, and transparency currently depends entirely on voluntary disclosure.

title: Prespecification and outcome-driven choice of sensitivity ranges
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Leahy et al. 2023, International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
HTA workshop recommendations requiring that input parameters be identified through a systematic and transparent approach and specified a priori in a protocol or analysis plan, that evidence be collected transparently, that all code and data be shared with HTA bodies, and that decision makers be engaged early. Already covers the prespecification principle; supplies no registration mechanism or correction for selection over ranges.

title: Prespecification and outcome-driven choice of sensitivity ranges
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Operationalize the guidance that already exists rather than restate it: time-stamp the sensitivity specification, including scales, ranges, distributions and dependence assumptions, in the protocol or analysis plan lodged with the decision maker before results are known, and engage the appraisal body early as the workshop recommends. Build auditable tooling that records the specification and any later change so a post hoc range change is visible in the record alongside reproducible code, seeds and elicitation materials. Label a post hoc tipping search as exploratory and disclose the full search rather than presenting it as confirmatory, using existing selective-inference or multiverse reporting where a disclosed search has to be summarized.

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text: QBA-25 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text:
Statement
For an HTA governed by cost-effectiveness the decision-relevant QBA output is the economic model evaluated over the plausible bias region, reported as incremental net benefit surfaces, decision-reversal proportions and expected regret against clinical and cost-effectiveness thresholds, and because HTA needs lifetime survival the bias region must be carried through the extrapolation model as well. A p = 0.05 tipping boundary is a valid answer to an inferential question and merely insufficient for the decision, though the entry’s exemplar analysis does read its result off exactly that boundary. The claim that nothing links the ITC sensitivity region to the economic model is wrong: Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13) explicitly recommend incorporating sensitivity results into economic scenario analyses and judging robustness by whether all scenarios yield ICERs below the threshold; what does not exist is a link to the model’s probabilistic sensitivity analysis through a shared parameter space, or any framework indexing the survival extrapolation model jointly with the bias parameters.

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text:
Why it is open
The map from a bias parameter to a decision runs through survival extrapolation, costs and QALYs and is strongly nonlinear, so a modest change in a hazard ratio can move the decision quantity far more than it moves the effect estimate, and propagating a single corrected point estimate cannot reproduce that. Economic models are usually built by a different team in different software from the ITC, so evaluating the model at every point of the bias surface is organizationally and computationally expensive, and nothing shares draws or parameters between the ITC sensitivity region and the model’s probabilistic sensitivity analysis even though nesting or conditioning over bias scenarios is statistically possible. Bias parameters are naturally specified for the observed follow-up while the decision depends mostly on a period in which no data exist, and no framework indexes the extrapolation model choice by the bias parameters, so the two are explored separately and their interaction is never displayed. With several bias parameters the tipping point is a surface with no accepted summary, and judging whether the tipping region is attainable still requires the elicitation the method was often adopted to avoid.

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Recommends that sensitivity analysis results be incorporated into scenario analyses within economic models, explicitly assessing their impact on the ICER, with robustness judged by whether all scenarios fall below the threshold. Counter-evidence to the claim that no link to the economic model exists; it does not link to the model’s probabilistic sensitivity analysis or share a parameter space. Its case study also reads a significance-crossing point off a deterministic sensitivity curve.

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Move from the scenario analysis published guidance already recommends to a shared parameter space: nest or condition the economic model’s probabilistic sensitivity analysis over bias scenarios using shared draws, and report incremental net benefit surfaces, decision-reversal proportions and expected regret against noninferiority margins and cost-effectiveness thresholds alongside the feasibility and support map. Index the extrapolation model jointly with the bias parameters so the sensitivity surface reports lifetime survival and net benefit rather than in-trial effects only. Build interfaces so a PAIC QBA object can be consumed directly by the health-economic model, and pass a single effect parameter only where it demonstrably carries the whole modeled bias.

title: Decision QBA: net benefit, tipping surfaces and extrapolation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The decision-relevant QBA quantity is incremental net benefit as a function of the bias parameters, together with the probability of recommendation reversal and expected regret, not whether a 95% interval for a log hazard ratio excludes zero. Tipping points should be surfaces computed against clinical and cost-effectiveness thresholds rather than a p = 0.05 boundary, and because HTA needs lifetime survival the bias region has to be carried through the extrapolation model as well.”
What was wrong with it. The literature auditor found the claim that nothing links the ITC sensitivity region to the economic model contradicted by Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), which recommends precisely that link as scenario analysis against the ICER threshold, leaving only the probabilistic-sensitivity-analysis link and the shared parameter space missing. GPT-5.6 Sol softened two absolutes: a p = 0.05 tipping boundary is legitimate when the prespecified conclusion is statistical significance, and passing one effect parameter into the economic model is adequate when that parameter is a sufficient conduit for the modeled biases and its full scenario or uncertainty distribution is propagated, rather than a misuse in every case.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Claim 2 is corroborated by the very method the agenda holds up as the state of the art: Ren et al. 2025’s case study reads its sensitivity result off a significance boundary, ‘If the proportion is greater than 28%, then the treatment effect becomes statistically significant’, which is exactly the p=0.05 anchoring claim 2 calls a misuse. The caveat is claim 9. Ren et al. 2025 do explicitly link the sensitivity region to the economic model, recommending that ‘These sensitivity analysis results can be incorporated into scenario analyses within economic models, explicitly assessing their impact on the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER)’, with decision rules based on whether all scenarios fall below or above the threshold. So a link to the economic model exists in published guidance; what does not exist is a link to the model’s probabilistic sensitivity analysis or a shared parameter space, and no published work indexes the survival extrapolation model jointly with the bias parameters (claims 7, 8). Claims 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 are normative and correct in substance. Tipping-point machinery for evidence synthesis exists but only for arm-based network meta-analysis correlation parameters, not for unanchored PAIC bias surfaces.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is correct only after defining the reference point, feasible set, direction, or metric: with several parameters the tipping set is a boundary or hypersurface, but ‘smallest departure’ is otherwise undefined. C2 is too categorical. A p=0.05 tipping boundary is valid when the prespecified conclusion is statistical significance; it is merely insufficient for an HTA decision. C3 is appropriate for a conventional cost-effectiveness decision rule, but incremental net benefit is not the only possible HTA decision quantity and cannot replace clinical, budget, equity, or other constraints. C4, C5, C7, and C8 are valid possibility statements. C6 is false as a universal rule: if bias acts only through one treatment-effect parameter and the full scenario or uncertainty distribution for that parameter is passed to the economic model, it can be sufficient; a single corrected point estimate is inadequate only for a question about the whole bias region. C9 is an absolute practice claim outside a technical audit and is not a statistical impossibility: probabilistic sensitivity analysis can be nested or conditioned over bias scenarios using shared draws. The remaining open work is integration, extrapolation specification, and software workflow, not a new identification result, so the asserted very-high severity is inflated.

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text: QBA-23 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text:
Statement
A decision-grade unanchored PAIC QBA should inventory and propagate the material data and model uncertainties, state which sensitivity assumptions are held fixed and which are probabilistic, and separately quantify numerical integration and Monte Carlo error rather than folding them into inferential uncertainty as if they were random scientific parameters. The source’s count of eleven layers is not defensible: read literally the list names thirteen entities and about ten categories when paired items are grouped, and it conflates sampling uncertainty, model uncertainty, nonidentified sensitivity assumptions, deterministic numerical error, Monte Carlo estimation error and downstream decision-model uncertainty. Nested resampling and a fully joint Bayesian model are two important options but not the only credible ones, since sandwich or estimating-equation variance, the delta method, multiple imputation, modular Monte Carlo schemes, parametric bootstrap and hybrids also apply, and only the resampling route has a failed-replicate problem at all.

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text:
Why it is open
Several uncertainty sources are produced by different teams in different software and delivered only as summary numbers, so there is no object in which they can be combined and completeness is determined by what the software happens to support. Pseudo-IPD reconstruction error, and integration and Monte Carlo error for the fits that do not report them, are conventionally treated as negligible without ever being quantified. Nested bootstrap cost is multiplicative in replicates, grid points and model fits wherever every outer replicate must re-solve the calibration or refit outcome models at each bias-grid point, though it depends on which quantities must be refitted and which computations can be reused or approximated. Where failed replicates are dropped the reported interval is conditional on the weighting having succeeded, which understates exactly the positivity problem the sensitivity analysis was meant to expose, and there is no accepted way to represent failures inside an interval.

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9, cmaic() and plot_integration_error()
The stratified bootstrap in cmaic() re-estimates weights and refits the outcome model, propagating weighting and outcome-model uncertainty jointly, and fails closed below a minimum successful-replicate fraction rather than silently keeping an arbitrary subset. plot_integration_error() reports quasi-Monte-Carlo integration convergence for non-survival cML-NMR fits but not for survival fits. It propagates only part of the list.

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Specify one propagation scheme appropriate to the estimator, whether nested resampling, a joint Bayesian model, sandwich or delta-method variance, multiple imputation or a hybrid, and require the analysis to state which layers were propagated and which were held fixed. Report numerical integration and Monte Carlo error as computational diagnostics next to the statistical uncertainty rather than inside it, extending the integration-convergence diagnostic that already exists for non-survival fits to survival fits. Report the failure map alongside the effect surface and develop resampling schemes that bound the contribution of failed replicates or return an identified set instead of an interval when a nonnegligible fraction fail, reducing cost with warm starts, surrogate models over the bias grid or analytic approximations validated against the full nested computation.

title: Propagating every uncertainty layer without prohibitive cost
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “A complete unanchored PAIC QBA may need to propagate eleven distinct uncertainty layers, from IPD outcome-model and aggregate-outcome uncertainty through estimated weights, target moments, sensitivity parameters, measurement-error validation data, censoring models, pseudo-IPD reconstruction, numerical integration and Monte Carlo error, component and bridge drift, to economic-model uncertainty. The two credible implementations, nested resampling and a fully joint Bayesian model, are respectively prohibitively expensive and prone to conditioning on the replicates that happened to succeed.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol found the eleven-layer count incoherent and the two-implementation dichotomy false, and noted that a fully joint Bayesian fit has no bootstrap replicates, so the entry’s paired criticism was category-confused. It also read cpaic at commit 9d150e9 and found that cmaic() already re-estimates weights and refits the outcome model in one stratified bootstrap, propagating both sources together, that plot_integration_error() reports quasi-Monte-Carlo integration convergence for non-survival fits, and that failed resamples are not silently accepted, because the package rejects an edge below an 80% success threshold, although above that threshold the standard deviation is still conditional on success.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1’s exact count is not coherent: read literally, the list names 13 entities; with the paired items grouped, it names about 10 categories. More importantly, it conflates sampling uncertainty, model uncertainty, nonidentified sensitivity assumptions, deterministic numerical error, Monte Carlo estimation error, and downstream decision-model uncertainty. For C2, numerical integration error and Monte Carlo standard error should be checked, reduced, and reported, but ordinarily should not be folded into inferential uncertainty as if they were random scientific parameters. C3 applies only when the economic model is part of the target decision analysis. C4 is an unverified universal absence claim; cpaic already propagates weight-estimation and outcome-model uncertainty together in cmaic(), but not the full list. C5 is possible, not inherent: cost depends on which quantities must be refitted and which grid calculations can be reused or approximated. C6 is correct if failed replicates are silently omitted. cpaic does omit failed resamples when computing the successful-replicate SD, but rejects the entire edge below an 80% success threshold, so it does not silently accept an arbitrarily selected subset; above the threshold, the SD is still conditional on success. C7 is false: estimating-equation or sandwich methods, the delta method, multiple-imputation or modular Monte Carlo schemes, parametric bootstrap, and hybrids are credible alternatives. A fully joint Bayesian fit also has no bootstrap replicates, so the statement’s ‘respectively prone to conditioning on successful replicates’ is category-confused.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. No prior_work, and the load-bearing claims are enumerations internal to the source report (claim 1’s eleven layers) or no-implementation-exists assertions (claim 4). Claims 5 and 6 are the substantive and checkable part, and both are consistent with what I retrieved: Ren et al. 2025 use a non-parametric bootstrap with 10,000 replications for a single deterministic grid, which makes the multiplicative cost of nesting that inside a probabilistic bias-parameter layer immediately apparent, and they note MAIC extensions ‘may even fail to produce feasible weights’, which is exactly the failed-replicate selection problem in claim 6. But neither the eleven-layer enumeration nor claim 4 can be adjudicated against literature, and I found no PAIC paper that quantifies pseudo-IPD reconstruction, numerical integration or Monte Carlo error as propagated layers. Claim 7 (nested resampling and fully joint Bayesian modelling are the two broad credible implementations) is a taxonomy statement rather than a finding. I vote unverifiable on support.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1’s exact count is not coherent: read literally, the list names 13 entities; with the paired items grouped, it names about 10 categories. More importantly, it conflates sampling uncertainty, model uncertainty, nonidentified sensitivity assumptions, deterministic numerical error, Monte Carlo estimation error, and downstream decision-model uncertainty. For C2, numerical integration error and Monte Carlo standard error should be checked, reduced, and reported, but ordinarily should not be folded into inferential uncertainty as if they were random scientific parameters. C3 applies only when the economic model is part of the target decision analysis. C4 is an unverified universal absence claim; cpaic already propagates weight-estimation and outcome-model uncertainty together in cmaic(), but not the full list. C5 is possible, not inherent: cost depends on which quantities must be refitted and which grid calculations can be reused or approximated. C6 is correct if failed replicates are silently omitted. cpaic does omit failed resamples when computing the successful-replicate SD, but rejects the entire edge below an 80% success threshold, so it does not silently accept an arbitrarily selected subset; above the threshold, the SD is still conditional on success. C7 is false: estimating-equation or sandwich methods, the delta method, multiple-imputation or modular Monte Carlo schemes, parametric bootstrap, and hybrids are credible alternatives. A fully joint Bayesian fit also has no bootstrap replicates, so the statement’s ‘respectively prone to conditioning on successful replicates’ is category-confused.
