title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text: HET-02 Overstated High priority Promising

title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text:
Statement
MAIC-style weighting is defined for one pairwise comparison against one aggregate study, so a two-stage weighting workflow that outputs separately adjusted contrasts with only marginal standard errors loses the covariance induced by a shared common arm and the covariance induced by shared weight estimation. Regression-based population adjustment already solves this at the network level: multilevel network meta-regression is a one-stage arm-level likelihood valid for networks of any size (Phillippo et al. 2020, doi:10.1111/rssa.12579), implemented in multinma since 2020, where multi-arm studies carry correlated multivariate-normal random effects (Perren et al. 2025, doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887). What is open is the weighting branch: there is no arm-level MAIC-style estimator, and no sandwich or multivariate bootstrap variance estimator for weighted multi-arm contrasts that also carries weight-estimation uncertainty has been derived or benchmarked. The same split holds in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN: at commit 9d150e9 cmlnmr() gives within-study deviations from a study baseline the standard 0.5 NMA correlation, while cmaic() and cstc() refuse IPD studies with more than two arms rather than processing them pairwise.

title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text:
Why it is open
Multi-arm trials produce correlated contrasts because they share a common arm, and a network likelihood needs that correlation; a two-stage pipeline that adjusts one contrast at a time and passes on only marginal standard errors has nowhere to store it. Weight estimation adds a second source of correlation between contrasts that naive variance formulas ignore. Neither is a theoretical obstacle, because one weight set can feed a joint arm-level outcome model and a multivariate bootstrap that re-estimates the weights recovers the full contrast covariance; the obstacle is that nobody has derived, implemented or benchmarked this for the weighting branch. The consequence surfaces as distorted precision and as spurious or masked inconsistency rather than as an obvious failure, which is why nobody is forced to confront it.

title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al., 2020, Multilevel network meta-regression for population-adjusted treatment comparisons, JRSS-A
Defines an individual-level regression model and fits aggregate data by integrating over the covariate distribution to form the likelihood; this is the arm-based one-stage population-adjusted estimator the source says does not exist, and it is valid for networks of any size including multi-arm trials.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (version 0.9.1)
Working implementation: nma() fits ML-NMR with arm-based likelihoods, and multi-arm studies receive correlated multivariate-normal random effects.


Perren, Pedder, Welton and Phillippo, 2025, Network Meta-Analysis with Class Effects: A Practical Guide and Model Selection Algorithm
States the multi-arm covariance parameterization used in multinma, confirming that studies with more than one non-baseline arm have multiple correlated random effects modeled as multivariate normal.


Phillippo et al., 2019, Population adjustment methods for indirect comparisons: a review of NICE technology appraisals
Cited by the audit as counter-evidence that the problem is real in practice: larger treatment networks were commonplace in NICE appraisals (10 of 18) while the population adjustment methods in use could not account for them.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
cmlnmr() jointly fits IPD and aggregate arms by integrating the individual-level model over each aggregate study’s covariate distribution, and cmlnmr_random.R gives multi-arm deviations from a study baseline the standard 0.5 NMA correlation; cmaic() and cstc() support two-arm IPD studies only.

title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not rebuild the one-stage arm-level likelihood, which ML-NMR in multinma already provides; extend the weighting branch to match it. Derive a MAIC-style estimator that applies one weight set to a joint arm-level model, with a sandwich or multivariate bootstrap variance that accounts for weight estimation as well as the outcome model, and give two-stage implementations a joint covariance matrix to export instead of marginal standard errors. Benchmark it in simulations that inject three-arm and four-arm studies with correlated contrasts and unequal variances, reporting variance recovery, inconsistency inflation and undercoverage, with ML-NMR as the reference rather than as the thing being replaced. In cpaic the concrete step is multi-arm support for cmaic() and cstc(), which currently reject such studies outright.

title: Multi-arm covariance is lost when contrasts are adjusted pairwise
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. MAIC-style weighting is defined for a single pairwise comparison against one aggregate study, so weighting-based PAIC applied contrast by contrast loses the covariance induced by a shared common arm. Regression-based population adjustment already solves this: multilevel network meta-regression (Phillippo et al. 2020, implemented in multinma) is a one-stage arm-level likelihood that keeps multi-arm structure intact. The open part is a weighting-based arm-level estimator and a variance estimator for it that accounts for weight estimation.
The source said. “MAIC-style weighting is defined for one pairwise comparison against one aggregate study, so a multi-arm trial is processed contrast by contrast and the covariance induced by the shared common arm is never carried into the network likelihood. Standard NMA software handles that structure correctly, but it sits downstream of the weighting step and is not wired into it.”
What was wrong with it. The source claimed no arm-based or multivariate PAIC estimator preserving multi-arm covariance is available, and cited nothing; the literature auditor found that multilevel network meta-regression is exactly that estimator and has been on CRAN in multinma since 2020 (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579), and the code auditor found cpaic’s cmlnmr() already implements the shared-baseline multi-arm correlation. The code auditor also rejected the framing that it is not established whether weighting before contrast formation preserves the correct covariance: weighting is not inherently pairwise, and the weighted covariance is estimable by joint estimating equations or a bootstrap that re-estimates the weights, so this is undone work rather than an unverifiable assumption.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim ‘No arm-based or multivariate PAIC estimator that preserves multi-arm covariance is currently available’ is contradicted by work the entry does not cite. Phillippo et al. (2020) multilevel network meta-regression is exactly a one-stage individual-level (arm-based) likelihood for population adjustment: ‘An individual level regression model is defined, and aggregate data are fitted by integrating over the covariate distribution to form the likelihood’, and it applies to ‘networks of any size’. It is implemented in multinma 0.9.1. Perren, Pedder, Welton & Phillippo (2025) describe the same package’s multi-arm handling verbatim: ‘Studies with more than 1 nontreatment arm therefore have multiple RE, which are correlated and modeled using a multivariate normal distribution.’ So the arm-based, multi-arm-preserving population-adjusted estimator exists and has been in CRAN software since 2020. What remains open is narrower and real: MAIC-style weighting itself has no arm-based extension, and no sandwich or multivariate bootstrap variance estimator for weighted multi-arm contrasts that also carries weight-estimation uncertainty has been derived or benchmarked. The ‘Standard NMA software handles multi-arm correlated contrasts maturely’ claim is correct. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Provides the arm-based one-stage likelihood for population adjustment that the entry says does not exist, valid for networks of any size including multi-arm trials.. Cites cran:multinma 0.9.1: Working implementation: nma() fits ML-NMR with arm-based likelihoods; multi-arm studies get correlated multivariate-normal random effects.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887: States the multi-arm covariance parameterization used in multinma, confirming multi-arm correlation is carried in the likelihood..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2, C5, C7, and C8 are technically sound with appropriate implementation. Weighting is not inherently pairwise: one set of patient weights can feed a joint arm-level outcome model, and joint estimating equations or a multivariate bootstrap that re-estimates the weights can recover the full contrast covariance. Thus C4 is framed incorrectly; the weighted covariance need not equal the unweighted covariance, but it is estimable rather than an intrinsically unverified assumption. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, cmaic() and cstc() reject IPD studies with more than two arms rather than processing them pairwise. More importantly, cmlnmr() is already a population-adjusted, joint arm-level estimator and implements the standard shared-baseline multi-arm random-effects correlation. This directly refutes C6 and the statement that covariance is never carried. The remaining open part is multi-arm support for the two-stage cMAIC and cSTC paths, including export of their joint covariance. C3’s claim about what workflows often do is unsourced. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements a one-stage model that jointly fits IPD and aggregate arms while integrating over aggregate-study covariate distributions.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Preserves the standard covariance among random-effects contrasts sharing a baseline arm in cMLNMR..

Decision path

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text: EVB-05 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Statement
Generic baseline-covariate reporting is already mandated: CONSORT 2025 item 25 requires a table of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group, and CONSORT presents itself as a minimum set of items for a trial report (doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1004587). What no standard specifies is what population adjustment needs: which covariates, dispersion measures, any joint or correlation structure, and reporting on the analysis set that matches the reported effect estimate. In practice the adjustment set is therefore bounded by what the comparator publication happened to print; a review of 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment lists availability among the bases on which covariates were selected (Phillippo et al. 2019, doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333).

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Why it is open
The analyst does not control the comparator publication, so the moments needed for balancing are supplied or withheld by a third party with no stake in the later comparison. A CONSORT-style baseline table does not close the gap, because what is required varies with the estimand and the model, and marginal means and proportions can be insufficient when joint distributions, nonlinear terms or interactions matter. No journal, regulator or registry mandates that PAIC-specific increment, and how often it is missing has not been quantified, though reviews of PAIC practice report inconsistent and incomplete covariate reporting (Truong et al. 2023, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1653). The nearest thing to a PAIC reporting standard governs the analyst’s own reporting of the comparison rather than what the comparator publication must carry (Ishak et al. 2025, doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1).

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2019, International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
Review of 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment; reports that covariates were included on the basis of availability, expert opinion, effective sample size, statistical significance or cross-validation, sourcing the availability-bounded adjustment set.


CONSORT 2025 statement, PLOS Medicine
Trial reporting standard whose item 25 mandates a baseline demographic and clinical characteristics table per group; establishes that a mandated minimum baseline reporting set does exist, without specifying what population adjustment needs.


Harari et al. 2023, Research Synthesis Methods
Network meta-interpolation: adjusts for effect modification using subgroup analyses reported in aggregate publications, with standard errors, instead of treating the reported covariate set as a fixed constraint.


Truong et al. 2023, Research Synthesis Methods
Methodological review of PAIC practice documenting inconsistent reporting and incomplete covariate information; cited by the recency auditor as support that partial reporting is a live obstacle, without giving a prevalence estimate for the specific summaries PAIC needs.


Ishak et al. 2025, PharmacoEconomics
Framework for reliable, transparent and reproducible PAICs; the closest existing thing to a PAIC reporting standard, but it governs the analyst’s reporting rather than the comparator publication’s covariate summaries.

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define and benchmark the PAIC-specific increment over CONSORT, namely which covariates, which dispersions, any joint or correlation structure, and reporting on the analysis set matching the reported effect estimate, and pursue it as an addition to trial reporting guidance rather than as an analyst-side workaround. Quantify how often that increment is missing, which no auditor found measured, so the case for a standard rests on evidence rather than assertion. In the meantime, methods that build effect-modifier adjustment out of the subgroup information aggregate publications do report already exist and should be extended (network meta-interpolation, Harari et al. 2023, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1608); treating unreported summaries as missing data propagates uncertainty only once identifying assumptions, external information or priors are added, so partial identification and sensitivity analysis are the honest fallback.

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “No minimum covariate-reporting standard for aggregate-data trials” The title says no minimum covariate-reporting standard exists, but CONSORT 2025 item 25 already mandates a baseline characteristics table for each group.
The source said. “The covariate summaries that population adjustment needs are frequently absent from the comparator publication, or reported for a different analysis set, and no benchmarked minimum reporting set exists that would require them. Which covariates can be balanced is therefore decided by what a journal printed rather than by what causal reasoning requires.”
What was wrong with it. The claim was unattributed in the source and stated flatly that no benchmarked minimum reporting set exists; the literature auditor read CONSORT 2025 and found item 25 mandates baseline data (doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1004587), so only the narrower PAIC-specific version survives, and it is now sourced to Phillippo et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333). GPT-5.6 Sol added that there is no universal finite set of summaries every PAIC requires, because the requirement depends on the estimand, the effect-modification basis, the link and outcome models and the weighting method.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): This entry is source_unsourced, so I judged it against the literature. I read the CONSORT 2025 full text. It does contain a mandated baseline-covariate reporting item, item 25 ‘Baseline data’, and the statement describes itself as ‘a minimum set of items to be included in a report of a randomised trial’, endorsed by ICMJE, WAME and CSE, with the same item present as CONSORT 2010 item 15. Claim 2 as written (‘No benchmarked minimum reporting set of baseline covariate summaries currently exists’) is therefore contradicted at face value. What CONSORT does not do is specify which covariates, require dispersion measures, require any joint or correlation structure, or require alignment with the analysis set used for the reported effect estimate; that narrower version survives and I found no PAIC-benchmarked standard. Claim 1 is supportable and I can source it: Phillippo et al. 2019 IJTAHC reviewed 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment and found availability was among the bases on which covariates were selected. Harari et al. 2023 network meta-interpolation exists precisely because full effect-modifier summaries are not uniformly reported. Claim 3 remains without a prevalence estimate.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. This entry is source_unsourced, so I judged it against the literature. I read the CONSORT 2025 full text. It does contain a mandated baseline-covariate reporting item, item 25 ‘Baseline data’, and the statement describes itself as ‘a minimum set of items to be included in a report of a randomised trial’, endorsed by ICMJE, WAME and CSE, with the same item present as CONSORT 2010 item 15. Claim 2 as written (‘No benchmarked minimum reporting set of baseline covariate summaries currently exists’) is therefore contradicted at face value. What CONSORT does not do is specify which covariates, require dispersion measures, require any joint or correlation structure, or require alignment with the analysis set used for the reported effect estimate; that narrower version survives and I found no PAIC-benchmarked standard. Claim 1 is supportable and I can source it: Phillippo et al. 2019 IJTAHC reviewed 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment and found availability was among the bases on which covariates were selected. Harari et al. 2023 network meta-interpolation exists precisely because full effect-modifier summaries are not uniformly reported. Claim 3 remains without a prevalence estimate. Cites doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333: Supplies a real reference for claim 1, converting an unsourced assertion into a sourced one: in 18 NICE appraisals using population adjustment, availability was one of the reported bases for covariate selection.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1608: Existing partial response to the proposed direction: builds effect-modifier adjustment out of whatever subgroup information aggregate publications do report, with standard errors, rather than treating the reported set as a fixed constraint.. Cites doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1: Nearest existing thing to a PAIC reporting standard, but it governs the analyst’s own reporting of the comparison, not the covariate summaries the comparator publication must carry; so it does not close the gap the entry describes..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / unverifiable. The technical core of C2 is correct: absent or incompatible target-population summaries can prevent balancing of prespecified effect modifiers or make PAIC strongly assumption-dependent. C1 contains no substantive proposition. C3 is an uncited absence claim and C4 is an uncited frequency claim, so neither can be verified under the specified technical-only, no-literature lens. Moreover, there is no universal finite collection of summaries that every PAIC requires; requirements depend on the estimand, effect-modification basis, link and outcome models, and weighting method. Marginal means and proportions may be insufficient when joint distributions, nonlinear terms, or interactions matter. Treating unreported summaries as missing data propagates uncertainty only after adding identifying assumptions, external information, or priors; otherwise sensitivity analysis or partial identification is required. The reporting limitation remains open, but its alleged prevalence and the nonexistence of standards are not established here.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted search looked for a benchmarked minimum covariate-reporting set that would make aggregate-data publications PAIC-ready. Methodological reviews of PAIC practice document inconsistent reporting and incomplete covariate information as live obstacles (Serret-Larmande et al. 2023, J Clin Epidemiol; Truong et al. 2023, Res Synth Methods, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1653), supporting C2 and C4. CONSORT and trial reporting norms require baseline characteristic tables, but they do not mandate the full set of moments PAIC needs (means and SDs for continuous covariates on the analysis set of interest, consistent analysis populations, and joint/correlation structure). PRISMA-NMA update work (Veroniki et al. 2025 scoping/update papers) targets NMA reporting gaps (nodes, consistency, certainty of evidence) and is not a minimum AD covariate package for population adjustment. NICE DSU TSD 18 and EU HTA 2024 quantitative synthesis guidance describe what analysts need for MAIC/STC/ML-NMR but do not create a journal/registry mandate for publishers of comparator AD trials. No 2024–2026 standard was found that benchmarks a minimum reporting set and closes the reporting failure as a solved policy problem. C3 therefore still holds: the constraint remains what journals print. Treat incompletely reported AD as missing data with propagated uncertainty remains a proposed analyst-side response, not a solved standard.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text: EVB-03 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Statement
Trials grouped under one outcome label may estimate non-equivalent quantities because they differ in follow-up, endpoint definition, analysis population or intercurrent-event handling; simulation of treatment switching in oncology shows that pooling estimates targeting different estimands yields a pooled estimator that targets no estimand of interest, even under a random-effects model (Metcalfe et al. 2025, doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10039). Estimand mapping is the response and it is no longer a proposal: it has been argued into the evidence-synthesis literature (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741), given a pragmatic framework with a worked NMA case study varying intercurrent-event strategies (arxiv:2510.15762), and codified as step 1 of a population-adjusted indirect comparison framework (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1). What remains open is per-trial estimand mapping from published reports, where the needed detail is often not reported, and structured encoding of intercurrent-event handling and analysis population.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Why it is open
Indirect comparison arithmetic assumes the contrasts refer to a common estimand, but conformity is usually checked at the level of the outcome label rather than the outcome definition. Differences in intercurrent-event strategy and analysis population change the causal question each trial answers, and no covariate adjustment repairs that mismatch. Published reports frequently do not carry the detail needed to do the mapping trial by trial, and uptake of estimand-aware synthesis remains modest, particularly without IPD. An outcome taxonomy exists for classifying outcomes, but nothing machine-readable encodes intercurrent-event strategy or analysis population.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Metcalfe et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Simulation of treatment switching in oncology showing that pooling treatment-policy and hypothetical estimands produces a pooled estimator targeting no estimand of interest, and that this can mislead even under random effects.


Remiro-Azocar and Gorst-Rasmussen 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Position paper arguing that the language of estimands belongs in network meta-analysis and HTA, especially under the narrow treatment and target-population perspective HTA takes.


Remiro-Azocar et al., Incorporating estimands into meta-analyses of clinical trials (preprint)
Pragmatic framework for estimands in meta-analysis and NMA for HTA, applied to an NMA of semaglutide versus dulaglutide contrasting treatment-policy and hypothetical strategies for discontinuation and rescue.


Ishak et al. 2025, PharmacoEconomics
Six-element framework for reliable, transparent and reproducible population-adjusted indirect comparisons in which definition of the comparison as an estimand is element 1.


Ades et al. 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Names integration of the estimand framework with evidence synthesis as an explicit agenda item of the core NMA methods group.


Analysis of opinions from studies citing the COMET outcomes taxonomy, 2025
Shows an outcome taxonomy for evidence synthesis already exists and is widely cited, narrowing the gap to estimand-level, machine-readable detail rather than outcome classification as such.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The direction is to make the existing estimand frameworks routine rather than to invent them: apply the published meta-analysis and PAIC estimand frameworks to each contributing trial and report the mapping alongside the synthesis, so mismatches are visible before pooling rather than after. Extend outcome taxonomies such as COMET beyond outcome classification to encode intercurrent-event strategy and analysis population in structured form. Latent harmonization and multivariate endpoint models are appropriate only where a defensible linking model connects the endpoints and the available data identify its parameters; they cannot generally reconcile different treatment-policy questions, intercurrent-event strategies, populations or time points.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Trials in the same comparison differ in follow-up duration, endpoint definitions, handling of intercurrent events, and analysis populations, so the quantities being combined are not the same estimand even before population adjustment.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented ICH E9(R1)-style estimand mapping and outcome ontologies as promising future directions; the literature auditor and Grok both found an active published programme already doing the mapping (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741, arxiv:2510.15762, doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) and a widely used outcome taxonomy already in routine use (COMET, pmid:40754038). GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the claim that endpoint definitions live in prose no tool can read: the obstacle is incomplete reporting and unreliable structured interpretation, not literal unreadability.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, yet an active published programme addresses exactly claim 2. Metcalfe et al. 2025 Res Synth Methods simulated pooling of treatment-policy and hypothetical estimands across oncology RCTs allowing treatment switching, and showed the pooled estimator targets nothing of interest; that converts the entry’s assertion from conjecture into a quantified result. Remiro-Azocar and Gorst-Rasmussen 2024 RSM argue the estimand language belongs in NMA and HTA; Ades et al. 2024 RSM call for integration of the estimand framework with evidence synthesis; Ishak et al. 2025 PharmacoEconomics already makes estimand definition element 1 of a six-element PAIC framework. Claim 1 is uncontroversial and is documented by the COMET outcome-heterogeneity literature. Claim 3 needs softening: the COMET outcome taxonomy exists and is in routine use for classifying trial outcomes, so an outcome classification standard is not absent, though I found nothing machine-readable that encodes intercurrent-event handling or analysis population. Claim 4 I could not verify with a retrieved source this session. Status is partially-solved: the diagnosis and the framework are published; per-trial estimand mapping from published reports is not. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10039: Quantifies the bias from combining trials whose estimands differ, which the entry states only qualitatively. Also confirms the gap is real.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741: Claim 2 is already a published position paper in the NMA/HTA literature, not a novel proposed direction.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745: Establishes that estimand-framework integration is an explicitly stated agenda item of the core NMA methods group.. Cites doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1: Shows estimand-first definition is already codified as step 1 of a PAIC analysis framework, so the ITC-specific version of claim 2 is partly operationalized.. Cites pmid:40754038: Narrows claim 3: an outcome taxonomy for evidence synthesis already exists and is widely cited, so what is missing is estimand-level, machine-readable detail rather than outcome classification as such..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central estimand warning is correct and can be decision-critical. Differences in follow-up, outcome variable, analysis population, summary measure, or intercurrent-event strategy produce different estimands when they change the causal quantity being estimated; a common outcome label is insufficient. C2 is technically sound because structured estimand mapping exposes these differences before synthesis. C3 describes useful infrastructure, not a mathematical necessity for valid ITC. C4 holds only when a defensible measurement or linking model connects the endpoints and the available data identify its parameters. Latent or multivariate models cannot generally reconcile different treatment-policy questions, intercurrent-event strategies, populations, or time points. The assertion that no tool can read endpoint definitions in prose is false; the problem is incomplete reporting and unreliable structured interpretation, not literal unreadability.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. That trials sharing an outcome label often target different estimands (follow-up, endpoint definition, intercurrent events, analysis population) remains correct and is now a central theme in synthesis methodology rather than a neglected gap. Remiro-Azócar and Gorst-Rasmussen (2024) argue for estimand thinking as a parallel to narrow research questions in evidence synthesis. Remiro-Azócar et al. (arXiv:2510.15762, versions through 2026) propose a pragmatic framework for estimands in meta-analyses for HTA, apply it to an NMA of semaglutide versus dulaglutide, and contrast treatment-policy versus hypothetical strategies for discontinuation/rescue. EU HTA quantitative evidence-synthesis guidance (2024) also stresses that a common estimand should apply across studies in a synthesis. These works partially resolve C2: ICH E9(R1)-style mapping is no longer only a vague proposal; it is formalized for synthesis and illustrated. They do not close the problem: authors still note modest uptake, difficulty without IPD, and residual cross-trial misalignment. C3 (machine-readable outcome ontology standards for ITC evidence bases) and C4 (latent outcome harmonization models as deployed standards) were not found as solved; semantic-variability/LLM and specialized outcome ontologies exist outside routine ITC pipelines. Mismatched estimands therefore remain open as an operational constraint; the mapping response is partially developed. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741: Places estimands at the center of evidence-synthesis question formulation; partially resolves the claim that estimand mapping is only aspirational (C2).. Cites arxiv:2510.15762: Provides a pragmatic estimand framework for meta-analysis/NMA in HTA and a worked NMA case study varying intercurrent-event strategies; partially operationalizes ICH E9(R1)-style mapping for synthesis (C2)..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text: EVB-01 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Statement
Individual patient data enter a network non-randomly: reviews of individual participant data meta-analyses find that requested data are frequently not obtained (Nevitt et al. 2017, pmid:28381561; Ahmed et al. 2012, pmid:22214758) and that funding support is associated with retrieval (Wu et al. 2021, doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011). Selective availability threatens transportability whenever inference links the IPD subset to the rest of the network, so a combined IPD and aggregate-data analysis needs explicit assumptions about that link plus sensitivity analysis for departures the observed data cannot identify. It is not a universal identification requirement: inference conditional on a fixed set of studies does not require a stochastic model of IPD availability.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Why it is open
Availability is determined by commercial and legal control, so it is informative about the trials themselves and cannot be assumed ignorable once the analysis generalizes beyond the IPD subset. Because withheld data are unavailable by definition, non-ignorable availability is not identified from observed data without restrictions or sensitivity parameters, and Ahmed et al. 2012 found that most IPD meta-analyses failing to obtain all requested data did not examine what that implied. Senior evidence-synthesis methodologists have asked in print why IPD are not routinely released to reimbursement authorities and guideline developers (Ades et al. 2024, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745), which locates the constraint in the access process. Separately, high-dimensional treatment-by-covariate interactions and within-study missing data remain hard even among the trials that do share, though these are estimation difficulties rather than proof that no IPD-NMA works.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Nevitt et al. 2017, BMJ
Systematic review of 760 IPD meta-analyses showing that only 25% retrieved 100% of eligible IPD and 43% retrieved 80% or more; documents that IPD availability is not a random subset.


Wu et al. 2021, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Cross-sectional study of 210 IPD meta-analyses tying data retrieval to trial number, funding support and intervention type; supplies the funding-related mechanism the entry asserted without a citation.


Ahmed et al. 2012, BMJ
Database survey naming data availability bias as a distinct threat in IPD meta-analysis and showing that most analysts who failed to obtain requested data did not examine or even mention the consequences.


Ades et al. 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Response to discussants of ‘NMA, the first 20 years’ asking in print why IPD are not routinely made available to reimbursement authorities and guideline developers; sources the framing of availability as an access process.


MOLGENIS Armadillo: a lightweight server for federated analysis using DataSHIELD, Bioinformatics 2024
Production federated-analysis infrastructure already used for one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts; shows federated analysis is deployed rather than speculative, while leaving sponsor-controlled participation untouched.


Phillippo et al. 2023, Medical Decision Making
Validates population-adjustment assumptions in multilevel network meta-regression by checking model predictions against observed aggregate study outcomes; partly realizes the external-validation idea without needing the withheld IPD.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Selection or pattern-mixture models of IPD availability, framed as sensitivity parameters rather than automatic correction, remain to be developed; the literature auditor searched for them and found none. Federated analysis should be treated as infrastructure to extend rather than to build, since DataSHIELD-based servers already run one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts (MOLGENIS Armadillo, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae726); what federation cannot do is compel a sponsor to join, so it broadens participation without removing selection. External validation is partly realized by comparing population-adjustment predictions against observed aggregate outcomes (Phillippo et al. 2023, doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162); completely withheld IPD cannot themselves serve as a validation set. Interaction terms need regularized or hierarchical structure rather than unrestricted high-dimensional models.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “IPD availability is sponsor-controlled and not ignorable” The title calls IPD availability not ignorable as a universal property, which the audit rejected since inference conditional on a fixed study set needs no availability model.
The source said. “Individual patient data are supplied for the sponsor’s own trials rather than for a random subset of the network, so the set of studies that can be population-adjusted or entered into an IPD network meta-analysis is systematically related to who paid for them. IPD-NMA identification requires an availability mechanism, and that mechanism is a data-access process rather than a statistical nuisance.”
What was wrong with it. The source made the availability mechanism a universal identification requirement for IPD-NMA and asserted that no configuration works straightforwardly once IPD are obtained; GPT-5.6 Sol judged both false, because inference conditional on a fixed study set needs no stochastic availability model. The empirical core carried no citation and is now sourced to Nevitt et al. 2017 (pmid:28381561), Wu et al. 2021 (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011) and Ahmed et al. 2012 (pmid:22214758), the last of which names data availability bias directly.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, so there was no citation to check; I built the case independently. The empirical core is well established and the entry simply fails to cite it: Nevitt 2017 BMJ (760 IPD-MAs), Wu 2021 JCE (210 IPD-MAs) and Ahmed 2012 BMJ all quantify non-random IPD retrieval, and Wu identifies funding support as a predictor of retrieval. Ades 2024 RSM explicitly asks why IPD is not routinely released to reimbursement authorities. So claim 2 is supported and should be sourced. Claims 1 and 4 are defensible but I found no paper formalizing an IPD-availability mechanism as an identification requirement. Claim 5 (‘can be modeled explicitly’) is aspiration: I searched for selection/pattern-mixture models of IPD availability and found none. Claim 6 understates maturity: federated IPD analysis is deployed infrastructure (DataSHIELD/MOLGENIS Armadillo, EU Child Cohort Network), though not for trial NMA in HTA, and it does not solve sponsor withholding since joining the federation is still the sponsor’s choice. Claim 7 is partly realized by Phillippo 2023 MDM, which validates population-adjustment predictions against observed aggregate outcomes. Cites pmid:28381561: Supplies the missing empirical citation for claim 2 (IPD availability is not a random subset). Does not solve the problem; it documents it.. Cites doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011: Directly ties IPD retrieval to funding/sponsorship, which is the specific mechanism the entry asserts without citation.. Cites pmid:22214758: Names ‘data availability bias’ as a distinct threat in IPD meta-analysis and shows analysts mostly do not address it. Supports the ‘cannot be checked from inside the analysis’ framing.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745: Senior evidence-synthesis methodologists state the access problem in print, which sources the entry’s ‘data-access process rather than a statistical nuisance’ framing.. Cites doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae726: Partially deflates claim 6: federated IPD analysis is production infrastructure already used for one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts, not a speculative response. It does not address sponsor-controlled participation.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162: Partially realizes claim 7: population-adjustment assumptions are checked by comparing model predictions against the aggregate studies rather than against withheld IPD..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Selective IPD access is a genuine transportability and sensitivity-analysis problem, but the statement overgeneralizes. C1 is false as a universal identification claim: inference conditional on a fixed set of studies does not require a stochastic IPD-availability model. Such a model becomes relevant when generalizing from the IPD subset or correcting selection, and nonignorable availability is not identified from observed data without restrictions or sensitivity parameters. C3 and C4 are technically sound. C2 is an unsupported frequency claim. C5 is feasible as a selection or sensitivity model, not an automatically identified correction. C6 can reduce data-sharing barriers but cannot correct refusal to participate. C7 requires the withheld study to disclose suitable aggregate outcomes or participate in independent or federated validation; completely withheld IPD cannot themselves be a validation set. The assertion that there is no configuration in which IPD-NMA works straightforwardly is false.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted search treated availability bias and IPD-NMA identification as already solved. What exists documents the problem and gives partial workarounds, not a closed identification theory for sponsor-controlled IPD. Riley et al. (BMJ Evid Based Med 2022/2023) and the 2021 IPDMA handbook (Ch. 9.3) state that requested IPD are often unavailable and that availability bias must be examined, typically by comparing or combining IPD-based results with aggregate-data results from non-IPD trials. That is sensitivity to selective availability, not an explicit model of a commercial/legal availability mechanism inside IPD-NMA identification. Federated platforms (DataSHIELD and related 2022–2025 work) reduce the need to release IPD and are a real response to access barriers, but they do not identify effects when the set of contributing studies is non-ignorable by design, and they are not HTA-ITC-specific solutions for sponsor-owned IPD. Pattern-mixture work in meta-analysis targets missing outcomes within studies, not study-level IPD release. High-dimensional treatment-by-covariate interactions and within-study missing data remain widely acknowledged practical limits. Queries run: IPD-NMA availability mechanism/pattern mixture; availability bias Riley/Tierney/Ahmed; federated IPD meta-analysis/DataSHIELD; arXiv/medRxiv IPD-NMA selective availability; R packages multinma/maicplus/netmeta/crossnma for related PRs. Nothing retrieved closes the problem as stated.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text: EST-10 Unverifiable Very high priority Established

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text:
Statement
The Bucher adjusted indirect comparison and aggregate-data network meta-analysis produce relative effects whose formulas specify no target covariate distribution, and those effects are routinely read as common-population quantities. The assumption list is looser than the source states: what is required is transportability of same-scale direct effects to a common target, not literal balance of every effect modifier or identical trial designs, the direct evidence entering each contrast may itself synthesize several trials rather than one, and a random-effects network replaces homogeneity with an exchangeability model while also requiring connectedness. Neither method names the population its estimate refers to, and in wholly aggregate networks none can, since the population-adjusted successor that carries a network-wide target requires IPD from at least one study. The two auditors split on whether this leaves the problem open or partly solved.

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text:
Why it is open
None of the identification conditions for Bucher or aggregate-data NMA pins down a covariate distribution, so there is no formal object against which population mismatch could be measured, and bias cannot even be defined until a target is chosen. Aggregate covariate summaries cannot separate individual-level effect modification from between-study gradients without strong assumptions, which is why assessment stays informal in practice. The successor that does carry a network-wide target needs IPD from at least one study, so it is unavailable exactly where the aggregate-only default is used. The maturity of the theory and software makes the common-population reading feel safe precisely where the underlying populations differ most.

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2018, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD18)
States that a standard indirect comparison or fixed-effect network meta-analysis assumes constancy of relative effects on the linear predictor scale, requiring effect modifiers to be balanced between the trial populations, and tabulates those assumptions. It is the source for the descriptive claims about what Bucher and aggregate-data NMA assume; it does not supply a target covariate distribution for aggregate-only networks.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
Its cML-NMR relative-effect path requires a named one-row effect-modifier profile, partially implementing explicit target labeling, and states that ML-NMR relative effects are population-specific whenever effect modifiers are present. It returns a conditional contrast at that profile rather than a marginal effect standardized over a population.

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Where IPD exist for at least one study, use ML-NMR as the successor that carries a network-wide target and label every network effect with the population it refers to. Where no IPD exist, the open work is different: state the population the network is being read as referring to and quantify how far the pooled parameter can sit from an effect in that population, since no aggregate-only estimator supplies one. Move effect-modification assessment from informal comparison of baseline tables to explicit modeling of within-study and between-study interaction components where the network supplies enough variation to identify them, and keep Bucher as a transparent estimator that remains decision-grade when its transport assumptions hold rather than demoting it by default.

title: Bucher ITC and aggregate-data NMA name no target population
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “The Bucher adjusted indirect comparison identifies a relative effect in an implicitly common population defined only by the two connected trials sharing a comparator, and aggregate-data NMA produces network relative effects that are routinely read as common-population effects. Neither method names the population its estimate refers to, and population mismatch and effect modification across the network are only weakly assessed.”
What was wrong with it. The literature auditor confirmed every descriptive claim against NICE DSU TSD18 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) and voted the problem open for aggregate-only networks; GPT-5.6 Sol judged the same entry overstated, correcting that Bucher needs common-comparator direct evidence rather than exactly two RCTs, that the requirement is transportability rather than literal effect-modifier balance, that connectedness and exchangeability belong in the NMA assumption list, and that Bucher can still be decision-grade when its transport assumptions hold, so calling it a benchmark only inflates the severity. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is accurate for the canonical Bucher calculation when relative effects are population-dependent: the formula itself does not specify a target covariate distribution. For C2 and C3, the actual requirement is transportability of the same-scale direct effects to a common target; literal balance of effect modifiers or identical designs is not necessary, and differences matter only when they modify effects or introduce bias. C4 is a reasonable practical judgment, not a mathematical result. C5 is false literally: Bucher needs direct evidence linked through a common comparator, but each direct estimate may synthesize multiple RCTs rather than exactly one trial. C6 describes sufficient fixed-effect NMA conditions incompletely: connectedness is also required, while random-effects NMA replaces homogeneity with an exchangeability/distributional model. C7 and the “usually” part of C8 are practice claims outside this audit; technically, aggregate summaries alone cannot separate within-study effect modification from between-study gradients without strong assumptions. C9 is broadly plausible but qualitative. The pooled NMA parameter is model- and weight-defined and need not equal an effect in any literal mixture population. cpaic partially addresses the target-labeling gap by requiring a named effect-modifier profile for cML-NMR output, but that output is conditional rather than marginally standardized. Bucher can still be decision-grade when its transport assumptions hold, so benchmark-only language inflates severity.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Every descriptive claim is confirmed by the full text of Phillippo et al. 2018 Med Decis Making: ‘A standard indirect comparison or (fixed effect) network meta-analysis assumes constancy of relative effects on the linear predictor scale … This requires that any and all effect modifiers are balanced between the 2 trial populations’, with Table 1 tabulating exactly those assumptions for the standard indirect comparison. Fragility to effect-modifier imbalance and design differences, the requirement of two connected RCTs sharing a comparator, and the maturity of aggregate-data NMA theory and software (netmeta, gemtc, multinma; the NICE DSU evidence-synthesis TSD series) are all uncontroversial. Weak assessment of population mismatch is corroborated by Phillippo et al. 2019 (NICE appraisal review) and Serret-Larmande et al. 2023 (3 of 133 PAIC articles reported all key methodological aspects adequately). I vote open rather than partially-solved because the entry’s scope is the aggregate-data-only setting: ML-NMR is the coherent successor that carries a network-wide target, but it requires IPD from at least one study, so for wholly aggregate networks no method names a target covariate distribution.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is accurate for the canonical Bucher calculation when relative effects are population-dependent: the formula itself does not specify a target covariate distribution. For C2 and C3, the actual requirement is transportability of the same-scale direct effects to a common target; literal balance of effect modifiers or identical designs is not necessary, and differences matter only when they modify effects or introduce bias. C4 is a reasonable practical judgment, not a mathematical result. C5 is false literally: Bucher needs direct evidence linked through a common comparator, but each direct estimate may synthesize multiple RCTs rather than exactly one trial. C6 describes sufficient fixed-effect NMA conditions incompletely: connectedness is also required, while random-effects NMA replaces homogeneity with an exchangeability/distributional model. C7 and the “usually” part of C8 are practice claims outside this audit; technically, aggregate summaries alone cannot separate within-study effect modification from between-study gradients without strong assumptions. C9 is broadly plausible but qualitative. The pooled NMA parameter is model- and weight-defined and need not equal an effect in any literal mixture population. cpaic partially addresses the target-labeling gap by requiring a named effect-modifier profile for cML-NMR output, but that output is conditional rather than marginally standardized. Bucher can still be decision-grade when its transport assumptions hold, so benchmark-only language inflates severity. It does not provide a marginal population-standardized estimand..

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text: EST-08 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text:
Statement
Odds ratios and hazard ratios are not automatically population-invariant, so they should not be treated as portable decision inputs without an explicit transport argument; that much holds. The source’s stronger claim, that risk differences, standardized risks, RMST differences and incremental net benefit are more portable across populations, does not: Dahabreh, Robertson and Steingrimsson (doi:10.1007/s10654-023-01067-4) show transportability for relative measures is largely incompatible with transportability for difference measures, and Xiao et al. (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2021.08.002) conclude that neither the odds ratio nor the risk ratio is universally portable. The defensible core is narrower and already formalized: direct collapsibility makes marginal effects easier to standardize to a declared target (Remiro-Azocar, doi:10.1002/sim.10111), and Colnet et al. (arxiv:2303.16008) give formal criteria for which causal measure generalizes, so the selection theory the source calls missing partly exists. Incremental net benefit is the least portable quantity on the list, since it depends on local costs, utilities and willingness-to-pay thresholds.

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text:
Why it is open
Choosing a scale trades off several things at once: how easily the estimand standardizes to a declared target, how stable it is across populations, how usable it is as a decision-model input, and how it behaves under random-effects synthesis, sparse events and censoring. Collapsibility settles only the first of these and no measure is stable everywhere, so an analyst who wants to switch still has no criterion that scores a measure jointly on transport and decision use for a given problem. The generalization theory that exists was developed for simple causal-inference settings rather than for indirect comparisons with aggregate targets, non-collapsible link functions and network structure. In component or additive-model settings the choice is further constrained, since marginal component effects are not generally additive, as documented at commit 9d150e9 of cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not installable from CRAN.

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Dahabreh, Robertson and Steingrimsson 2024, European Journal of Epidemiology
Shows that transportability for relative effect measures is largely incompatible with transportability for difference effect measures unless the treatment has no effect on average, which contradicts a blanket ranking of absolute measures as more portable.


Xiao, Chu, Cole, Chen, MacLehose, Richardson and Greenland 2021, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Concludes that neither the odds ratio nor the risk ratio is universally portable, so no ratio measure can be assumed stable across populations by default.


Remiro-Azocar 2024, Transportability of model-based estimands in evidence synthesis, Statistics in Medicine 43(22):4217-4249
Gives the formal argument that directly collapsible measures facilitate the transportability of marginal effects between studies, which is the defensible core of the source’s Direction D and is about ease of standardization rather than empirical constancy.


Colnet, Josse, Varoquaux and Scornet, Risk ratio, odds ratio, risk difference… Which causal measure is easier to generalize?
Existing formal theory for selecting an effect measure for generalization, showing that only the risk difference has its conditional and average treatment effects disentangled from the baseline regardless of outcome type, and that the covariate set needed depends on the measure chosen. It is developed outside the indirect-comparison setting.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (R package)
Its marginal_effects() defaults to a difference scale, contradicting the claim that software defaults push analysts toward odds ratios and hazard ratios.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
Documents that marginal component effects are not generally additive and add exactly only when the standardized treatment effects remain affine in the component design, which constrains scale choice in component analyses.

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build on Colnet et al. rather than starting from nothing: extend measure-selection criteria to the indirect-comparison setting, where the target is described by aggregate summaries and the network imposes its own constraints, and score candidates on standardization cost and decision usability rather than on a presumed portability ranking. Establish how the candidate scales behave under random-effects synthesis, sparse events and censoring, so that a switch is statistically supported rather than advocated. Keep odds ratios and hazard ratios as modeling parameters where convenient, standardize to the declared target before any decision use, and check component additivity on whichever scale the analysis runs on.

title: Effect scales chosen by convention rather than transportability
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Directly collapsible measures make marginal effects easier to standardize to a declared target covariate distribution, because for non-collapsible measures even purely prognostic variables shift the marginal effect; this is a reason to standardize explicitly before decision use, not evidence that risk differences or RMST differences are empirically more constant across populations than odds or hazard ratios.
The source said. “Direction D proposes selecting the effect measure for transportability and decision usability, prioritizing risk differences and standardized risks, mean differences, survival-probability differences at clinically relevant times, RMST differences, cumulative incidence differences, and incremental net benefit. Odds ratios and hazard ratios may remain useful model parameters but should not automatically be treated as population-invariant decision inputs.”
What was wrong with it. The source ranked collapsible and absolute measures as more portable and said no theory exists for selecting a scale; the literature auditor found the ranking contradicted by Dahabreh et al. (doi:10.1007/s10654-023-01067-4) and Xiao et al. (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2021.08.002), found existing selection theory in Colnet et al. (arxiv:2303.16008), and found the software-default claim false since multinma’s marginal_effects() defaults to a risk difference. GPT-5.6 Sol added that risk differences move with baseline risk under a constant conditional odds ratio, that standardized risks, survival differences, RMST and cumulative-incidence differences all depend on the target law, time horizon and competing events, and that incremental net benefit additionally depends on costs, utilities and thresholds.
Dissent. codex dissented (open): C2 and C3 are correct: marginal odds ratios are non-collapsible, and marginal hazard ratios depend on risk-set composition; neither is automatically population-invariant, although conditional log-odds and log-hazard parameters remain useful modeling devices. C1 and C4 conflate collapsibility, decision relevance, and transportability. Under a constant conditional odds ratio but differing baseline risks, risk differences vary across populations. Standardized risks, survival differences, RMST, and cumulative-incidence differences likewise depend on the target distribution, baseline hazards, competing events, and time horizon. Incremental net benefit additionally depends on costs, utilities, and willingness-to-pay. These quantities are often better decision outputs after target standardization, but they are not intrinsically more portable. Component PAIC also requires compatibility with the component model: cpaic at 9d150e9 documents that marginal component effects need not be additive. The context-specific scale-selection issue remains open, but the blanket prioritization and very-high severity are inflated.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that collapsible and absolute measures are ‘more portable across populations’ than odds and hazard ratios conflates collapsibility with transportability, and the epidemiological literature actively contradicts it. Dahabreh, Robertson & Steingrimsson (Eur J Epidemiol 2024) note that ‘many epidemiologists and applied statisticians believe that relative effect measures … are transportable across populations or at least more likely to be transportable compared with difference (absolute) effect measures’, and prove that ‘transportability for relative effect measures is largely incompatible with transportability for difference effect measures’. Incremental net benefit, being cost- and threshold-dependent, is the least jurisdiction-portable quantity on the list. title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text: EST-06 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text:
Statement
Reversing which trial supplies the IPD can reverse the direction of the apparent active-treatment comparison while each analysis remains internally coherent, because the two analyses estimate effects in different target populations. This is not new with Jiang et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10), who credit NICE DSU TSD18: Phillippo et al. 2018 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) documented the same reversal in a real appraisal, two competing manufacturers’ MAICs of secukinumab and adalimumab, and prescribed the remedy this entry proposes, namely deciding which population represents the decision target and transporting the comparison to it under the shared effect modifier assumption. Jiang et al.’s increment is that the paradox persists even when both analyses use the same covariate set. A target-population difference is also not the only way two MAICs can disagree; sampling error, different adjustment sets, model misspecification and measurement differences can each do it.

title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text:
Why it is open
Pairwise MAIC contains no mechanism forcing both directions of an analysis to answer the same question, because the target is set by which trial supplies IPD rather than by the decision. The remedy has been on the books since 2018 and has not changed sponsor behavior, since each sponsor’s own trial is the natural source of its IPD and nothing obliges two competing submissions to share a target. Transporting both effects to one declared target also needs common support, compatible outcome definitions and enough information to carry both transports, which is often exactly what is missing when the two populations differ enough to produce the reversal. How often the reversal arises and under what covariate configurations is unmeasured, so it is still discovered after submission rather than anticipated.

title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Jiang et al. 2025, A critical assessment of matching-adjusted indirect comparisons in relation to target populations, Research Synthesis Methods
Describes the reversal, its internal coherence and its population explanation, stating that both conclusions are potentially valid within the context of the specific populations considered, and shows the paradox persists with a common covariate set. It credits TSD18 for the original example and recommends IPD sharing rather than ruling on averaging.


Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2018, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD18)
Documents the two-way MAIC reversal in practice, with two MAIC analyses from competing manufacturers comparing treatments for ankylosing spondylitis, and prescribes the fix the entry proposes: decide which population represents the decision target and transport the comparison to it under the shared effect modifier assumption.


Fang and He 2026, Arbitrated Indirect Treatment Comparisons
A dedicated methodological response to the MAIC paradox that fixes a single common target, the overlap population, rather than a sponsor-specific one. It does not establish how often the reversal occurs or which target a committee should prefer.

title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not average conflicting MAICs unless the average is deliberately defined as an effect in a specified mixture population and the conditions for that definition hold. The remaining work is empirical and procedural rather than conceptual: characterize how often and under which covariate configurations the reversal arises, and give appraisal committees a rule for what to do when two sponsor submissions target different populations. Fang and He’s arbitrated indirect comparison (arxiv:2510.18071) is an existing methodological response that fixes a single common overlap target instead of a sponsor-specific one, so the task is to evaluate it against transporting both effects to an external decision target, not to reinvent it.

title: The MAIC paradox: swapping the IPD trial can reverse the comparison
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Jiang et al. describe a target-population problem in which reversing which trial supplies the IPD can reverse the apparent active-treatment comparison, even when each analysis is internally coherent. The two analyses are not contradictory implementations; they estimate effects in different target populations.”
What was wrong with it. The source read as though Jiang et al. 2025 discovered the reversal and as though the ban on averaging came from them; the literature auditor found the reversal documented with an applied case in NICE DSU TSD18 nine years earlier (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740), along with the same prescribed fix, and found no recommendation against averaging in Jiang et al., who instead call for IPD sharing with HTA agencies. GPT-5.6 Sol added that a target-population difference is not the only cause of discordant MAICs and that a weighted average is not invalid in principle if it is deliberately defined as an effect in a specified mixture population.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I read the full text of Jiang et al. 2025 (PMC12527493). The reversal, its internal coherence and its population explanation are all verbatim there (‘both conclusions … are potentially valid within the context of the specific populations considered’). But the entry reads as if Jiang et al. discovered the phenomenon. They did not, and they say so, crediting NICE DSU TSD18. Phillippo et al. 2018 Med Decis Making documented the same reversal with a real applied case nine years earlier and prescribed the entry’s own proposed direction: ‘the real conflict lies not in the different results produced by the 2 MAICs but in deciding which of the 2 study populations better represents the decision target population … the shared effect modifier assumption, if justified, may be used to transport indirect comparisons into the target population for the decision.’ Jiang et al.’s genuine increment is that the paradox persists with the same covariate set. Separately, the claim that averaging is invalid is not in Jiang et al.; they recommend IPD sharing to HTA agencies. Fang & He (arXiv:2510.18071, v2 May 2026) is an explicit methodological response targeting the overlap population. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Documents the two-way MAIC reversal in practice and prescribes the fix the entry proposes: declare the decision target and transport both effects to it under the shared effect modifier assumption.. Cites arxiv:2510.18071: A dedicated methodological response to the MAIC paradox that fixes a single common target (the overlap population) rather than a sponsor-specific one..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1 and C2 are technically possible: if swapping the IPD trial swaps the target population and the marginal treatment contrast varies across populations, the sign can reverse without a software error. C3 explains the constructed target-population paradox but is not the only possible cause of discordant MAICs; sampling error, different adjustment sets, model misspecification, and measurement differences can also reverse results. C4 is right for an unprincipled average of different estimands. A weighted average can be valid only if it is deliberately defined as an effect in a specified mixture population and the required linearity or standardization conditions hold. C5 states the correct design principle, subject to common support, compatible outcome definitions, and sufficient data or assumptions to transport both effects. C6 is acceptable as saying Jiang et al. describes the phenomenon, not that it uniquely discovered it. The conceptual cause and common-target remedy are already available; feasibility and empirical frequency remain open, so very-high severity is conditional rather than automatic. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10: Demonstrates and explains the reversal as comparison of population-specific estimands rather than necessarily a software contradiction.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Already prescribes choosing the decision target and transporting effects to it under stated assumptions.. Cites arxiv:2510.18071: Implements a common overlap-population target as one concrete response to sponsor-specific target reversal..

title: Methods return incompatible marginal and conditional estimands
text:
Statement
MAIC targets a marginal effect while a regression-based analysis returns a conditional one, so results from different population-adjustment methods are not directly comparable, and effect modification together with non-collapsibility can drive conditional and marginal estimates to conflicting treatment rankings (Phillippo et al. 2025, doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2). The source’s description of standard STC as yielding a clean conditional effect is wrong: in typical use it subtracts a published marginal comparator contrast from a conditional coefficient, and is biased for either estimand (Phillippo et al. 2021, doi:10.1002/sim.8965). The reconciliation the source proposes already exists and has been evaluated: parametric G-computation (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565) and multiple imputation marginalization (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02157-x) marginalize an outcome regression over a target population, and outstandR ships both (arxiv:2601.07532). What is left is discipline in use rather than a missing method: comparative evaluations still have to hold the estimand fixed, and some implementations return only one of the two quantities.

title: Methods return incompatible marginal and conditional estimands
text:
Why it is open
The methods differ in where averaging over covariates happens, and on a non-collapsible scale averaging before and after the link function gives different numbers, so the discrepancy is not an artifact that better fitting removes. Applied comparisons of MAIC, STC and ML-NMR therefore often measure the estimand difference rather than estimator performance, and both quantities are printed on the same scale under the same name, so a reviewer cannot detect the switch from the output alone. Marginalization is available but is not the default everywhere: multinma returns conditional and marginal population-average effects as separately named outputs, while cpaic returns a conditional profile contrast from cML-NMR and documents that no population-standardized path exists yet. Marginalizing also requires a correctly specified outcome model, a defined target joint covariate law and adequate support, so it recovers a compatible marginal functional rather than making the conditional and marginal parameters identical.

title: Methods return incompatible marginal and conditional estimands
text:

What it contributes

Supplies the missing citation for the conflicting-decisions claim and for reporting both estimands in the decision target population, and states that multilevel network meta-regression is currently the only population-adjustment method able to produce both conditional and marginal estimates in any decision target population.

cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9

title: Methods return incompatible marginal and conditional estimands
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use the existing marginalization routes instead of proposing them as new work: parametric G-computation or multiple imputation marginalization, both implemented in outstandR, and multinma’s separately named conditional and marginal outputs. Report conditional and marginal quantities in the declared decision target population where each is policy relevant, following the recommendations in Phillippo et al. 2025. Hold the estimand fixed before comparing MAIC, STC and ML-NMR, so head-to-head evaluations measure estimator performance rather than an estimand difference. Where an implementation returns only one quantity, as cML-NMR does in cpaic, the concrete task is to add the standardization step rather than to relabel the output.
