title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text: DIA-14 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Statement
Recovering the truth when supplied with the true sensitivity parameters is a necessary implementation check but says nothing about whether a QBA classifies robustness honestly when those parameters are unknown. The measures that would show this are not reported: false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, sensitivity-set truth inclusion, tipping-point error, calibration of probabilistic intervals, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, feasibility across the QBA grid, and Monte Carlo error of the QBA computation itself. Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13) exemplifies the practice: the QBA is demonstrated by graphical presentation of point estimates and intervals across assumed bias parameters on a case study, with none of these measures and no simulation evaluation of the method. The further claim that no minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation in PAIC is an absence claim the literature auditor could not verify.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Why it is open
Supplying the true sensitivity parameters removes exactly the uncertainty QBA exists to represent, so the evaluation is circular and every correctly coded method passes. A QBA produces a qualitative verdict, robust or fragile, that ordinary bias and coverage measures cannot score, and false reassurance is the costly error yet stays invisible unless the simulation deliberately places the truth outside the analyst’s assumed region. Evaluating classification honesty requires simulating the elicitation process itself, including ranges, priors, dependence and expert error, a behavioral component that statistical simulation conventions have no vocabulary for.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Exemplifies the reporting practice the entry criticizes: the QBA is demonstrated by scenario exploration on a case study, with none of the classification-honesty measures reported and no simulation evaluation of the method itself.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Score QBA methods as classifiers of robustness against an explicit decision rule, reporting false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, sensitivity-set truth inclusion over simulated data and elicitations, tipping-point error where a tipping point exists and a distance is defined, interval calibration, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, and evaluate estimation at the true parameters separately from classification when the parameters are unknown. Report Monte Carlo error and computational failure of the QBA computation itself, and check support and effective sample size across the QBA grid wherever the QBA changes weighting or the implied target distribution. Fit the required data-generating factors and comparator set to the QBA estimand and mechanism rather than imposing a single universal blueprint.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “QBA methods are evaluated by whether they recover the truth when supplied with the true sensitivity parameters, which is only an implementation check, and no minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation studies. The measures that would show whether a QBA is honest are not reported: sensitivity-set truth inclusion, false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, tipping-point or tipping-surface error, calibration of probabilistic QBA intervals, robustness to misspecified sensitivity-parameter distributions, support and ESS failure across the QBA grid, the frequency with which bias cancellation masquerades as validity, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, and the computational failure and Monte Carlo error of the QBA itself.”
What was wrong with it. The source asserted that no published minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation in PAIC and then prescribed one universal blueprint; the literature auditor recorded the absence claim as unverified rather than confirmed, and GPT-5.6 Sol judged the prescribed data-generating content and comparator set to be one particular benchmark design rather than a necessary minimum, with several proposed measures (tipping-point error, truth inclusion, support and ESS checks) applying only under stated conditions.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Consistent with the entry: in Ren et al. 2025, the newest QBA method for unanchored PAIC, the evaluation is graphical presentation of point estimates and intervals across assumed bias parameters on a case study, with no false-reassurance or false-fragility rate, no tipping-point error, no interval calibration, no sensitivity-set truth inclusion, and no Monte Carlo error for the QBA computation itself. That is positive evidence of the practice the entry describes. The caveat is the calibration rule: ‘No published minimum ADEMP standard exists for quantitative bias analysis simulation studies in PAIC’ is an absence claim and I found no source that asserts the absence, so I record it as unverified rather than confirmed. The remaining items are normative proposals for a blueprint, which cannot be true or false, only adopted or not. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.13: Exemplifies the reporting practice the entry criticizes: the QBA is demonstrated by scenario exploration on a case study, with none of the classification-honesty measures reported and no simulation evaluation of the method itself..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Oracle-parameter recovery is necessary evidence about implementation and identification under correct inputs, but it is insufficient evidence about practical QBA performance when sensitivity parameters are unknown; C1-C2 are therefore sound with that qualification. False reassurance, false fragility, truth inclusion, tipping error, decision classification, feasibility, and computational error are useful distinct targets when the QBA is intended to support a robustness decision. The proposed universal minimum is not technically established, however. C4 and C5 prescribe one large benchmark rather than a necessary ADEMP minimum; a direct QBA may itself be a bounding or partial-identification method. C6 is required for decision classification and regret, not for every inferential QBA. In C9, truth inclusion is a binary property for one fixed sensitivity set and becomes a probability only over simulated data, elicitation, or random sets. Tipping-point error requires existence, uniqueness, and a defined distance for multidimensional surfaces. Support and ESS checks apply when the QBA changes weighting or the implied target distribution, not automatically to every algebraic bias correction. Publication-frequency claims C3, C7, and C8 were not adjudicated. Honest classification is a high-priority validation goal, but the exact blueprint is roadmap guidance rather than a universal standard.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text: DIA-12 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Statement
A standard generator for component nonadditivity exists and has been used to quantify its consequences: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) adds log-scale interaction departures at mild and strong magnitudes, crosses them with three heterogeneity levels, and reports mean squared error and coverage separately for connected and disconnected networks. Competing bridges have also been compared on the same disconnected network, component additivity against a matching bridge, by Rucker et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339). Conditional on a specified drift model the bias is quantifiable rather than unknown: main-effect drift enters the decision contrast as an inner product of the contrast loading with the drift vector, interaction drift as the same loading applied to the drift matrix evaluated at the target covariate value, and cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package not on CRAN, already maps bounded main-effect drift to a worst-case decision-contrast shift and threshold. What is genuinely open is generating data under one bridge and fitting the competing bridges to rank them by worst-case behavior under misspecification, and any parameterization of drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Why it is open
Each bridge imports a different structural assumption, so their failures are not on a common scale and can only be ranked by generating data under one bridge and fitting the others, which no study has done; applied analysts therefore choose a bridge by data availability rather than robustness. A violation is untestable only when it lies in an observationally equivalent cross-subnetwork direction or the bridge supplies no overidentifying restriction, so a shared component estimable in more than one subnetwork, or an additive model with residual degrees of freedom, can reveal incompatibility, although failure to reject cannot validate the bridge. Drift on component-by-modifier interactions is the violation that interacts with population adjustment and has no parameterization at all, and because drift oriented along the target contrast biases the decision while orthogonal drift may cancel, magnitude alone cannot summarize it.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Supplies a reusable parameterization for generating additivity (bridge) violations at mild and strong magnitudes and quantifies the resulting mean squared error and coverage penalty in disconnected networks.


Rucker et al. 2020, Component network meta-analysis compared to a matching method in a disconnected network: A case study
Compares two competing bridges, component additivity and a matching-adjusted indirect comparison using single-arm observational studies, on the same disconnected network, contradicting the absolute form of the no-evidence claim.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Its bridge_fragility() implements a worst-case mapping from bounded component main-effect drift to decision-contrast movement with a tipping threshold, verified by a regression test; it does not cover interaction drift, hidden synergy, stochastic drift correlation or comparative bridge ranking.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the additivity-violation generator that already exists to cover interaction drift alongside main-effect drift, crossed with drift correlation and with drift direction relative to the target contrast, and extend the existing worst-case main-effect fragility mapping to interaction drift, hidden synergy, treatment-version differences, class outliers, wrong dose-response shape and external-control confounding. Then run the comparative study nobody has run: generate networks under each bridge mechanism in turn, fit all competing bridges, and report bias, decision error and detectability, ranking bridges by worst-case behavior under misspecification rather than by efficiency when correct. Publish the resulting mapping from drift magnitude, correlation and direction to decision-contrast bias as a function of network geometry, in units applied analysts can elicit.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. A standard generator exists for component nonadditivity and has been used to quantify its consequences, but no study generates data under one disconnected-network bridge and fits the competing bridges to rank them by worst-case behavior under misspecification, and no parameterization exists for drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices.
The source titled this. “Bridge violations have no standard generator or robustness ranking” The title says bridge violations have no standard generator, but a published, code-shared generator for additivity violations already quantifies error and coverage.
The source said. “There is no standard way to generate violations of bridging assumptions in simulation, no quantitative mapping from plausible component nonadditivity or cross-subnetwork drift to bias in the decision contrast, and no evidence on which bridge (baseline-risk exchangeability, reference prediction, component additivity, class exchangeability, dose-response, external controls, expert priors) degrades least dangerously when its assumption is misspecified.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no standard way to generate bridging violations and no quantitative mapping from nonadditivity or drift to decision-contrast bias; the literature auditor found a published, code-shared generator for additivity violations with quantified error and coverage penalties (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) and a head-to-head comparison of two bridges on one disconnected network (doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339), and GPT-5.6 Sol found the drift-to-decision mapping already implemented as bridge_fragility() in cpaic at commit 9d150e9.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim ‘There is no standard way to generate violations of bridging assumptions in simulation’ is contradicted for the component-additivity bridge. Petropoulou et al. 2023 use exactly such a parameterization: log-scale interaction departures added to the additive combination effect, with mild (exp(lambda)=1.5) and strong variants applied to different combinations, crossed with three heterogeneity levels, and scored by mean squared error and coverage separately for connected and disconnected networks. That is a published, code-shared generator plus a quantified mapping from violation magnitude to error in the affected contrasts. The cross-bridge ranking claim fares better but is not untouched: Rucker, Schmitz & Schwarzer 2020 fit the CNMA bridge and a matching/propensity bridge to the same disconnected multiple-myeloma network and compare, and Beliveau et al. 2017 stress-test the random-baseline bridge by disconnecting real networks. What remains genuinely open is a common scale, generating under one bridge and fitting all the others, and specifically drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices, for which I found no parameterization. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Supplies a standard, reusable parameterization for generating additivity (bridge) violations at mild and strong magnitudes and quantifies the resulting MSE and coverage penalty in disconnected networks.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.201900339: Directly compares two competing bridges (component additivity vs matching-adjusted indirect comparison using single-arm observational studies) on the same disconnected network, contradicting ‘no evidence on which bridge…’ in its absolute form..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2 and C8-C12 are broadly valid scenario distinctions, but the categorical impossibility and unquantified-bias claims are false. A bridge violation is untestable only when it lies in an observationally equivalent cross-subnetwork direction or the bridge supplies no overidentifying restriction. If a shared component is independently estimable in multiple subnetworks, or the additive model has residual degrees of freedom, heterogeneity or lack-of-fit can reveal incompatibility, although failure to reject cannot validate the bridge or identify the mechanism. Conditional on a specified drift model, bias is mathematically quantifiable: main-effect drift contributes an inner product such as m’Δ, while interaction drift contributes m’Λx. At cpaic 9d150e9, bridge_fragility() already maps a bounded main-effect drift to a worst-case decision-contrast shift and threshold. It does not address interaction drift, hidden synergy, stochastic drift correlation, or comparative bridge ranking, so the broader agenda remains open. Claims about a standard generator or the state of published comparative evidence were not adjudicated. Bridge fragility is critical for decision-grade disconnected comparisons; a universal robustness ranking is roadmap work. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: R/sensitivity.R implements a worst-case mapping from bounded component main-effect drift to decision-contrast movement, and tests/testthat/test-regression.R verifies the threshold arithmetic. This partially resolves the claimed absence of any quantitative drift mapping..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text: DIA-10 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Statement
No PAIC simulation varies informative IPD availability, selective baseline or outcome reporting, MNAR covariate or outcome missingness, informative censoring, differential loss to follow-up, or sampling error on published target summaries, so access-driven error goes unmeasured and is attributed to method failure by default. Two parts of the original claim need narrowing. A simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error already exists in the reconstruction literature (doi:10.1177/23814683221077643); what is missing is its propagation into PAIC estimator performance. And a sponsor holding IPD for its own trial makes access treatment-dependent without making it depend on the study-specific treatment effect, so an explicit availability model is needed when inference generalizes over studies and availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics, not automatically.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Why it is open
Simulating informative availability requires an explicit model coupling data access to effect-relevant study characteristics, which no PAIC generator contains. Treating published target moments as fixed removes a genuine uncertainty component whenever the estimand is a superpopulation target, and no simulation can show the consequence if the generator never adds sampling error to them. Selective reporting mechanisms are simply absent from the design space, and digitization error, although it has a standard evaluation design of its own in the reconstruction literature, has never been carried through into PAIC estimator performance.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




A Method for Reconstructing Individual Patient Data From Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves That Incorporate Marked Censoring Times, 2022
Illustrates the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error, narrowing the claim that digitization error has no standard generator. Retrieved at title, venue and summary level only.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Add data-access mechanisms to the generator: reconstruction error using the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct design, sampling error on published target summaries wherever the estimand is a superpopulation target, selective reporting of baseline characteristics and outcomes, MNAR covariate and outcome missingness, informative censoring, and differential loss to follow-up. Model informative IPD availability explicitly where availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics rather than assuming sponsor ownership makes it informative. Report how each mechanism degrades estimator and interval performance separately from the primary causal assumptions, so that access-driven error is not attributed to method failure.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Simulation designs treat data access as benign: IPD is assumed available at random, published target summaries are treated as fixed and known, and pseudo-IPD is treated as exact. MAR and MNAR covariate missingness, outcome missingness and informative censoring, selective baseline and outcome reporting, informative IPD availability, digitization error, sampling error in target summaries and differential loss to follow-up are not varied.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated digitization error as having no standard generator and sponsor-held IPD as automatically informative; the literature auditor found an established simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design (doi:10.1177/23814683221077643), and GPT-5.6 Sol separated structurally asymmetric access from an effect-informative availability mechanism and noted that fixed target summaries are appropriate when the target is the realized comparator-trial sample rather than a superpopulation.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I found no PAIC simulation that varies informative IPD availability, selective baseline or outcome reporting, MNAR covariate or outcome missingness, informative censoring, differential loss to follow-up, or sampling error on published target summaries, so the core of the entry stands. The digitization sub-claim needs narrowing: the pseudo-IPD reconstruction literature does have a standard evaluation design in which curves are simulated, digitized and reconstructed and hazard ratios and survival quantiles are compared with the originals, and there is recent work propagating reconstruction uncertainty into downstream synthesis by bootstrapping pseudo-IPD. So a digitization-error generator is not absent from evidence synthesis generally; what is absent is its propagation into PAIC estimator performance. I retrieved these reconstruction items at title/summary level only, hence the moderate confidence. Cites 10.1177/23814683221077643: Illustrates the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error, narrowing the claim that digitization error has no standard generator. Retrieved at title/venue and summary level only..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2, C4, and C5 identify legitimate and distinct mechanisms. C1, however, confuses a structurally asymmetric data configuration with an informative missing-data mechanism. A sponsor possessing IPD for its own treatment makes access treatment-dependent, but it does not by itself make access depend on the study-specific treatment effect or induce selection bias. An explicit availability model is needed only when inference generalizes over studies and availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics. C3 also needs an estimand condition: target summaries have sampling uncertainty for inference to a target superpopulation, but they may properly be conditioned on as fixed when the target is the realized comparator-trial sample. Consequently, treating them as fixed does not remove uncertainty from every valid downstream interval. Claims about what simulations usually assume are outside this audit. The access and missingness extensions are valuable, but their necessity and severity depend on the inferential target and actual evidence-acquisition process.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text: DIA-08 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Statement
PAIC simulation generators have begun to include non-normal, bimodal and Gamma covariates and deliberate positivity violations: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) includes Gamma covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep from no overlap to full overlap, Serret-Larmande et al. 2025 (arxiv:2507.12241) runs eight scenarios from ideal conditions to positivity violations with bimodal covariates, and copula (NORTA) generation of comparator covariates from reported summaries is already in use (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13). The premise also needs correcting: matching the full mean vector and covariance matrix of a nonsingular multivariate normal fixes the joint law, so the matched-moments failure mode comes from balancing a finite set of reported moments rather than from Gaussianity as such, and a shared-linear generator can still separate methods on efficiency, variance and finite-sample behavior even though it cannot test robustness to departures. The gap that survives is on the effect-modification side: component-specific, nonlinear-threshold and subnetwork-varying modification, decoupling of the within-study interaction from the between-study ecological gradient, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are all absent.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Why it is open
Data generated under shared linear effect modification cannot evaluate robustness to departures from that structure or demonstrate the benefit of relaxing it, so on the question that matters most the comparison is decided by the generator rather than by the methods. The distinction between a within-study interaction and a between-study ecological gradient exists only with multiple studies and varying covariate distributions, so single-pair templates cannot represent aggregation bias at all. Variables that drive participation but not outcome, and trial-engagement effects, require an explicit selection model that standard generators do not contain.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Serret-Larmande et al. 2025, Assessing the Impact of Covariate Distribution and Positivity Violation on Weighting-Based Indirect Comparisons: a Simulation Study
Runs eight scenarios from ideal conditions to positivity violations with non-normal and bimodal covariate distributions and reports which weighting estimators break, contradicting the claim that PAIC simulations cannot produce the limited-support failure mode.


Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Includes Gamma-distributed covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep from no overlap to full overlap, contradicting the multivariate-normal-only premise; also varies the validity of the shared effect modifier assumption.


Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Uses NORTA (Gaussian copula) sampling to build comparator covariate distributions from reported summaries, showing that copula generation is already standard practice in this literature.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Take the non-normal, bimodal and copula-based covariate generators that already exist and add explicit control over local support gaps, tail behavior and correlation, so that scenarios matching every reported moment while having disjoint local support can be produced on demand; vary target definition (trial, registry, pooled, overlap), measurement error, differing cut-points and missing target moments with wrong dependence assumptions as factors rather than fixing them. Concentrate new work on the effect-modification side by generating treatment-specific, component-specific, nonlinear-threshold, modifier-by-modifier and subnetwork-varying modification, and explicitly decoupling the within-study interaction from the between-study ecological gradient so aggregation bias becomes measurable. Add participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects through an explicit selection model to test whether adjusting for them inflates variance or induces bias.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. PAIC simulation generators have begun to include non-normal, bimodal and Gamma covariates and deliberate positivity violations, but effect-modification generators remain almost entirely shared-and-linear: component-specific, nonlinear-threshold and subnetwork-varying modification, decoupling of within-study interaction from between-study ecological gradient, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are absent.
The source titled this. “Covariate and modifier generators are too benign to break methods” The title says covariate generators are too benign, but the audit found Gamma and bimodal covariates and deliberate positivity violations already in published generators.
The source said. “Simulations generate multivariate normal covariates and shared linear effect modification, so by construction they cannot produce the two failure modes that dominate practice: populations that match on every reported global moment while containing regions of covariate space with no source support, and effect modification that is treatment-specific, component-specific, nonlinear, subnetwork-varying, or driven by an ecological gradient different from the within-study interaction. Non-Gaussian and multimodal marginals, ordinal and skewed variables, tail behavior, rare biomarker subgroups, temporal drift, measurement error, differing cut-points, alternative target definitions, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are all absent.”
What was wrong with it. The source said PAIC simulations use multivariate normal covariates and therefore cannot produce matched moments with disjoint support, and that the required copula machinery is missing from simulation code; the literature auditor found Gamma and bimodal covariate scenarios with deliberate positivity violations already published (doi:10.1002/sim.8759, arxiv:2507.12241) and NORTA copula generation already in use (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13). GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the Gaussian argument itself, since matching the full mean and covariance of a nonsingular normal identifies the joint law, and the claim that a shared-linear truth cannot distinguish methods at all.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The premise that PAIC simulations generate multivariate normal covariates ‘so by construction’ cannot produce matched-moments-with-disjoint-support is factually wrong for at least two studies I retrieved. Phillippo et al. 2020 simulated Gamma covariates in dedicated scenarios alongside normal ones and swept an overlap parameter from no overlap to full overlap. Serret-Larmande et al. 2025 ran eight scenarios spanning ideal conditions through positivity violations and non-normal, explicitly including bimodal, covariate distributions, and found MAIC-2 and propensity-score weighting sensitive to positivity violations while MAIC-1 stayed unbiased. Copula machinery is also already in use in this literature: Ren et al. 2025 use NORTA/Gaussian copula sampling to build comparator covariate distributions from reported summaries. The effect-modification half of the entry fares better: Phillippo 2020 varied validity of the shared effect modifier assumption, but I found nothing generating component-specific, nonlinear-threshold, subnetwork-varying modification, nor anything decoupling within-study interaction from an ecological gradient, nor participation-only variables or trial-engagement effects. Cites arXiv:2507.12241: Directly contradicts the claim that PAIC simulations cannot produce the matched-moments/limited-support failure mode: it deliberately simulates non-normal and bimodal covariates with positivity violations and reports which estimators break.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Includes Gamma-distributed covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep, contradicting the multivariate-normal-only premise.. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.13: Shows copula (NORTA) covariate generation from reported marginals is already standard practice in this literature, contradicting ‘requires copula machinery that most simulation code does not contain’..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The core validation concern is real, but several absolutes fail. C1 holds for a finite set of reported moments; a complete moment-determining sequence is a different claim. For nonsingular multivariate normals, matching the full mean vector and covariance matrix fixes the joint law and both populations have support on all of R^p. Matching only marginal means and variances does not fix correlations, however, and finite Gaussian samples can still have severe practical overlap problems. MAIC balances selected moments rather than establishing joint-law equality, while ML-NMR integration requires a specified joint distribution. C3, C5-C6, and C8-C12 are defensible scenario dimensions. C7 is false as written: a shared-linear truth can still distinguish methods on efficiency, variance, regularization, computation, and finite-sample behavior; it merely cannot evaluate robustness to departures or demonstrate the benefit of relaxing the shared-linear assumption. C4’s prevalence claim is outside this technical audit. The proposed expansion is primarily a validation roadmap, not uniformly a very-high-severity defect in every decision analysis.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text: DIA-06 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Statement
Factorial simulations have already located the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted indirect comparison: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) sweeps overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size and missing modifiers and reports that MAIC may even increase bias compared with standard indirect comparisons; Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511) locates the bias-variance crossover over 162 scenarios; and Liu et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1) runs a 729-scenario full factorial and finds MAIC more biased than naive indirect comparison at low covariate overlap with high covariate strength. What no study does is characterize and contrast the failure signatures of weighting-based, outcome-model-based and machine-learning estimators as overlap deteriorates, or report whether those failures are visible in any reported diagnostic. Flexible learners are absent from this simulation literature entirely.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Why it is open
Adjustment trades a bias term that depends on unobserved cross-study modifier imbalance against an observable variance penalty, so the exact data-specific gain cannot be learned from the data at hand without causal and modeling assumptions, although observed imbalance, prespecified effect modifiers, trial design and external knowledge still inform the decision. Weighting estimators fail by variance explosion and weight concentration while outcome-model estimators fail silently by extrapolating a fitted surface into regions with no data, so the two signatures are not comparable on any single performance measure, and flexible learners make this worse because their extrapolation behavior is set by regularization rather than by an explicit functional form. The existing factorials fix the estimator set narrowly, so the differential behavior near the support boundary is never observed even in the studies that have mapped the crossover region.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Factorial simulation crossing overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size, missing modifiers and covariate distributions across MAIC, STC and ML-NMR, reporting where adjustment fails to pay.


Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021, Methods for population adjustment with limited access to individual patient data: A review and simulation study
162-scenario simulation locating the bias-variance crossover as covariate overlap degrades.


Liu et al. 2025, Is the Use of Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Always Superior to Naive Indirect Comparison on Survival Outcomes? A Simulation Study
729-scenario three-level full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and covariate strength, identifying the region where MAIC is more biased than naive indirect comparison.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Records a factorial comparison across imbalance and overlap for naive bridging, cSTC and cMAIC; narrow in estimator coverage, and the auditor notes its validation pipeline was not publicly tracked and the result was not independently reproducible from the public commit.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing overlap-by-effect-modification factorials rather than repeat them: hold their design fixed and add outcome-model, ML-NMR, doubly robust and flexible-learner arms, sweep overlap from complete to near-disjoint, and record for each estimator family the onset of bias, the onset of variance inflation, and whether either is visible in any diagnostic the analyst would actually report. Report failure signatures rather than only average performance, so the output is a map of how each family degrades rather than a single winner. Publish the code so the comparison can be re-run as new estimators appear.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Factorial simulations have located the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted indirect comparison, but no study characterizes and contrasts the failure signatures of weighting-based versus outcome-model-based versus machine-learning PAIC estimators as overlap deteriorates, nor reports whether those failures are visible in any diagnostic.
The source titled this. “When adjustment pays, and how each estimator fails, is unknown” The title says when adjustment pays is unknown, but three published factorial simulations already locate the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted comparison.
The source said. “The field cannot say under which conditions population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC or NMA and under which it merely adds variance without reducing bias. Nor has it characterized how MAIC, standardized outcome regression, ML-NMR, doubly robust methods and flexible learners each fail as source-target overlap deteriorates.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no evidence base specifying when population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC; the literature auditor found three factorial simulations that map exactly that region (doi:10.1002/sim.8759, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511, doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1), and GPT-5.6 Sol found a factorial imbalance-and-overlap comparison of naive bridging, cSTC and cMAIC in the cpaic development package. What survives is the comparative failure-signature question across estimator families.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that there is no evidence base specifying when population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC is contradicted by at least three factorial simulations I retrieved. Phillippo et al. 2020 crossed sample size, missing effect modifiers, strength of effect modification, shared-effect-modifier validity, extrapolation validity, between-study overlap (a proxy parameter kappa swept from no overlap to full overlap) and covariate distributions, and reported that MAIC ‘may even increase bias compared with standard indirect comparisons’ - i.e. the region where adjustment does not pay. Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 ran 162 scenarios and located the crossover explicitly. Liu et al. 2025 ran 729 scenarios in a three-level full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and covariate strength and identified the failure region for MAIC versus naive comparison. What remains genuinely open is the comparative failure-signature question: no study I found sweeps overlap to near-disjoint and records, per estimator family, onset of bias versus onset of variance inflation and whether any diagnostic sees it, and flexible learners are absent entirely. Cites 10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1: 729-scenario full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and strength; identifies the region where adjustment is worse than not adjusting.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Factorial simulation crossing overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size, missing modifiers and covariate distributions across MAIC, STC and ML-NMR, and reporting where adjustment fails to pay.. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1511: 162-scenario simulation locating the bias-variance crossover as overlap degrades..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2, C5, and C6 are correct qualitative statements. Basic theory already identifies the crossover: without relevant effect modification or source-target imbalance, adjustment cannot remove that bias and may add variance; under positivity failure, weighting becomes concentrated while outcome regression relies on extrapolation and model correctness. Exact data-specific MSE improvement cannot be learned from observed data without causal and modeling assumptions, but adjustment decisions can still use observed imbalance, prespecified effect modifiers, trial design, and external knowledge. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, the README reports a factorial overlap-and-imbalance comparison of naive bridging, cSTC, and cMAIC, so “no evidence base” is false. That evidence is narrow, and the commit itself says its validation pipeline was not publicly tracked. A broad comparison including ML-NMR, doubly robust estimators, and flexible learners remains open. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: The package records a factorial comparison across imbalance and overlap for naive bridging, cSTC, and cMAIC, partially characterizing when adjustment changes bias and uncertainty. It does not cover the full estimator set and was not independently reproducible from the public commit..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text: DIA-04 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Statement
ADEMP already requires estimands to be defined and instructs analysts to consider whether each method is appropriate for the estimand identified, and Section 3.4 of Morris et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/sim.8086) works through the marginal-versus-conditional example that produces exactly the spurious bias this entry describes. What ADEMP does not provide is a structured per-scenario identification map recording which estimands are identified under the data-generating mechanism and under each fitted method’s own assumptions, and no journal or software requirement enforces one, so PAIC simulations routinely omit it. The underlying dispute has already been argued in public in this field, in the exchange over the anchored population-adjustment simulation and the reply on target estimands for efficient decision making (doi:10.1002/sim.8965), so reviewers do have ground on which to demand the mapping.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Why it is open
In PAIC the compared estimators target different populations (index trial, comparator trial, decision target) and different conditional or marginal contrasts, so a single scalar true value is ambiguous and non-identification can be reported as estimator bias. ADEMP’s instruction to check method-to-estimand compatibility is prose guidance rather than a required per-scenario artifact, so it is easy to skip and reviewers have nothing concrete to insist on. What is actually needed is a way to distinguish four things that all surface as bias: estimand mismatch, non-identification under the generating mechanism, model misspecification, and finite-sample bias.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Morris et al. 2019, Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Defines the ADEMP framework; its Methods element already instructs investigators to consider whether each method is appropriate for the estimand or target identified, and Section 3.4 works the marginal-versus-conditional example that produces spurious bias. It does not formalize a per-scenario identification map.


Target estimands for efficient decision making: Response to comments on Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study, 2021
A published exchange in the PAIC literature about which estimand a simulation’s true value refers to and whether the compared methods target it, showing the dispute is already live rather than unrecognized.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write a PAIC-specific extension of ADEMP rather than a competing framework: a per-scenario identification table stating, for each method, which estimand it targets and whether that estimand is identified under the data-generating mechanism, so that every reported bias is labeled as estimand mismatch, non-identification, misspecification or finite-sample bias. Do not restrict bias reporting to estimands a method claims to identify, since robustness simulations legitimately score every method against the policy-relevant estimand under deliberate assumption violation; label the cell rather than remove it. Attach the table to the simulation protocol so that journals and reviewers have something specific to require.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. ADEMP tells analysts to consider whether each method is appropriate for the stated estimand, but provides no structured per-scenario identification map recording which estimands are identified under the data-generating mechanism and under each method’s assumptions; no journal or software requirement enforces such a map, and PAIC simulations routinely omit it.
The source said. “Simulation studies of ITC and PAIC follow ADEMP, but no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to state which estimands are identified under the generating assumptions and which are identified under each fitted method’s own assumptions. Bias is therefore computed against a truth some compared methods never claimed to estimate.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to check whether a method can recover the stated estimand; both auditors found this false, since Table 1 of Morris et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/sim.8086) instructs investigators to identify methods and consider whether they are appropriate for the estimand or target identified, and Section 3.4 uses the conditional-versus-marginal case as its worked example. What is missing is a formalized per-scenario identification map, not the underlying instruction.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Morris, White & Crowther 2019. The five-element claim is right (element three is ‘Estimands and other targets’, slightly broader than ‘Estimands’). But the central claim, that no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to consider whether each fitted method can recover the stated estimand, is contradicted by the paper itself. Table 1 lists under Methods: ‘Identify methods to be evaluated and consider whether they are appropriate for estimand/target identified.’ Section 3.4 devotes a passage to precisely the PAIC failure mode described, using the marginal-versus-conditional logistic regression example, i.e. non-collapsibility. Further, the specific dispute has already been litigated in the PAIC literature: Remiro-Azocar, Heath & Baio’s comment on Phillippo et al.’s simulation and Phillippo et al.’s reply, ‘Target estimands for efficient decision making’, are an explicit argument about bias being computed against a truth a compared method did not target. Reviewers therefore do have ground to demand the mapping. What is genuinely missing is a formalized per-scenario identification map as a required reporting element. Cites 10.1002/sim.8086: The ADEMP Methods element and Table 1 already instruct analysts to check method-estimand compatibility, and Section 3.4 works the exact marginal-vs-conditional example that produces spurious bias in PAIC.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8965: Demonstrates that the PAIC field has already had a public, published argument about which estimand a simulation’s true value refers to and whether competing methods target it..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is correct, and ADEMP does not prescribe a formal per-scenario identification matrix. The report nevertheless overlooks that Morris et al. already require explicit estimands, require methods to be assessed for compatibility with those estimands, and use conditional versus marginal odds ratios as the exact example of a misleading bias comparison. The proposed rule that bias be computed only for estimands a method claims to identify is also too restrictive: robustness simulations legitimately evaluate a method against the policy-relevant estimand under deliberate assumption violation. The necessary distinction is among estimand mismatch, nonidentification, misspecification, and finite-sample bias. A PAIC-specific identification table would improve reporting, but this is a partially addressed reporting extension rather than an unrecognized very-high-priority barrier. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.8086: ADEMP defines the five stated elements and already instructs investigators to check whether each method is appropriate for the chosen estimand, including explicit treatment of conditional-versus-marginal mismatch. It does not formalize a PAIC-specific identification matrix..

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text: DIA-02 Unverifiable Very high priority Promising

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Statement
A global effective sample size is a scalar function of the weight distribution, so it does not encode where in covariate space the support lies or whether the supported region is relevant to the decision contrast. Reporting is demonstrably incomplete in practice: of 117 oncology MAICs reviewed by Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088), only three fulfilled all NICE recommendations and the distribution of weights was among the least reported items. The claim that software reports ESS alone and never computes contrast-specific influence is too strong: cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, already exports a weight panel with effective sample size, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration and residual balance, plus an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast. What remains missing is a definition set agreed across packages and the support-geometry diagnostics that no package computes: region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted moments.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Why it is open
Effective sample size is the squared sum of the weights divided by the sum of their squares, so it is invariant to where the weights sit in covariate space; the same value can come from a broad shifted distribution or from a decision-relevant subgroup with no source support at all. Balance is conventionally reported on the moments that were matched, which is tautological, while balance on the omitted moments is the informative check and is usually skipped. Because no body owns the definitions and at least three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment have been proposed, two analyses of the same evidence can report incomparable numbers, and no empirical knowledge accumulates about which diagnostic values predict bias.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Farinasso et al. 2025, Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Studies in Oncology: A Scoping Review Focused on Reporting Quality
Scoping review of 117 oncology MAICs finding that only three fulfilled all NICE recommendations and that the distribution of weights was among the least reported items; sources the previously unattributed claim that diagnostic practice is heterogeneous and incomplete.


Three new methodologies for calculating the effective sample size when performing population adjustment, 2024
Proposes three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment, evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. The literature auditor retrieved this at title and venue level only.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Exports a weight-quality panel (ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, residual balance) and an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast, documented as approximate for multi-arm networks.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Standardize and extend what exists rather than specify a panel from scratch: agree one definition set across packages, starting from the multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific influence already implemented in cpaic, and add the support-geometry diagnostics no package computes, namely region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance between source and target support, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted as well as fitted moments. Require the agreed panel in publications and submissions. Evaluate each member of the panel in simulation for its ability to predict realized error, and drop the ones that only describe the fit.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “ESS reported alone and overlap diagnostics are not standardized” The title says software reports effective sample size alone, which the audit judged too strong given an implemented multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence.
The source said. “Overlap is summarized by a single effective sample size, which cannot show the geometry of covariate support, where the analysis is extrapolating, or whether the supported region is relevant to the target contrast. The definitions and displays of overlap, ESS, extrapolation and modifier-balance diagnostics also differ between packages and publications, so two analyses of the same evidence report incomparable numbers.”
What was wrong with it. The claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced: the literature auditor supplied Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088) for heterogeneous and incomplete diagnostic reporting, and a 2024 paper proposing three competing ESS calculations (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) for the non-standardization of ESS itself. GPT-5.6 Sol read cpaic at commit 9d150e9 and found a multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence already implemented, so the ESS-only claim fails there; the two auditors disagreed on whether the entry as written was supported or overstated, and the weaker reading is published here.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): This entry is source_unsourced; I found real references that support it. Farinasso et al. 2025 scoping-reviewed 117 oncology MAICs and reports that only 3 fulfilled all NICE DSU recommendations and that among the least reported items was the distribution of weights, with mean sample-size reduction 44.9%. That is direct published evidence that diagnostic reporting practice is heterogeneous and suboptimal. Independently, a 2024 BMC Med Res Methodol paper proposes three new ESS calculations for population adjustment, which is itself evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. I found no PAIC package or publication reporting local (region-specific) ESS, optimal-transport cost, convex-hull distance, out-of-distribution maps, balance on omitted moments, or influence alignment between IPD study edges and the decision contrast; those remain absent, though absence found by search is weaker evidence than the reporting review. codex dissented (overstated): C4 through C7 follow directly from ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2): the same weights can be reassigned to different covariate locations without changing ESS, despite different local support and contrast relevance. The claim that software reports only ESS and never computes contrast-specific influence is already false for cpaic at the requested commit. It exports weight_diagnostics() with ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, and residual balance, plus edge_influence() for a named treatment contrast. The latter is documented as approximate for multi-arm networks. Local ESS, convex-hull distance, density ratios, and transport costs are complementary diagnostics requiring careful definitions and validation, not established replacements for ESS. Cross-package standardization and fuller support-geometry diagnostics remain open.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text: DEC-13 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Statement
Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record: 78% of 117 oncology MAICs did not report the source of the individual patient data and 66% conducted no systematic review to select the compared trials (10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088), and outcome-model fitting results were adequately reported in 3 of 18 analyses that required a model (10.1002/jrsm.1653). Independent verification does not require public release, though: secure reviewer access to the protocol, inputs, code and environment would support replication, so the requirement is auditability rather than publication. Whether a public protocol or statistical analysis plan is required in most HTA settings was checked by no auditor and is not asserted here. Machine-readable provenance is partly demonstrated rather than absent: the component ML-NMR path in cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package that is not on CRAN, stores engine and package versions, a Stan-source hash, the seed, the integration count, assumptions and priors in the fit object, while no path in it records a git commit, a dependency lock, an extraction audit trail or a failed-model history.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Why it is open
Submission dossiers are confidential and prepared under commercial pressure, so a prespecified protocol would fix analytic choices before the results are known and remove flexibility that currently exists. Extraction of aggregate data from publications is manual and its audit trail is rarely retained, so the inputs cannot be verified independently even in principle. Reporting failed models exposes what was tried and rejected, which is precisely what a reviewer needs and a submitter would rather omit, and no agency asks for it. The provenance that software does capture is uneven within a single package, so a reader cannot rely on its being present.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Farinasso et al. 2025
Sources the data-provenance component with measured figures: 69% of 117 oncology MAICs used pseudo-IPD, 78% did not report the source of the IPD, and 66% conducted no systematic review to select trials.


Truong et al. 2023
Sources the claim that model specification is not reported in enough detail to be reproduced or checked: results of the model-fitting procedure were adequately reported in 3 of 18 analyses (16.7%).


cpaic (development package, audited at commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package on GitHub, confirmed by an auditor not to be on CRAN. Its component ML-NMR fit objects store engine and package versions, a Stan-source hash, the seed, the numerical-integration count, assumptions, priors and refit arguments, partially implementing a machine-readable manifest; its MAIC path does not retain target standard deviations, seed or successful-bootstrap counts, and no path records a git commit, dependency lock, extraction audit trail or failed-model history.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require what makes independent verification possible under confidentiality: reviewer access to the protocol or statistical analysis plan, a documented extraction audit trail, executable code with the environment, versions and seeds, and disclosure of prespecified or materially different model attempts, convergence failures and exclusion rules with counts. Treat the machine-readable manifest as a convenience rather than a prerequisite, since executable code plus a locked environment is the authoritative specification and a separate manifest can drift; where one is used, make it package-wide instead of confined to a single analysis path. Reserve independent replication for high-stakes submissions.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record

Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “ITC submissions are not reproducible or independently checkable” The title asserts submissions are not independently checkable, which the audit rejected as too absolute since secure reviewer access supports replication without public release.
The source said. “Decision-grade ITC submissions cannot be reproduced or independently verified: a public protocol or statistical analysis plan, a data provenance and extraction audit trail, code with package versions, commit hashes, seeds and a lock file, a machine-readable model manifest, disclosure of all failed models and excluded simulation replicates, and independent review or replication for high-stakes submissions are all absent from standard practice.”

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text: DEC-11 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text:
Statement
The estimated-weights component of this problem is solved and evaluated: Chandler and Proskorovsky 2024 (10.1002/jrsm.1759) compared four families of MAIC variance estimator across 108 scenarios and give guidance by overlap, effective sample size and outcome type, following Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (10.1002/jrsm.1511), which had shown the robust sandwich estimator understates variability at small ESS. What remains unpropagated is model-selection uncertainty where selection used the analyzed data, pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty, target-summary uncertainty, and any decomposition separating sampling from prior and structural contributions. Bridge uncertainty belongs on that list only with a caveat: it is structural rather than sampling-based and should be reported through separate sensitivity or tipping analysis unless a defensible probability model supports joint propagation. The claim that standard software returns one interval with no components is also not true of cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package not on CRAN, which re-estimates MAIC weights inside an arm-stratified bootstrap, preserves multi-arm covariance, and carries an integration-error diagnostic for component ML-NMR.

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text:
Why it is open
Interval estimates are conditional on the selected model, so a selection step carried out on the analyzed data leaves the reported interval too narrow, and no ITC reporting convention requires selection uncertainty to be accounted for. Each remaining component enters at a different stage of a multi-step pipeline, and the final stage that produces the interval has no access to what earlier stages introduced. Numerical integration error is a deterministic approximation error, so the fix is bounding and convergence assessment rather than treatment as another random variance component; the existing diagnostic traces nested approximations against the final grid rather than against the exact integral and is unavailable for survival models.

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler and Proskorovsky 2024
108-scenario simulation comparing four families of MAIC variance estimator; finds raw-weight conventional estimators understate variability under poor or moderate overlap, ESS-weighted conventional estimators accurate across most scenarios, and sandwich estimators downward-biased at small ESS without finite-sample adjustment.


Remiro-Azocar, Heath and Baio 2021
Earlier evidence that the robust sandwich variance estimator underestimates variability in MAIC where effective sample sizes are small.


cpaic (development package, audited at commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package on GitHub, confirmed by an auditor not to be on CRAN. Re-estimates MAIC weights and refits the outcome model inside an arm-stratified bootstrap, preserves multi-arm covariance through netmeta for the frequentist bridge and the standard 0.5 baseline-shift correlation for random effects, and provides a nested-Sobol integration-error diagnostic; selection, target-summary, pseudo-IPD and bridge-uncertainty decomposition remain unimplemented.

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adopt the published variance-estimation guidance for weights instead of treating it as open, and extend propagation to the stages still conditioned on: pseudo-IPD reconstruction, target summaries including their covariance, and model selection where the selection used the analyzed data. Require full model specification with priors and random-effects structure, explicit separation of within-study from between-study effect modification, justification of shared versus treatment- or component-specific interactions, and presentation of substantively plausible alternative models. Report structural bridge uncertainty and numerical error separately, as sensitivity regions and convergence bounds, rather than merging them into a single interval.

title: Intervals omit selection, reconstruction and target-summary error
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Reported intervals omit selection, weighting and bridge uncertainty” The title lists weighting uncertainty as unpropagated, but the audit found the estimated-weights variance question settled across a 108-scenario evaluation with actionable guidance.
The source said. “Reported ITC and PAIC intervals are computed conditional on one selected model and on upstream inputs treated as fixed. Model specification and the selection process are not fully reported, and uncertainty from estimated weights, multi-arm covariance, pseudo-IPD reconstruction, target summaries, priors, numerical integration and the bridge itself is neither propagated nor decomposed.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated estimated-weight uncertainty in MAIC as unaddressed and said standard software offers no decomposition. The literature auditor found the variance-estimation question settled by a 108-scenario evaluation with actionable guidance (10.1002/jrsm.1759), and GPT-5.6 Sol found weight bootstrapping, multi-arm covariance and an integration-error diagnostic already implemented in cpaic and objected that structural bridge uncertainty should not be folded into a confidence interval.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 applies when model selection used the analyzed data, not to a genuinely prespecified model; its claimed frequency is not established here. C2-C3 are correct because between-study interaction gradients are ecologically confounded and shared interactions are structural assumptions. C4 is warranted for substantively plausible alternatives, not every imaginable model. C5 should say random-effects structures and priors can materially affect conclusions and must be reported. C6-C8 are sound when those stages are estimated, with target-summary covariance also needed where applicable. C7’s necessity is exact, but its frequency claim is unverified. C9 is important, but bridge uncertainty is structural and cannot be inserted into a confidence interval without a defensible probability model; sensitivity regions or tipping analyses should ordinarily remain separate. C10 should require convergence assessment and control of numerical error, not automatic treatment as a stochastic variance component. The blanket software claim is false for cpaic: cMAIC re-estimates weights inside an arm-stratified bootstrap, network engines preserve multi-arm dependence, and cML-NMR has an integration-error diagnostic. Selection, target-summary, pseudo-IPD, and full bridge-uncertainty decomposition remain unresolved.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. One component of this bundle has been formally settled. Chandler & Proskorovsky 2024 (Res Synth Methods, doi 10.1002/jrsm.1759, PMID 39323097) ran a 108-scenario Monte Carlo study comparing four families of variance estimator for MAIC (conventional with raw weights, conventional with ESS-rescaled weights, robust sandwich variants, bootstrap) across anchored and unanchored designs and binary and time-to-event outcomes, and gives concrete guidance: raw-weight conventional estimators understate variability under poor or moderate overlap, sandwich estimators are downward-biased at small ESS unless finite-sample-adjusted, bootstrapping is unstable at small ESS. The remaining components, model-selection uncertainty, pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty, target-summary uncertainty, multi-arm covariance preservation, numerical integration error, and a decomposition separating sampling from bridge and prior uncertainty, I found no work addressing, and they remain open. title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text: DEC-09 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text:
Statement
Population-adjustment reports frequently omit the inputs that determine the adjustment: which variables were predefined as effect modifiers rather than prognostic-only, the clinical and empirical rationale, measurement definitions and harmonization, the provenance of each target moment, the assumptions used to reconstruct the target joint distribution, and any uncertainty in the target summaries. Farinasso et al. 2025 (10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088) found evidence of effect-modifier status and adjustment for all effect modifiers among the least-reported items across 117 oncology MAICs. The joint-distribution assumption is an undisclosed requirement rather than an unrecognized one: multilevel network meta-regression (10.1111/rssa.12579) reconstructs the target joint distribution with a Gaussian copula whose correlations are borrowed from the IPD studies, and multinma implements it, so an analyst has a named convention to state. A correlation matrix alone does not identify a joint distribution, since marginal families and a dependence model are also needed, and moment-matching MAIC and identity-link models do not require a full joint distribution at all.

title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text:
Why it is open
Modifier selection is usually made after seeing which variables the comparator publication happens to report, so predefinition would expose that availability rather than clinical reasoning drove the choice. Target summaries are published as point estimates, so treating them as fixed constants is the path of least resistance and no reporting rule forces the uncertainty to be propagated or its neglect justified; conditioning on them is defensible only for a fixed policy target or negligible sampling error. Software does not push back either: the component ML-NMR path in cpaic stores the copula, marginal families and correlation matrix in the fit, but no path records the source of each target moment, harmonization decisions or target-summary uncertainty, and its MAIC object retains target means without target standard deviations. cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub and is not on CRAN.

title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020 (multilevel network meta-regression)
Reconstructs the target joint covariate distribution from published marginals using a Gaussian copula with correlations matched to the IPD studies, making explicit the assumption the entry says is undisclosed; implemented in multinma.


Farinasso et al. 2025
Finds evidence of effect-modifier status and adjustment for all effect modifiers and prognostic variables among the least-reported items across 117 oncology MAICs.


cpaic (development package, audited at commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package on GitHub, confirmed by an auditor not to be on CRAN. Its component ML-NMR path makes the Gaussian-copula dependence model, marginal families and correlation matrix explicit and retains them in the fit; it does not record moment sources, harmonization decisions or target-summary uncertainty, and its MAIC object stores target means but not target standard deviations.

title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require the reporting elements the methods already imply: predefined effect modifiers with clinical and empirical rationale, harmonized measurement definitions, a complete listing of target moments with sources, an explicit statement of the marginal families and dependence model used to reconstruct the target joint distribution, and either propagation of target-summary uncertainty or a justification for treating it as negligible. Fix the estimand and effect scale first, because on a non-collapsible scale a variable that is only conditionally prognostic still moves the marginal effect, so prognostic-only cannot mean ignorable. Make the fit object carry the provenance so the disclosure is emitted by the software rather than asserted by the analyst.

title: Modifier selection and target moments reported without provenance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Population-adjustment reporting omits the inputs that determine the adjustment: predefinition of effect modifiers as distinct from prognostic-only variables, clinical and empirical rationale for each variable, measurement definitions and harmonization, all target moments and their sources, the reconstruction of the target joint distribution with its correlation assumptions, and propagation of uncertainty in the target summaries.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated the correlation assumption behind a reconstructed target joint distribution as an unrecognized gap. The literature auditor found it is an explicit, documented component of multilevel network meta-regression (Phillippo et al. 2020, 10.1111/rssa.12579, implemented in multinma), so the claim narrows to non-disclosure; GPT-5.6 Sol added that correlations alone do not identify a joint distribution and that moment-matching MAIC does not need one.

Farinasso et al. 2025 found that ‘evidence of effect modifier status’ and ‘adjustment for all effect modifiers and prognostic variables’ were among the least-reported items across 117 oncology MAICs, and Truong et al. 2023 found extensive heterogeneity assessment in only 37.0% of PAIC analyses. So a willing analyst has a named convention to state, and the entry should say the assumption is rarely disclosed rather than that it is unrecognized. I could not verify with any measured figure how often correlation assumptions or target-moment provenance are actually reported, nor find a method paper propagating target-summary uncertainty; those sub-claims are plausible but unmeasured.

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1 and C5 are sound only after fixing the estimand and effect scale. On non-collapsible scales, a conditionally prognostic variable can alter a marginal treatment effect even without a conditional treatment interaction, so prognostic-only must not mean irrelevant. C2’s frequency is not assessable from the supplied evidence.
