title: Computational diagnostics and Monte Carlo error go unreported
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adopt the existing template rather than write a new one: ADEMP-style preregistration and reporting as specified by Siepe et al., run through a framework such as SimDesign that already captures errors, re-simulates non-convergent replicates, and records the session environment. Report diagnostics and failure counts per scenario cell rather than averaged, and report the MCSE of each performance measure and of the paired differences that carry a ranking; treat seed and initialization sensitivity as a diagnostic of an unstable fit rather than as a separate performance estimand. Publish replicate-level outputs including truths, estimates and failure indicators so new measures can be computed without rerunning the study. A review of what ITC and PAIC simulation studies actually report would put a number on the field-specific gap that is currently assumed.

title: Computational diagnostics and Monte Carlo error go unreported
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Simulation studies in this field publish performance summaries without the computational context that produced them or the precision of the summaries themselves: runtime and memory, optimizer and sampler failure rates, divergent transitions and maximum tree depth, R-hat and bulk/tail effective sample size, numerical integration error, sensitivity to initialization and seed, replicate-level outputs, and the Monte Carlo standard error of each reported performance measure are all routinely absent.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented this as an unmet methodological need. The literature auditor found the reporting standard and the tooling already exist (Siepe et al. 2024, doi:10.1037/met0000695; SimDesign on CRAN), so the gap is adoption rather than invention, and noted that the prevalence figures are from psychology because no ITC or PAIC specific review has been done. The source-code auditor narrowed the ranking claim: separating two methods needs the MCSE of their paired difference, and a close ranking is not automatically indeterminate.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 and C6 are empirical prevalence claims not established by the supplied evidence. C2 is correct whenever numerical integration is approximate. C3 is correct: diagnostic failure rates should be stratified by scenario rather than hidden in an average. C4 is useful when optimization or sampling is initialization-sensitive, but seed sensitivity is not automatically a separate method-performance estimand; ordinary simulation variation should instead be quantified by MCSE. C5 is plausible under informative failure but is not a theorem. C7 is too absolute: if replicate counts or raw outputs are available, uncertainty can sometimes be derived or bounded, and method rankings require the MCSE of paired differences rather than merely separate MCSEs. C8 is correct when raw outputs include truths, estimates, and failure indicators. cpaic now records fit-level divergences, tree-depth saturation, E-BFMI, R-hat, and ESS, but supplies no simulation-level runtime, memory, failure aggregation, performance-measure MCSE, or replicate archive.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I retrieved Siepe, Bartos, Morris, Boulesteix, Heck & Pawel (2024, Psychological Methods, doi 10.1037/met0000695, PMID 39541533; full text PMC7616844). It reviewed 321 articles, 100 of which report a simulation study, and reports: 77% did not report uncertainty of performance measures; convergence reported in 19%; full computational-environment information in 2%; code unavailable for 64%. That is direct empirical support for the general claims, and the same paper supplies MCSE formulae and a repetition-count calculation, so the methodological prescription is solved and packaged (ADEMP-PreReg, building on Morris/White/Crowther’s ADEMP). SimDesign (CRAN 2.25.5) already catches errors and warnings, re-simulates non-convergent results, and records sessioninfo. Caveat, and it is the material one: none of this evidence is field-specific. I found no review of ITC, PAIC or ML-NMR simulation studies quantifying failure-rate, divergence, R-hat or MCSE reporting, so every claim qualified ‘in PAIC and ML-NMR simulation studies’ is an extrapolation from psychology and general biostatistics. Separately, the integration-error sub-claim is now automated by multinma int_check (default TRUE since 0.6.0). Cites doi:10.1037/met0000695: Supplies the empirical rates of non-reporting and a complete reporting/preregistration template with MCSE formulae and repetition-count calculation; solves the prescription, not the field’s adoption.. Cites cran:SimDesign 2.25.5: Provides the infrastructure for automatic re-simulation of non-convergent results, error/warning capture, and high-quality parallel RNG..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 and C6 are empirical prevalence claims not established by the supplied evidence. C2 is correct whenever numerical integration is approximate. C3 is correct: diagnostic failure rates should be stratified by scenario rather than hidden in an average. C4 is useful when optimization or sampling is initialization-sensitive, but seed sensitivity is not automatically a separate method-performance estimand; ordinary simulation variation should instead be quantified by MCSE. C5 is plausible under informative failure but is not a theorem. C7 is too absolute: if replicate counts or raw outputs are available, uncertainty can sometimes be derived or bounded, and method rankings require the MCSE of paired differences rather than merely separate MCSEs. C8 is correct when raw outputs include truths, estimates, and failure indicators. cpaic now records fit-level divergences, tree-depth saturation, E-BFMI, R-hat, and ESS, but supplies no simulation-level runtime, memory, failure aggregation, performance-measure MCSE, or replicate archive. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Automates collection and warning for the main HMC convergence and geometry diagnostics at the fitted-model level..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. General simulation-study methodology has long required Monte Carlo standard errors and computational transparency (White 2010; Morris, White & Crowther 2019 ADEMP tutorial; Williams et al. 2024 TRISS checklist for reporting MCSE). Those works propose standards; they do not show that PAIC/ML-NMR simulation papers now report optimizer/sampler failure rates, divergences, tree-depth, R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, integration error, seed/init sensitivity, or MCSE of performance measures per scenario severity. Field-focused searches (RSM, SiM, Pharm Stats, Value in Health, 2024–2026; multinma/maicplus simulation vignettes) did not surface a convention shift that would close C1, C3, C5–C7 as practice claims. C2 remains tied to ML-NMR (integration vs MC error), where multinma diagnostics help applied fits more than published simulation tables. C8 (share replicate-level outputs) is technically trivial and still uncommon. Problem remains open as an ITC/PAIC reporting practice gap, not as absence of general methodology.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text: CMU-02 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Statement
In population-adjusted network and bridge models a proper prior with a finite, positive marginal likelihood yields a proper posterior even along directions the likelihood cannot identify, so a narrow credible interval can reflect the prior rather than the evidence, and a clean R-hat does not rule that out. The diagnostics that would expose it already exist as general Bayesian workflow tools: power-scaling sensitivity (Kallioinen et al., arXiv:2107.14054, with the priorsense package on CRAN) and multinma’s plot_prior_posterior(), shipped since version 0.1.0. What is missing is their application here: the literature and recency auditors found no power-scaling or per-parameter contraction analysis of PAIC bridge or disconnected-network models, and no released ITC package computes a contraction measure or benchmarks a decision contrast against a prior-only fit.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Why it is open
The posterior blends prior and likelihood and nothing in a printed interval separates them, so a well-behaved posterior for a cross-gap contrast or an aggregate-only interaction is formatted exactly like an evidence-based estimate. Convergence diagnostics interrogate the sampler rather than the likelihood’s contribution, though the exemption is not total: Kallioinen et al. note that a case with both an uninformative prior and a noninformative likelihood will usually announce itself through fitting problems. The gap is wiring and practice rather than method: no released ITC package computes power scaling or prior-to-posterior contraction, so running either on a bridge model is bespoke work, and because prior dominance grows with scenario severity a single check on one benign dataset says nothing about the cases that matter.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Kallioinen, Paananen, Burkner and Vehtari 2024, power-scaling sensitivity for priors and likelihoods, Statistics and Computing (arXiv:2107.14054)
defines power-scaling sensitivity: prior sensitivity with little or no likelihood sensitivity is the signature of a likelihood that is noninformative relative to the prior; notes that a jointly uninformative prior and likelihood usually shows up as fitting problems instead


priorsense R package
implements power-scaling prior and likelihood sensitivity diagnostics for fitted Bayesian models; named by the recency auditor as available but not wired into ITC packages


multinma R package, plot_prior_posterior() since version 0.1.0
plots prior against posterior for model parameters, a partial prior-versus-posterior facility that stops short of a numerical contraction measure or power scaling


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commits 7563a64 and a99b718
returns NA instead of a finite summary for contrasts the component design does not identify, and adds prior predictive checks plus refits under tighter and looser prior scales as an empirical identification diagnostic; it implements no formal power scaling, no numerical contraction measure, and no prior-only benchmark fit

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Apply the existing tools rather than build new ones. Run power-scaling sensitivity and per-parameter prior-to-posterior contraction on PAIC bridge, component and disconnected-network models, benchmark each decision contrast against a prior-only fit, and report contraction for the contrasts that carry the decision and not only for model parameters, since contraction is parameterization-dependent. Wire these into released packages so they stop being bespoke scripts, and evaluate them conditional on scenario severity rather than at one benign scenario.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “In population-adjusted network and bridge models a proper prior guarantees a proper posterior even for contrasts the likelihood cannot identify, so a narrow credible interval can reflect the prior rather than evidence. Prior predictive checks, power-scaling sensitivity, and per-parameter prior-to-posterior contraction are not routinely reported, so a reader cannot tell which quantities the data actually informed.”
What was wrong with it. The source implied the diagnostics themselves were absent. Power scaling (Kallioinen et al. 2024, arXiv:2107.14054; priorsense on CRAN) and multinma’s plot_prior_posterior() have existed for years, and the source-code auditor found that cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub and not on CRAN, already returns NA for structurally non-identified contrasts and ships prior predictive checks and tight/loose prior refits; the other two auditors found nothing equivalent in released ITC packages, and that disagreement stands. The propriety claim was also narrowed: a proper prior gives a proper posterior when the marginal likelihood is finite and positive, not unconditionally.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): I read the power-scaling paper in full (arXiv 2107.14054; Kallioinen, Paananen, Burkner, Vehtari, Stat Comput 2024) and the SBC test-quantities paper (arXiv 2211.02383). Kallioinen supports the diagnostic claim directly: prior sensitivity with little or no likelihood sensitivity is the signature of a likelihood that is noninformative relative to the prior. Modrak et al. independently corroborate the core worry: standard rank-based SBC ‘could never detect … when the posterior is equal to the prior’. Both are generic Bayesian-workflow tools, not ITC methods. I found no application of priorsense or power-scaling to PAIC bridge or disconnected-network models; PubMed returns nothing, and multinma’s R/ directory and NEWS contain no priorsense or power-scaling entry, so the tooling is genuinely not wired in. text: CMP-26 Partially addressed Very high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Statement
cpaic is an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, and its evidence base is a local, gitignored factorial simulation over synthetic examples whose summaries omit Monte Carlo standard errors, with no real full-IPD benchmark in the repository and no evidence of independent replication. The repository is not bare: it contains tracked analytic, adversarial, and recovery unit tests and a continuous integration workflow that checks agreement between its two Stan backends. The report’s ten-item minimum validation standard is internally consistent as a list, but several items restate the established ADEMP standard for simulation studies rather than being bespoke requirements, and a public factorial CNMA simulation benchmark already exists for the non-adjusted case.

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Why it is open
Synthetic data generated from the model family the estimator assumes can confirm that the code implements the model, not that the model recovers truth under realistic violations, and when the author of the theory writes the only implementation, agreement between theory and program is guaranteed rather than informative. Without committed generators, scenario manifests, seeds, raw outputs, and Monte Carlo standard errors, a reported operating characteristic cannot be checked, rerun, or extended by anyone else. Several validation items require resources the author cannot unilaterally obtain, including full-IPD gold standards, connected empirical networks suitable for bridge deletion, and independent replication, and adversarial scenario design is itself an open task because it requires knowing which violations matter most, which is what the validation is supposed to reveal.

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Move the existing local factorial simulation into a public version-controlled repository under continuous integration, with generators, manifests, seeds, and raw outputs, and report Monte Carlo standard errors with predeclared estimands, following the ADEMP structure rather than presenting these as bespoke requirements. Extend the existing public CNMA simulation benchmark to the population-adjusted component case with adversarial scenarios that violate additivity, interactions, the target distribution, overlap, and the bridge, and compare against NMA, CNMA, MAIC, g-computation, ML-NMR, unanchored, and partial-identification alternatives. Validate against full-IPD gold standards and by empirical bridge deletion in connected networks, and obtain independent review and replication, treating the ten items as a strong evidence agenda rather than as individually non-waivable preconditions, since equivalent analytic or external validation can sometimes substitute.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text: CMP-24 Partially addressed Medium priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Statement
edge_influence() in cpaic, an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, asks whether a given IPD edge contributes to a requested target contrast. Its diagonal-weight calculation is exact for two-arm common-effect models with fixed weights and approximate for multi-arm studies, because the underlying frequentist CNMA fit uses within-study covariance; under random effects the fitted tau-squared is included in the weights, so the residual approximation comes from not re-estimating tau under perturbation rather than from ignoring shrinkage. Exact contribution machinery already exists for CNMA component effects and for study importance in NMA; what those do not cover is contribution to a target-specific, population-adjusted cross-gap contrast.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Why it is open
The approximation drops the correlation structure introduced by multi-arm trials and the re-estimation of heterogeneity under perturbation, both of which redistribute information across edges in ways a first-order calculation misses, and either can change an influence ranking. The diagnostic matters precisely because it exposes edges with excellent effective sample size that nonetheless carry no weight for the cross-gap contrast, a question standard MAIC overlap and weight diagnostics cannot answer, so an incorrect ranking undermines the one tool that answers it. The published exact decompositions operate on component effects in an unadjusted CNMA, not on a target-specific population-adjusted contrast, so they cannot simply be called.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Yang et al. 2026
gives an exact decomposition of which studies and comparisons contribute to each component effect in CNMA using pseudo-paths and the component-level hat matrix; does not cover population-adjusted target-specific contrasts


Rucker et al. 2020, study importance
defines an exact, uniquely defined per-study influence measure for a specified NMA estimate as the reduction in that estimate’s variance when the study is added, for one-stage and two-stage models


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018
establishes the flow-network proportion-contribution matrix showing how much each direct treatment effect contributes to each NMA estimate


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; provides edge_influence() to test whether an IPD edge contributes to a requested target contrast, using inverse-variance weights that include the fitted tau-squared and are approximate for multi-arm studies

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing exact contribution machinery, the flow and pseudo-path decomposition for component effects and the variance-reduction definition of study importance, to a target-specific population-adjusted contrast, rather than deriving a new influence measure from scratch. Where an exact extension is not available, compute influence from the model Jacobian and Hessian or by posterior perturbation of the observed edge, including re-estimation of heterogeneity. Report the approximation status alongside each ranking, since the diagnostic is already exact in the two-arm common-effect case.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “cpaic’s edge_influence() diagnostic asks whether a given IPD edge actually contributes to the requested target contrast, but its computation is approximate in multi-arm and random-effects settings, so influence rankings may not match exact fitted influence.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated edge influence as a novel diagnostic with no prior art and said random-effects shrinkage is ignored. The literature auditor found three established exact methods, including a component-level decomposition whose flow-weighted sum matches the CNMA component estimate within numerical tolerance (doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02766-8; doi:10.1186/s12874-020-01075-y; doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3); GPT-5.6 Sol found that the implementation does include the fitted tau-squared in its weights and is exact for two-arm common-effect models.

The source explicitly describes the diagonal-W calculation as approximate for multi-arm studies because discomb() uses within-study covariance. For two-arm common-effect models with W fixed, the displayed linear influence is exact. Under random effects, cpaic does include the fitted tau-squared in W; remaining approximation arises if exact perturbation influence is defined to include re-estimation of tau, not because random-effects weighting is ignored. Such omissions can change rankings. C3 is algebraically possible and is demonstrated by the package tests: ESS measures within-edge weight dispersion, whereas target influence is a network-design leverage quantity and can be zero. C4 is correct because ordinary MAIC overlap and weight diagnostics do not evaluate downstream leverage for a requested cross-gap contrast. This is a useful diagnostic refinement, but not a defect in the fitted estimator itself.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text: CMP-22 Confirmed open High priority Emerging

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Statement
IPD availability may be informative rather than random, and the premise has empirical support: a survey of 31 IPD meta-analyses found that 16 (52 percent) did not obtain all the individual participant data requested, five of those did not mention it as a limitation, and only six examined how the trials without IPD might affect conclusions. Component PAIC conditions on the supplied IPD and provides neither a selection model for availability nor grouped leave-IPD-out validation. Nonrandomness has to be demonstrated or posited as a sensitivity assumption rather than assumed categorically: availability can be modeled where it depends on observed trial-level variables, and only selection on unobserved IPD quantities is unidentified without additional data or assumptions.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Why it is open
The IPD edges are the ones that get population-adjusted and the ones that inform interaction parameters, so a selection mechanism on availability propagates into which parts of covariate space are informed by causal evidence rather than by aggregate association. Selection depending on unobserved IPD characteristics cannot be estimated from within the network, because the trials with unobserved IPD are precisely the ones that would identify it. Federated approaches or a full selection model require access or assumptions that are currently unavailable, and no leave-IPD-out facility exists in component PAIC software to at least measure the dependence.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ahmed, Sutton and Riley 2012
surveys 31 IPD meta-analyses and documents that most did not obtain all requested individual participant data and few assessed the impact, establishing that IPD availability is not random


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Implement grouped leave-IPD-out validation first, since it measures how conclusions depend on which trials contributed individual data even though it does not identify or correct the mechanism. Model availability where it depends on observed trial-level characteristics, and treat selection on unobserved characteristics as an explicit sensitivity assumption with a stated selection model rather than as an unmodeled default. Pursue federated methods that let non-sponsor trials contribute individual-level information without releasing data, which is the only route that addresses the cause rather than the symptom.

Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The trials for which IPD is available are typically sponsor-owned and are not a random subset of the evidence base, yet component PAIC treats IPD availability as an exogenous feature of the network.”
What was wrong with it. The source asserted non-random IPD availability categorically and cited nothing. GPT-5.6 Sol flagged the categorical form as unsupported and distinguished selection on observed trial-level variables, which is modelable, from selection on unobserved IPD quantities, which is not identified; the literature auditor supplied the missing empirical source, doi:10.1136/bmj.d7762.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The premise is sourceable and the entry sources nothing. Ahmed, Sutton and Riley 2012 surveyed 31 recent IPD meta-analyses of randomised trials and found that ‘Sixteen (52%) of the 31 meta-analyses did not obtain all the individual participant data requested, yet five of these (31%) did not mention this as a potential limitation, and only six (38%) examined how trials without individual participant data might affect the conclusions’, concluding that ‘Publication, availability, and selection biases are a potential concern for meta-analyses of individual participant data’. That converts ‘IPD availability is not random’ from assertion to evidence, and it also shows the field’s partial response - their recommendation is to include aggregate data from the IPD-less studies to gauge impact, which is what a network with mixed IPD and AgD already does. What remains open is exactly what the entry says: a selection model for IPD availability, and leave-IPD-out validation, neither of which I found in the PAIC literature.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text: CMP-20 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Statement
For an aggregate Poisson arm, component ML-NMR multiplies total exposure by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If unweighted participant moments are supplied, that is exact only when exposure has zero covariance with the modeled individual rate; full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary, and treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is already absorbed by each arm’s own total exposure. The problem is within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates, which is what differential follow-up by prognosis produces, and publications almost never report exposure-weighted covariate summaries. This is a property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood rather than of any one package: multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Why it is open
The integration over the aggregate covariate distribution uses reported unweighted moments while the Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, and sicker patients typically contribute less follow-up, which is exactly the association that breaks the zero-covariance requirement. The correct input, exposure-weighted covariate summaries, is essentially never published, and the current interface neither labels which weighting a supplied moment set represents nor models the weighting itself. There is no diagnostic that tells an analyst whether the omitted covariance is material for their contrast.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




multinma 0.8.0 NEWS, Poisson time-at-risk offset
fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset, so the same exposure-weighting requirement applies outside component models


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; computes each aggregate Poisson arm as total exposure times the mean modeled rate over unweighted covariate integration points, with no exposure-weighted moment interface and no joint exposure-covariate model

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Label the weighting convention in the interface, so an analyst who can obtain exposure-weighted covariate moments can supply them and make the existing likelihood correct, and request those summaries from data holders as a reporting item. Where only unweighted moments exist, model exposure and covariates jointly so the person-time weighting is generated by the model rather than assumed away. Add a sensitivity calculation for the magnitude of the exposure-rate covariance that would move a target contrast, since the severity is entirely conditional on that quantity.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “Poisson AgD likelihood assumes exposure independent of covariates” The title states independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition, but the audit showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate.
The source said. “The Poisson aggregate-data likelihood in component ML-NMR assumes exposure time is independent of covariates. When exposure depends on prognosis or on treatment, the exposure-weighted covariate moments that actually drive the rate differ from the unweighted moments reported in publications.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition and framed the issue as package-specific. GPT-5.6 Sol read the Poisson Stan code at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate, not independence, and that supplying exposure-weighted covariate summaries through the existing moment fields makes the same likelihood correct; the literature auditor noted the same requirement applies to multinma’s Poisson models, so this is field-level rather than a defect of one implementation.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm’s own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The statistical point is correct and non-trivial: a Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, published covariate moments are person-weighted, and the two coincide only under independence of exposure and covariates, which is exactly what differential follow-up by prognosis violates. I found no paper addressing exposure-weighted covariate moments in an aggregate-data integrated likelihood. Caveat for the editor: this is a field-level property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood, not a cpaic defect. multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset (its 0.8.0 NEWS records a bug fix to that offset), and the same independence assumption applies there, so framing it as ‘cpaic’s Poisson aggregate-data likelihood assumes…’ understates the reach of the problem. The claim that joint exposure and covariate models are not implemented in cpaic is a code fact I cannot verify from public sources.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm’s own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. cpaic man/cmlnmr.Rd and NEWS state that Poisson aggregate arms use E * mean(exp(eta)) over unweighted covariate integration points and assume exposure independent of covariates; there is no interface for exposure-weighted moments or a joint exposure–covariate model. Literature search for Poisson AgD ML-NMR with person-time depending on covariates did not surface an evaluated method that closes this for component ML-NMR. The statistical claim that exposure-weighted moments differ from unweighted moments under dependence is standard rate epidemiology, not a solved software gap. Queries: Poisson aggregate exposure covariate independent ML-NMR; cpaic poisson exposure; person-time weighted covariate moments NMA. All three claims remain supported; problem open.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text: CMP-18 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Statement
Component survival models place time-invariant component effects on the hazard, with flexible piecewise and M-spline baselines that vary the study-specific baseline hazard but do not create time-varying treatment or component effects. Combination-therapy components can produce delayed, waning, or crossing effects, and if two components have different time profiles the additive combination of their time-constant summaries has no clear correspondence to the combination’s actual hazard trajectory. Non-proportional hazards is not an open gap at the non-component level: multinma has supported it since 0.6.0 (2024-01-24) through aux_regression, which allows treatment and covariate effects on shape parameters and spline coefficients across a wide family of baseline hazards. Cure and multistate models are absent from both.

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Why it is open
Allowing time-varying component effects multiplies the parameters that must be assumed constant across subnetworks, so it worsens the untestable-constancy problem that makes the bridge work in the first place. The bridge itself becomes time-dependent when components have different time profiles, which means the cross-gap contrast has to be reported as a trajectory rather than a number. Decision-relevant summaries such as restricted mean survival time then depend on extrapolation beyond the observed follow-up, and cure and multistate structures that would discipline that extrapolation are not implemented in component or non-component ML-NMR.

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




multinma 0.6.0 (2024-01-24), aux_regression
implements non-proportional hazards in ML-NMR by allowing a regression model for auxiliary parameters (shape parameters and spline coefficients) across exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, log-normal, log-logistic, gamma, generalized gamma, M-spline, and piecewise-exponential baselines


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; provides piecewise and M-spline baseline hazards with time-invariant component effects and component-by-covariate interactions, and implements no time-varying-effect, cure, or multistate likelihood

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing auxiliary-parameter regression approach to component effects, so component-specific shape parameters and spline coefficients can carry delayed, waning, and crossing profiles, and state explicitly which of those parameters the bridge now requires to be constant across subnetworks. Make restricted mean survival time an estimand rather than a derived quantity, since it is the summary that survives non-proportionality. Cure and multistate component models are genuinely new work, absent from the non-component packages as well.

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Component survival models assume component effects that are proportional or constant over time. Combination-therapy components commonly produce delayed, waning, or crossing effects, so a single time-constant component parameter can misrepresent the whole survival experience.”
What was wrong with it. The source proposed building time-varying effects and flexible hazard models as though none existed. The literature auditor found that multinma 0.6.0’s aux_regression already implements non-proportional hazards for ML-NMR via regression on auxiliary parameters, so the gap is specific to component effects; GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 that piecewise and M-spline baselines give flexible baselines but not time-varying component effects, and declined to assess the word ‘commonly’.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The clinical premise (combination therapies show delayed, waning or crossing effects) is uncontroversial, and the structural point that time-varying component effects multiply the parameters requiring cross-subnetwork constancy is a good one I found nowhere else. But non-proportional hazards in population-adjusted synthesis is not an open gap at the non-component level: multinma added survival models in 0.6.0 (2024-01-24) with exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, log-normal, log-logistic, gamma, generalised gamma, M-spline and piecewise-exponential baselines, and its aux_regression argument allows treatment and covariate effects on shape parameters and spline coefficients, which is exactly a time-varying treatment effect. Phillippo et al. 2025 add that under effect modification marginal hazard ratios are intrinsically time-varying. So the entry should be scoped to component effects specifically. Cure and multistate models are indeed absent from multinma as well, so that sub-claim generalises beyond cpaic. Cites cran:multinma 0.6.0 (2024-01-24), aux_regression argument: Non-proportional hazards in ML-NMR are implemented via regression on auxiliary parameters (shape parameters and spline coefficients) across a wide family of baseline hazards; not available for component effects..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1, C3, and C4 are supported. cpaic records proportional hazards as a survival assumption, and the Stan survival linear predictor contains time-invariant component effects and component-by-covariate interactions. Piecewise and M-spline baselines allow flexible study-specific baseline hazards but do not create time-varying treatment or component effects. No time-varying-effect, cure, or multistate likelihood is implemented. C2 is technically correct: delayed, waning, or crossing effects can violate this structure. The empirical word ‘commonly’ was not assessed, and ‘very high’ severity is conditional on material non-proportionality and on the decision estimand; it is not an automatic defect in every survival analysis.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Treatment-level non-proportional hazards NMA/ML-NMR advanced in 2025 (Phillippo et al., arXiv:2509.10383; multinma M-spline NPH, treatment effects on spline coefficients or stratification). That closes part of the survival-NMA NPH agenda but not the stated component-PAIC problem: additive time-constant component effects on the hazard, with delayed/waning/crossing combination profiles, plus cure and multistate components in cpaic. cpaic 0.1.0 still documents piecewise/M-spline baselines with time-constant component effects and proportional hazards for survival. No time-varying component-effect, cure, or multistate implementation in cpaic or a component ML-NMR package was found. Queries: Phillippo 2025 M-spline NPH; cpaic proportional hazards; time-varying component NMA survival; cure multistate component NMA. Claims C1–C4 about cpaic remain accurate; adjacent treatment-level NPH software does not make the component problem solved.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text: CMP-16 Unverifiable High priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Statement
cpaic, an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, declares at most one between-study heterogeneity parameter tau when random effects are requested and applies it to all study-arm deviations, with no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity. Its Gaussian component ML-NMR likelihood uses one residual sigma across all IPD rows, although aggregate arms use their own supplied standard errors and the two-stage routes fit study-specific regressions, so the shared residual scale is narrower than stated. A common tau is also the near-universal default in netmeta and multinma, so this is a field-level convention rather than a package idiosyncrasy.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Why it is open
A single tau borrows strength across parts of a network that may not be exchangeable, so a heterogeneous subnetwork can inflate uncertainty in a homogeneous one and vice versa, and in a disconnected network that directly changes how much support the bridge appears to have. Forcing one residual scale across IPD studies that differ in instruments, populations, and follow-up transfers weight between studies and makes model-based intervals wrong even where the mean model is right. Allowing structured heterogeneity or study-specific scales immediately runs into identifiability, because sparse disconnected networks rarely have enough studies per stratum to estimate several variance components, so shrinkage is needed and prior dependence returns.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; every Stan family declares at most one tau applied to all study-arm deviations, and the Gaussian likelihood uses one residual sigma across IPD rows while aggregate arms use supplied standard errors

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Allow heterogeneity structured by component, component class, or subnetwork with shrinkage across strata, and add identifiability checks that flag a variance component driven entirely by its prior, since that is the binding constraint in sparse networks. Support study-specific or hierarchically shrunk residual scales for the IPD likelihood and robust residual distributions so heavy tails and unequal precision do not distort weighting. Report the diagnostic separately from the correction, so an analyst can see whether stratum-specific heterogeneity is supported before fitting it.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “cpaic assumes a single heterogeneity and residual variance” The title implies an installable package and a single residual variance across all studies, but cpaic is a GitHub development package and the shared sigma covers IPD rows only.
The source said. “cpaic’s models assume one common between-study heterogeneity parameter across the network and, for continuous outcomes, one Gaussian residual standard deviation shared across all studies. Different component classes or subnetworks may plausibly have different heterogeneity, and unequal true residual variances distort study precision and network weighting.”
What was wrong with it. The source said the single residual standard deviation is shared across all studies and that it biases both the point estimate and its interval. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and narrowed both: the shared sigma covers IPD rows only, since aggregate arms use supplied se_agd and the two-stage routes fit study-specific regressions, and residual heteroskedasticity misallocates precision and invalidates model-based uncertainty without by itself implying biased mean-effect coefficients under a correct conditional mean model. The literature auditor added that a common tau is the standard default in netmeta and multinma too.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): When random effects are requested, C1-C3 are supported for cML-NMR: every Stan family declares at most one tau and applies tau[1] to all study-arm deviations; no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity scale exists. C4 and C6 require qualification. The Gaussian cML-NMR likelihood has one sigma across all IPD observations, but aggregate arms use their separately supplied se_agd values, and cMAIC/cSTC fit study-specific regressions rather than sharing this sigma. Unequal IPD residual variances do misrepresent relative precision, efficient weighting, and model-based uncertainty. However, heteroskedasticity alone does not imply biased mean-effect coefficients when the conditional mean model is correct, contrary to the report’s narrative. The priority is conditional on material variance or heterogeneity differences and the amount of evidence each affected stratum contributes.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. Every claim here is about cpaic’s internals (single heterogeneity parameter, single residual standard deviation, absence of structured or study-specific scales). cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository, so I have nothing to read and this belongs to the source-code auditor. On the literature side the statistical assertions are textbook and safe: a common tau borrows strength across possibly non-exchangeable parts of a network, and forcing a common residual variance misallocates precision weights. I did not retrieve a specific paper on comparison-specific or class-specific heterogeneity variances in network meta-analysis in this session, so I will not cite one; note only that a common tau is the near-universal default in netmeta and multinma too, so this is a field-level convention rather than a cpaic idiosyncrasy, and the entry would be stronger if it said so. The identifiability tension the entry raises (too few studies per stratum in sparse disconnected networks) is genuine and, as far as I found, unaddressed.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. When random effects are requested, C1-C3 are supported for cML-NMR: every Stan family declares at most one tau and applies tau[1] to all study-arm deviations; no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity scale exists. C4 and C6 require qualification. The Gaussian cML-NMR likelihood has one sigma across all IPD observations, but aggregate arms use their separately supplied se_agd values, and cMAIC/cSTC fit study-specific regressions rather than sharing this sigma. Unequal IPD residual variances do misrepresent relative precision, efficient weighting, and model-based uncertainty. However, heteroskedasticity alone does not imply biased mean-effect coefficients when the conditional mean model is correct, contrary to the report’s narrative. The priority is conditional on material variance or heterogeneity differences and the amount of evidence each affected stratum contributes.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. cpaic 0.1.0 (README, cmlnmr Rd, NEWS) still fits one common tau and one network-wide Gaussian residual sigma; no component-class, subnetwork, or study-specific residual hierarchy is implemented. Broader NMA has class-effect and hierarchical heterogeneity models (e.g. class-effects NMA practice literature), but those are not component-PAIC residual or component-structured tau models and do not close the stated cpaic gap. No CRAN/GitHub change in multinma/maicplus/netmeta/cpaic was found that adds study-specific residual scales inside component ML-NMR. Queries: cpaic tau sigma; multinma study-specific residual; structured heterogeneity component NMA 2024–2026; class-effects NMA residual variance. Claims C1–C6 are faithful software/limitation statements; the methodological problem remains open as stated.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text: CMP-14 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Statement
Interaction parameters informed only by aggregate data can be regularized into finite posterior intervals by the prior, so a proper credible interval is not evidence that the likelihood contributed anything. Implemented component PAIC already ships partial mitigation: plot_prior_posterior() compares each prior with its posterior, prior_sensitivity() quantifies how far target contrasts move when priors are tightened or loosened, and estimable_effects_at() separates no first-order information from IPD-supported and aggregate-only information. What is missing is a default numerical summary: prior-to-posterior contraction per interaction parameter and an effective likelihood rank, reported without the analyst having to ask.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Why it is open
A proper prior yields a proper posterior under ordinary integrability conditions, so the usual output gives no signal that the likelihood contributed nothing, and the parameters where this bites hardest are exactly the weakly identified interaction terms that a bridged component model depends on. The existing diagnostics are visual or require a deliberate refit, so an analyst who does not run them sees a clean interval with no warning attached. Prior-to-posterior contraction and effective likelihood rank are the summaries that would make this visible by default, and neither is computed.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; records prior specifications, provides plot_prior_posterior(), prior_sensitivity(), and estimable_effects_at(), documents that weakly identified interaction parameters are regularized by priors, and reports no numerical prior-to-posterior contraction or effective likelihood rank

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Promote the existing prior-versus-posterior comparison and prior-sensitivity refit from optional diagnostics to default reported output, and add numerical prior-to-posterior contraction for every interaction parameter plus an effective likelihood rank for the fitted model. Attach to each reported interaction the label of whether it is identified by IPD, by aggregate arms, or by neither, which the estimability screen already computes. Calibrate these summaries specifically to interaction parameters in a bridged component model, since the generic Bayesian workflow versions are already standard.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Interaction parameters informed only by aggregate data can be regularized into finite posterior intervals by the prior rather than by the likelihood. A finite credible interval may therefore reflect the prior rather than information in the data.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no diagnostic in standard output separates prior-driven from likelihood-driven interaction estimates. GPT-5.6 Sol found three at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 (plot_prior_posterior(), prior_sensitivity(), estimable_effects_at()), so the gap narrows to their being optional rather than default and to the absence of numerical contraction and likelihood-rank summaries; it also corrected the wording, since a prior regularizes a posterior but never makes the likelihood identify a parameter.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The statistical content is uncontroversial Bayesian bookkeeping: a proper prior always yields a proper posterior, so a finite credible interval is not evidence of likelihood information. I found no paper offering a routine prior-versus-likelihood diagnostic for effect-modifier interactions in ML-NMR or CNMA, and no source asserting that absence, so the ‘no diagnostic in standard output’ claims are unverifiable rather than established. Two caveats for the editor. The generic remedies named (prior-to-posterior contraction, prior predictive checks, prior sensitivity) are standard Bayesian workflow rather than a research gap, so the novel part is specifically calibrating them to interaction parameters in a bridged component model. And the claim about what cpaic’s documentation recognises cannot be checked: cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository. Confidence is capped because I read no text bearing directly on this entry.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C2-C4 are supported: a proper posterior interval can be dominated by prior regularization, cpaic has no numerical prior-to-posterior contraction table or effective-likelihood-rank report, and its documentation explicitly recognizes prior regularization of weakly identified Gamma. C1 should say prior-regularized or prior-driven posterior rather than likelihood identification: a prior does not make the likelihood identify a parameter. Proper-prior/proper-posterior language also requires ordinary posterior-integrability conditions rather than holding as an unrestricted theorem. The report understates existing mitigation: plot_prior_posterior() directly compares each prior and posterior, prior_sensitivity() quantifies contrast movement under changed priors, and estimable_effects_at() distinguishes IPD, aggregate, and absent first-order information. These are optional rather than default numerical contraction or likelihood-rank summaries, so the remaining work is useful but is a diagnostic-roadmap item, not automatically a very-high-severity correctness failure. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Provides a direct visual diagnostic for a posterior that merely reproduces its prior.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Quantifies whether target contrasts move when interaction or component priors are tightened or loosened.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Separates no first-order information from IPD-supported and aggregate-only information before interpreting posterior contrasts..

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text: CMP-12 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Statement
When a multi-arm trial’s contrasts are population-adjusted one at a time, the within-study covariance induced by a shared arm and a shared weighting step is not recovered by naive variance formulas, so standard errors and network precision would be wrong. Current implementations avoid the error by refusing the capability rather than by solving it: both the component MAIC and component STC routes reject IPD studies with more than two arms, so multi-arm IPD trials must be split or dropped. The covariance is handled natively on the synthesis side of frequentist CNMA and in the one-stage ML-NMR likelihood, which keeps multi-arm trials inside a single arm-level model; what is missing is a two-stage adjusted estimator that carries it, and any multi-arm handling in component PAIC.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Why it is open
Population adjustment reweights or re-fits per contrast, and a two-stage route that processes one contrast at a time has no natural place to carry the induced correlation, so multi-arm studies must be split, which double counts the shared arm, or dropped, which discards evidence. A stratified bootstrap could recover the covariance only if replicates are carried jointly across a trial’s contrasts rather than per contrast, which requires multivariate estimating equations or an arm-level likelihood and therefore changes the two-stage architecture. Until then the practical cost is lost evidence rather than wrong intervals.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020
handles multi-arm trials natively within a one-stage arm-level NMA likelihood, so the within-study covariance is never discarded


Petropoulou et al. 2023
records that multi-arm study weights are adjusted in the netmeta CNMA machinery, showing the covariance loss is introduced by the adjustment stage rather than by component modeling


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; re-estimates weights and outcome models in arm-stratified bootstrap replicates, fails closed when too few replicates succeed, and rejects IPD studies with more than two arms in both cmaic() and cstc()

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use a multivariate bootstrap or stacked estimating equations that carry all of a trial’s contrasts jointly, so the two-stage route can accept multi-arm IPD studies with the correct correlation structure. Alternatively move to a one-stage arm-level component likelihood, where the full contrast covariance is produced by the model rather than reconstructed afterwards, which is how the non-component version already handles multi-arm trials. Either way the fix should lift the current two-arm restriction rather than adding a variance correction on top of it.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Two-stage adjustment loses multi-arm within-study covariance” The title asserts the covariance is lost in practice, but the audit found both component routes reject multi-arm IPD studies outright, so it is a refused capability rather than a wrong-standard-error defect.
The source said. “When a multi-arm trial’s contrasts are population-adjusted one at a time in a two-stage workflow, the within-study covariance among those contrasts can be lost or misstated, so standard errors and network precision can be wrong. The same limitation appears as a hard restriction in the cSTC route, which accepts only two-arm IPD studies.”
What was wrong with it. The source implied that adjusted multi-arm contrasts are emitted with lost covariance. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and found both cmaic() and cstc() reject IPD studies with more than two arms, so this is a refused capability rather than a current wrong-standard-error defect; the literature auditor added that the one-stage fix is published and implemented for non-component networks (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579) and that netmeta’s CNMA machinery already adjusts multi-arm weights.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I found no paper that recovers within-study covariance among multi-arm contrasts after two-stage population adjustment, so that specific gap is real. Two qualifications. First, the multi-arm covariance problem is already solved on the synthesis side of CNMA: Petropoulou et al. 2023 record that in the netmeta CNMA machinery ‘For multi-arm studies, the weights are assumed to be adjusted as described in [Rucker and Schwarzer]’, so the loss is introduced by the adjustment stage, not by component modelling. Second, the one-stage alternative avoids the problem entirely: ML-NMR keeps multi-arm trials inside a single arm-level likelihood, and Phillippo et al. 2020 give the limitation of the two-stage route as a motivation for it. So the practical need is met for non-component networks; what is open is a two-stage estimator that carries the covariance, and any multi-arm handling in a component PAIC. The claim that cSTC accepts only two-arm IPD studies is a code fact I cannot check. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Handles multi-arm trials natively within a one-stage NMA likelihood, so the covariance is never discarded; does not solve the two-stage or component case..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1, C2, and C6 are correct for a workflow that estimates several shared-arm contrasts separately and passes only their marginal variances onward. C3 and C4 are source-confirmed: cMAIC jointly re-estimates weights and its arm-only outcome model within arm-stratified bootstrap replicates, fails closed below the success threshold, and both cMAIC and cSTC reject IPD studies with more than two arms. Consequently, current cpaic does not silently emit multi-arm adjusted contrasts with incorrect covariance; it avoids the error by refusing that capability. Joint multi-arm adjustment remains an open feature, but this is a roadmap limitation rather than a current wrong-standard-error defect. C5 is an empirical prevalence claim outside the assigned lens and was not assessed. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Propagates weight and outcome-model uncertainty for supported two-arm studies and refuses unsupported multi-arm IPD rather than discarding covariance silently.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Prevents cSTC from producing a falsely independent set of adjusted multi-arm contrasts..

title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text: CMP-10 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text:
Statement
No component-additive PAIC produces target-standardized arm outcomes or marginal contrasts. ML-NMR already does this for non-component networks: multinma has provided marginal_effects() since 0.7.0 (2024-05-07), which standardizes absolute predictions over a target population’s covariate distribution and contrasts them, including hazard, survival probability, median survival, and RMST contrasts, and Phillippo et al. 2025 state that ML-NMR is currently the only population-adjustment method producing both conditional and marginal estimates in any decision target population. Once treatment effects are decomposed into components, no equivalent path exists: component STC centers modifiers at supplied target means and reports the treatment coefficient, and component ML-NMR returns a conditional linear-predictor contrast at one covariate profile. Evaluating a component regression at target covariate means is exact only under an identity link and linearity in covariates, so it is not a substitute.

title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text:
Why it is open
The correct operation is g-computation or posterior standardization, integrating the fitted model over the whole target covariate distribution for every posterior draw, which requires that distribution rather than only its means and therefore inherits the target-reconstruction problem and its uncertainty. The proposed arm-mean formula also requires an identified or externally supplied target baseline alpha*, which study-specific intercepts do not provide. Because the choice between conditional and standardized output changes the reported number, this is an estimand decision rather than a presentation preference, and decision modelers currently apply conditional component coefficients to marginal baselines, which is incoherent on non-collapsible scales.

Propagate uncertainty from model parameters and, where the target distribution is estimated or reconstructed rather than fixed, from that reconstruction as well, and retain conditional component effects as model parameters rather than as the policy estimand.

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text: CMP-08 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Statement
For linear observed-contrast models, target estimability is characterized exactly by row-space membership of the target-specific contrast vector v(m,x) = (1, x’) Kronecker m with m = C_t - C_u. Implemented component PAIC applies an augmented target-dependent row-space diagnostic that is exact for specified non-survival IPD regressions and only a first-order design screen for aggregate-data and survival likelihoods, and it labels which verdict is which. Once a nonlinear inverse link is integrated over a covariate distribution, no published conditions characterize local or global identification by outcome family and integration structure, so a target functional can pass the screen and still be unidentified.

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Why it is open
Once the inverse link is nonlinear and integrated over a covariate distribution, the map from parameters to the observed-data distribution is not linear in the parameters, so a design-based row-space criterion no longer characterizes identification. Deriving conditions requires analyzing the observed-data information of an integrated aggregate likelihood, which depends on the outcome family, the covariate distribution, and the integration scheme, so results must be stated case by case rather than once. The complementary numerical diagnostics that would substitute in the interim, singular values of the observed-information matrix and likelihood or posterior profiles for a requested contrast, are not computed by any component PAIC implementation the auditors read.

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Probable solution or research direction
A methodological paper should derive local and global identification conditions for nonlinear component ML-NMR by outcome family and integration structure, since that is the part with no results. In the interim, supplement the row-space screen with Jacobian and Fisher-information rank diagnostics, observed-information singular values, and likelihood or posterior profiles for each requested target contrast, together with prior-data conflict diagnostics that detect when the prior rather than the data supplies the answer. The precedent for the design-level screens already exists in frequentist CNMA, where an algorithm identifies inestimable interactions so that only estimable ones enter interaction models.

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text: CMP-06 Confirmed open High priority Emerging

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Statement
Component PAIC as implemented takes covariates as observed values with no calibration or latent measurement-error model, and derives the component matrix by deterministically parsing treatment labels with no probability model for component assignment. Because a bridge exists exactly when two subnetworks share a component, a coding error can change the design matrix, its rank, and its row space, and so can create or remove shared-component paths rather than merely perturbing a coefficient. Not every miscoding changes connectivity, and measurement error in a variable that is not an effect modifier need not bias the estimand, so the concern is conditional on which covariate or component is uncertain.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Why it is open
Component coding is currently a deterministic analyst decision with no uncertainty attached, so the network topology is treated as known when it is inferred from trial reports. Covariate measurement error additionally biases the weighting step and attenuates the interaction terms that carry effect modification, and the direction depends on the unknown error structure, so a post hoc correction has nothing to key on. The mature general machinery for this problem, regression calibration, SIMEX, and Bayesian measurement-error and misclassification models, has not been applied to population-adjusted or component synthesis in any work the auditors could retrieve.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Introduce probabilistic component coding so that assignment uncertainty propagates into the design matrix, the row space, and therefore the estimand, and report how often the cross-gap contrast becomes non-estimable under plausible codings. Add covariate calibration models for effect modifiers using existing measurement-error machinery, prioritizing the modifiers that actually load the requested contrast. Because the concern is conditional, the first deliverable is a diagnostic that identifies which coding and measurement uncertainties would matter for a given target contrast.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Component methods ignore measurement error in covariates and misclassification in how interventions are coded into components. Component misclassification can create an apparent bridge between subnetworks where none exists, or destroy a real one.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated the absence at field level and implied any miscoding changes the bridge. GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed the absence at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 but scoped it to that package, and qualified the mechanism: not every miscoding changes connectivity, and measurement error does not bias every estimand; the literature auditor searched and found no measurement-error or misclassification method for MAIC, STC, ML-NMR, or CNMA and no source asserting the absence, so recorded it as unverifiable at field level.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. I searched PubMed and the web for measurement error or misclassification methods in MAIC, STC, ML-NMR or CNMA and found nothing that models covariate measurement error in the weighting step or treats component coding probabilistically. The general statistical machinery (regression calibration, SIMEX, Bayesian measurement-error models, misclassification priors) is of course mature, but I retrieved no application to population-adjusted or component synthesis, so I cannot supply a locator. The claim is a ‘no method exists’ claim and no source I found asserts the absence, so per calibration it is unverifiable rather than supported. The substantive observation that misclassifying a component changes network topology rather than a coefficient is a genuine and, as far as I can tell, unpublished point; it is the strongest part of the entry. Entry has no prior_work at all, which is a presentation weakness rather than a factual error.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 is source-confirmed at 9d150e9. Covariates enter cMAIC, cSTC, and cML-NMR as observed values without a calibration or latent measurement-error model, while build_C_matrix() deterministically parses the supplied labels with no probability model for component assignment. C2 is correct: changing a component assignment changes C and can consequently create or remove shared-component paths, alter rank, or change the row space, although not every miscoding changes connectivity. The cpaic-specific part of C3 is supported; the claim about every existing component NMA/PAIC package is outside this audit. Measurement error is not guaranteed to bias every estimand, for example when the mismeasured variable is not an effect modifier, but it can attenuate interaction estimates, leave true imbalance after weighting, and invalidate transport. This is decision-critical when coding or modifier measurement is genuinely uncertain; for carefully curated, effectively error-free inputs it is a lower-priority roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Searched for probabilistic component coding, misclassification models that randomize the CNMA design/combination matrix, and covariate measurement-error correction inside component NMA/PAIC. General measurement-error and exposure-misclassification methods exist for meta-analysis and IPD (e.g., Jrsm work on misclassification adjustment), but none were found that (a) treat component assignment as uncertain topology or (b) ship in netmeta, multinma, gemtc, MBNMAdose, or a public cpaic. Queries: ‘component network meta-analysis misclassification’, ‘probabilistic component coding NMA’, ‘measurement error effect modifiers PAIC CNMA’, plus 2024–2026 journal and package scans. No merged PR or CRAN release notes close this gap. C1–C3 therefore remain open as stated; confidence is moderate because absence-of-evidence for a niche software feature is harder to prove exhaustively than a positive locator.
