title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text: CMP-04 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Statement
Forward selection of component and interaction structures, as implemented in the netmeta CNMA workflow, makes a sequence of data-driven decisions whose uncertainty is not carried into the reported intervals. Petropoulou et al. 2023 measured the failure in disconnected networks: forward selection recovered the correct interaction model in only 12.0 to 15.2 percent of runs under mild additivity violation and 21.6 to 26.3 percent under strong violation, and tended to select sparse, often additive, models even when additivity was violated. In connected networks the measured coverage penalty was modest. Where an analyst selects a structure externally and then reports intervals conditional on it, those intervals omit selection uncertainty and are optimistic.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Why it is open
Post-selection intervals condition on the selected structure and ignore the sequence of decisions that produced it, so they are too narrow and the chosen structure is unstable under resampling. In a disconnected network the candidate structures are also poorly separated by the data, because the contrasts that would discriminate between them are the ones spanning the gap, so selection instability translates into instability of the bridge rather than of nuisance terms. No selection-aware inference has been developed for component structures, and the auditors found no application of projection predictive inference or stacking to CNMA additivity structures.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023
evaluates forward CNMA model selection in 1000 simulated connected and disconnected networks and quantifies its failure in the disconnected case


netmeta
supplies the frequentist component NMA machinery, including the forward-selection routine whose uncertainty is not propagated

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Replace forward selection with shrinkage priors, projection predictive inference, or stacking across candidate additivity structures, and report selection-aware uncertainty so the reported interval includes the cost of having chosen a structure from the data. Because the failure is documented specifically for disconnected networks, the first target should be selection-aware inference for the cross-gap contrast rather than for the whole network fit. Where selection is done outside the fitting package, the resulting intervals should be labeled as conditional on the chosen component coding.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Selecting which components and which interactions enter the additive model by forward selection inflates optimism and can fail outright in sparse disconnected graphs. The uncertainty introduced by the selection step is not carried into the reported intervals.”
What was wrong with it. The source attributed the selection step to cpaic. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and found no forward, stepwise, projection-predictive, or stacking routine there: the package builds a fixed binary component matrix from the supplied treatment labels, so there is no in-package selection whose uncertainty could be propagated, and the problem belongs to the analyst’s upstream choice and to netmeta’s forward-selection workflow; the literature auditor supplied the missing source and the measured failure rates, doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The entry cites only ‘netmeta’ but the claim has a direct published evidence base it does not cite: Petropoulou, Rucker, Weibel, Kranke, Schwarzer 2023 evaluated the forward CNMA selection strategy in 1000 simulated connected and disconnected networks. Their disconnected-network result is stronger than the entry’s: forward selection recovered the correct interaction model in only 12.0-15.2 percent (mild violation) and 21.6-26.3 percent (strong violation) of runs, and ‘Forward selection tended to select sparse (often additive) CNMA models for disconnected networks even if additivity was mildly or strongly violated.’ So ‘can fail in sparse disconnected graphs’ is established, not conjectural. Caveat on ‘inflates optimism’: in CONNECTED networks the measured penalty was modest - coverage for the selected CNMA fell outside Monte-Carlo limits only at moderate heterogeneity, and per-comparison coverage was ‘somewhat smaller … however, not dramatically different’. Selection-uncertainty propagation is still unsolved, so the problem stands. ‘Projection predictive inference and stacking have not been applied to component NMA’ - I found no counterexample, but absence is unverifiable. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Establishes empirically (not fixes) that forward CNMA selection fails in disconnected networks; the missing citation for this entry’s central claim..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

not-a-problem / misattributed. C1 is generally correct: naive inference after forward selection is optimistic and conditions on the selected structure. C2 is also possible when candidate component models are rank-deficient, saturated, or numerically unstable. The attribution to current cpaic in C3 is wrong, however. At 9d150e9, cpaic deterministically constructs a binary C matrix from the supplied treatment labels and fits that fixed structure; NAMESPACE and the R sources contain no forward, stepwise, projection-predictive, stacking, or component-structure selection routine. There is therefore no package selection step whose uncertainty cpaic intervals could propagate. If an analyst performs external selection first, the resulting cpaic intervals are conditional on that externally chosen coding, but that is a different and conditional problem. C4 is a literature-coverage claim outside the assigned lens.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. The main prior-art hit is Petropoulou et al. 2023 (and the related netmeta forward-selection machinery), which evaluates forward selection of CNMA structures and finds poor selection of the correct interaction structure under mild additivity violation, degraded performance with heterogeneity, and bad performance when the network is disconnected. That paper characterizes instability; it does not replace forward selection with selection-aware intervals, projection predictive inference, or stacking for component structures. netmeta still exposes netcomb/discomb and selection utilities without post-selection inference for the bridge. Searches for projpred, stacking, or Bayesian model averaging applied to CNMA additivity structure (RSM/SIM/BMC MRM 2023–2026, arXiv, CRAN) found no applied work. Claims C1–C2 are supported by that simulation evidence; C3 is consistent with netmeta/cpaic not advertising selection-aware intervals; C4 remains true as a gap. Status stays open: the problem is documented, not solved.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=1)

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text: CMP-02 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Statement
Once population adjustment is added to a component bridge, cross-subnetwork constancy is required for the interaction projection that loads the requested contrast, not only for component main effects: for a target profile x, the quantity (C_t - C_u)’ Gamma x must be stable in addition to the corresponding main-effect projection. The assumption count grows with adjusted covariates but is smaller than the number of interaction terms, because zero target values, zero component loadings, and interactions supported by covariate variation in two subnetworks all reduce it. The combined assumption set is strictly stronger than main-effect constancy only when a nonzero relevant interaction is present. Phillippo et al. 2022 show that in a connected network the shared-effect-modifier assumption can be examined and relaxed one covariate at a time; that machinery has no analogue across a disconnection.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Why it is open
Interaction parameters are estimated from less information than the corresponding main effects, so requiring the target-relevant projection of them to be stable across a gap that carries no evidence compounds an already weak identification problem. Component cML-NMR as implemented uses a single shared interaction matrix with no subnetwork index and no hierarchical alternative, so a drifting interaction has nowhere to go except into the shared parameter. No published diagnostic distinguishes a genuinely shared interaction from one whose apparent stability is an artifact of shrinkage or of limited covariate range within each subnetwork, and no target-specific interaction-drift tipping surface exists in any component PAIC software found by the auditors.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2022
assesses and relaxes the shared effect modifier assumption one covariate at a time in a connected ML-NMR network; no analogue exists across a disconnection


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; fits one global component-by-modifier interaction matrix shared across all subnetworks in cML-NMR, with no subnetwork-specific drift and no interaction tipping surfaces

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Fit hierarchical subnetwork-specific interaction matrices Gamma_s that shrink toward a common value rather than being forced equal, with reference or zero-mean constraints so Gamma and the drift blocks are separately defined. Add interaction-drift sensitivity expressed on the projection that loads the requested contrast, with target-specific tipping surfaces showing which covariate values make the conclusion fragile. Report, for each requested contrast, which interaction directions are supported by covariate variation in more than one subnetwork, since those are the only ones with any cross-gap evidence.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Component-by-modifier constancy is a strictly stronger assumption” The title asserts the assumption is strictly stronger unconditionally, but the audit restricted that to cases where a nonzero relevant interaction is present.
The source said. “Once population adjustment is added to a component bridge, cross-subnetwork constancy is needed not only for component main effects but for every relevant component-by-effect-modifier interaction, so the untestable surface grows with the number of adjusted covariates. Component ML-NMR therefore stacks CNMA assumptions on top of transportability, an integration distribution, and stable component-by-modifier interactions.”
What was wrong with it. The source said every component-by-modifier interaction must be constant and that disconnection makes each one unverifiable. GPT-5.6 Sol restricted this to the interaction projection (C_t - C_u)’ Gamma x that loads the requested target, noted that interactions supported by covariate variation in two subnetworks can be compared, and confirmed at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 that the package fits one global gamma[C,Q] with no subnetwork index; the literature auditor added Phillippo et al. 2022 (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), which shows the connected-network analogue is assessable.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I searched PubMed, arXiv and the netmeta/multinma literature for any published component + population-adjustment model; the closest published object is Rucker/Schmitz/Schwarzer 2021, which compares CNMA against a matching method but does not fit component-by-modifier interactions. I found no paper that formalises or tests cross-subnetwork constancy of interaction matrices, so the problem is open. The core claim (‘interaction constancy is strictly stronger than main-effect constancy’) is a logical containment, not an empirical finding, and is defensible as stated. Supporting context the entry omits: Phillippo et al. 2022 (Med Decis Making) report that in a CONNECTED network the shared-effect-modifier assumption can be assessed and relaxed one covariate at a time (‘A shared effect modifier assumption may also be necessary for identifiability’; they ‘relax the shared effect modifier assumption for each covariate in turn’). That machinery has no analogue across a disconnection, which strengthens rather than weakens the entry. The claims naming cpaic’s internals are unverifiable from literature: cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162: Does NOT solve it. Supplies the missing citation showing shared-effect-modifier assumptions ARE assessable in connected networks, sharpening the claim that they are not across a gap..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. At choxos/cpaic@9d150e9, C5 is source-confirmed: .cpaic_fixed_design() creates one global component-by-modifier block, and each Stan model has one matrix gamma[C,Q] with no subnetwork index or hierarchical gamma_s. Interaction-drift tipping surfaces are absent, and bridge_fragility() expressly excludes Lambda, supporting the cpaic-specific part of C6. C9 and C10 are also correct: reported effects are conditional contrasts (C_t-C_u)’(beta+Gamma x), while aggregate likelihoods integrate over study covariate distributions. C1-C4 and C11 nevertheless need rank and estimand qualifications. Only the projection (C_t-C_u)’Lambda_s x relevant to the requested target must be stable; zero target values, zero component loadings, and estimable linear combinations reduce the assumption count. Interactions supported by covariate variation in multiple subnetworks can be compared, so disconnection does not make every interaction unverifiable. The combined main-effect-plus-interaction assumption set is strictly stronger only when a nonzero relevant interaction is introduced. For C8, the integration distribution is required for aggregate-study likelihood construction, but cpaic has no marginal target-standardization path and needs only a covariate profile for its reported target contrast. Software-wide nonexistence in C6 is outside this audit.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Sought component-by-effect-modifier interactions that vary by subnetwork, hierarchical Gamma_s, interaction-drift tipping surfaces, or component ML-NMR software beyond a shared interaction matrix. Public search found no CRAN package named cpaic (404 on cran.r-project.org/package=cpaic) and no published component-ML-NMR with hierarchical subnetwork-specific interaction matrices or target-specific interaction-drift fragility tools. Multinma and related PAIC/ML-NMR work address population adjustment for whole treatments, not the stacked CNMA-plus-modifier-constancy surface described here. Veroniki et al. 2026 and Rücker et al. 2020 discuss interaction CNMA for component–component terms, not component-by-covariate constancy across a disconnection. Queries covering Research Synthesis Methods, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv, and package ecosystems (multinma, maicplus, netmeta, gemtc, MBNMAdose, crossnma) through 2026 returned no evaluation that identifies or bounds Lambda^(s) from disconnected evidence. Claims that population adjustment multiplies untestable cross-gap stability assumptions (C1–C4, C8–C11) remain faithful; software claims about cpaic (C5–C6) are consistent with the absence of a public package implementing hierarchical interaction drift, but cpaic itself was not independently retrievable. Interaction-drift fragility (C7) is still only a proposal.

Decision path

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text: ADJ-20 Confirmed open Medium priority Speculative

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Statement
No method exists for indirectly comparing dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences across studies. The estimand, however, is definable: a policy contrast is the target-population difference between the values of two well-specified policies, so what is missing is cross-study identification and data rather than the definition. Identification requires compatible policies, treatment histories and outcomes, plus consistency, positivity, suitable sequential randomization or exchangeability, and transportability; longitudinal histories are generally needed, though sequentially randomized designs carry different confounding assumptions and sufficiently detailed regime-level estimates could sometimes support a second-stage synthesis.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Why it is open
Sequential decision estimands generally require longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounder data at the individual level, which trial publications and most shared individual data do not contain. Existing network structures encode fixed-regimen contrasts, so a policy contrast cannot simply be attached to them; prespecified policies could in principle enter as network nodes, but only once the transport and sequential exchangeability conditions are checked, and no convention exists for doing so. Reinforcement learning supplies neither identification nor the missing data.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
What has been tried
No prior work is identified for this problem in the reviewed sources.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Treat sequential-regime comparison as a long-term program that starts from the policy-value contrast rather than from a new definition: specify which policies are being contrasted, in which population, and what compatibility across trials would require. Then specify the longitudinal treatment and confounder data such a comparison needs, and test whether prespecified policies can enter existing network structures as nodes before building bespoke estimators.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Reinforcement learning and dynamic treatment regime methods are proposed for comparing adaptive treatment sequences rather than fixed regimens across studies. The report labels this long-term research.”
What was wrong with it. The source said what an indirect comparison of two adaptive strategies even means has not been defined. GPT-5.6 Sol showed the estimand is already definable as a contrast of policy values in a target population, so the open work is cross-study identification, data and convention rather than the definition itself.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no method for indirectly comparing dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences across studies, and no definition of what such an estimand would be in an evidence network. Treatment sequences are modeled in HTA cost-effectiveness models, and dynamic treatment regimes are a mature single-study literature, but the two have not been joined for indirect comparison in anything I retrieved. The entry’s diagnosis is correct on both counts I could check: sequential-regime estimands require longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounder data at the individual level, which trial publications do not contain, and the target of inference changes from a fixed-regimen contrast to a policy over time, so it cannot be attached to existing network structures. This is a negative search result rather than a positive finding, so confidence is moderate; but the claim being made here is weak and well hedged, which is the right posture for a ‘long-term research’ item.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C3, and C4 are supportable in qualified form. A policy contrast is already mathematically definable, for example as the target-population difference between V(pi1)=E[Y under pi1] and V(pi2)=E[Y under pi2]. The assertion that the target of inference has not been defined is therefore false as a general statement. Cross-study identification requires well-defined and compatible policies, treatment histories and outcomes, consistency, positivity, appropriate sequential randomization or exchangeability conditions, and transportability. C2 is also too absolute: longitudinal histories are generally needed for primary estimation, but sequentially randomized designs require different confounding assumptions, and sufficiently detailed regime-level estimates may sometimes support a second-stage synthesis. Existing network machinery could treat prespecified policies as treatment nodes when those conditions hold, although this would not be ordinary fixed-regimen ITC. Reinforcement learning supplies neither identification nor missing data. General PAIC methods remain a legitimate long-term research program, not a current decision-grade requirement.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No cited prior_work. Dynamic treatment regimes and clinical RL are large mature fields for single-source longitudinal IPD (reviews through 2025 on RL for DTRs in healthcare), but they do not define or implement an indirect comparison of adaptive policies across trials that publish only fixed-regimen contrasts and sparse IPD. Search for network meta-analysis / indirect comparison of dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences found no standard estimand definition, required data structure for multi-study sequential comparison, or software path that reuses existing NMA graphs for policy-vs-policy contrasts. C1 remains a long-horizon possibility. C2–C3 correctly state that sequential-regime comparison needs longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounders and is not ordinary fixed-regimen ITC. C4 is a report label consistent with missing estimand and data. Queries: (dynamic treatment regime|adaptive treatment|reinforcement learning) + (network meta-analysis|indirect comparison|multi-study); sequential regime ITC 2023–2026.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text: ADJ-18 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Statement
No application of simulation-based inference to bridge disconnected evidence through a mechanistic or pharmacometric model exists, so the entry stands open; the generic method is mature and surveyed (arXiv:1911.01429), and the non-simulation-based version of the idea is already routine in evidence synthesis as model-based meta-analysis and dose-response NMA, where a parametric dose-response curve connects arms that are not directly compared (MBNMAdose). Simulation-based inference approximates posterior, likelihood or likelihood-ratio quantities within a specified simulator; it does not itself identify a bridge, so it can support one only where mechanistic assumptions and data already define it. The misspecification claim needs care: a misspecified simulator does not return a well-calibrated posterior, it returns a posterior calibrated only relative to the wrong model, and the approximation can add miscalibration of its own.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Why it is open
The inferential guarantee is inherited from the simulator, so a mechanistic model that is wrong produces a bridge that carries the error without signaling it. Calibration of the inference procedure itself is computationally expensive and rarely performed, so in practice neither the model nor the approximation is checked. The result is a bridge whose apparent precision is a property of the simulator, the prior and the approximation rather than of the evidence.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Cranmer, Brehmer & Louppe, The frontier of simulation-based inference (2019)
Survey of the generic machinery, including the dependence of every guarantee on the assumed simulator and the cost of calibrating the inference procedure.


MBNMAdose (R package)
The near neighbor the source omitted: dose-response network meta-analysis in which a parametric curve connects arms that are not directly compared, doing the same bridging job with a tractable likelihood.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Develop simulation-based inference for pharmacometric and disease-process bridges across disconnected evidence, benchmarked against the dose-response and model-based network meta-analysis approaches that already perform the same bridging job with tractable likelihoods. Make simulator-misspecification checks and explicit calibration of the approximation mandatory, and report the bridge’s sensitivity to the mechanistic assumptions alongside the estimate so the inherited error is visible.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Simulation-based inference is proposed to approximate intractable likelihoods in mechanistic or pharmacometric models, so that disease-process or exposure-response models can act as bridges between disconnected pieces of evidence. The report labels it emerging.”
What was wrong with it. The source said a misspecified simulator returns a well-calibrated posterior for the wrong model; GPT-5.6 Sol corrected this, since calibration holds only relative to the assumed simulator and the approximation adds error of its own. The literature auditor also named the near neighbor the source omitted, dose-response and model-based network meta-analysis, which already bridges arms that are not directly compared.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no application of simulation-based inference to bridge disconnected evidence via a mechanistic or pharmacometric model, so the entry stands open. The generic method is mature and well surveyed (Cranmer, Brehmer & Louppe, ‘The frontier of simulation-based inference’, arXiv:1911.01429), and the adjacent, non-SBI version of the idea already exists in evidence synthesis as model-based meta-analysis and dose-response NMA (MBNMAdose), where a parametric dose-response curve connects arms that are not directly compared; the entry does not mention this near neighbour. The two limitation claims are correct and standard in the SBI literature: the posterior is only as good as the simulator, so a misspecified mechanistic model yields a well-calibrated posterior for the wrong model, and calibration checks of the inference procedure itself are computationally expensive and often skipped. Confidence is moderate because I read surveys and abstracts, not full texts.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C3, C4, and C5 are correct in qualified form. SBI approximates posterior, likelihood, or likelihood-ratio quantities within a specified simulator; it does not itself identify a bridge between disconnected evidence. C2 therefore holds only when mechanistic assumptions and data already define that bridge. Simulator misspecification does not imply that SBI returns a well-calibrated posterior: even an algorithm validated under the simulator is calibrated only relative to that model, while approximation error can introduce additional miscalibration. Posterior precision depends on the observations, simulator, prior, and approximation, not on the simulator alone. Calibration cost is method- and scale-dependent. The PAIC adaptation remains open but is an optional computational roadmap item unless an analysis actually relies on such a mechanistic bridge.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No cited prior_work. Simulation-based / likelihood-free inference is mature in machine learning and physics, and mechanistic/pharmacometric models are standard in model-informed drug development, but search did not find an evaluated SBI pipeline that bridges disconnected trial evidence for ITC/PAIC with mandatory simulator-misspecification checks and calibration reporting tied to a transported effect. C1 is true of SBI in general (capability, not a solved ITC problem). C2 remains a proposal. C3–C4 correctly restate well-known SBI failure modes (misspecified simulator yields calibrated wrong-model posteriors; calibration is expensive and often skipped). C5 is a report maturity label. A proposal-without-ITC-evaluation does not close the problem. Queries: simulation-based inference + (pharmacometric|disease model|meta-analysis|indirect treatment|evidence bridge); likelihood-free MIDD NMA 2023–2026; arXiv stat.ME SBI bridging trials.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text: ADJ-16 Confirmed open High priority Emerging

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Statement
Versioned ontologies for intervention components, doses and schedules already exist: the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology family, built on Basic Formal Ontology and released through OBO Foundry, covers intervention content, delivery mode, source, schedule and dose, setting and target population, with the Behaviour Change Technique Ontology as its content layer (PMC10427801; pmid:33447665), while ATC/DDD, SNOMED, CDISC and COMET cover drugs, doses, trial data structure and outcome sets. What is missing is an ITC-specific vocabulary bound to component network meta-analysis design matrices and effect-modifier definitions, an operational boundary between appropriate and inappropriate LLM roles, and a provenance chain in which every extracted datum carries its source span, an extraction confidence flag and a human verification state through to the analysis object. The LLM half is empirically supported: extraction studies report high headline accuracy alongside errors in roughly one outcome cell in five and observed hallucinations, LLM extraction for evidence synthesis is now evaluated in the methods literature (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710), and provenance is the standard mitigation, though raw model confidence is not calibrated and must not be read as evidence of correctness.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Why it is open
No existing vocabulary is bound to component network meta-analysis design matrices or to effect-modifier definitions, so component coding errors and version drift still enter analyses silently; ontology work produces no effect estimate, so it attracts less methodological effort than estimator work while blocking it. Permitted and forbidden LLM roles produce identical-looking output: a model that suggests candidate modifiers and one that selects them return the same list, and one asked for a missing target correlation supplies a plausible number rather than refusing. Once extracted values reach an analysis dataset they are indistinguishable from hand-curated ones, and no current pipeline, data format or synthesis package carries span-level provenance and verification state through to the analysis object, so the verification regime that would make machine extraction acceptable cannot be checked. The role boundary is a governance proposal rather than a finding, and it has no enforcement mechanism.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




The Behaviour Change Technique Ontology: Transforming the Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy v1 (2023)
A versioned, OBO-Foundry-aligned ontology of intervention components, part of a family covering delivery mode, schedule and dose, setting and target population. Contradicts the claim that no shared versioned component vocabulary exists; it is not bound to component NMA design matrices.


Ontologies relevant to behaviour change interventions: a method for their development (2021)
Documents the versioning and maintenance methodology behind that ontology family.


Gartlehner et al., Res Synth Methods 2024 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710)
Evaluation of large language model data extraction for evidence synthesis, named by the recency auditor as the reference for the LLM half; extraction studies of this kind report high headline accuracy alongside a material per-cell error rate, which is why provenance and human verification state are the mitigation.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing ontology families rather than starting a new one, binding component, dose, schedule, outcome and modifier terms to component network meta-analysis design matrices and machine-readable analysis specifications. Codify the permitted and forbidden LLM roles as an operational standard, with tooling that structurally prevents moment invention, unreviewed modifier selection, similarity-based transitivity claims and unverified component mappings. Implement a provenance schema in which every extracted datum carries its source span and human verification state into analysis datasets and reporting objects, and keep any model confidence flag labeled as uncalibrated.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Ontologies, LLM extraction roles, and datum-level provenance” The title lists ontologies as missing, but the audit found the versioned Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology family already covering components, doses and schedules.
The source said. “The machine-readable evidence layer for ITC is missing three things: versioned ontologies and knowledge graphs for treatments, components, doses, outcomes and effect modifiers; an operational boundary between appropriate LLM roles (extraction, ontology population, candidate modifier generation, auditable extraction suggestions, assumption-versus-text comparison) and inappropriate ones (inventing missing target moments, selecting modifiers without expert review, asserting transitivity from semantic similarity, replacing statistical estimation, producing unverified component mappings); and datum-level provenance carrying a source span, a confidence flag and a human verification state.”

C18 and C20 are strong provenance requirements. Retaining a confidence flag under C19 can aid auditability, but raw LLM confidence is generally not calibrated and must not be treated as evidence of correctness. The two maturity descriptions in C4 and C21 match the report. The claims that no shared vocabulary or suitable pipeline currently exists are landscape claims, not consequences of statistical theory, and cannot be established under this audit’s technical-only lens. The remaining work is chiefly infrastructure and governance; it is important for scalable automated evidence engineering but not a prerequisite for every manually curated decision-grade analysis.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. No cited prior_work in the problem card. Search of RSM/JCE/medRxiv/arXiv and SR-automation literature shows active LLM extraction for evidence synthesis (e.g. Gartlehner et al., Res Synth Methods 2024, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710; follow-on Annals 2025 AI-assisted extraction; TrialMind-style pipelines with source linking), and emerging provenance / span-return designs in clinical LLM operations literature, but none of that closes the three-part machine-readable ITC layer as stated. There is still no shared, versioned ontology/KG covering treatments, components, doses/schedules, outcomes, and effect modifiers that ITC/CNMA packages consume; no community operational standard that structurally forbids moment invention, unreviewed modifier selection, similarity-based transitivity, or unverified component maps; and no synthesis package or standard analysis object that propagates span-level source, confidence, and human verification state through to the final ITC/PAIC report. C1–C3 and C5–C17 are proportionate research-agenda framing (ontologies do not identify causal effects; LLMs extract and hallucinate; inventing moments or replacing estimation is inappropriate). C18–C20 are normative design claims with partial adjacent tooling, not solved infrastructure. C4 and C21 are report-internal labels. Queries: ontology/KG + (NMA|CNMA|component|effect modifier); LLM extraction + (systematic review|evidence synthesis) + provenance; PICO knowledge graph Cochrane; span-level verification 2024–2026.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:literature

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text: ADJ-14 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Statement
Federated individual-data synthesis is not prospective. DataSHIELD has run privacy-preserving individual-data meta-analysis for years, including federated Cox models for survival (PMC9166323); Bayesian Federated Inference reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries (doi:10.1002/sim.10072; doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.6; arXiv:2402.02898; CRAN package BFI); and federated target-trial emulation is published and validated across 192 hospitals and five health systems (doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y), which confirms the source’s own claim that federated target-trial methods are appearing in clinical research. What is unsolved is the specific object: federated Bayesian ML-NMR, where each posterior draw needs numerical integration over covariate distributions held by different custodians, together with federated posterior predictive checking and characterized approximation error. The ranking claim, that asymmetric individual-data access is the biggest practical limitation in PAIC, is unsupported; it is one major limitation.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Why it is open
Bayesian ML-NMR requires repeated evaluation of a joint likelihood with numerical integration over covariate distributions, and splitting that across custodians who cannot exchange records forces a choice between exact protocols whose cost compounds per sampling iteration and approximations whose posterior error is uncharacterized; general nonlinear ML-NMR also has no finite sufficient statistic to aggregate, so secure exactness is relative to a specified finite-precision computation and threat model. Model checking compounds the problem, because posterior predictive checks normally need the data being predicted and the analyst never sees it. Federation does not remove the reasons the data differ: site heterogeneity in measurement, case mix and definitions persists and is now harder to inspect, and no shared standard supplies harmonized component and outcome definitions. Every participant must also run compatible infrastructure under an agreed protocol, which is an organizational problem before it is a statistical one.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Li et al., Federated target trial emulation using distributed observational data for treatment effect estimation, npj Digital Medicine 2025
Federated protocol design, federated inverse-probability weighting and federated Cox models across 192 hospitals and five health systems; the reference for the entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing.


dsSurvival: Privacy preserving survival models for federated individual patient meta-analysis in DataSHIELD (2022)
Federated individual-data meta-analysis for survival outcomes without pooling records. Does not cover ML-NMR’s integration over covariate distributions or federated posterior predictive checks.


Jonker, Pazira & Coolen, Bayesian federated inference for estimating statistical models based on non-shared multicenter data sets, Stat Med 2024
Reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries, without sharing patient-level records.


Bayesian Federated Inference for regression models based on non-shared medical center data, Res Synth Methods 2025
Extends Bayesian federated inference to regression models under heterogeneous populations.


Bayesian Federated Inference for regression models based on non-shared multicenter data sets from heterogeneous populations (preprint, 2024)
Preprint with details of the federated regression construction and package illustration.


BFI (R package)
Shipped implementation of Bayesian federated inference, so the machinery is available rather than prospective.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the federated Bayesian machinery that exists rather than building federation from scratch: apply Bayesian Federated Inference and DataSHIELD-style protocols to ML-NMR’s integration step, and characterize exact versus approximate distributed computation so the approximation error is known rather than assumed small. Define federated posterior predictive checks, handle site-specific missingness and measurement, harmonize component and outcome definitions, and quantify secure-computation cost against the analytic gain. Treat asymmetric individual-data access as one major constraint among several rather than as the ranking premise for the program.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Federated and secure computation for multi-sponsor IPD synthesis” The title treats federated computation for multi-sponsor IPD synthesis as prospective, but the audit found federated Bayesian inference, survival meta-analysis and target-trial emulation already published.
The source said. “Asymmetric IPD access is named the biggest practical limitation in PAIC. Federated learning and secure multiparty computation are proposed so that trial custodians contribute gradients, likelihood summaries or exact secure sufficient statistics instead of row-level records, letting ML-NMR and other IPD models be fitted across sponsors and jurisdictions.”
What was wrong with it. The source described federated learning and secure computation as proposals and called asymmetric individual-data access the biggest practical limitation in PAIC. Auditors found federated Bayesian inference, federated survival meta-analysis and federated target-trial emulation already published, and GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the superlative as an uncited comparative claim; what remains open is federated ML-NMR and federated model checking.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Federated IPD evidence synthesis is not prospective: DataSHIELD has run privacy-preserving IPD meta-analysis across sites for years, including federated Cox models for survival IPD meta-analysis (dsSurvival, PMC9166323), where ‘the individual-level data remain within each site and only non-disclosive aggregated data are shared’. The entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods ‘are already appearing in clinical research’ is confirmable and should be cited: ‘Federated target trial emulation using distributed observational data for treatment effect estimation’ (npj Digital Medicine 2025, doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y), validated across 192 hospitals (eICU/MIMIC-IV) and five NYC health systems. What is genuinely unsolved is the specific object: federated Bayesian ML-NMR, where each posterior draw requires numerical integration over covariate distributions held at different custodians, and federated posterior predictive checking. The caveat is the superlative ‘Asymmetric IPD access is the biggest practical limitation in PAIC’, which I could not verify against any source that ranks limitations. Cites doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y: Supplies a real reference for the entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing; federated protocol design, federated IPTW and federated Cox across 192 hospitals.. Cites pmc:PMC9166323: Covers federated IPD meta-analysis for survival outcomes without pooling records. Does not cover ML-NMR’s integration over covariate distributions or federated posterior predictive checks..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is an unsupported comparative superlative; asymmetric IPD access is a major limitation, not demonstrably the biggest. C2 and C7 are feasible when site likelihoods decompose and custodians agree on a common model and protocol. C13 needs qualification: general nonlinear ML-NMR has no universal finite sufficient statistic, and SMPC exactness is relative to the specified finite-precision computation and threat model, although secure aggregation of local likelihood or gradient evaluations is possible. C3 describes facilitation, not access itself. C4 through C6 and the qualified forms of C14 and C15 are sound. C8 through C10 are too broad as open theoretical claims: exact distributed likelihood evaluation, local posterior-predictive discrepancies, and missing-data models are conceptually available, while model-specific approximation error, privacy-preserving checks, measurement harmonization, and implementation remain open. C11 is an uncited literature-state claim outside this audit’s permitted evidence, C12 is promotional, and C16 accurately reports the labels. Federated ML-NMR adaptation remains open and potentially high-value, but Very high is a roadmap priority rather than a demonstrated decision-grade severity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Federated Bayesian analysis of non-pooled multi-center IPD is no longer only speculative: Bayesian Federated Inference (BFI) reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries without sharing records (Jonker, Pazira, Coolen, Statistics in Medicine 2024; Research Synthesis Methods 2025 regression extension; CRAN package BFI; survival extension 2025). Federated target-trial emulation for distributed observational treatment-effect estimation is also published (Li et al., npj Digital Medicine 2025), confirming the report’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing in clinical research. These works partially resolve C2, C3, C11, and parts of C7/C14 for multi-center regression-style and TTE analyses. They do not close federated ML-NMR: repeated joint likelihood evaluation with numerical integration over covariate distributions, characterized exact-vs-approximate distributed Bayesian error, federated posterior predictive checks when the analyst never sees the data, harmonized component/outcome definitions, or SMPC cost characterization specific to evidence-synthesis MCMC. Site heterogeneity and governance remain unsolved by federation itself (C4–C6 still hold). Asymmetric IPD access remains a dominant practical PAIC constraint; calling it the single biggest limitation is slightly absolute but directionally supported. Cites 10.1002/sim.10072: Establishes BFI so multi-center Bayesian models can be combined from local inferences without sharing patient-level data.. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.6: Extends BFI to regression models under heterogeneous populations; CRAN BFI software.. Cites arXiv:2402.02898: Preprint/details for BFI regression and package illustration.. Cites 10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y: Demonstrates federated target-trial methods in clinical research, as the report claims..

Decision path

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text: ADJ-12 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Statement
Most of the quantities this entry calls computable but not computed are computed and published. Connectivity and minimal path length between treatments are in Thom et al. (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329); contrast-specific evidence paths and per-study contribution are in Papakonstantinou et al. (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3) and shipped as netmeta::netcontrib; component estimability has a signal-flow graph in Li, Shih and Tu (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), written in answer to the same complaint this entry makes; and precision-based ranking of the next study design is in Nikolakopoulou et al. (doi:10.1002/sim.6608). The development package cpaic, which lives on GitHub and cannot be installed from CRAN, already computes connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast estimability and contrast-specific edge influence. What is genuinely open is that these diagnostics are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, that articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration and removal vulnerability are still missing, and that there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study’s individual data to acquire.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Why it is open
The quantities exist in papers and in scattered implementations but not in standard NMA output, so an analysis can rest entirely on one articulation edge or one study without that dependence appearing anywhere a reviewer would see it. Component networks are worse, because information flows through the component design matrix rather than through visible treatment edges; note also that null-space dimension is a linear-algebra property of that matrix rather than a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not settle whether a requested contrast is estimable. Acquisition decisions remain informal because expected information gain and the value of individual-data placement cannot come from topology alone: they require a target contrast and population, a sampling model, priors and a decision utility, and no such machinery has been built for evidence networks. Design also cannot substitute for data, since where no evidence exists for the required contrast an optimal design still requires someone to collect it.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Automated methods to test connectedness and quantify indirectness of evidence in network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124
Graph algorithms for connectivity, indirect connection and minimal path length between treatments, covering the articulation and minimal-bridge questions, with R and Stata code.


Papakonstantinou et al., Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Res 2018;7:610
Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, that is, vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib.


Li, Shih & Tu, Graphical evaluation of evidence structure within a component network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607
Signal-flow graph over components showing which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence, written in response to the same complaint this entry makes about component networks.


Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti, Planning future studies based on the precision of network meta-analysis results, Stat Med 2016;35:219
Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, covering the design-prioritization half of this entry.


netmeta::netcontrib reference manual
Shipped implementation of the contribution matrix in network meta-analysis, evidence that per-study contribution is available to practitioners today.


Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio & Welton, Value of Information for Clinical Trial Design: The Importance of Considering All Relevant Comparators, PharmacoEconomics 2024
Value-of-information trial design that accounts for the full comparator set, the natural starting point for ranking candidate bridging studies by expected decision value.


cpaic connectivity, estimability and edge-influence diagnostics (development package, GitHub commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package, not installable from CRAN. Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast row-space estimability, and a contrast-specific edge-influence diagnostic that reports whether individual data inform the contrast at all.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Make the existing diagnostics routine rather than rebuilding them: bring connectivity, contribution, component estimability and design-precision tools into standard reporting for treatment and component networks, and add what is genuinely missing, articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration and removal vulnerability. Build expected-value-of-information methods on top by specifying the target contrast, population, sampling model, priors and decision utility, so candidate new edges, individual-data acquisitions and bridging studies can be scored by their effect on identification and on the decision. Existing value-of-information work for multi-comparator trial design (doi:10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0) is the natural starting point.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Connectivity, evidence-flow contribution, component estimability graphs and precision-based design of the next trial are all published and partly implemented in netmeta; what is missing is that they are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, and there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study’s IPD to acquire.
The source titled this. “Graph and value-of-information diagnostics for network design” The title names graph diagnostics as an open item, but the audit found connectivity, evidence-flow and component-estimability methods published and partly shipped in netmeta.
The source said. “The report lists computable structural quantities that evidence and component networks should report (articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific paths of component information, vulnerability to removal of a study or component, centrality of IPD placement, expected information gain from adding an edge) and proposes Bayesian experimental design and active learning to rank which IPD to acquire or which bridging trial to run.”
What was wrong with it. The source listed articulation treatments, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific information paths and vulnerability to study removal as computable but not computed. The literature auditor found four published methods covering most of them, one of which ships in netmeta, and GPT-5.6 Sol found rank, null space, bridging components, per-contrast estimability and edge influence already implemented in the unreleased cpaic development package; what survives is routine reporting and value of information for individual-data acquisition.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Most of the listed ‘computable but not computed’ quantities are computed, published and shipped. Connectivity, indirect connection and the minimum number of steps between a treatment pair: Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329), with R code and a Stata implementation. Contrast-specific paths of information and vulnerability to removing a study: Papakonstantinou et al., F1000Res 2018;7:610 (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3), the proportion contribution matrix, shipped as netmeta::netcontrib. Component estimability specifically: Li, Shih & Tu, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), a signal-flow graph over components, motivated by the exact complaint in this entry’s why_open. Freeman et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023;23:208) add CNMA-UpSet, heat map and circle plots. Design-side: Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti (Stat Med 2016;35:219, doi:10.1002/sim.6608) compute which study design and sample size to run next from NMA precision, extended in Trials 2019 (doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2). Genuinely open: null-space dimension reporting, centrality of IPD placement, and formal VOI for IPD acquisition. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329: Graph algorithms for connectivity, indirect connection and minimal path length between treatments, i.e. articulation and minimal-bridge questions.. Cites doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3: Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, i.e. vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623: Directly answers the component-network complaint: a signal-flow graph over components that shows which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.6608: Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, i.e. the design-prioritization half of this entry..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is straightforward for articulation treatments, but an articulation component needs an explicit bipartite or hypergraph definition and is not equivalent to statistical estimability. C2 and structural leave-one-out versions of C6 are computable once the bridge set is defined. C3 is a design-matrix linear-algebra calculation, not a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not determine a requested contrast. C4 requires a model and weighting rule and can be non-unique in cyclic or rank-deficient networks. C5 and C7 cannot be obtained from topology alone: expected information gain and the inferential value of IPD require a target contrast and population, sampling model, sample size, overlap, priors, and usually a decision utility. C8 through C10 are sound with those ingredients, and C11 reports the source label. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, cpaic_connectivity already returns connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, rank, null space, and per-contrast estimability, while edge_influence reports contrast-specific edge weights and whether IPD placement informs the contrast. Thus the blanket claim that the quantities are not computed is false, although articulation or cut-set enumeration, removal vulnerability, and model-based value-of-information design remain open. Very high is justified for estimability and fragility diagnostics, not for the entire active-learning bundle. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, and per-contrast row-space estimability.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements a contrast-specific estimating-weight diagnostic and identifies whether an IPD edge contributes to the requested contrast..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast. Cites 10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0: Shows VOI-based trial design should account for the full comparator set (network-relevant), supporting information-gain ranking of new evidence relative to multi-arm decision problems.. Cites 10.1002/sim.10072: Not a graph-diagnostic resolver; listed only if needed for multi-source computation. Prefer omit if empty required—use only VOI paper as primary..

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text: ADJ-10 Partially addressed Medium-high priority Emerging

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Statement
The study-aware causal forest already exists: Multi-Study Causal Forest (arXiv:2502.02110) is built to borrow individual patient data across studies when the sources of heterogeneity differ, and causal forests are routinely fitted to pooled multi-trial individual data. What is not done is aggregating the fitted conditional average treatment effect to an external HTA target population inside an indirect comparison, and no work applies causal discovery to a treatment network. Neither method selects a causally sufficient transport adjustment set, resolves unmeasured transport bias, or stays reliable with sparse events and few informative environments, so both remain hypothesis-generation aids.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Why it is open
Aggregating a fitted conditional effect to a declared target distribution needs the target covariate distribution, overlap and a transport argument, none of which the forest supplies. Discovered heterogeneity can reflect between-study differences rather than modification, and neither method distinguishes a causal interaction from one induced by an unadjusted study-level factor. Causal discovery returns observationally equivalent graphs with different transport implications; randomized treatments can orient some edges, but nothing in the output selects an adjustment set or certifies transportability. The identifying signal for cross-study structure is the number of distinct environments, and evidence networks supply few.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Multi-Study Causal Forest (MCF): A flexible framework for data borrowing in the presence of varying treatment effect heterogeneity (2025)
Covers the study-aware causal forest for effect-modifier discovery across studies. Does not cover aggregation of the fitted conditional effect to an external target population within an indirect comparison.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Take the existing multi-study causal forest and add what an indirect comparison needs: standardization of the fitted conditional effect to a declared external target distribution, with overlap and transport assumptions stated. Quantify how many trials and events are required before discovered structure is stable, and validate against known-truth simulations. Treat all output as candidate hypotheses for expert review and sensitivity analysis, requiring external confirmation before a discovered modifier enters an adjustment set.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Study-aware causal forests are proposed to discover effect modifiers and aggregate conditional average treatment effects to a target population, and causal discovery algorithms to generate candidate DAGs and interaction structures across studies. Both are offered as replacements for pre-specified modifier lists but are labeled hypothesis-generation aids rather than selection procedures.”
What was wrong with it. The source proposed study-aware causal forests as something still to develop and labeled them ‘Promising-emerging’; the literature auditor found a published multi-study causal forest (arXiv:2502.02110), so the forest half is not awaiting adaptation and the open part is aggregation to an external target. GPT-5.6 Sol also corrected the claim that few trials and rare events compromise validity: they damage power, stability and calibration, while a large randomized trial can still identify within-trial conditional effects.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The ‘study-aware causal forest’ is already published: ‘Multi-Study Causal Forest (MCF): A flexible framework for data borrowing in the presence of varying treatment effect heterogeneity’ (arXiv:2502.02110), which is explicitly built to borrow individual patient data across studies when the sources of heterogeneity differ. Causal forests are also routinely fitted to pooled multi-trial IPD (e.g. the type 2 diabetes application, BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2023; the psychiatry tutorial, Int J Methods Psychiatr Res 2025). So the forest half is not a proposal awaiting adaptation; what remains open is aggregating the fitted CATE to an external HTA target population inside an indirect comparison. I found nothing applying causal discovery to a treatment network, and the entry’s limitations (few trials, rare events, observational equivalence of returned graphs, inability to distinguish modification from between-study confounding) are all standard and correct. The caveat is the ‘Promising-emerging’ label for causal forests, which understates the multi-study work already done. Cites arxiv:2502.02110: Covers the study-aware causal forest for effect-modifier discovery across studies. Does not cover aggregation of the CATE to an external target population within an indirect comparison..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is feasible with sufficiently large randomized IPD, study-aware fitting or splitting, overlap, and a declared target covariate distribution. C2 is not a guaranteed improvement, and C3 confuses low information with validity: few trials and rare events primarily damage power, stability, calibration, and transport assessment, while a large randomized trial can still identify within-trial CATEs. C4 is correct for unmeasured transport factors. C5 and C6 are defensible only as candidate generation. C7 holds for purely observational discovery without added interventional, temporal, functional-form, or background-knowledge restrictions; randomized treatments and multiple interventions can orient some edges, so observational equivalence does not categorically prevent all orientation. C8 applies when cross-study shifts are the identifying signal, not simply because the individual-level sample came from few trials. C9 and C10 reproduce the labels. Calling either approach a replacement for pre-specified, causally justified modifiers is unsound, and Medium-high is inflated for tools restricted to hypothesis generation.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Causal forests are actively used on single RCTs and in multi-study synthesis contexts (e.g. Van Vogt et al. 2025 BMC Medical Research Methodology application; broader multi-study causal ML surveys 2024), and causal discovery remains a general tool for candidate DAGs. Neither closes the stated ITC problem. Forests still need substantial within-study signal and do not remove hidden confounding or certify that discovered heterogeneity is modification rather than study-level confounding; discovery still returns observationally equivalent graphs with different transport implications. No 2024–2026 work makes study-aware causal forests or multi-study discovery a reliable adjustment-set selector under typical NMA study counts and rare events. Treating output as hypothesis generation (as the report does) is still the honest status. Queries: causal forest network meta-analysis; study-aware causal forest IPD meta-analysis; causal discovery multi-trial transportability.

text: ADJ-08 Overstated High priority Promising

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Statement
Both halves of this machinery are long established in evidence synthesis rather than emerging. Bayesian nonparametric random effects for non-normal heterogeneity go back to Burr and Doss (JASA 2005) and Branscum and Hanson (pmid:18162115), with a 2024 review and simulation study of meta-analysis models that relax normality (arXiv:2412.12945); commensurate priors are already in NMA (JRSS-C 2018;67:1047) and robust mixture priors are standard (pmid:25355546). What is unvalidated is their use to bridge a disconnected subnetwork: with no shared contrast the commensurability parameter has nothing to be identified from, and the posterior for the cross-gap contrast is supplied by the assumed bridge and its prior.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Why it is open
Across a disconnected gap there is no likelihood contribution for the contrast of interest, so the posterior in that direction is determined by the assumed bridge and its prior, even where other parameters remain data-informed. A nonparametric prior aggravates the presentation problem because it looks agnostic while still supplying the structure that produces a finite estimate. Dynamic borrowing normally lets the data adjudicate how similar two sources are, but with no shared contrast there is nothing to adjudicate with, so the commensurability parameter is weakly identified. The exchangeability assumption that licenses the borrowing cannot be tested from the disconnected data, though it can be calibrated externally.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Branscum & Hanson, Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis using Polya tree mixture models, Biometrics 2008
Shows that flexible non-normal random-effects distributions in evidence synthesis are an established rather than emerging capability.


Power and Commensurate Priors for Synthesizing Aggregate and Individual Patient Level Data in Network Meta-Analysis, JRSS-C 2018;67:1047
Commensurate priors for controlled borrowing already exist inside NMA; the novelty in this entry is confined to the disconnected case.


arXiv:2412.12945 (2024 methodological systematic review and simulation study of meta-analysis models relaxing the random-effects normality assumption)
Reviews and evaluates meta-analysis models that relax the normal random-effects assumption, further evidence that the flexible-heterogeneity half is mature.


Schmidli et al. (pmid:25355546), robust mixture meta-analytic-predictive priors

jarbes (R package)
Named by the recency auditor as shipped Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis tooling, evidence that the machinery is available rather than prospective.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use nonparametric mixtures and commensurate or robust-mixture priors where the network is connected and the likelihood can inform them, and where it is disconnected require an explicit prior-versus-likelihood decomposition reporting how much of the estimate comes from the prior. Calibrate externally in settings where the bridge can be checked, for example by severing edges in connected networks and comparing the borrowed estimate against the known contrast. The contribution is the disconnected-gap protocol and its calibration evidence, not the priors, which already exist.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Bayesian nonparametric random-effects models and commensurate/robust priors are established tools in meta-analysis and NMA; what is unvalidated is their use to bridge a disconnected subnetwork, where the commensurability parameter has no shared contrast to be identified from.
The source said. “Bayesian nonparametric priors are proposed for flexible study and population mixtures and for non-normal random-effects distributions, and commensurate or robust-mixture priors for letting a disconnected subnetwork borrow imperfectly from another rather than assuming full exchangeability or full independence. Both place additional structure in the prior at precisely the point where the likelihood is silent.”
What was wrong with it. The source labeled Bayesian nonparametrics ‘Emerging’ and commensurate priors ‘Promising’ and treated both as proposals; the literature auditor showed they have been in use in evidence synthesis for one to two decades (pmid:18162115; JRSS-C 2018;67:1047; pmid:25355546). Only the disconnected-subnetwork application is novel, and GPT-5.6 Sol added that a proper posterior in a likelihood-unidentified direction should not be called identification.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Both halves of the ‘proposed’ machinery are long established in evidence synthesis, which makes the maturity labels wrong. Bayesian nonparametric random effects in meta-analysis date to Burr & Doss (JASA 2005) and Branscum & Hanson, ‘Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis using Polya tree mixture models’ (Biometrics 2008, PMID 18162115); a 2024 methodological systematic review plus simulation study of meta-analysis models relaxing the random-effects normality assumption exists (arXiv:2412.12945). Commensurate priors are already in NMA: ‘Power and Commensurate Priors for Synthesizing Aggregate and Individual Patient Level Data in Network Meta-Analysis’ (JRSS-C 2018;67:1047), and robust mixture MAP priors are standard (Schmidli et al., PMID 25355546). So ‘Emerging’ for Bayesian nonparametrics and ‘Promising’ for commensurate priors both understate maturity by 10-20 years. What is genuinely open is the disconnected-subnetwork application, and the entry’s diagnosis is corroborated: work on Bayesian disconnected NMA finds the standard approach unusable under vague priors and dependent on moderately informative ones, i.e. the posterior for the disconnected contrast is prior-driven. Cites pmid:18162115: Flexible non-normal random-effects distributions in evidence synthesis are an established, not emerging, capability.. Cites https://academic.oup.com/jrsssc/article/67/4/1047/7058351: Commensurate priors for controlled borrowing already exist inside NMA; the novelty in this entry is confined to the disconnected case..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 and C4 are technically sound capabilities. C2 and C5 are conditional, not guaranteed improvements: flexible or robust priors trade parametric restriction for prior and hyperparameter sensitivity and need enough likelihood information. C3 should not call a proper posterior identification. For a contrast outside the likelihood-identified subspace, the hierarchical or bridge prior supplies the otherwise unidentified direction, although other parameters can remain data-informed. C6 is too absolute. Exchangeability for the actual missing cross-gap contrast cannot be tested by that disconnected likelihood, but empirical calibration is possible with external or connected networks and edge-severing exercises, as the proposed direction itself recognizes. C7 and C8 accurately reproduce the report’s labels. Transparent prior attribution and sensitivity remain open and are decision-critical only when the target decision uses a cross-gap posterior; the general High priority is otherwise a roadmap judgment.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search finds mature building blocks, not a closed ITC gap. Bayesian nonparametric mixtures for flexible random-effects / non-normal heterogeneity exist in pairwise meta-analysis (Dirichlet-process / DPM style work; recent bias-corrected BNP in Biometrical Journal 2025; CRAN jarbes). Commensurate and robust-mixture dynamic borrowing are well established for historical controls when a shared endpoint/likelihood contributes information (Hobbs et al.; recent robust-mixture / SAM literature 2023–2025). None of this removes the structural fact that a disconnected contrast has no likelihood contribution for the bridge: the posterior remains prior-driven, and the commensurability parameter is weakly identified when there is no shared contrast with which to adjudicate similarity. I found no 2024–2026 NMA/ITC paper or multinma/crossnma/gemtc/netmeta feature that validates exchangeability across a disconnected subnetwork gap or that supplies an accepted prior-versus-likelihood decomposition for that case. C1 and C4 are true as method existence claims outside pure disconnected ITC; C3 and C6 correctly describe why the problem remains open; maturity labels C7/C8 are report-internal taxonomy and were not re-verified against a report file. Queries: Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet process NMA; commensurate/robust mixture disconnected NMA; crossnma disconnected borrowing; jarbes BC-BNP.
