title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text: ADJ-06 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Statement
Instead of picking one synthetic target distribution consistent with the reported marginals, distributionally robust optimization would define the set of laws whose moments lie in the admissible moment set and which sit within a divergence distance of a reference distribution, then report the infimum and supremum of the treatment effect over that set. No work in evidence synthesis does this; the generic machinery exists elsewhere, including distributionally robust generalization of heterogeneous treatment effects across sites (arXiv:2412.11136) and distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation (arXiv:2512.12781), but none takes reported marginal means and proportions as moment constraints and bounds a PAIC effect. Two limits belong in the statement: the bounded set is the intersection of the moment constraints and the divergence ball, so it is not an interval over every moment-compatible law, and the resulting range describes target-law ambiguity rather than sampling uncertainty.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Why it is open
Current practice fixes the unreported correlation and tail structure by fiat when it reconstructs a target distribution, so a point estimate hides a family of equally compatible target laws, and for non-collapsible measures the marginal effect depends on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables (arXiv:2210.01757). Computing the bounds means optimizing an effect functional over an infinite-dimensional constrained set, and the bounds can be infinite or undefined if outcome behavior outside the observed support is left unrestricted. The ambiguity set has no accepted calibration: a loose set contains implausible target laws and gives an interval too wide to inform a decision, while a tight set encodes an unverifiable assumption, so justifying the set reintroduces the judgment the method was meant to remove.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




arXiv:2412.11136 (distributionally robust generalization of heterogeneous treatment effects across sites, minimax regret over a multisite uncertainty set)
Generic machinery the entry would draw on: distributionally robust optimization over a set of plausible target distributions. Does not take published marginal summaries as moment constraints.


arXiv:2512.12781 (distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation)
Generic distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation. Does not bound a PAIC effect over target laws compatible with reported summaries.


Remiro-Azocar, Transportability of model-based estimands in evidence synthesis, Stat Med 2024;43(22):4217-4249
Establishes that marginal effects for non-collapsible measures depend on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables, which is why unreported dependence structure matters here.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define the ambiguity set from the admissible target moment set plus a divergence ball around a reference distribution, and report the induced interval as target-law ambiguity, labeled separately from sampling uncertainty. Develop tractable optimization for the infimum and supremum, restrict outcome behavior outside the observed support so the bounds stay finite, and establish conventions for the divergence radius. Build elicitation and justification procedures for the set so it can survive review in a real submission, applying the method first where the effect measure is non-collapsible or interactions are nonlinear.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Instead of picking one synthetic target distribution consistent with the reported marginals, distributionally robust optimization would define the set of distributions whose moments lie in the admissible moment set and which sit within a divergence distance of a reference distribution, then report the infimum and supremum of the treatment effect over that set. This is a direct treatment of uncertainty in unreported correlations and tails.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed two claims: the reported range covers only the intersection of the moment constraints and the divergence ball rather than all moment-compatible laws, and non-collapsibility makes marginal effects depend on the covariate distribution without guaranteeing a wide range. The source also cited nothing for the generic machinery it draws on; the auditors named it.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I searched for distributionally robust bounds constructed from an ambiguity set of target laws consistent with published summary statistics and found nothing in evidence synthesis. What exists is the generic machinery the entry would draw on: DRO over plausible target distributions for generalizing heterogeneous treatment effects across sites (arXiv:2412.11136, minimax regret over a multisite uncertainty set), DRO treatment-effect estimation (arXiv:2512.12781), and Wasserstein ambiguity sets whose radius calibration is itself an active problem. None of these takes reported marginal means and proportions as moment constraints and reports the infimum and supremum of a PAIC effect over the compatible set, which is the entry’s specific proposal. The entry’s stated obstacles are also accurate: the ambiguity-set calibration problem is acknowledged in the DRO literature, and the dependence of non-collapsible effects on unreported joint structure is established (Remiro-Azocar, arXiv:2210.01757, shows marginal effects for non-collapsible measures depend on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables). I read abstracts only, hence the moderate confidence.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The proposed optimization is mathematically coherent when the ambiguity set is nonempty, the target effect functional is identified and integrable over its support, and the extrema exist. It can expose sensitivity to unreported dependence and tail behavior. The bounded set is the intersection of the moment constraints and divergence ball, however, so C3 is not literally an interval over every moment-compatible law. Divergence direction, reference support and radius can strongly constrain which correlations and tails vary. Non-collapsibility makes marginal effects depend on the prognostic covariate distribution, but does not guarantee a wide range. The resulting bounds describe target-law ambiguity, not sampling uncertainty, and can be infinite or undefined if outcome behavior outside observed support is unrestricted. Calibration and computation remain genuine open work.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Distributionally robust and ambiguity-set methods for treatment effects under model or distributional risk appear in general causal/ML venues, but no retrieved PAIC/HTA method defines an ambiguity set from published target moments plus a divergence ball, optimizes inf/sup of the target-population effect for non-collapsible measures or nonlinear interactions, calibrates the radius for reimbursement use, and ships software usable with MAIC/STC/ML-NMR. The report’s institutional caveats (loose sets uninformative; tight sets reintroduce judgment) remain live. Queries: DRO treatment effect target population moments; distributionally robust PAIC MAIC; ambiguity set covariate correlations tails causal; RSM/SiM/Value Health 2024–2026 DRO ITC.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R12:supported

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text: ADJ-04 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Statement
No published STC or ML-NMR analysis uses BART or a Gaussian process as the outcome surface, so that adaptation is open. All the proposals share one limit: standardizing a fitted surface over a target distribution with mass outside the source support is extrapolation however flexible the learner, and BART’s behavior outside the observed support is prior-driven rather than evidential (arXiv:2204.10963). The conformal half needs narrowing. Ordinary split-conformal prediction does not itself detect unsupported covariate profiles, since an interval can keep the same width far outside source support, and the covariate-shift repair already exists: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes and Ramdas (NeurIPS 2019) show the guarantee rests on exchangeability and restore it by likelihood-ratio weighting, which is the natural route with PAIC weights.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Why it is open
A flexible learner fits only where data exist; outside that region BART’s priors and a Gaussian process’s kernel and prior mean produce plausible predictions and prior-driven intervals that are modeling artifacts, and Gaussian-process uncertainty is calibrated conditional on the kernel, prior and likelihood rather than automatically. Fitted interactions are predictive structure rather than identified effect modification. Conformal coverage does not transfer under the covariate shift a transport problem creates by construction, and the weighted repair needs estimable density ratios and target support, which is exactly what is in doubt. Gaussian-process inference also scales poorly in data and integration points, which collides with the numerical integration burden already present in ML-NMR.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift, NeurIPS 2019
Canonical source for the claim that conformal coverage does not transfer under shift, and supplies the likelihood-ratio-weighted repair that is the natural route for PAIC. Does not address the ITC problem itself.


Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference (2022)
Direct evidence that BART’s behavior outside the observed covariate support is prior-driven rather than evidential. Does not address the ITC problem itself.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build BART and Gaussian-process outcome standardization for STC and ML-NMR paired with mandatory support and out-of-distribution diagnostics, and use weighted conformal prediction with the PAIC weights so the coverage claim is stated correctly rather than assumed. The open work here is adapting an existing shift-aware conformal method, not inventing a diagnostic. Make behavior in unsupported target regions visible instead of smoothed over, address Gaussian-process cost with sparse or approximate methods, and forbid reading fitted interactions as causal effect modification.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “BART and Gaussian processes are proposed as flexible nonlinear outcome and treatment-by-covariate surfaces for standardization in STC and ML-NMR, with GPs also covering dose-response curves, and conformal prediction is proposed as the diagnostic that flags target profiles the source data do not support. All three inherit one problem: standardizing a fitted surface over a target distribution with mass outside the source support is extrapolation however flexible the learner is.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented conformal prediction as the diagnostic that flags target profiles the source data do not support. GPT-5.6 Sol pointed out that a split-conformal interval can retain the same width far outside source support, so it is not an out-of-support detector, and the literature auditor supplied the weighted-conformal repair for covariate shift (Tibshirani et al., NeurIPS 2019) that the source did not cite.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): I found no published use of BART or Gaussian processes as the outcome surface inside STC or ML-NMR standardization, so the ITC-specific proposal stands open. The supporting claims are each backed by retrievable work outside ITC. BART is routinely used to fit the outcome model on trial data and predict potential outcomes in a target population in the generalizability literature; its extrapolation behavior outside the covariate support is a known, separately studied failure mode (arXiv:2204.10963, ‘Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference’). The conformal claim is exactly right and has a canonical source: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, ‘Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift’ (NeurIPS 2019), which shows the standard guarantee rests on exchangeability and must be repaired by likelihood-ratio weighting; note this also means a route exists (weighted conformal with the MAIC odds weights), which the entry does not mention. I did not verify the ‘Promising’/‘Speculative diagnostic’ labels; those are claims about the source report, not the literature.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no published use of BART or Gaussian processes as the outcome surface inside STC or ML-NMR standardization, so the ITC-specific proposal stands open. The supporting claims are each backed by retrievable work outside ITC. BART is routinely used to fit the outcome model on trial data and predict potential outcomes in a target population in the generalizability literature; its extrapolation behavior outside the covariate support is a known, separately studied failure mode (arXiv:2204.10963, ‘Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference’). The conformal claim is exactly right and has a canonical source: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, ‘Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift’ (NeurIPS 2019), which shows the standard guarantee rests on exchangeability and must be repaired by likelihood-ratio weighting; note this also means a route exists (weighted conformal with the MAIC odds weights), which the entry does not mention. I did not verify the ‘Promising’/‘Speculative diagnostic’ labels; those are claims about the source report, not the literature. Cites https://candes.su.domains/publications/downloads/WeightedCP.pdf: Does NOT resolve the ITC problem. It is the canonical source for the entry’s claim that conformal coverage does not transfer under shift, and it supplies the weighted-conformal repair the entry should cite as the natural PAIC route.. Cites arxiv:2204.10963: Does NOT resolve the ITC problem. It is direct evidence for the claim that BART’s behavior outside the observed covariate support is prior-driven rather than evidential..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1-C8 and C11 are broadly correct with model-dependent qualifications: BART and Gaussian processes can represent flexible surfaces, but neither supplies causal effect-modifier interpretation, support or extrapolation validity. Gaussian-process uncertainty is conditional on the kernel, prior and likelihood, not automatically calibrated. C9-C10 are too strong. Ordinary conformal prediction does not inherently detect unsupported covariate profiles; a split-conformal interval can retain the same width far outside source support. Exchangeability failure removes its usual coverage result, while covariate-shift variants require additional assumptions, estimable density ratios and target support. The critical issue is positivity and visible model dependence; adopting BART or GPs is principally a modeling roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No retrieved 2024–2026 STC/ML-NMR implementation pairs BART or GPs as routine outcome surfaces with mandatory support diagnostics inside multinma or equivalent PAIC software. General BART/GP and conformal literature is active (including GP plus conformal calibration work), but conformal coverage under transport/covariate shift requires extra assumptions and is not solved as a PAIC product. The report’s own caveats (extrapolation remains extrapolation; conformal exchangeability fails by construction under shift; GP cost versus ML-NMR integration) match the broader ML literature and are not resolved by a PAIC-specific package. C1–C11 read as research proposals plus correct limitations, not closed methods. title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text: ADJ-02 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Statement
Standard transport estimators assume an individual-level sample from the target population and HTA targets are usually described only by published summaries, but that obstruction is no longer untouched. Chen et al. (doi:10.1111/biom.13825) reweight to target summary moments, Yan et al.’s TADA (doi:10.1002/pst.70029) transports survival effects from target aggregate data while adjusting for covariate-dependent censoring, and Vo et al. (arXiv:2503.05634) and Shi et al. (arXiv:2605.27272) extend causally interpretable meta-analysis to trials whose individual data are inaccessible. What is missing is a general-purpose transportability library that plugs into the NMA stack: the only NMA-integrated transport is multinma’s own ML-NMR, which requires a copula reconstruction of the target joint covariate distribution from published marginals, while TransportHealth and similar stacks are separate codebases rather than drop-ins for multinma, netmeta or gemtc.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Why it is open
Published marginals identify the target joint distribution only in special cases. Unless the reported summaries happen to identify every target expectation the estimand and model require, the dependence structure and nonlinear expectations must be assumed rather than estimated, and that assumption’s contribution to uncertainty is not propagated into the interval. The existing aggregate-target estimators are built for a single source trial and a specified estimand rather than for a connected network with multi-arm structure. Transport software and NMA software are developed as separate stacks, so an estimate produced by one cannot enter an evidence network fitted by the other without manual re-implementation.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Yan et al., Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data From the Target Population, Pharm Stat 2025
TADA: two-stage weighting that transports a survival effect when only target aggregate data exist, adjusting simultaneously for censoring bias and effect-modifier imbalance. Evaluated and applied; not integrated into an NMA package.


Yan et al., Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data from the Target Population (preprint, 2025)
Preprint version of TADA with assumptions, theory, simulations and an NSCLC case study under target aggregate data only.


Chen et al., Entropy balancing for causal generalization with target sample summary information, Biometrics 2023
Weighting transport of the average treatment effect using target summary-level moments only. Not survival PAIC and not NMA software.


Vo et al., Integration of aggregated data in causally interpretable meta-analysis by inverse weighting (2025)
Transport and standardization across trials where individual data are inaccessible for some studies, by extending moment-based PAIC methods.


Shi, van Amsterdam, Dahabreh et al., Causally-interpretable meta-analysis using aggregate data (2026)
Causally interpretable meta-analysis and indirect comparison in a target population from aggregate trial data only.


multinma package documentation (Phillippo)
Counter-evidence to the claim that no transportability software interoperates with mainstream NMA packages: multinma produces population-adjusted effects for any study population in the network or for an external target population.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the estimators that exist rather than build new ones: take TADA and target-moment entropy balancing to the estimands and outcome types HTA needs, and derive the extra uncertainty induced by reconstructing a joint distribution from marginals so that it appears in the reported interval. Characterize when reported summaries are sufficient for the required target expectations and when they are not, and pair the insufficient case with sensitivity analysis. Then make the result interoperable with mainstream NMA packages so a transported estimate can enter an evidence network directly.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. There is no general-purpose transportability library that plugs into the NMA stack; the only NMA-integrated transport is multinma’s own ML-NMR, which requires a copula reconstruction of the target joint covariate distribution from published marginals.
The source titled this. “Transport estimators and software for aggregate-only targets” The title lists transport estimators for aggregate-only targets as missing, but the audit found TADA and three further estimators published, narrowing the gap to NMA-integrated software.
The source said. “Standard transportability estimators assume an individual-level sample from the target population, but HTA targets are described only by published summaries. The report proposes extending target-aggregate-data methods such as TADA and building transportability software that interoperates with existing NMA packages instead of standing alone.”
What was wrong with it. The source, which cited nothing, said TADA needs extension before it can be used and that no transportability software interoperates with mainstream NMA packages. The literature auditor found TADA published, evaluated and applied (doi:10.1002/pst.70029) alongside three further aggregate-target estimators, and multinma documenting population-adjusted effects for an external target population; the claim was unattributed in the source, is now sourced, and narrows to the absence of a general-purpose transport library that interoperates with the NMA stack.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Target-AgD transport is no longer empty. Chen et al. (Biometrics 2023) give entropy balancing from target summary moments; Josey-style calibration and related AgD transport work predate that. Yan et al. TADA (Pharm Stat 2025; arXiv:2412.12335) is a two-stage MoM plus IPCW method for transporting survival effects with covariate-dependent censoring when only target AgD exist, with simulation and a case study, code on GitHub, and inclusion as a module in TransportHealth (Park et al. 2025). Le et al. (arXiv:2408.04854) address transporting aggregate trial results in causally interpretable meta-analysis. C2 remains supported for standard IPD-target transport estimators. C3 is partly overstated because TADA and Chen already exist for key estimands; further extension for full PAIC/NMA estimands and uncertainty from reconstructed joints is still needed. C4 remains largely supported: TransportHealth and CausalMetaR are transport stacks, not drop-ins for multinma/netmeta/gemtc. C5 remains supported for ITC-network validation and NMA interop. Queries: TADA transport AgD; Chen entropy balancing target summary; TransportHealth; CausalMetaR multinma interop; DIPW Quan; NMA package release notes 2024–2026.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The entry names TADA and then says it needs extension; TADA is published and evaluated: Yan et al., ‘Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data From the Target Population’ (Pharm Stat 2025, doi:10.1002/pst.70029; arXiv:2412.12335), a two-stage weighting framework applied to transport a KM curve to an Ontario NSCLC target. Two further 2025-2026 estimators cover the aggregate case: Vo et al. (arXiv:2503.05634) integrate aggregate trials with inaccessible IPD into causal meta-analysis by extending PAIC moment methods; Shi, van Amsterdam, Dahabreh et al. (arXiv:2605.27272) build causally-interpretable meta-analysis from marginal and one-at-a-time subgroup effects plus covariate summaries. The claim I cannot let stand is ‘No transportability software currently interoperates with mainstream NMA packages.’ multinma is a mainstream NMA package that performs the transport itself: its documentation states population-adjusted effects ‘can be produced for any study population in the network, or for an external target population.’ Standalone packages (TransportHealth, generalize) exist alongside it. Cites doi:10.1002/pst.70029: TADA exists, is evaluated and applied; the aggregate-only-target obstruction is partly addressed for a single source trial with a survival outcome.. Cites arxiv:2503.05634: Transport/standardization across trials where IPD is inaccessible for some studies, by extending PAIC moment-based methods.. Cites arxiv:2605.27272: Causally-interpretable meta-analysis and indirect comparison in a target population from aggregate trial data only..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 is generally correct but not categorical. Aggregate summaries can suffice when they identify the target expectations required by the chosen outcome or effect model, such as when the relevant conditional contrast lies in the linear span of reported balance functions. Otherwise, marginal summaries do not identify the target joint distribution, dependence structure or nonlinear expectations. Individual-level target data and density estimation are therefore common requirements, not universal ones. C3 and C5 are plausible development assessments but unsourced; C4 is an unsupported universal software claim. The genuine open core is identification and uncertainty propagation under insufficient target summaries, plus usable network integration.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Target-AgD transport is no longer empty. Chen et al. (Biometrics 2023) give entropy balancing from target summary moments; Josey-style calibration and related AgD transport work predate that. Yan et al. TADA (Pharm Stat 2025; arXiv:2412.12335) is a two-stage MoM plus IPCW method for transporting survival effects with covariate-dependent censoring when only target AgD exist, with simulation and a case study, code on GitHub, and inclusion as a module in TransportHealth (Park et al. 2025). Le et al. (arXiv:2408.04854) address transporting aggregate trial results in causally interpretable meta-analysis. C2 remains supported for standard IPD-target transport estimators. C3 is partly overstated because TADA and Chen already exist for key estimands; further extension for full PAIC/NMA estimands and uncertainty from reconstructed joints is still needed. C4 remains largely supported: TransportHealth and CausalMetaR are transport stacks, not drop-ins for multinma/netmeta/gemtc. C5 remains supported for ITC-network validation and NMA interop. Queries: TADA transport AgD; Chen entropy balancing target summary; TransportHealth; CausalMetaR multinma interop; DIPW Quan; NMA package release notes 2024–2026. Cites 10.1002/pst.70029: Operational AgD-target transport for survival with MoM participation weights and IPCW; software prototype (TADA/TransportHealth). Not full PAIC-into-NMA interop.. Cites arxiv:2412.12335: Preprint/version of TADA with assumptions, theory sketch, simulations, and NSCLC case study under target AgD only.. Cites 10.1111/biom.13825: Weighting transport of ATE using target summary-level moments only (binary/continuous-style generalization). Not survival PAIC/NMA network software..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: How this was verified
text:
This catalog is derived from a set of deep-research documents produced by a large language model (ChatGPT deep research) in July 2026, covering open methodological problems in indirect treatment comparisons, population-adjusted indirect comparisons, component methods, and quantitative bias analysis.
That origin is the reason this page exists. A machine-generated research agenda is a plausible-sounding artifact whether or not it is correct, and publishing one as settled fact would be a disservice. Nothing from the source documents appears on this site without a verification verdict attached, and the evidence behind each verdict is shown on the entry itself.
The source documents are kept as working material and are not published here.

title: How this was verified

What was checked mechanically

The conclusion from that pass shaped everything after it. Fabricated citations are not the failure mode of this corpus. The claims are attached to real papers with real numbers. The risks that remained were subtler: a real paper cited for a claim it does not quite make, a problem described as open that the literature has partly closed, a severity claim pitched too strong, and claims about a software package that had moved on since the report was written.

title: How this was verified
text:
The audit
Every problem carries a set of atomic, falsifiable claims extracted from the source. Those claims, not the prose around them, are what was tested.

Literature verification
For each problem, an agent with web and PubMed access checked that each cited work actually supports the claim attributed to it, and searched for later work that would resolve or narrow the problem.


Adversarial refutation
A second agent was instructed to refute the proposition that the problem is open, and to default to “not open” when uncertain. Asking an agent to confirm a claim and asking it to break the claim produce different results; only the second is informative.


Independent external auditors
Two frontier models outside this system were given the same claims, blind to each other and to the verdicts above:

GPT-5.6 Sol at maximum reasoning effort, via the codex CLI
Grok 4.5 at high reasoning effort, via the grok CLI

Both were constrained to answer from their own knowledge of the evidence-synthesis and causal inference literature, and asked to return a graded verdict, a reason, and any counterevidence.
Coverage was not equal, and that matters. Grok’s usage balance was exhausted partway through the run, so it reached only a fraction of the catalog. Entries it never saw carry two independent opinions rather than three. This is recorded rather than smoothed over, because an entry judged by two auditors is weaker evidence than one judged by three.



Auditor
Entries covered




Literature and prior-art check (Claude)
232 of 232


GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
232 of 232


Grok 4.5, recency lens
47 of 232





Checking the auditors
An audit is only worth what its auditors are worth, so their own load-bearing claims were spot-checked by hand against primary sources. Every checked claim held: marginal_effects() does exist in multinma 0.7.0, nmathresh is on CRAN, the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology papers resolve, and Ishak et al. 2025 in PharmacoEconomics is real. No invented locator, version number, or function name was found.
One auditor finding is worth stating on its own, because it changed several entries: the source report proposes a reporting and credibility standard for population-adjusted indirect comparisons without citing Ishak et al. 2025, which published one.
Using two auditors rather than one is the point. On a pilot run they agreed that a claim about the emptiness of the quantitative bias analysis literature was overstated, both citing the mature epidemiological bias-analysis toolkit. On a different claim, about whether cross-subnetwork component constancy is testable at all, they disagreed — and the disagreement was substantive rather than noise. Where auditors disagree, this site shows the disagreement rather than resolving it silently.


Code verification
Problems that describe limitations of a specific software implementation were re-checked against that package’s current source, not against the report’s description of it. Some had already been fixed; those are marked as resolved rather than deleted, because the underlying methodological problem is still worth recording.


Adjudication
Verdicts follow a fixed rule, applied to the evidence gathered above:







Condition
Verdict




Later work resolves it, in the literature or in code
Resolved since report


At least two of the three independent checks call it overstated
Overstated


All checks agree it is open and no counterevidence surfaced
Confirmed open


Existing work covers part of it
Partially addressed


Checks disagree, or evidence is insufficient
Unverifiable, with the dissent shown


No support could be found
Not supported

title: How this was verified
section: Which fields are audited, and which are editorial
text:
Which fields are audited, and which are editorial
Not everything on an entry page is a verified claim, and the difference matters.
Audited. The statement, the reasons the problem is open, the cited prior work, and every claim extracted from them. These went through the process above and carry the verdict.
Editorial. Maturity and tractability are not stated anywhere in the source material. The source has no such fields; these values are a classification applied during extraction to make the catalog browsable. They are one reader’s judgment, they were not audited, and they should not be cited as findings.
Deliberately rebuilt. Priority is not carried over from the source either. The source’s own master matrix grades 30 of its 46 rows “Very high” and 15 “High”, which is under half a bit of information and not usable as a ranking. Priority here reflects three observable things instead: whether the problem blocks a decision-grade estimand, whether any method addresses it at all, and whether any software implements it.

title: How this was verified
section: What the verdicts do not mean
text:
What the verdicts do not mean
A verdict of Confirmed open means the claim survived the checks described above. It does not mean the problem is provably unsolved. Absence of counterevidence in a targeted search is weaker evidence than a systematic review, and this was not a systematic review: there was no protocol registration, no duplicate screening, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment.
A verdict of Overstated is a refinement, not a dismissal. In almost every case the underlying problem is real and the correction concerns how strongly it was stated.
Model-based auditors have their own failure modes. They can be confidently wrong, they share training data with the system that produced the source documents, and their knowledge has a cutoff. They were used because two independent expert opinions are better than none, not because they are authoritative.
Where an entry matters to a decision, read the cited primary sources. This catalog is a map of where the problems are, and a record of how hard each claim was pushed on. It is not a substitute for the literature it points to.

title: How this was verified
text:
Reproducing this
The site source, the build script, and the workflow definitions are in the repository. Entry pages are generated from a structured registry rather than hand-written, so the audit metadata on each page is the same data the adjudication used.

title: Open Problems in Indirect Treatment Comparisons
text:
The field is not short of estimators. It is short of identification discipline, estimand discipline, target-population discipline, and diagnostics that expose how much of an answer is supplied by data rather than by assumption.
This site catalogs the open problems, one entry at a time. Each says what the problem is, why it stays open, what has already been tried, and the most probable route to a solution.

title: Open Problems in Indirect Treatment Comparisons
text:
Start here


Browse the catalog
Every problem in one filterable table. Sort by priority, filter by category or verdict, or search across all fields.


The prioritized agenda
What should change in practice now, what should be built next, and what is high-risk and high-reward.


The method landscape
What each approach identifies, where it breaks, and a decision path from a comparison problem to a defensible method.


How this was verified
The provenance of this material, the audit protocol, and an honest account of what the verdicts do and do not establish.

title: Open Problems in Indirect Treatment Comparisons
text:
The organizing distinction
The decisive division in this field is anchored versus unanchored evidence, not matching versus regression versus multilevel modeling.
In an anchored comparison, randomization still identifies the within-trial relative effect, and population adjustment is mainly about transporting effect modification. In an unanchored or disconnected comparison, the analyst has to reconstruct a causal contrast across studies: every prognostic factor and effect modifier that creates cross-study outcome differences becomes relevant, and residual confounding is generally not testable. Most of the hardest entries in this catalog live on the unanchored side of that line.
Three consequences run through the whole collection:
Adjustment to one trial population is not transport to the decision population. Pairwise matching and regression approaches usually target the population of the trial that supplied aggregate data. Applying that effect to a reimbursement population is a second transport step, and it is commonly hidden.
Weak overlap is not a nuisance diagnostic; it changes the scientific question. When weights are extreme or a model extrapolates beyond its support, the nominal target estimand may cease to be credibly identified. Reporting an effective sample size does not repair that.
In a disconnected network, some assumption carries the information across the gap. Baseline risk, a dose-response curve, a treatment class, a shared component — each answers a different question and imports different bias. That software produced a connected posterior is not evidence that the effect is identified.

title: Open Problems in Indirect Treatment Comparisons
text:
Reading a verdict
Every entry carries a verdict recording what happened when its claims were checked against the literature and against two independent external auditors. A verdict of Overstated does not mean the problem is not real; it usually means the underlying issue is real and a claim about its severity was pitched too strongly. Entries marked Resolved since report are kept rather than deleted, because knowing that something was recently closed is as useful as knowing it is open.
The source material for this catalog was produced by a large language model and then audited. How this was verified explains what that means in practice, including where the audit’s own limits are.

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
The catalog lists problems. This page ranks them, in three tiers plus a list of work the field does not need. Tier 1 requires no new methodology: every item is something an analyst could do differently in the next analysis. Tiers 2 and 3 are research programs.
Priorities carried in the source material are weak evidence and are treated as such. Of the 46 rows in the source’s own master matrix, 30 are graded “Very high” and 15 “High”, which is under half a bit of information. Where a priority appears in this catalog it reflects three observable things instead: whether the problem blocks a decision-grade estimand, whether any method addresses it at all, and whether any software implements it.

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 1: change current practice now
These need no new theory. They are conventions the field could adopt in its next submission.

Declare one decision target population. Do not let data availability choose it implicitly. See estimands and target populations.
Separate conditional and marginal estimands. Do not combine a conditional regression coefficient with a published marginal effect without justifying the combination.
Prefer anchored analyses whenever a credible randomized path exists. Label unanchored methods as cross-study causal reconstructions, not routine adjustments. See the method landscape.
Require formal quantitative bias analysis for any decision-grade unanchored comparison. At minimum quantify omitted prognostic and modifier bias plus the most credible selection, measurement, or design threat. Otherwise label the result exploratory. See quantitative bias analysis.
Report support and influence, not effective sample size alone. An adjusted study that does not influence the decision contrast is not evidence for that contrast. See positivity, overlap and extrapolation.
Expose the bridge in a disconnected network. State exactly which parameter carries information across the gap. See disconnected networks.
Use target-standardized outcomes for non-collapsible and survival measures. Do not treat odds ratios and hazard ratios as population-invariant decision inputs.
Distinguish sampling, target-distribution, sensitivity, prior, and bridge uncertainty. An ordinary confidence or credible interval usually conditions on every major structural assumption being true.
Make sensitivity analysis decision-based, and joint where biases could interact. Report how much plausible bias changes the recommendation, and whether biases cancel or reinforce. One-at-a-time analyses can make a cancellation accident look like robustness.







NoteThe one-page test



A committee-facing summary should answer nine questions. If an analysis cannot, the problem is not the statistics.
What is being estimated? For which population? Which comparisons are supported by randomization? What connects any disconnected evidence? Which variables are assumed to remove population differences? Where is overlap weak? What is data-driven versus prior-driven or bridge-driven? Which residual biases were quantified, from what parameter sources? How much assumption violation changes the decision?

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 2: develop and validate next
Tractable programs where a first publishable contribution is within reach.

Estimand-specific deterministic and probabilistic bias analysis for matching, outcome regression, and unanchored meta-regression
Multiple-bias analysis combining confounding, selection, measurement, censoring, and design drift, with dependence preserved between bias parameters
Target-standardized multilevel network meta-regression, including the component case
Doubly robust network transport with study-level cross-fitting, nested inside explicit residual-bias analysis rather than presented as a substitute for it
Partial-identification and bias-function modules in mainstream software
Separation of within-study from between-study effect modification
Subnetwork-specific component drift with robust borrowing
Non-proportional-hazards, restricted-mean-survival, and multistate population adjustment, plus survival-specific bias analysis
Target-distribution uncertainty and distributionally robust standardization
Optimal individual-patient-data acquisition and bridging-trial design
Public validation datasets and cross-package benchmarks

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 3: high risk, high reward
Where the payoff is large and the probability of a clean result is not.

Federated cross-sponsor evidence synthesis
Mechanistic and statistical hybrid bridges
Invariant component effects across environments
Probabilistic component ontologies and treatment embeddings
Proximal methods using validated proxies for unmeasured modifiers
Graph-learning tools for design and diagnostics
Sequential and dynamic-regime indirect comparisons
Privacy-preserving release of target joint-distribution summaries

title: A prioritized agenda
section: What the field does not need
text:
What the field does not need
Stated plainly, because an agenda that only adds is not an agenda.

Another weight optimizer with no estimand contribution
Another package reproducing conventional matching under different function names
Simulation studies restricted to linear models, good overlap, measured modifiers, and correctly specified outcomes, which is to say studies run where every method works
Disconnected-network analyses reporting one narrow interval and no bridge sensitivity
Black-box machine-learning outcome regression evaluated only by predictive accuracy
Component models that add every pairwise interaction without identification or hierarchy
Ranking metrics presented without uncertainty or decision relevance

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
The organizing discipline

No effect estimate without an estimand, no disconnected estimate without a stated bridge, no population-adjusted estimate without a named target, and no structural bridge without fragility or partial-identification analysis.

title: The method landscape
text: The catalog is organized by problem. This page is organized by method: which approach answers which question, what each one assumes, and where each one fails. It exists so an entry in the catalog can be read against the method it constrains.

title: The method landscape
text:
Choosing a method





flowchart LR
    A[Decision problem] --> B{Connected randomised network?}
    B -- Yes --> C{Effect modifiers plausibly balanced?}
    C -- Largely yes --> D[Standard ITC / NMA]
    C -- No, IPD available in subset --> E[Anchored PAIC]
    E --> F[ML-NMR preferred when feasible]
    E --> G[MAIC or STC only with explicit diagnostics]
    B -- No --> H{Single-arm or disconnected evidence?}
    H -- Yes --> I[Unanchored comparison]
    I --> J{Conditional constancy plausible?}
    J -- Weak --> K[Do not make strong causal claims]
    J -- Strong but uncertain --> L[Unanchored MAIC / STC / ML-UMR plus aggressive sensitivity analysis]
    H --> M[Alternative linking: ALM, baseline RE, dose-response MBNMA, class effects]






The branch that matters most is the one ending in “do not make strong causal claims.” That is a legitimate destination, not a failure of the analysis.

title: The method landscape
text:
Where the bias enters





flowchart TB
    X[Measured baseline covariates] --> S[Study membership]
    X --> Y[Outcome]
    Z[Effect modifiers] --> T[Treatment effect]
    Z --> S
    T --> Y
    U[Unmeasured design / care differences] --> S
    U --> Y
    O[Overlap quality] --> W[Weight stability / extrapolation]
    W --> Y






Read this for what it says about \(U\). Weighting and outcome regression both act on \(X\) and \(Z\). If the determinants of the cross-study outcome difference sit in \(U\) instead, no amount of balancing on \(X\) repairs the comparison; at best it disguises the bias more elegantly. That observation is why quantitative bias analysis is the largest category in this catalog.

title: The method landscape
text:
What each method identifies











Method
Evidence structure
Nominal estimand
Main identifying assumptions
Principal unresolved weakness




Bucher adjusted ITC
Two connected RCTs, common comparator
Relative effect in an implicitly common population
Transitivity; compatible effect scale; no material modifier imbalance
No explicit target population; fragile to modifier imbalance and design differences


Aggregate-data NMA
Connected RCT network
Network relative effects
Homogeneity, transitivity, consistency
Population mismatch and effect modification often only weakly assessed


IPD-NMA
IPD from all or many trials
Conditional or standardized effects
Correct individual-level model; exchangeability; IPD availability mechanism
IPD availability is selective; high-dimensional interactions remain difficult


Anchored MAIC
IPD index trial, AgD comparator, common comparator
Usually a marginal effect in the AgD trial population
All relevant modifiers balanced; overlap; correct weighting moments
ESS collapse, incomplete moments, target ambiguity, non-collapsibility, second-stage transport


Anchored STC
IPD index trial, AgD comparator, common comparator
Often a conditional effect at target means unless standardized
Correct outcome model; all relevant modifiers included; valid extrapolation
Model misspecification; conditional and marginal incompatibility; target joint distribution unavailable


Parametric g-computation
IPD source plus target summaries
Compatible marginal effect in a specified target
Correct outcome model and target-distribution model
Sensitive to misspecification; target-summary uncertainty usually ignored


ML-NMR
Mixed IPD and AgD in a connected network
Population-specific effects from one hierarchical model
Conditional constancy; individual-level model; integration distribution
Computational burden; partial identifiability; within and between interaction conflation


Unanchored MAIC or STC
Disconnected trials or single-arm studies
Cross-study contrast in a chosen target
All prognostic factors and modifiers that differ across studies measured and correctly adjusted
No randomization anchor; extreme vulnerability to omitted variables and design heterogeneity


Baseline synthesis, reference prediction
Disconnected AgD, possibly single-arm
Relative effects linked through baseline-outcome structure
Exchangeable or modelled baseline effects; correct arm-level model
Baseline risk is not a universal bridge; ecological and design confounding remain


Dose-response MBNMA
Treatments linked through dose or exposure
Effects along a shared dose-response function
Common pharmacologic curve form and modifiers
A wrong curve or class assumption produces precise but artificial links


Class-effect NMA
Treatments grouped into classes
Shrunk treatment effects and class contrasts
Within-class exchangeability; correct class variance
Class definitions are contestable and may hide genuine heterogeneity


Additive CNMA
Multicomponent treatments sharing components
Component and reconstructed treatment effects
Additivity; stable component effects across subnetworks
Cross-gap component constancy; synergy and treatment-version differences may invalidate the bridge


Component ML-NMR
Component network with mixed IPD and AgD
Component-adjusted contrasts at target covariate values
CNMA assumptions plus transportability and stable component-by-modifier interactions
Strong, partly untestable structural assumptions; marginal standardization incomplete


Doubly robust transport
Source IPD plus target IPD or adequate summaries
Target-population marginal effect
Conditional exchangeability plus either a correct weight model or a correct outcome model
No protection against unmeasured modifiers, positivity failure, or both models being wrong


Partial identification
Any structure with uncertain assumptions
Bounds or a bias-adjusted set
Explicit bounds rather than point identification
Requires defensible sensitivity parameters; less convenient for decision models




This table is not a ladder. A richer model helps only when its added structure is scientifically defensible and adequately informed by data. A faster sampler does not cure non-identification, a doubly robust estimator does not cure positivity failure, perfect covariate balance does not cure unmeasured effect modification, and a narrow interval does not establish that the target population was the right one.

title: The method landscape
text:
How to evaluate a method
Simulation studies in this field routinely report bias without naming the population-specific estimand the bias is relative to, which makes the number uninterpretable. A usable evaluation covers six families at minimum.








Metric family
Minimum metrics




Estimand recovery
Bias, relative bias, RMSE, mean absolute error, sign error, target-standardized bias


Uncertainty calibration
95% coverage, empirical to nominal standard-error ratio, posterior calibration, type I error, power


Decision quality
Incremental net-benefit decision error, wrong-treatment probability, rank-reversal frequency


Overlap and weighting
ESS, ESS over nominal \(n\), coefficient of variation of weights, maximum weight, entropy, proportion trimmed


Model adequacy
Calibration slope, posterior predictive checks, leave-one-study-out predictive error, divergence counts, \(\hat{R}\), effective posterior draws


Computation and reproducibility
Runtime, failure rate, seed sensitivity, sensitivity to starting values, container reproducibility




The decision-quality row is the one most often omitted. A method that is slightly more biased but better calibrated for a reimbursement decision may be preferable to one that looks efficient but is anti-conservative when overlap is weak.





flowchart LR
    A[Define estimand] --> B[Data-generating mechanism]
    B --> C[Connected / disconnected evidence]
    C --> D[Manipulate: overlap, modifiers, misspecification]
    D --> E[Fit competing methods]
    E --> F[Evaluate against the declared estimand]
    F --> G[Publish code, seeds, manifests]

title: The method landscape
text:
Software
Verified against CRAN and GitHub during the audit; versions as at 25 July 2026.




Package
Status
Strengths
Cautions




multinma
CRAN 0.9.1
The most mature open Bayesian NMA, NMR, and ML-NMR platform; mixed IPD and AgD; target integration; class effects
Runtime and integration burden; disconnected-network support sits in an open, unmerged pull request


maicplus
CRAN 0.1.2
Maintained MAIC workflow; anchored and unanchored binary and survival analyses
Open needs include continuous and count outcomes, trimming, weight-estimation-aware variance, and non-proportional-hazards measures


netmeta
CRAN 3.6-1
Mature frequentist NMA; component NMA through discomb; rare-event methods
Not a population-transport platform


outstandR
Active
Compatible marginal effects by model-based standardization
Pairwise focus; sensitive to the target distribution and outcome model


drMAIC
CRAN 0.1.0
Early doubly robust MAIC with diagnostics
New; requires independent audit and adversarial simulation


gemtc, MBNMAdose, crossnma
CRAN
Bayesian NMA, dose-response linking, cross-design synthesis
None has a native population-transport layer




Two packages that appear in older workflows are no longer maintained. maic was archived from CRAN on 22 July 2025 because the maintainer’s email had become undeliverable, and Roche/MAIC states in its own README that it “is no longer developed”, recommending maicplus instead. Legacy installs belong in reproducibility archaeology, not in a new workflow.
No package unifies target-population definition, connected and disconnected evidence, marginal and conditional estimands, doubly robust transport, component structure, complex outcomes, missing data, sensitivity analysis, and regulatory reporting. That gap is itself catalogued, under software and benchmarks.

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text: ADJ-01 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text:
Statement
PAIC has already been restated in transportability and estimand terms: Chandler and Ishak (arXiv:2602.17041) reframe PAICs as transportability problems and show that pairwise PAIC identifies an effect defined in the comparator population, so applying it elsewhere is an additional transport step, and Remiro-Azocar (arXiv:2210.01757) treats the transportability of marginal versus conditional estimands in evidence synthesis. The estimators the source calls underused also exist for PAIC: Park et al. (doi:10.1016/j.jval.2023.11.011) implement and compare inverse odds weighting, regression adjustment and a doubly robust method for unanchored time-to-event comparisons, Campbell and Remiro-Azocar (arXiv:2505.00113) give augmented doubly robust MAIC, and drMAIC 0.1.0 ships it. What has not been done is the usability half: no transportability-first workflow, guidance document or reporting template matches MAIC’s one-page explanation, and routine HTA submissions still do not use these estimators. One auditor read that remainder as a workflow and communication objective rather than a well-posed statistical open problem.

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text:
Why it is open
The recasting exists on paper but nothing carries it into practice. The transport framing requires nuisance models, an explicit target covariate distribution and a diagnostic suite that MAIC’s single weighting step conceals, so the explainable option keeps winning over the more rigorous one. No guidance, training material or reporting template has been rebuilt around the transport vocabulary, so a submission written in transport terms costs the analyst more and buys no procedural credit. The case where the framing matters most, a target described only by published summaries, is also the case where standard transport estimators do not apply directly, so the umbrella cannot simply be imported.

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler & Ishak, Reframing Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons as a Transportability Problem: An Estimand-Based Perspective and Implications for Health Technology Assessment (2026)
Performs the recasting this entry called open: formalizes transportability in PAIC from an estimand perspective, shows pairwise PAIC identifies a comparator-population effect and that using it elsewhere is an extra transport step. Does not address the accessibility half.


Remiro-Azocar, Transportability of model-based estimands in evidence synthesis, Stat Med 2024;43(22):4217-4249
Transportability of marginal versus conditional estimands across studies in evidence synthesis, including the non-collapsibility obstruction.


Park et al., Unanchored Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Methods for Time-to-Event Outcomes Using Inverse Odds Weighting, Regression Adjustment, and Doubly Robust Methods, Value in Health 2024
Implements and compares inverse odds weighting, regression adjustment and a doubly robust method for unanchored PAIC with time-to-event outcomes; contradicts the claim that PAIC methodology underuses all three.


Campbell & Remiro-Azocar, Doubly robust augmented weighting estimators for the analysis of externally controlled single-arm trials and unanchored indirect treatment comparisons (2025)
Adds doubly robust augmentation (outcome model plus balancing weights) to MAIC for unanchored and external-control comparisons.


drMAIC 0.1.0: Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA
Ships doubly robust MAIC with NICE DSU TSD18-aligned outputs, so the doubly robust option is available to practitioners rather than only in theory.

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The derivation work is done, so the direction is dissemination and tooling rather than a new framework: convert the published estimand-based recasting into a workflow, checklist and reporting template whose inputs, outputs and one-page explanation are as simple as MAIC’s. Validate the doubly robust and inverse-odds estimators that already exist for PAIC in realistic HTA settings and get them into guidance, so the causally principled option becomes the operationally convenient one. Measure success by whether a committee can follow the analysis, not by whether the estimator is new.

title: No transportability-first PAIC workflow matches MAIC’s usability
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. PAIC has now been formally restated in transportability/estimand terms in the methods literature, but that restatement has not been converted into a workflow, guidance and reporting template with MAIC’s operational simplicity, and routine HTA submissions still do not use inverse-odds, standardisation or doubly robust estimators.
The source titled this. “Recasting PAIC as a transportability problem without losing usability” The title poses the transportability recasting as the open work, but the audit found it already published (arXiv:2602.17041, arXiv:2210.01757), leaving only the usability half.
The source said. “Population-adjusted indirect comparison is a restricted case of the causal transportability problem, yet it is practised as a set of bespoke HTA estimators with their own vocabulary. The open question is whether PAIC can be rebuilt on an explicit source/target transport framework while keeping the practical accessibility that made MAIC attractive.”
What was wrong with it. The source cited nothing and claimed both that the recasting was undone and that PAIC underuses inverse-odds weighting, standardization and doubly robust estimators; the literature auditor found the recasting published (arXiv:2602.17041, arXiv:2210.01757) and all three estimators implemented for PAIC (doi:10.1016/j.jval.2023.11.011, arXiv:2505.00113, drMAIC 0.1.0). The claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced; what survives is the usability half, which GPT-5.6 Sol read as a workflow objective rather than a statistical problem.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted-prior search finds a near-literal hit: Chandler and Ishak (arXiv:2602.17041, 2026) reframe PAICs as transportability problems from an estimand-based HTA perspective, distinguish conditional versus marginal transport, and clarify when SEMA alone fails for non-collapsible measures. That paper formalizes and diagnoses the dual-transport structure of pairwise MAIC/STC; it does not ship a transportability-first workflow with MAIC-like one-page accessibility, software, training, or reporting templates. Separately, Campbell and Remiro-Azócar (arXiv:2505.00113, 2025) import doubly robust augmentation into entropy-balancing MAIC for unanchored and external-control settings, so C4 is already partly outdated for pairwise unanchored work. C2 is supported as a restricted-case relationship; C3 remains broadly true of HTA practice; C6 is only partly true because target-AgD transport methods exist but still struggle where only published summaries are available; C8 and C9 remain largely open on the usability half of the dual requirement. Queries: PAIC transportability Remiro/Phillippo; Chandler PAIC transportability; DR MAIC; TransportHealth; RSM/SiM 2024–2026 PAIC transport; NICE DSU/EUnetHTA 2025–2026.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. prior_work is empty, yet a preprint whose title is almost this entry’s title exists and is cited elsewhere in this same corpus (EST-02, EST-03): Chandler & Ishak, ‘Reframing Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons as a Transportability Problem: An Estimand-Based Perspective and Implications for HTA’ (arXiv:2602.17041, Feb 2026, rev. Jul 2026). Its abstract: ‘We examine and formalize transportability in PAICs from an estimand-based perspective’ and ‘pairwise PAIC approaches typically identify effects defined in the comparator population and … applying these estimates to other populations entails an additional, often implicit, transport step.’ Remiro-Azocar (arXiv:2210.01757, Stat Med 2024) does the same for transportability of estimands. The recast half is done. The ‘underuses inverse-odds weighting, standardisation and doubly robust estimators’ claim is also weak: Park et al. (Value in Health 2024) implement exactly those three for unanchored PAIC, Campbell & Remiro-Azocar (arXiv:2505.00113) give augmented doubly robust MAIC, and drMAIC 0.1.0 ships it. What genuinely remains open is the usability half: no transportability-first workflow matches MAIC’s one-page explanation. Cites arxiv:2602.17041: Performs the recasting this entry calls open: formalizes transportability in PAIC from an estimand perspective, shows pairwise PAIC identifies a comparator-population effect and that using it elsewhere is an extra transport step. Does NOT address the accessibility/usability half.. Cites arxiv:2210.01757: Transportability of marginal vs conditional estimands across studies in evidence synthesis, including the non-collapsibility obstruction.. Cites doi:10.1016/j.jval.2023.11.011: Directly contradicts ‘PAIC underuses inverse-odds weighting, standardisation and doubly robust estimators’ at the methods level; all three are implemented and compared for time-to-event PAIC.. Cites cran:drMAIC 0.1.0: Ships doubly robust MAIC with NICE DSU TSD18-aligned outputs, so the doubly robust option is available to practitioners, not only in theory..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

not-a-problem / overstated. As phrased, this is a workflow and communication objective rather than a well-posed statistical open problem. C2 is defensible only after specifying the source, target, causal estimand, treatment versions, conditional transportability and positivity; PAIC procedures are not automatically valid transport estimators. C3-C5 and C7-C10 are unsourced empirical, causal or normative assertions, not mathematical consequences. Aggregate-only targets make direct transport estimation harder; that does not establish C6’s claim that the framing matters “most” there. The asserted very-high severity is therefore unsupported.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search finds a near-literal hit: Chandler and Ishak (arXiv:2602.17041, 2026) reframe PAICs as transportability problems from an estimand-based HTA perspective, distinguish conditional versus marginal transport, and clarify when SEMA alone fails for non-collapsible measures. That paper formalizes and diagnoses the dual-transport structure of pairwise MAIC/STC; it does not ship a transportability-first workflow with MAIC-like one-page accessibility, software, training, or reporting templates. Separately, Campbell and Remiro-Azócar (arXiv:2505.00113, 2025) import doubly robust augmentation into entropy-balancing MAIC for unanchored and external-control settings, so C4 is already partly outdated for pairwise unanchored work. C2 is supported as a restricted-case relationship; C3 remains broadly true of HTA practice; C6 is only partly true because target-AgD transport methods exist but still struggle where only published summaries are available; C8 and C9 remain largely open on the usability half of the dual requirement. Closes the pure-vocabulary gap; does not close the MAIC-level accessibility product gap.. Cites arxiv:2505.00113: Imports DR (outcome model plus balancing weights) into MAIC-style PAIC for unanchored/external-control pairwise settings. Does not rebuild a full transportability-first HTA stack or network workflow..

title: Efficient influence-function transport estimators for ITC networks
text:
Statement
multinma’s ML-NMR already produces population-average marginal treatment effects in a chosen target population across a connected network with partial individual data, through marginal_effects(), and Dahabreh et al. (doi:10.1111/biom.13716) give a doubly robust, influence-function-based estimator of target-population potential-outcome means from a collection of randomized trials. What does not exist is the specific object proposed here: a semiparametric-efficient, cross-fitted efficient-influence-function estimator defined over a mixed individual and aggregate-data likelihood that preserves within-study randomization and multi-arm covariance and delivers valid inference when the number of studies is small. The entry’s negative claims survive scrutiny: double robustness covers the two nuisance models only, so unmeasured effect modification, absent overlap, a false network bridge and, in the component extension, a wrong additivity structure all pass through untouched.

title: Efficient influence-function transport estimators for ITC networks
text:
Why it is open
An efficient influence function cannot be written down until the observed-data experiment is specified: which quantities are sampled, what the aggregate summaries are as random objects, what the independent units are and which asymptotic regime is in force. Published aggregate estimates are not automatically likelihood contributions, and the mixed likelihood is not a single i.i.d. sample, so the usual efficiency and cross-fitting arguments do not transfer; cross-fitting organized by study is justified only when studies are the relevant independent units. With few studies the asymptotic regime behind influence-function inference and the rate conditions behind debiased machine learning are strained, though GPT-5.6 Sol noted this is not universal if another justified regime applies. The component extension is not a change of design matrix alone: it imposes a structural model whose identification depends on row-space conditions and treatment-version assumptions, and it needs its own influence-function derivation.

title: Efficient influence-function transport estimators for ITC networks
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Specify the observed-data model for a mixed individual and aggregate-data network first, then derive the efficient influence function for arm-level potential outcomes in a declared target population, with cross-fitting organized by whatever the independent units turn out to be. title: Efficient influence-function transport estimators for ITC networks
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No semiparametric-efficient, influence-function-based estimator exists for a connected network with mixed IPD and aggregate data that preserves multi-arm covariance and delivers valid small-study inference; likelihood-based ML-NMR and doubly robust multi-trial transport estimators already deliver target-population marginal estimands by other routes.
The source said. “No estimator currently targets marginal, policy-relevant potential outcomes in a chosen population across a connected treatment network in which IPD are available for only some studies. The proposal is an AIPW/TMLE-style efficient influence-function estimator that combines an outcome model and a study-participation model, uses cross-fitted flexible nuisance estimation organized by study, preserves within-study randomization and multi-arm covariance, uses aggregate-data likelihood contributions where IPD are absent, and extends to components by replacing treatment indicators with component and interaction design vectors.”
What was wrong with it. The source opened by saying no estimator targets marginal, policy-relevant potential outcomes in a chosen population across a connected network with partial individual data. The literature auditor showed multinma’s ML-NMR and marginal_effects() do exactly that, and that Dahabreh et al. (doi:10.1111/biom.13716) supply an influence-function-based multi-trial transport estimator; what remains open is the efficiency-theory version over a mixed individual and aggregate-data likelihood.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The lead sentence, ‘No estimator currently targets marginal, policy-relevant potential outcomes in a chosen population across a connected treatment network in which IPD are available for only some studies’, is false as written. ML-NMR in multinma does precisely this, and multinma’s marginal_effects() ‘generates population-average marginal treatment effects … formed from population-average absolute predictions’; the package documents that estimates can be produced ‘for an external target population’. Separately, Dahabreh et al. (Biometrics 2023;79:1057-1072, doi:10.1111/biom.13716) give a doubly robust, influence-function-based estimator of the potential outcome mean in a target population from a collection of randomized trials, and Vo et al. (arXiv:2503.05634) extend causal meta-analysis to trials with inaccessible IPD. What is genuinely absent is the specific object proposed: a cross-fitted efficient-influence-function estimator over a mixed IPD/AgD likelihood that preserves within-study randomization and multi-arm covariance, with valid inference at small study counts. The entry’s own negative claims (AIPW/TMLE cannot fix unmeasured effect modification, absent overlap, a false bridge; DML rate conditions fail with few studies) are all defensible. Cites doi:10.1111/biom.13716: Covers the all-IPD multi-trial case: doubly robust, efficiency-theory-based estimator of arm-level potential outcome means in a target population. Does not cover mixed IPD/AgD networks or multi-arm covariance.. Cites https://dmphillippo.github.io/multinma/reference/marginal_effects.html: Delivers population-average marginal treatment effects in a chosen target population across a connected network with partial IPD, by Bayesian ML-NMR rather than by an efficient influence function..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1-C5, C9, C12-C13 and C19-C20 capture sound principles under explicit consistency, conditional transportability, positivity and network-identification assumptions. The rest overstates what follows. An efficient influence function cannot be specified until the observed-data experiment, aggregate summaries, sampling units and asymptotic regime are defined; published aggregate estimates are not automatically likelihood contributions. Cross-fitting by study is appropriate only when studies are the relevant independent units, and few studies do not universally invalidate DML if another justified asymptotic regime applies. Flexible nuisance learning does not automatically improve estimation. A false bridge may sometimes be flagged by network inconsistency, although AIPW cannot generally identify or repair it. Arm-level absolute outcomes require stronger baseline-risk transport assumptions than relative effects. Most importantly, replacing treatment indicators with component vectors is not a complete extension: it imposes a component structural model and requires rank or row-space identification, treatment-version assumptions and revised nuisance and influence-function derivations. The claimed nonexistence of any current estimator is a literature claim outside this technical audit.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Pieces exist but not the joint object. Dahabreh et al. (Biometrics 2023) and CausalMetaR (Wang et al.; arXiv:2402.04341) give multi-trial transport with robust/efficient estimators to a declared target, typically assuming richer multi-source individual-level structure and a target sample, not a mixed IPD/AgD connected treatment network with multi-arm covariance and AgD likelihood contributions. Campbell and Remiro-Azócar DR-MAIC covers pairwise unanchored augmentation, not network EIF. multinma/crossnma implement mixed IPD/AgD NMA/ML-NMR without participation models or EIF/TMLE foundations. No retrieved work jointly delivers: EIF for arm-level potential outcomes in one policy population, study-organized cross-fitting, multi-arm covariance, AgD likelihood where IPD are missing, small-K valid uncertainty, and component design-vector extension with explicit non-identification statements. Caveat claims (unmeasured effect modification, no overlap, false bridge, component additivity outside DR) are consistent with identification theory and are not solved by any paper. C1–C3 and C7–C8 are directions with partial pairwise/multi-trial prior art, not completed network solutions. Queries: EIF AIPW TMLE network meta mixed IPD AgD; Dahabreh multi-trial transport; CausalMetaR; DR MAIC network; debiased ML few studies NMA.

Decision path

title: Optimal transport for distributional rather than moment balance
text: ADJ-05 Partially addressed High priority Emerging

title: Optimal transport for distributional rather than moment balance
text:
Statement
Optimal-transport weighting for source-to-target distributional balance already exists in general causal inference: Dunipace (arXiv:2109.01991) builds weights by minimizing an optimal transport distance between a source and a target population, is semiparametrically efficient and model-free, and can impose moment constraints as well. It requires samples from both distributions, so the PAIC case that matters, a target described by a published table of marginals, is untouched. The overlap claim also needs narrowing: transport cost is a metric-, scaling- and regularization-dependent global discrepancy rather than a positivity measure, so a small cost does not rule out local support failure and a large cost can reflect benign displacement. A 2025 preprint (arXiv:2511.04658) does use an optimal transport distance as an operational shift measure for choosing study sites.

title: Optimal transport for distributional rather than moment balance
text:
Why it is open
Optimal transport rebalances existing mass and manufactures no observations where the source trial has none, so a coupling that moves covariate mass creates no outcome evidence and source-unit reweighting stays inside source support. Distributional matching needs a target joint distribution, and aggregate publications report marginals, which do not recover the dependence structure or the tails the method is supposed to balance. Matching a distribution better also leaves the causal assumptions untouched: neither conditional constancy nor transitivity becomes more plausible because the tails line up.
