title: No versioned intervention ontology maps onto CNMA component matrices
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Map the existing intervention ontologies onto CNMA component matrices rather than building a new ontology, so that dose, schedule, delivery, and setting attributes become the source of the component coding and the equivalence decisions become auditable data that can be rerun under alternative groupings. Use dose-response models where dose is the dimension that varies, since that machinery is released and validated. The genuinely new work is a hierarchical equivalence-class or embedding model in which related component versions borrow strength with a shrinkage parameter rather than being forced to share one.

title: No versioned intervention ontology maps onto CNMA component matrices
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No component ontology is wired into component NMA or component PAIC software: existing versioned, machine-readable intervention ontologies (BCIO and its mode-of-delivery and setting modules) record dose, schedule and delivery, but nothing maps them onto CNMA component matrices, and no hierarchical equivalence-class model lets related component versions borrow strength without being forced to share a parameter.
The source titled this. “Component ontology is label-based, not versioned or quantitative” The title says component ontology is not versioned or quantitative, but the audit found three published versioned OWL ontologies with dose and delivery metadata plus continuous dose modeling in netdose.
The source said. “Components in current component NMA and component PAIC are defined by text labels. The same label can hide differences in dose, schedule, formulation, device, adherence, provider skill, and cointerventions, so two studies nominally sharing a component may not share a parameter.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no versioned component ontology with dose and intensity metadata exists and that equivalence decisions are analyst judgment buried in code. The literature auditor found three published, versioned OWL ontologies covering exactly that metadata (BCIO, Mode of Delivery, Intervention Setting); Grok 4.5 added that dose can be modeled continuously via dose-response NMA and the CRAN package netdose; and GPT-5.6 Sol found that choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 stores the chosen C.matrix in the fitted network object, so the coding is recorded and rerunnable even though no ontology backs it.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Label-based component coding is still the default in CNMA practice (Veroniki et al. 2026 treat component definition/coding as a critical node-making decision and point to TIDieR for richer trial reporting, not a machine-versioned ontology). Partial prior art does exist on one dimension of versioning: quantitative dose. Pedder et al. 2021 show dose–response MBNMA can link disconnected networks via shared dose-response assumptions; Petropoulou, Rücker, and Schwarzer 2026 introduce frequentist DR-NMA with linear/nonlinear dose functions and ship the CRAN package netdose (2026). Watt et al. 2022 discuss hierarchical dose nodes. Wigle et al. arXiv:2605.15142 (2026) address estimability and ranking hierarchies of components/treatments, not versioned implementation attributes. No versioned component ontology covering dose, schedule, formulation, device, adherence, provider skill, and cointerventions with auditable equivalence classes was found for CNMA/PAIC. Hierarchical embeddings that share strength without forcing equality of versions were not found in CNMA software. Caveat: dose-response methods partially solve quantitative intensity; they do not close the broader ontology claim.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim ‘No versioned component ontology with dose and intensity metadata currently exists’ is false as a field-level statement. The Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology, built inside the Wellcome-funded Human Behaviour-Change Project explicitly for evidence synthesis, is a versioned, machine-readable OWL ontology whose upper level specifies 42 entities covering intervention content and delivery; intervention content is decomposed into behaviour change techniques plus dose, and the companion Mode of Delivery Ontology gives 65 modes across 15 upper classes with measured inter-rater reliability (kappa 0.80 for trained annotators), with a further Setting Ontology of 72 entities. The TIDieR reporting checklist independently mandates dose, schedule and delivery reporting (I did not retrieve it, so I give no locator). What is genuinely absent is any linkage of these ontologies to CNMA/CPAIC component coding, and any equivalence-class model that lets related component versions share a prior without being forced equal. The entry has zero prior_work, which is the more serious defect: this is an area with a decade of published ontology engineering. Cites doi:10.12688/wellcomeopenres.15902.2: A versioned, machine-readable ontology of intervention components built for evidence synthesis already exists; it is not yet connected to CNMA.. Cites doi:10.12688/wellcomeopenres.15906.2: Supplies the ‘delivery/formulation/device’ metadata layer the entry says does not exist, in OWL, with tested inter-rater reliability.. Cites doi:10.12688/wellcomeopenres.15904.1: Context/setting metadata layer, same programme; further evidence the ontology infrastructure exists..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is source-confirmed for cpaic, not a mathematical necessity of component NMA: build_C_matrix() splits treatment strings on sep.comps and creates a binary C matrix. C2 is technically correct. cpaic has no structured fields for dose, schedule, formulation, device, adherence, delivery, or hierarchical equivalence, supporting the package-specific versions of C3 and C4; software-wide claims are outside this audit. C5 applies when component coefficients receive a causal interpretation; purely statistical prediction requires the coding to support the assumed common additive surface, not necessarily a separately manipulable causal component. The report overstates that equivalence decisions cannot be recorded or audited: cpaic stores the treatment labels, component names, separator, and exact C.matrix in the network object, and these inputs can be version-controlled or rerun under alternative labels. Distinct versions can already be encoded as distinct component labels, albeit without structured metadata or borrowing. C6 is a reasonable data-governance direction. For C7, embeddings could support graded borrowing, but an embedding alone neither defines causal equivalence nor guarantees valid effect sharing. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: The exact chosen component mapping is retained in the fitted network object, making the coding reproducible and auditable even though no formal ontology exists..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Label-based component coding is still the default in CNMA practice (Veroniki et al. 2026 treat component definition/coding as a critical node-making decision and point to TIDieR for richer trial reporting, not a machine-versioned ontology). Partial prior art does exist on one dimension of versioning: quantitative dose. Pedder et al. 2021 show dose–response MBNMA can link disconnected networks via shared dose-response assumptions; Petropoulou, Rücker, and Schwarzer 2026 introduce frequentist DR-NMA with linear/nonlinear dose functions and ship the CRAN package netdose (2026). Watt et al. 2022 discuss hierarchical dose nodes. Wigle et al. arXiv:2605.15142 (2026) address estimability and ranking hierarchies of components/treatments, not versioned implementation attributes. No versioned component ontology covering dose, schedule, formulation, device, adherence, provider skill, and cointerventions with auditable equivalence classes was found for CNMA/PAIC. Hierarchical embeddings that share strength without forcing equality of versions were not found in CNMA software. Caveat: dose-response methods partially solve quantitative intensity; they do not close the broader ontology claim. Cites 10.1177/0272989X20983315: Shows dose–response modeling can reconnect or strengthen disconnected networks by treating dose as a quantitative shared structure rather than a pure treatment label.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-025-02754-4: Implements frequentist DR-NMA with multiple dose-response functions; associated CRAN package netdose makes quantitative dose modeling available for multi-intervention networks.. Cites cran/netdose: Released R software for dose-response NMA, addressing the dose/intensity dimension of component/version heterogeneity..

title: Causal meaning of a component effect is ambiguous
text: CMP-07 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: Causal meaning of a component effect is ambiguous
text:
Statement
The statistical estimand of a component model is well defined: implemented component ML-NMR states it as theta_t(x) = C_t’(beta + Gamma x), and row-space machinery determines which such functionals are identified. What is not defined is the causal reading of beta_c as the effect of adding component c, which additionally requires a well-defined and stable component intervention, consistency across component versions, no relevant interference, valid transport, and the assumed additivity or interaction structure. None of those conditions is formalized in any component PAIC implementation the auditors could read, and the auditors found no work connecting separable effects, component interventions, or interference to CNMA parameters.

title: Causal meaning of a component effect is ambiguous
text:
Why it is open
Component coefficients are routinely read as the effect of adding or removing a component, but the conditions that would license that reading are not stated anywhere in the component synthesis literature or in the implementations. Multiple versions of the same nominal component exist and the model does not say which one a coefficient targets, so consistency is assumed rather than argued. The relevant causal machinery for separable effects, component interventions, and interference is mature outside evidence synthesis but has not been connected to component NMA parameters, so there is no formal statement of what a component parameter identifies.

title: Causal meaning of a component effect is ambiguous
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “A component effect is treated as the change from removing or adding one component while holding the others fixed, but removing a component can change adherence, delivery, and the operation of the remaining components. The causal quantity a component coefficient targets is therefore not well defined.”
What was wrong with it. The source said the targeted quantity is not well defined and that no trial in the network randomizes single-component removal. GPT-5.6 Sol corrected both from choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: the statistical estimand is stated explicitly as theta_t(x) = C_t’(beta + Gamma x), and add-on and factorial trials do randomize component addition or removal, so what is open is the causal interpretation rather than the estimand. The literature auditor searched for separable-effects, potential-outcomes, and interference work applied to CNMA, found none, and also found no source asserting the absence, so the two auditors disagree on whether the gap is demonstrated or merely unretrieved.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): The statistical estimand is not undefined: cpaic explicitly defines component and treatment contrasts through theta_t(x)=C_t’(beta+Gamma x), and its row-space machinery determines which such functionals are identified. That partially resolves the estimand question. C1 is valid only as a warning about causal interpretation: adding or removing a component may not define a stable intervention when it changes delivery, adherence, versions, or interactions. The cpaic-specific part of C2 is supported because the package supplies no potential-outcomes definition, consistency statement for component versions, or interference model. C3 is a literature-coverage claim outside this audit. The report’s rationale is too broad in saying no trial randomizes component addition or removal: add-on and factorial trials can do exactly that, and direct single-component randomization is not necessary when a randomized contrast design identifies beta under a correctly specified additive model. A causal interpretation requires well-defined component interventions and versions, consistency, no relevant interference, valid transport, and the assumed additivity or interaction structure. This is high priority if component coefficients themselves are presented causally; it is less fundamental when the decision estimand is a well-defined complete-regimen contrast.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. PubMed searches combining separable effects, potential outcomes, interference and treatment-version concepts with component network meta-analysis returned no hits. The separable-effects and treatment-version (multiple-versions-of-treatment) literature is well developed outside evidence synthesis, but I did not retrieve specific papers in this session and will not cite what I have not read. The three claims are all absence claims about a link that has not been made, and no source I found asserts that absence, so unverifiable is the honest support vote. Independent support for the underlying worry does exist in the CNMA literature: Petropoulou et al. 2023 declined to interpret their selected interactions clinically (‘A clinical interpretation of the identified interactions was not the main focus of this work. We think that this would be futile…’), which is a published hint that component and interaction parameters lack a settled causal reading. The entry cites nothing at all; adding that reference would help.

Separable-effects theory is mature for multicomponent interventions in general causal inference, but no paper was retrieved that formally connects those frameworks to component NMA parameters or to cross-subnetwork bridges. Wigle et al. 2026 discuss statistical estimability and ranking of component effects, not causal intervention versions. Veroniki et al. 2026 stress clinical meaningfulness of component definitions but do not give potential-outcomes definitions. Queries across SIM/RSM/JCE, arXiv, and medRxiv 2022–2026 for ‘separable effects component network meta-analysis’, ‘potential outcomes CNMA’, ‘causal estimand component NMA’ returned no resolving application. Claims C1–C3 therefore still describe an open mapping problem between CNMA coefficients and well-defined interventions.

title: cMAIC combines marginal effects through an additive component model
text: CMP-09 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: cMAIC combines marginal effects through an additive component model
text:
Statement
Component MAIC reweights IPD edges to produce marginal effects and then feeds those marginal effects into an additive component model. On non-collapsible scales such as the odds ratio and hazard ratio, marginalization applies a nonlinear functional to each regimen’s component sum, so marginal component effects are not generally additive even when conditional ones are, and the resulting error is structural rather than statistical: it does not shrink with perfect covariate matching or infinite sample size. The error is zero on collapsible scales and in special covariate and effect configurations, so its practical magnitude is context-dependent. Phillippo et al. 2025 sharpen the survival case: with covariates present, marginal hazard ratios are time-varying, so they cannot be a constant additive component parameter at all.

title: cMAIC combines marginal effects through an additive component model
text:
Why it is open
Non-collapsibility means the marginal contrast is not the same functional of the component parameters as the conditional contrast, so an additivity structure holding conditionally does not carry over to the marginal scale. For time-to-event outcomes an arm-only weighted Cox coefficient is a particular marginal projection rather than a constant marginal hazard ratio, so the additive component model is being fitted to quantities that are not even stable over time. Removing the error requires either a collapsible estimand scale or reconstructing target-population arm outcomes and standardizing before forming component contrasts, both of which change what component MAIC is.

The candor of existing documentation about the irreducible bias should be preserved rather than softened.

title: cMAIC combines marginal effects through an additive component model
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Component MAIC reweights IPD edges to produce marginal effects and then feeds those marginal effects into an additive component model. On non-collapsible scales such as the odds ratio and hazard ratio, marginal component effects are not generally additive even when conditional component effects are.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors supported the claim; the corrections are scope and sourcing. GPT-5.6 Sol noted the error is zero on collapsible scales and in special configurations, so the asserted very high severity is not automatic, and the literature auditor supplied the missing reference establishing the premise and extending it to time-varying marginal hazard ratios, doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The statistical content is correct and now heavily documented, though the entry cites none of it. Phillippo, Remiro-Azocar, Heath, Baio, Dias, Ades and Welton 2025 (Res Synth Methods 16:323-349) set out exactly why marginal and conditional estimands diverge under non-collapsibility plus effect modification, show that the divergence can flip treatment rankings, and note that ‘For time-to-event outcomes, the presence of covariates implies that marginal hazard ratios are time-varying’ - which sharpens the entry’s point, because a time-varying marginal hazard ratio cannot be an additive component parameter at all. The structural, non-vanishing character of the error is right: it is a property of the estimand map, not a finite-sample bias. I found nothing that repairs additive combination of marginal component effects, so the problem is open. The claim about what cpaic’s documentation says is unverifiable from public sources. maicplus is cited only as the weighting engine, which is fair but decorative for this specific claim.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The statistical content is correct and now heavily documented, though the entry cites none of it. Phillippo, Remiro-Azocar, Heath, Baio, Dias, Ades and Welton 2025 (Res Synth Methods 16:323-349) set out exactly why marginal and conditional estimands diverge under non-collapsibility plus effect modification, show that the divergence can flip treatment rankings, and note that ‘For time-to-event outcomes, the presence of covariates implies that marginal hazard ratios are time-varying’ - which sharpens the entry’s point, because a time-varying marginal hazard ratio cannot be an additive component parameter at all. The structural, non-vanishing character of the error is right: it is a property of the estimand map, not a finite-sample bias. I found nothing that repairs additive combination of marginal component effects, so the problem is open. The claim about what cpaic’s documentation says is unverifiable from public sources. maicplus is cited only as the weighting engine, which is fair but decorative for this specific claim. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2: Does NOT solve the additive-combination problem, but is the missing citation that establishes the entry’s premise and extends it to time-varying marginal hazard ratios..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1-C4 are supported. With a conditional additive predictor, marginalization applies a nonlinear functional to each regimen’s component sum, so marginal log odds ratios generally fail component additivity. Marginal hazards are mixtures and may not even remain proportional, so an arm-only weighted Cox coefficient is a particular marginal Cox projection rather than a unique constant marginal hazard ratio. Perfect matching and infinite sample size remove estimation and transport error but not this structural projection error. The code re-estimates weights, fits an arm-only weighted outcome model, replaces the IPD edge, and passes the resulting contrast to cnma_bridge(); its documentation explicitly states the irreducible bias and recommends conditional routes where material. The caveat is that the error is zero on collapsible scales and in special covariate/effect configurations, and its practical magnitude is context-dependent, so the asserted very-high severity is not automatic.

title: Two-stage component PAIC adjusts only the IPD edges
text: CMP-11 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Two-stage component PAIC adjusts only the IPD edges
text:
Statement
In two-stage component MAIC and component STC, only edges with IPD are reweighted or re-fitted to the target population; aggregate-data-only edges enter the component bridge in their own study populations, so under effect modification the fitted component parameters combine contrasts with different population referents, and component STC additionally mixes target-profile conditional coefficients with usually marginal published aggregate contrasts. The incompatibility disappears when the relevant effects are transportable, for example with no effect modification or effectively identical populations. The coherent one-stage alternative is not hypothetical: ML-NMR gives every aggregate study its own reconstructed covariate distribution, integrates the individual-level model over it, and can predict into any target population, but no component version of that path is implemented.

title: Two-stage component PAIC adjusts only the IPD edges
text:
Why it is open
Adjusting the aggregate-only edges would require their covariate distributions, which are typically reported only as marginal summaries or not at all, so a two-stage workflow has nothing to transport them with. Labeling the output as partially target-adjusted makes the mixture visible but does not remove it, and the pooled component parameters still have no single population referent. Closing the gap requires either imputing those distributions with acknowledged uncertainty or building the component version of the one-stage integrated likelihood, which does not exist.

title: Two-stage component PAIC adjusts only the IPD edges
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “In two-stage component MAIC and component STC, only edges with IPD are reweighted or re-fitted to the target population; aggregate-data-only edges enter the component bridge as effects in their own study populations. The fitted component model therefore mixes target-population contrasts with study-population contrasts.”
What was wrong with it. The source said nothing in the fitted model records which contrasts were transported, leaving the mixture invisible, and presented the one-stage fix as hypothetical. Both are wrong: GPT-5.6 Sol found that choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 already labels the result ‘only partially target-adjusted’ in the documentation and print methods for both cmaic() and cstc(), and the literature auditor pointed to Phillippo et al. 2020, where the one-stage model is published and implemented for non-component networks.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1-C4 and C6 are correct. Both two-stage functions replace only contrasts belonging to IPD studies; aggregate-only edges remain in their original populations. Under effect modification this mixes population referents, and cSTC additionally mixes target-profile conditional coefficients with usually marginal published aggregate contrasts. The incompatibility disappears when relevant effects are transportable, for example with no effect modification or effectively identical populations. The report’s claim that the mixture is invisible and unrecorded is stale: both documentation and print methods explicitly call the result partially target-adjusted, and the fitted object retains the IPD-study information. C5 has therefore already been implemented, while transport or imputation of aggregate-only edges remains open.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The diagnosis is correct for two-stage designs and is a documented limitation of MAIC and STC generally: Phillippo et al. 2020 state that ‘current matching-adjusted indirect comparison and simulated treatment comparison methods are limited to pairwise indirect comparisons and cannot predict into a specified target population’, which is the same defect the entry describes in component form. But the entry presents the one-stage fix as hypothetical (‘Any fix therefore requires … abandoning the two-stage structure’), when the one-stage fix is published and implemented: ML-NMR gives every aggregate study its own reconstructed covariate distribution and integrates the individual-level model over it, so aggregate-only edges are not left in their own study populations, and predictions can be made into any target. That solves the mixed-referent problem for non-component networks; it does not solve it for a component bridge, which is what remains open. The multiple-imputation claim for component STC is an absence claim I cannot verify. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: The coherent one-stage model the entry describes as the required fix already exists for non-component networks: aggregate studies are fitted by integrating the individual-level model over their covariate distribution, and comparisons can be produced in any target population..

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text: CMP-13 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text:
Statement
Component ML-NMR estimates a single shared component-by-modifier interaction matrix Gamma from IPD and aggregate data together and does not separate within-trial from across-trial interaction information, so aggregate studies can pull the estimate toward a non-randomized across-trial association. It does not, however, plug in covariate means: ML-NMR integrates an individual-level model over each study’s covariate distribution precisely to avoid aggregation bias, so the ecological mechanism is not the one the source described. Aggregate data are also not categorically uninformative about Gamma, because a nonlinear integrated likelihood contains curvature-based information; in the implemented log-link case the aggregate data identify beta + log cosh(gamma) rather than beta alone. The within-trial and across-trial separation is standard practice in IPD meta-analysis and simply has not been ported to component models.

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text:
Why it is open
Between-study variation in covariate distributions is not randomized, so any association between a study’s covariate profile and its treatment effect is confounded by everything else that differs between studies, and a single Gamma lets that association share a parameter with the within-trial causal modification. The published fix for ordinary IPD meta-analysis, centering patient-level covariates at their trial mean so within-trial and across-trial interactions are separately estimated, has not been implemented for component ML-NMR, where the interaction is additionally shared across components and across subnetworks. Current implementations mitigate only by labeling whether a target contrast is supported by IPD or by aggregate arms and by excluding aggregate-only screen results from default rankings.

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hua et al. 2017
shows that centering patient-level covariates at their trial mean is required to separate within-trial from across-trial interaction information, with a worked reversal of an interaction estimate


Freeman et al. 2018
extends the within-trial and across-trial separation to IPD network meta-analysis and gives a practical framework including consistency checks between the two sources


Phillippo et al. 2020
defines ML-NMR as integrating an individual-level model over each study’s covariate distribution rather than regressing on covariate means, which is what avoids aggregation bias


Phillippo et al. 2022
describes ML-NMR as coherently synthesizing IPD and AgD while avoiding aggregation bias and non-collapsibility bias


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; fits one shared Gamma across IPD and AgD, labels each target contrast as identified by IPD, aggregate evidence, or neither, and excludes aggregate-only elements from default rankings

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the established within-trial and across-trial separation into component ML-NMR: estimate Gamma_W and Gamma_B as distinct parameters and restrict causal interaction learning to the directions actually informed by IPD, with the across-trial parameter reported separately rather than pooled in. Use the existing framework for identifying treatment-covariate interactions in IPD network meta-analysis, including its visual consistency checks between the two information sources, as the template. Keep the labeling of which contrasts are IPD-supported, since that is the partial mitigation already in place.

title: Shared Gamma conflates within- and between-study modification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Component ML-NMR would estimate a single shared component-by-modifier interaction matrix and, like ML-NMR generally, would not separate within-trial from across-trial interaction information, so aggregate studies can still pull the estimate toward a non-randomised across-trial association; unlike standard network meta-regression it does not plug in covariate means, so it does not incur aggregation bias from nonlinearity, and the within/across separation is already standard practice in IPD meta-analysis and merely needs porting to component models.
The source said. “Component ML-NMR estimates one shared component-by-modifier interaction matrix Gamma using both IPD and aggregate data. Aggregate covariate means identify ecological, between-study gradients, whereas randomization within a trial identifies only within-study effect modification, so combining them in one parameter conflates the two.”
What was wrong with it. The source said aggregate covariate means identify ecological gradients in ML-NMR; that describes standard network meta-regression, not ML-NMR, which was built to avoid aggregation bias by integrating over the covariate distribution (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579; doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162). The literature auditor also found the fix already exists outside component models: trial-mean centering separates within-trial from across-trial interaction information (Hua et al. 2017; Freeman et al. 2018), and GPT-5.6 Sol added that nonlinear aggregate likelihoods carry curvature-based information about Gamma, so the aggregate contribution is not purely ecological.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Two problems. First, the mechanism attributed to ML-NMR is wrong: ML-NMR does not regress on aggregate covariate means. Phillippo et al. 2020 built it precisely because ‘Existing meta-regression approaches incur aggregation bias’, by integrating an individual-level model over the covariate distribution; Phillippo et al. 2022 describe ML-NMR as ‘avoiding aggregation bias and noncollapsibility bias’. So ‘Aggregate-data covariate means identify ecological gradients’ describes standard network meta-regression, not ML-NMR. Second, the residual worry - that a single shared interaction does not separate within-trial from across-trial information - is real but already solved methodologically outside component models. Hua et al. 2017 show the fix (‘it is crucial to centre patient-level covariates by their mean value in each trial, in order to separate out within-trial and across-trial information’) with a worked reversal (interaction -0.011, p = 0.004 amalgamated, versus -0.007, p = 0.22 separated), and Freeman et al. 2018 give a full framework for IPD network meta-analysis. What is open is porting that separation into component ML-NMR. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.7171: Gives the established fix (trial-mean centring) that separates within-trial from across-trial interaction information; not yet applied to component or ML-NMR models.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1300: Extends the within/across separation to network meta-analysis and gives a practical framework including visual consistency checks between the two sources..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C3 and C4 are correct: randomization does not randomize study-level covariate distributions, and cpaic fits only one Gamma. C1 describes a real ecological-bias risk when aggregate information about Gamma comes from across-study distribution shifts. C2 is too categorical across the supported families. For an identity-link, first-moment aggregate contrast, the centered within-study interaction averages out. In a nonlinear integrated likelihood, however, an aggregate arm mean depends on the interaction through the entire covariate distribution; cpaic’s own log-link example identifies beta + log cosh(gamma). Such information is model-dependent and generally insufficient for nonparametric causal effect-modification identification, but it is not literally zero or reducible solely to a gradient in covariate means. The model-level separation remains open. cpaic partially mitigates it by labeling whether target contrasts are supported by IPD or only aggregate arms and excluding aggregate-only screen results from rankings by default. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Labels each target contrast as identified by IPD, aggregate evidence, or neither, exposing the information source.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Prevents aggregate-only first-order screens from entering default treatment or component hierarchies..

title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
text: CMP-15 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
text:
Statement
Component ML-NMR reconstructs each aggregate arm’s joint effect-modifier distribution from marginal summaries using parametric margins, quasi-Monte Carlo points, and a Gaussian copula, and then treats those margins and that correlation as fixed. This is inherited ML-NMR practice rather than a component-specific choice, and part of it has been addressed upstream: multinma 0.6.0 adjusts the correlation matrix used to generate integration points to the underlying Gaussian copula so output correlations better match the requested inputs. What remains open is that reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated into reported intervals in any implementation, and that a Gaussian copula imposes symmetric, tail-independent dependence which may be wrong however well the correlation is calibrated; vine copulas are not implemented.

title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
text:
Why it is open
Published target and aggregate summaries almost never include a joint distribution, so the joint must be assembled from marginals and assumed dependence, and because the outcome model is integrated over that joint through a nonlinear inverse link, errors in dependence and tails propagate directly into standardized outcomes with no target IPD to check against. The latent-to-observed correlation transformation has a closed form only for special margin combinations, so mixed and discrete margins require numerical inversion that component implementations currently approximate. Neither the component implementation nor multinma represents the reconstruction itself as a source of uncertainty in reported intervals.

title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adopt the upstream correlation calibration rather than re-deriving it, and extend it with numerical inversion for arbitrary margin combinations including mixed and discrete margins. Offer vine copulas for asymmetric and tail-dependent dependence and report sensitivity envelopes across dependence specifications, since a single Gaussian copula cannot be checked against anything. Represent target-distribution uncertainty explicitly in the posterior, use robust moment classes that bound the estimand over families of joints consistent with the reported margins, and validate against target IPD wherever it exists.

title: Target joint covariate distribution is only approximately known
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Component PAIC reconstructs the target joint covariate distribution from marginal summaries plus an assumed dependence structure, currently a Gaussian copula. Nonlinear outcome models depend on correlations, tails, and mixed margin types rather than on marginal means alone, and the mapping from a reported observed correlation to the latent Gaussian correlation is only approximate when margins are non-normal.”
What was wrong with it. The auditors split on the latent-correlation half: the literature auditor found it already corrected upstream in multinma 0.6.0’s add_integration(), while GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed the component implementation at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 still approximates it, so the text keeps the weaker claim and scopes the open part to uncertainty propagation and non-Gaussian dependence. GPT-5.6 Sol also found the source’s warning claim partly false: binary IPD covariates default to Bernoulli, but an explicit normal-margin override for a binary covariate is accepted without the claimed warning, and the issue belongs to the aggregate-data integration path rather than to the package generally.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The Gaussian-copula reconstruction is not a cpaic design choice but the published ML-NMR standard: Phillippo et al. 2020 state ‘Covariate correlation structures are accounted for by using copulas.’ More importantly, the latent-to-observed correlation problem the entry raises has an implemented upstream fix. multinma 0.6.0 NEWS: ‘The correlation matrix for generating integration points with add_integration() for ML-NMR models is now adjusted to the underlying Gaussian copula, so that the output correlations of the integration points better match the requested input correlations.’ The corresponding numerical problem - matching a target Pearson correlation through a Gaussian copula with arbitrary or discrete margins - is a solved one in the NORTA simulation literature via root-finding on the latent correlation (I did not retrieve a specific paper and give no locator). What remains genuinely open is propagating reconstruction uncertainty into reported intervals (also absent from multinma) and non-Gaussian, tail-dependent dependence such as vine copulas. Scope the entry to those two. codex dissented (open): The requested 9d150e9 source is behaviorally identical here to live aaa76c9; the later changes affect only src/Makevars.win. C1-C4, C6, and C7 are supported specifically for cmlnmr(): it constructs each AgD arm’s integration distribution using parametric margins, Sobol points, and a Gaussian copula; treats the resulting margins and correlation as fixed; approximates non-normal observed-to-latent correlations; and has no vine-copula implementation. For nonlinear inverse links, the integrated outcome generally depends on the distribution of the linear predictor, including relevant dependence and tail behavior. C5 is false in part: 0/1 IPD covariates default to Bernoulli, and gamma/lognormal/beta correlation approximations trigger a warning, but a user can explicitly override a binary covariate to a normal margin without the claimed warning. The report also generalizes a cmlnmr AgD-integration feature to cpaic generally. This is high severity only when the nonlinear estimand is materially sensitive to the unspecified dependence or tails.

Literature and prior-art check

The Gaussian-copula reconstruction is not a cpaic design choice but the published ML-NMR standard: Phillippo et al. 2020 state ‘Covariate correlation structures are accounted for by using copulas.’ More importantly, the latent-to-observed correlation problem the entry raises has an implemented upstream fix. multinma 0.6.0 NEWS: ‘The correlation matrix for generating integration points with add_integration() for ML-NMR models is now adjusted to the underlying Gaussian copula, so that the output correlations of the integration points better match the requested input correlations.’ The corresponding numerical problem - matching a target Pearson correlation through a Gaussian copula with arbitrary or discrete margins - is a solved one in the NORTA simulation literature via root-finding on the latent correlation (I did not retrieve a specific paper and give no locator). Scope the entry to those two. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Establishes copula-based joint-covariate reconstruction plus quasi-Monte Carlo integration as the published ML-NMR approach, so this is inherited field-level practice rather than a cpaic-specific choice..

C1-C4, C6, and C7 are supported specifically for cmlnmr(): it constructs each AgD arm’s integration distribution using parametric margins, Sobol points, and a Gaussian copula; treats the resulting margins and correlation as fixed; approximates non-normal observed-to-latent correlations; and has no vine-copula implementation. For nonlinear inverse links, the integrated outcome generally depends on the distribution of the linear predictor, including relevant dependence and tail behavior. C5 is false in part: 0/1 IPD covariates default to Bernoulli, and gamma/lognormal/beta correlation approximations trigger a warning, but a user can explicitly override a binary covariate to a normal margin without the claimed warning. The report also generalizes a cmlnmr AgD-integration feature to cpaic generally. This is high severity only when the nonlinear estimand is materially sensitive to the unspecified dependence or tails.

open / supported. Inverted prior search did not find a PAIC/ML-NMR or component-PAIC method that replaces approximate Gaussian-copula joint reconstruction with calibrated arbitrary-margin latent correlations, vine copulas, or posterior propagation of target-joint uncertainty. Prior art remains the same stack the problem cites: Phillippo ML-NMR/multinma use Sobol’ QMC with a Gaussian copula and document approximate latent correlations for non-normal margins; cpaic 0.1.0 reimplements that pattern and documents the same approximations and warnings. title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
text: CMP-17 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
text:
Statement
Component survival models condition on pseudo-IPD reconstructed from digitized Kaplan-Meier curves and at-risk tables as if the event and censoring times were observed, with no reconstruction-error layer, and the implemented route further rejects event-count and person-time summaries as insufficient for its exact individual survival likelihood. Reconstruction uncertainty now has some machinery behind it: RESOLVE-IPD (arXiv 2511.01785, November 2025) extracts coordinates and explicit censoring marks from vectorized figures, drops the uniform-censoring assumption, and generates ensembles of valid labelings so that a downstream meta-analysis propagates that uncertainty. It is a preprint and its propagated uncertainty is over subgroup label assignment rather than over pixel-level curve reading or at-risk-table rounding, so it narrows the gap without closing it, and no measurement model of this kind is implemented in component PAIC.

title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
text:
Why it is open
The reconstruction pipeline turns an image plus a risk table into an exact-looking event and censoring dataset, and every downstream likelihood then treats those synthetic records as real observations. Existing work addresses fidelity and subgroup-label ambiguity, not a measurement model for pixel-level curve reading or at-risk-table rounding, so the dominant error sources still have no distribution attached. In oncology this compounds with an exact individual survival likelihood that is deliberately more demanding than event-count summaries, so the model is precise about data whose provenance is uncertain.

title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Generate multiple reconstructions and pool across them, using the ensemble machinery that already exists for subgroup labeling as the template, and extend it to pixel-level curve reading and at-risk-table rounding. Build a Bayesian measurement model for those two error sources and propagate it into the posterior rather than conditioning on one reconstruction. Report how much of the reported precision survives the propagation, since that is the number a decision maker needs.

title: Survival pseudo-IPD reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Pseudo-IPD reconstructed from digitized Kaplan-Meier curves and at-risk tables is treated as if it were observed data. Digitization and reconstruction error are therefore not propagated into the reported uncertainty.”
What was wrong with it. The source said reconstruction error has no distribution to propagate. The literature auditor found RESOLVE-IPD (arxiv:2511.01785), which quantifies and propagates reconstruction ambiguity into a meta-analysis, though only for subgroup labeling and as a preprint; Grok 4.5 agreed it is partial prior art rather than a resolution, and GPT-5.6 Sol scoped the software-absence claim to choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 rather than to component PAIC software generally.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The premise that reconstructed pseudo-IPD is normally treated as observed data is correct and widely true, but the claim that reconstruction uncertainty has ‘no distribution to propagate’ is now dated. RESOLVE-IPD (arXiv 2511.01785, submitted November 2025, revised January 2026) is a framework whose stated purpose is high-fidelity reconstruction plus ‘uncertainty-aware subgroup meta-analysis’: VEC-KM extracts coordinates and explicit censoring marks from vectorised figures to minimise digitisation error, CEN-KM removes the uniform-censoring assumption, and MAPLE ‘generates ensembles of mathematically valid labelings, facilitating a propagating meta-analysis that quantifies and reflects uncertainty from subgroup reconstruction’. Two honest caveats: it is a preprint, and its propagated uncertainty is over subgroup label assignment rather than over pixel-level curve reading or at-risk-table rounding, so it narrows rather than closes the entry’s gap. The specific claim that no such measurement model exists in component PAIC software remains true. Cites arxiv:2511.01785: Quantifies reconstruction uncertainty and propagates it into a downstream meta-analysis, and removes the uniform-censoring assumption; covers subgroup-label uncertainty rather than digitisation and at-risk-table error..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C2, and C4 are source-confirmed. cmlnmr() accepts supplied or reconstructed event/censoring rows, passes their times and statuses directly into the survival likelihood, contains no reconstruction-error layer, and explicitly rejects event-count/person-time summaries for that intended exact individual likelihood. C3 is established only for cpaic. Neither this repository nor the cited package claim supports the ecosystem-wide assertion that no Bayesian measurement model exists in any component PAIC software, and the broader statement that there is no accepted measurement model is outside this source-code audit. The problem is potentially decision-critical when reconstructed pseudo-IPD materially drives the result, but irrelevant to analyses using genuinely observed individual survival data.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. cpaic still requires reconstructed event/censor rows and treats them as ordinary individual contributions; README and man/cmlnmr.Rd explicitly say uncertainty from KM reconstruction is not propagated. Adjacent 2025 work improves fidelity and some uncertainty handling but does not solve this problem for component PAIC: RESOLVE-IPD (arXiv:2511.01785) reduces digitization/censoring bias and propagates subgroup-label ensembles into meta-analysis, yet it is not a Bayesian measurement model for pixel/risk-table error inside a cML-NMR likelihood, nor integrated with cpaic. IPDfromKM/KM-GPT remain point-reconstruction pipelines. No Bayesian measurement model for KM curve plus at-risk table uncertainty in component PAIC software was found. Queries: RESOLVE-IPD; IPDfromKM uncertainty propagation; Bayesian measurement model Kaplan-Meier digitization; cpaic pseudo-IPD. Status remains open; RESOLVE is partial prior art for ensemble pooling of reconstruction ambiguity, not a resolution of cpaic’s conditioning on one pseudo-IPD.

title: Competing risks and recurrent events are absent from component PAIC
text: CMP-19 Confirmed open High priority Emerging

title: Competing risks and recurrent events are absent from component PAIC
text:
Statement
Implemented component PAIC has a single-event survival likelihood with no cause, no recurrent-event history, no within-patient dependence, no transition state, and no joint terminal-event process, so it cannot express competing risks, recurrent events such as exacerbations or hospitalizations, or a recurrent-plus-terminal structure. Multistate NMA exists at the treatment level, for example for progression-free and overall survival, but no cause-specific, subdistribution, recurrent-event, joint recurrent-terminal, or multistate component model was found by any auditor. The absence of these models from one package does not by itself establish that they have never been formulated elsewhere; two auditors searched and found none, and one recorded the negative result as weak.

title: Competing risks and recurrent events are absent from component PAIC
text:
Why it is open
Adding competing risks requires cause-specific or subdistribution hazards for every component, which multiplies the parameters that must be assumed constant across subnetworks and forces an explicit decision about the scale on which component additivity holds. Recurrent-event data require within-patient dependence structures that a first-event survival likelihood cannot represent, and aggregate publications rarely report cause-specific detail or individual event trajectories, so the aggregate-likelihood side is underdetermined. When a terminal event such as death censors recurrence informatively, valid analysis needs a joint model whose aggregate-likelihood counterpart in a component ML-NMR has not been written down.

title: Competing risks and recurrent events are absent from component PAIC
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing treatment-level multistate NMA formulation to components, letting component effects act on transition intensities rather than on a single all-cause hazard, and state explicitly the scale on which component additivity is assumed to hold. Develop cause-specific and subdistribution component models and recurrent-event component models, with the aggregate-likelihood counterpart specified for the summaries publications actually report. Joint recurrent-and-terminal component models are the hardest case and should follow rather than lead.

title: Competing risks and recurrent events are absent from component PAIC
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Component PAIC has no competing-risks models, no recurrent-event models, and no joint models for recurrent events with a terminal event. Many clinical decisions concern several mutually exclusive event types or repeated events such as exacerbations, hospitalizations, and relapses, which a single all-cause first-event model cannot express.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated the absence as a universal fact about the field. GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed it only for choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and flagged that a package’s capability set cannot establish that no multistate component ML-NMR exists anywhere; Grok 4.5 supplied the nearest existing prior art, treatment-level multistate NMA (pmid:37300446), which is not a component model.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. I searched PubMed for competing risks, cause-specific hazards, recurrent events and multistate models in network meta-analysis and found nothing usable; the queries that returned results were badly translated by the search backend, so my negative result is weak evidence rather than proof. All six claims are absence claims and no source I retrieved asserts the absence, so unverifiable is the correct support vote. The methodological arguments are sound and, I believe, unpublished: cause-specific decomposition multiplies the parameters that must be constant across subnetworks and forces a choice of the scale on which component additivity is asserted, and the aggregate-likelihood counterpart of a joint recurrent-terminal model has no obvious form when publications report neither cause-specific detail nor event trajectories. Given that component ML-NMR itself has no public existence outside cpaic, a competing-risks version of it almost certainly does not exist. Entry has no prior_work, which weakens it presentationally.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C4, and C5 are supported as cpaic-specific capability claims: its survival paths implement a single-event survival likelihood without cause, recurrent-event history, patient-level dependence, transition state, or a joint terminal-event process. C3 is technically correct because an all-cause first-event endpoint cannot distinguish event types or represent repeated events. C2 and C6 are universal formulation or software-existence claims, not source-code claims. The absence of these models from cpaic cannot establish that no multistate component ML-NMR exists or that joint recurrent-terminal models have never been formulated elsewhere. The gap is critical only when the decision question actually concerns event type, recurrence, or terminal-event dependence; otherwise it is a roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Standard multistate NMA for PFS/OS exists (Jansen, Incerti, Trikalinos 2023; PMID 37300446) and causal recurrent/competing-event frameworks exist outside PAIC, but no cause-specific, subdistribution, recurrent-event, joint recurrent-terminal, or multistate component ML-NMR was found in 2023–2026 journals, arXiv, or cpaic. cpaic families remain binomial/gaussian/poisson/survival (all-cause first-event style). Aggregate cause-specific detail and the scale of component additivity on transition intensities remain as the report describes. Queries: component network meta competing risks multistate recurrent; multistate component ML-NMR; cpaic competing recurrent; Jansen multistate NMA. C1–C6 hold as of the audit date.

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text: CMP-21 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Statement
No missing-data framework has been made congenial with component transport. Multiple imputation and MNAR tipping-point sensitivity have already been applied in an ordinary MAIC: Esnault et al. 2025 imputed missing covariates inside a prespecified propensity-score workflow with roughly half of ECOG performance status missing, and probed missingness with quantitative bias analysis including an explicit tipping-point analysis. What is absent is any specification of how an imputation model should be made compatible with a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, and of how a single MNAR sensitivity parameter propagates simultaneously through the adjustment step, the covariate overlap, and the bridging assumption. Implemented component ML-NMR rejects missing effect modifiers and outcomes and states that it does not impute.

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Why it is open
In PAIC, dropping incomplete records redefines the population being reweighted or standardized, so transport assumptions are evaluated against a population that is not the one reported, and the overlap diagnostics are computed on the wrong set. An imputation model must be congenial with a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, and no one has written down what congeniality means in that setting. Inverse probability of censoring weighting also interacts multiplicatively with MAIC weights, compounding variance and positivity problems, and a single MNAR sensitivity parameter propagates through several layers at once with no framework saying how those effects combine.

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:

What it contributes

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing MAIC-level multiple imputation and tipping-point workflow rather than inventing one, and state the congeniality conditions between the imputation model and a component transport likelihood that integrates over a target distribution. Add inverse probability of censoring weighting for outcome missingness with explicit treatment of its interaction with adjustment weights, and let imputation uncertainty flow into the standardized target estimand rather than being handled outside the model. Specify MNAR sensitivity parameters that are interpretable for both outcome and effect-modifier missingness and report how they propagate jointly with the population-adjustment and bridging assumptions.

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No missing-data framework has been made congenial with component transport: multiple imputation and MNAR tipping-point sensitivity have been applied in ordinary MAIC, but nothing specifies how imputation models should be made compatible with a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, nor how a single MNAR sensitivity parameter propagates simultaneously through the adjustment step, the covariate overlap, and the bridging assumption.
The source said. “Component PAIC has no full missing-data module and no sensitivity analysis for missing-not-at-random mechanisms. Complete-case handling of missing covariates or outcomes changes the effective analysis population and therefore the overlap between the IPD study and the target population, and MNAR mechanisms can only be addressed through explicit sensitivity parameters that are not offered.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no compatible multiple imputation exists and that MNAR can only be addressed through explicit sensitivity parameters. The literature auditor found multiple imputation plus MNAR tipping-point and E-value analysis already done inside a MAIC (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w), so the gap is congeniality with component transport rather than missing-data methods as such; GPT-5.6 Sol added that MNAR identification can also come from parametric restrictions, instruments, refreshment samples, or validation data, so sensitivity parameters are important but not the only route.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Framed at field level (‘Component PAIC has no full missing-data module and no sensitivity analysis for MNAR’), the entry is too strong. Esnault et al. 2025 report an applied MAIC in which missing covariates were handled by multiple imputation inside a prespecified propensity-score workflow, and missingness was probed by quantitative bias analysis including an explicit MNAR tipping-point analysis, with roughly half of ECOG performance status missing; they describe it as ‘the first in-depth application of QBA in the context of MAIC’. So multiple imputation plus MNAR sensitivity has been done in a population-adjusted indirect comparison, just not congenially with a component transport model. The genuinely open parts survive: congeniality between an imputation model and a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, the multiplicative interaction of IPCW with MAIC weights, and how a single sensitivity parameter propagates through adjustment, overlap and the bridge simultaneously. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w: Demonstrates multiple imputation of missing covariates plus MNAR tipping-point and E-value sensitivity analysis inside a MAIC; does not address congeniality with component transport..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C2, C4, and C6 are supported. cmlnmr() rejects missing effect modifiers and outcomes and explicitly says it does not impute; cSTC relies on standard regression handling, which can yield complete-case fits, and no cpaic path supplies MNAR sensitivity parameters. Complete-case selection can alter both the represented IPD population and its overlap with the target. C3 is an unsupported universal nonexistence claim: absence from cpaic does not show that compatible multiple-imputation procedures do not exist. C5 is also too absolute. Observed data alone generally cannot nonparametrically identify the missing values or distinguish MAR from MNAR without additional assumptions or information, but identification can come from imposed parametric restrictions, instruments, refreshment samples, validation data, or other external information; explicit sensitivity parameters are therefore important but not logically the only possible approach. This is potentially very high severity with material missing effect modifiers or outcomes, but not when missingness is negligible or absent.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. No full missing-data module or MNAR sensitivity framework for component PAIC/cpaic was found. Adjacent MAIC practice now includes multiple imputation and delta-shift/tipping-point MNAR QBA (Esnault et al. 2025, BMC Med Res Methodol; doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w), so claim C3 as a blanket ‘MI methods compatible with component transport do not exist’ is slightly strong: MI+MAIC workflows exist, but congenial MI under component transport with target integration and shared component parameters across subnetworks is still not a published, evaluated method. MNAR remains structurally untestable (C5); effect-modifier missingness still distorts overlap and adjustment (C2, C6). cpaic has no MNAR or full MI module (C1, C4). Queries: MNAR MAIC ML-NMR 2024–2026; Esnault MAIC missing; multiple imputation component transport; cpaic missing data. Problem open for component PAIC; MAIC-level MI/MNAR sensitivity is partial adjacent prior art only.

Decision path

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text: CMP-23 Overstated High priority Emerging

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Statement
The bridge fragility threshold BFT = |D - tau| / sum_c |m_c| is the smallest common per-component main-effect drift, under a worst-case axis-aligned box bound, that moves a target contrast D to a decision threshold tau. It is computed per posterior draw, so it does propagate within-model parameter uncertainty; what it does not cover is interaction drift, covariance-shaped or correlated drift, and structural model uncertainty. Decision-consequence machinery is not missing from the field: decision-invariant threshold analysis for network meta-analysis has existed since Phillippo et al. 2018, is on CRAN as nmathresh, and has been applied to covariate-adjusted networks and combined with GRADE. What no method does is perturb the structural component-bridging parameter itself and report the resulting decision regret.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Why it is open
The single-number threshold assumes all components can drift by the same amount and independently in the worst direction, which is a deterministic uncertainty set rather than the most plausible configuration, and in a population-adjusted analysis drift in effect-modification parameters can matter more than main-effect drift. The extended expressions for component-specific box drift, ellipsoidal drift r times sqrt(m’ Sigma_Delta m) with symmetric positive-definite Sigma_Delta, and interaction drift are analytically standard but need inputs no data source supplies: component-specific bounds, a drift covariance, and plausible interaction drift. Calibrating those from connected networks with repeated components requires an explicit exchangeability and transport model, which anchors rather than validates the sensitivity values, and no calculation reports regret conditional on the untestable bridge.

What it contributes

nmathresh 0.1.6

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend fragility to component-specific, ellipsoidal, and polyhedral drift sets and to joint main-effect and interaction drift, since the formulas are standard and the missing ingredient is the inputs. Connect the existing decision-invariant threshold machinery to the bridging parameter rather than rebuilding decision analysis: nmathresh perturbs data, and what is needed is the same treatment of the structural drift, reported as net benefit, probability of a wrong decision, value of information, and bridge-conditional regret. Calibrate plausible drift distributions from connected networks containing repeated components across contexts while stating that this anchors rather than validates the assumption, and consider whether the net-benefit layer belongs in a downstream decision model rather than in the effect-estimation package.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No sensitivity analysis perturbs the structural component-bridging parameters themselves: decision-invariant threshold analysis for network meta-analysis already exists and operates on the treatment recommendation rather than the link-scale effect (Phillippo et al. 2018, R package nmathresh), and the box and ellipsoidal worst-case bias formulas are standard dual-norm results, so what is genuinely absent is drift-specific inputs, interaction-drift and correlated-drift versions, and a regret calculation conditional on an untestable bridge.
The source titled this. “Bridge fragility covers only main-effect box drift, not decisions” The title says the fragility measure does not cover decisions, but it is computed against a user-supplied decision threshold and the package already reports decision probabilities and rankings.
The source said. “The bridge fragility threshold BFT = |D - tau| / sum_c |m_c|, for target contrast D, component loading m, and decision threshold tau, is the smallest common per-component main-effect drift under a worst-case box bound that moves the contrast to the decision threshold; it covers neither interaction drift, correlated drift, nor model uncertainty. Outputs are organized around link-scale effects rather than decision consequences such as net benefit, probability of a wrong decision, or value of information.”
What was wrong with it. The source said outputs are organized around link-scale effects rather than decision consequences and that the extended worst-case expressions are unavailable. The literature auditor found decision-invariant threshold analysis already established and released (doi:10.1111/rssa.12341; cran:nmathresh; doi:10.1002/jrsm.1393), and noted the box and ellipsoidal bias formulas are elementary dual-norm results rather than open problems; GPT-5.6 Sol added that choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 already accepts arbitrary decision thresholds and reports posterior probabilities, p_best, and full rank probabilities, and that BFT is computed per posterior draw.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that decision-consequence machinery does not exist is wrong at field level. Threshold analysis for network meta-analysis has existed since Phillippo et al. 2018 and is on CRAN as nmathresh, described as computing ‘decision-invariant bias adjustment thresholds and intervals for Network Meta-Analysis’, identifying the smallest data changes that would alter the conclusion. That is precisely a decision-fragility calculation, it is defined on the treatment recommendation rather than on a link-scale effect, and it has been extended to covariate-adjusted networks and combined with GRADE (Holper 2020). The BFT is nonetheless a genuinely different object - it perturbs a structural bridging parameter rather than a data point - and I found nothing that does that, so the entry keeps a real open core. But the two extended worst-case formulas the entry gives (box bound sum |m_c| d_c and ellipsoidal bound r sqrt(m’ Sigma m)) are elementary dual-norm results, not open problems, and framing them as unavailable overstates the gap; what is missing is the inputs, as the entry itself says elsewhere. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12341: Establishes decision-invariant threshold analysis for NMA: thresholds are defined on the treatment decision, not the effect scale, so ‘no decision-consequence machinery exists’ is false.. Cites cran:nmathresh 0.1.6: Working software implementation of decision-invariant threshold analysis, including for random-effects models.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1393: Shows threshold analysis already applied to covariate-adjusted network recommendations and integrated with a certainty-of-evidence framework..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1, C2, C3, C5, and C6 are mathematically correct, with C6 requiring a symmetric positive-definite Sigma_Delta. The box result follows from the L1 support function and is attainable by choosing each drift sign against m; it is a deterministic uncertainty set, not a probabilistic independence assumption. C4 is correct for interaction drift, covariance-shaped drift, and structural model uncertainty, but BFT is calculated per posterior draw and therefore does propagate within-model parameter uncertainty. C8 requires an explicit exchangeability and transport model; connected-network estimates can anchor a prior but cannot validate its applicability, as C9 correctly states. The decision-capability gap is overstated: cpaic already accepts arbitrary link-scale thresholds, reports posterior robustness, posterior probabilities, p_best, and full rank probabilities. It lacks net benefit, wrong-decision probability, value-of-information, and drift-fragility analyses for rankings. Those consequences are important for HTA, but they may properly reside in a downstream decision model rather than this effect-estimation package. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements the stated first-generation box-bound bridge fragility threshold for every posterior draw.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Already supplies a population-specific probability-of-being-best output..
