title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text: DIA-05 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Statement
No shared platform runs the field’s methods on common data-generating mechanisms with published scenarios, seeds, code and ground truth, so nothing accumulates across papers and the ranking of methods under assumption failure cannot be read off the literature. The oracle claim does not survive scrutiny: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) defines truth as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate, and the general-likelihood ML-NMR work (arxiv:2401.12640) includes full-IPD reference comparisons. A single full-IPD oracle also cannot separate information loss from method failure, because it changes data granularity, covariate availability and model specification at the same time; that decomposition needs nested arms that vary one feature at a time. The proposed 28-family minimum comparator set is a design proposal rather than a derived requirement, and several of its categories overlap.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Why it is open
Data-generating mechanisms, estimands and performance measures differ between papers, so published rankings do not compose and each new comparison starts over. Average-case simulation under correct specification rewards efficiency in a regime applied HTA data are rarely in, and building adversarial mechanisms that break one’s own method runs against the incentives of a methods paper. A shared benchmark needs shared code, shared scenarios and a maintainer, which is infrastructure work with no conventional publication reward.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Anchored population-adjustment simulation of ML-NMR, MAIC and STC named as a foundational benchmark in the source; the locator was missing and was recovered by the literature auditor. Defines the estimand as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate.


Hatswell et al. 2020, The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison: Results of a Simulation Study
Unanchored misspecification simulation named as a foundational benchmark in the source; the locator was missing and was recovered by the literature auditor. Varies the simulation setup to violate implicit and explicit MAIC assumptions.


Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods: synthesis of individual and aggregate data with applications to survival analysis, 2024
Contains simulated comparisons against a full-IPD analysis, that is an oracle-style reference arm, weakening the claim that PAIC simulations commonly omit one. Retrieved at abstract level.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build a public benchmark that prespecifies estimands, combines benign and adversarial scenarios, verifies implementations against known analytic results, and publishes scenarios, seeds, code and ground truth so that results accumulate. Choose the comparator set by applicability to each scenario rather than by a fixed family count, and where information loss is the question use nested paired arms that change one feature at a time (data granularity, covariate availability, model specification) instead of a single full-IPD oracle. Score on bias, coverage, ESS collapse, decision error and runtime, and report excess error against the appropriate nested reference rather than raw bias alone.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “No neutral adversarial benchmark, comparator set, or oracle arm” The title says no oracle arm exists, but the audit found a gold-standard full-IPD reference already defined and used, and rejected the 28-family comparator set as a derived requirement.
The source said. “No shared simulation platform compares the field’s methods on common data-generating mechanisms; published comparisons are pairwise contests run by method authors under benign conditions, against a handful of chosen comparators, and almost never include an oracle analysis that uses full IPD, the true bias variables and correct models. Consequently neither the ranking of methods under assumption failure nor the separation of information loss from method failure can be read off the literature.”
What was wrong with it. The source said PAIC simulations almost never include an oracle and that a minimum comparator set contains 28 method families; the literature auditor found the gold-standard full-IPD reference already explicit in Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) and full-IPD comparisons in arxiv:2401.12640, and GPT-5.6 Sol found no argument establishing 28 as a minimum, noting that exponential-tilting MAIC and entropy balancing can be dual formulations of the same calibration problem and that trimming is a tuning choice. The entry’s two prior_work items carried no locators; the literature auditor identified them as Phillippo et al. 2020 and Hatswell et al. 2020 (doi:10.1016/j.jval.2020.02.008), which are now cited.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Citation fidelity: the two prior_work entries carry no DOI, but they map cleanly onto real papers whose descriptions match. ‘Phillippo and colleagues, anchored population-adjustment simulation’ is Phillippo, Dias, Ades & Welton 2020 (Stat Med 39:4885-4911), which is exactly an anchored population-adjustment simulation of ML-NMR, MAIC and STC. ‘Hatswell and colleagues, unanchored misspecification simulation’ is Hatswell, Freemantle & Baio 2020 (Value Health 23:751-759), ‘The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison’. Both are accurately characterized; supplying the locators would make them non-decorative. I found no public neutral adversarial benchmark platform for PAIC; outstandR is a unified software interface, not a benchmark with shared scenarios and published ground truth. The oracle claim is too strong: Phillippo 2020 explicitly defines truth as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate, and full-IPD reference arms are actually run in ML-NMR and IPD-NMA simulation work. The ‘28 method families’ figure is a design proposal, not a checkable fact. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Confirms the ‘Phillippo and colleagues’ prior_work description and supplies the missing locator; also shows the gold-standard IPD network meta-regression concept is explicit in the anchored benchmark literature.. Cites 10.1016/j.jval.2020.02.008: Confirms the ‘Hatswell and colleagues’ prior_work description and supplies the missing locator.. Cites arXiv:2401.12640: Contains simulated comparisons against a full-IPD analysis, i.e. an oracle-style reference arm, weakening ‘PAIC simulation studies commonly omit an oracle comparator’. Retrieved at abstract/summary level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C6 is correct, C7 is a sound design principle, and C11 correctly counts ten grouped scenario families. The remainder is inflated. No mathematical or decision-theoretic argument establishes 28 families as a minimum, and several categories overlap. Conventional exponential-tilting MAIC and entropy balancing can be dual formulations of the same calibration problem when they use identical moments and base weights; trimming is a tuning intervention rather than necessarily a separate method family. A single full-IPD oracle cannot separate information loss from method failure because it simultaneously changes data granularity, available covariates, and model specification. That decomposition requires nested paired arms that change one feature at a time. Simulation truth itself can be the relevant reference, so an estimated oracle need not appear in every scenario. Claims about the absence of public benchmarks, author behavior, and routine oracle omission are literature claims unsupported here. A shared adversarial benchmark would be useful infrastructure, but not a decision-grade requirement in the asserted form.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text: DIA-07 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Statement
PAIC simulations are built on two-trial or three-treatment templates with no topology factor and index information by participants per arm, so their results cannot be extrapolated to the networks that submissions actually contain. A topology scenario generator does already exist in the wider network meta-analysis literature: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) publishes a procedure with R code that builds families of connected and disconnected topologies from a seed network, but it has not been wired to PAIC estimators. Two of the entry’s design prescriptions need narrowing: information for binary and survival outcomes depends on events plus non-events, allocation, baseline risk, risk sets, censoring and timing rather than on events per contrast alone, and post-weighting effective sample size is a method-dependent output that can be a calibration target but cannot be crossed as an independent data-generating factor.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Why it is open
The one-IPD-trial, one-AgD-trial template has no topology at all, and topology acts through the design matrix, its row space and the contrast-specific information matrix to determine which contrasts are identified and where information flows, so an estimator that behaves well on a single indirect comparison can fail on a loop-rich or hub-and-spoke network with articulation edges. Two networks with identical total sample size can differ entirely in the estimability of the decision contrast depending on where the IPD sit. Building larger networks and keeping track of information per contrast requires a generator wired to PAIC estimators, and the one generator that exists was written for component model selection instead.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Provides a reusable procedure and R code for generating families of distinct network topologies, connected and disconnected with differing subnetwork composition, from a seed network; the topology scenario generator the source says no platform provides, though it is not wired to PAIC estimators.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the published topology generator to drive PAIC and component-PAIC estimators rather than writing a new one, and report performance conditional on topology rather than averaged over it, treating articulation edges and articulation treatments as explicit fragility factors because they control the fragility of indirect paths. Index information with outcome-appropriate measures (events and non-events, allocation and baseline risk for binary outcomes; event counts, risk sets, censoring and timing for survival) and calibrate scenarios to a target ESS range instead of crossing achieved ESS as an input. Treat integration points as a numerical-convergence check for models that require numerical integration, and prior informativeness as a Bayesian sensitivity factor, rather than as mandatory factors in every design.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Simulation designs are built on the two-trial anchored template and index information by participants per arm, so they span neither the topologies HTA networks actually have (3 to 20 treatments, varying trial density, two-arm versus multi-arm trials, connected, weakly connected and disconnected graphs, 2 to 4 subnetworks, star, chain, loop-rich and hub-and-spoke shapes, articulation edges and treatments, unequal allocation, classes and doses) nor the quantities that actually carry information (events per contrast, studies per component, post-weighting ESS, IPD study placement, AgD precision, integration points and prior informativeness).”
What was wrong with it. The source said no shared platform provides a topology scenario generator; the literature auditor found one already published with code in the component network meta-analysis literature (Petropoulou et al. 2023, doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9), which is simply not connected to PAIC estimators. GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the information index for binary and survival outcomes and the treatment of post-weighting ESS as a crossable design factor.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): Topology and information placement matter through the design matrix, its row space, and the contrast-specific information matrix, so C4, C5, and C7 are sound. Articulation edges and treatments are reasonable fragility factors, but the specific treatment counts and two-to-four-subnetwork grid are not universal requirements. C6 is too strong: binary-outcome information depends on both events and non-events, allocation, and baseline risk; survival information depends on event counts plus risk sets, censoring, timing, and allocation. Post-weighting ESS is endogenous and method-specific, so it cannot generally be crossed as an independent data-generating factor, although scenarios can be calibrated to target an ESS range. Integration points are a numerical-convergence factor only for models requiring numerical integration, and prior informativeness is relevant when Bayesian robustness is an aim, not a mandatory factor in every simulation. Field-wide claims that particular grids or articulation effects have never been evaluated are unsupported here.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The gap is real for PAIC specifically: the retrieved PAIC simulations (Phillippo 2020, Remiro-Azocar 2021, Hatswell 2020, Liu 2025, Serret-Larmande 2025) are all built on two-trial or three-treatment templates with no topology factor and index information by participants. But the entry’s framing ignores that the broader NMA simulation literature already varies topology deliberately: Kiefer, Sturtz & Bender’s simulation spans networks with several interventions and inconsistency structures, degree-irregularity work simulates multiple network geometries and scores rank-probability bias, and Petropoulou et al. 2023 build an explicit generator that constructs many distinct connected and disconnected topologies from one seed network under a retain-all-interventions constraint. So a scenario generator over topology exists, just not one wired to PAIC estimators. Most remaining sub-claims (‘a comprehensive program must vary…’, ‘ESS should be a controlled design factor’) are normative design assertions rather than checkable facts, and the integration-points and prior-informativeness claims I could not verify. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Provides a reusable algorithm and R code for generating families of distinct network topologies (connected, and disconnected with differing subnetwork composition) from a seed network, i.e. the topology scenario generator the entry says no platform provides..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Topology and information placement matter through the design matrix, its row space, and the contrast-specific information matrix, so C4, C5, and C7 are sound. Articulation edges and treatments are reasonable fragility factors, but the specific treatment counts and two-to-four-subnetwork grid are not universal requirements. C6 is too strong: binary-outcome information depends on both events and non-events, allocation, and baseline risk; survival information depends on event counts plus risk sets, censoring, timing, and allocation. Post-weighting ESS is endogenous and method-specific, so it cannot generally be crossed as an independent data-generating factor, although scenarios can be calibrated to target an ESS range. Integration points are a numerical-convergence factor only for models requiring numerical integration, and prior informativeness is relevant when Bayesian robustness is an aim, not a mandatory factor in every simulation. Field-wide claims that particular grids or articulation effects have never been evaluated are unsupported here.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text: DIA-09 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Statement
Published PAIC simulations score survival on the hazard ratio: Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 on the log hazard ratio, Liu et al. 2025 on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, Hatswell et al. 2020 on mean error of the effect measure, and none reports time-indexed survival-probability error, RMST bias, integrated Brier score or extrapolation error. Under delayed, waning or crossing effects a hazard-ratio bias summary can be small while the survival curves the economic model consumes are badly wrong. Cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate processes, proportional-odds violations for ordinal outcomes and jointly generated efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes are absent from this simulation literature. The tooling is no longer the obstacle: ML-NMR has been extended to general individual-level likelihoods with flexible M-spline baseline hazards (arxiv:2401.12640), so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable even though simulations do not score on them.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Why it is open
PAIC theory is cleanest for collapsible linear-scale outcomes, so simulation practice has concentrated where the theory is tidy while HTA submissions are dominated by survival endpoints with non-proportional hazards. Generating crossing hazards, cure fractions or competing risks with a known target-population marginal estimand requires deriving that estimand analytically or by large-sample Monte Carlo, which is more work than a Gaussian scenario and is routinely skipped. Correlated multi-outcome generation is needed to evaluate net benefit and other nonlinear decision functionals, yet simulations generate one outcome at a time.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods: synthesis of individual and aggregate data with applications to survival analysis, 2024
Extends population-adjusted synthesis to arbitrary individual-level likelihoods with flexible M-spline baseline hazards and survival applications, so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable. Retrieved at abstract level.


Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021, Methods for population adjustment with limited access to individual patient data: A review and simulation study
Scores survival performance on the log hazard ratio, one of the studies the literature auditor cites as evidence of hazard-ratio-only survival scoring.


Liu et al. 2025, Is the Use of Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Always Superior to Naive Indirect Comparison on Survival Outcomes? A Simulation Study
Scores survival performance on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, with no absolute-scale or time-indexed measures.


Hatswell et al. 2020, The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison: Results of a Simulation Study
Scores on mean error and mean absolute error of the effect measure, again with no survival-probability, RMST or extrapolation measures.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend simulation generators to the missing outcome families with explicitly derived target-population marginal estimands (survival probability, RMST, cumulative incidence, cure fraction, event burden), using the general-likelihood ML-NMR machinery that already computes absolute-scale target-population quantities, so that bias is computed against the quantity the decision uses. Score survival PAIC on time-indexed survival-probability error and RMST bias by default, and add the remaining measures where they apply rather than universally: integrated Brier score where survival predictions and censoring handling are defined, extrapolation error where the pipeline extrapolates beyond observed follow-up, recurrent-event calibration where event burden is the estimand. Generate efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes jointly where the decision functional is nonlinear or joint uncertainty matters.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The simulation evidence base does not span the outcome families decision problems involve (rare and very rare binary events, overdispersed, zero-inflated and exposure-dependent counts, ordinal outcomes violating proportional odds, delayed, waning and crossing hazards, non-Weibull mixtures, cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate disease, and correlated efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes), and survival performance is scored by hazard-ratio bias rather than by the quantities decisions use.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors judged the problem open, and the correction is a caveat the source did not acknowledge: the literature auditor notes that survival PAIC methodology has moved, with ML-NMR extended to general likelihoods and flexible baseline hazards (arxiv:2401.12640), so the gap is in what simulations score rather than in what methods can produce. GPT-5.6 Sol also narrowed the proposed measures, since integrated Brier score, extrapolation error, joint outcome generation and recurrent-event calibration apply to specific pipelines and estimands rather than universally.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The survival-scoring claim is broadly right in the PAIC simulation literature I retrieved: Remiro-Azocar 2021 scores on the log hazard ratio, Liu et al. 2025 on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, Hatswell 2020 on mean error/mean absolute error of the effect measure. None reports time-indexed survival-probability error, integrated Brier score, RMST bias or extrapolation error. The caveat is that survival PAIC methodology has moved: ML-NMR has been extended to general likelihoods with M-spline baseline hazards and survival applications, and unanchored STC has been implemented with parametric and Royston-Parmar models explicitly to handle non-proportional hazards and extrapolation, so the tooling for absolute-scale survival quantities exists even though simulations do not score on them. I found no PAIC simulation work at all on cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate processes, ordinal proportional-odds violation, or jointly generated efficacy/safety/QoL/cost outcomes, so those parts of the claim stand. Cites arXiv:2401.12640: Extends population-adjusted synthesis to arbitrary individual-level likelihoods with flexible (M-spline) baseline hazards and survival applications, so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable even though simulations still score on the hazard ratio. Retrieved at abstract/summary level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The technical core is sound. Under non-proportional hazards, bias against a single constant hazard ratio does not characterize errors in survival probabilities, RMST, cumulative incidence, or downstream economic quantities. Delayed, waning, and crossing effects can have materially different decision consequences and merit distinguishable scenarios. Rare events and proportional-odds violations are also genuine factors. The proposed measures are not all universal requirements: integrated Brier score is a predictive-distribution score requiring defined survival predictions and censoring handling, not a generic measure of causal contrast estimation; joint outcome generation is essential for joint uncertainty and nonlinear decision functionals but not for every marginal-effect evaluation; extrapolation error belongs only to pipelines that extrapolate; and recurrent-event calibration is relevant only when recurrent burden is an estimand. The claims about which outcome families and measures appear in published studies are literature-coverage claims and were not adjudicated. Very high priority is proportionate for methods making survival decision claims, while the full outcome catalogue is a broader roadmap.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Statement
Estimability in component networks is neither unstudied nor unimplemented: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) implements a screen for inestimable interactions and reports inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in both simulation and a real Cochrane network, Rucker et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/bimj.201800167) formalizes the design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, Mao et al. 2025 (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w) identifies comparisons whose removal destroys component identifiability, and cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, implements target-dependent augmented row-space screening that labels contrasts exact, first-order or not identified and suppresses nonidentified estimates. What does not exist is a canonical published scenario library spanning the five estimability classes with target-dependent estimability, and the identification-focused performance measures: true and false estimability classification rates, false finite-estimate rate, smallest singular value of the design or information matrix, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and target mass outside source support. The design claim also needs precision: a contrast is structurally estimable when its contrast vector lies in the row space of the relevant design, and rank and nullity counts alone give dimensions rather than saying which contrasts qualify.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Why it is open
Estimability in component models is a property of a design matrix crossed with a target covariate value, not of data volume, so it cannot be discovered by running more replicates and has to be constructed deliberately. The dangerous cases are the ones that produce output: a proper prior yields a finite posterior for a direction the likelihood does not inform, and a first-order rank-based screen can pass while the nonlinear aggregate-data likelihood remains weakly identified. Bias, coverage and RMSE can reveal poor behavior for particular truths but cannot certify structural identification or say whether a method should have abstained, so nothing in the standard performance set penalizes software that silently reports prior-driven answers, and without a scenario library there is nothing to test screens against.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Implements an algorithm to identify inestimable interactions and reports inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in simulation and in a real Cochrane network, where eleven combinations of two interventions yield only ten estimable two-way interactions.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis
Identifies which direct comparisons are essential for component identifiability and defines behavior when their removal makes a component unidentifiable.


Rucker et al. 2019, Network meta-analysis of multicomponent interventions
Formalizes the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component combination matrix, the structure the entry’s rank and nullity claim refers to.


Graphical evaluation of evidence structure within a component network meta-analysis, 2023
Addresses evidence structure and component identifiability in component network meta-analysis. The literature auditor could not retrieve the full text and relied on title and venue only, so no claim is made about its exact content.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Implements target-dependent augmented row-space estimability classification with exact, first-order and not-identified labels, suppresses nonidentified contrasts rather than reporting finite posterior summaries, and refits under tighter and looser priors as an identification diagnostic. It does not supply the five-class scenario library or the identification performance measures.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the canonical scenario library with known ground truth over the five estimability classes, including cases where estimability changes with the target covariate value and where a first-order screen passes while the nonlinear likelihood stays weakly identified, and validate the screens that already exist, in component network meta-analysis and in cpaic, against it rather than writing new ones. Add identification measures to the standard performance set: true and false estimability classification rates, false finite-estimate rate, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and target mass outside source support. Report the smallest singular value only with the weighting and parameter scaling made explicit, since it is not scale-free, and score error on estimable row-space contrasts and predictions rather than on arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Estimability failure is neither simulated nor measured” The title says estimability failure is neither simulated nor measured, but published screens report inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in simulation and in a real network.
The source said. “No published library of simulation scenarios spans component-network estimability (rank and nullity of the treatment-by-component matrix X = BC, contrasts inside versus outside its row space, subnetwork-unique and duplicated components, coding errors, higher-order and antagonistic interactions, and the five estimability classes), and performance measurement stops at bias, coverage and RMSE with no measures for identification. True and false estimability classification, the false finite-estimate rate for non-estimable contrasts, the smallest singular value of the design or information matrix, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and the proportion of target mass outside source support are not reported.”
What was wrong with it. The source framed estimability failure as neither simulated nor measured; the literature auditor found published estimability screens and reported inestimable contrasts in component network meta-analysis (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9, doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w), and GPT-5.6 Sol found target-dependent row-space screening and prior-sensitivity refits already implemented in cpaic at commit 9d150e9, a GitHub development package that is not on CRAN. The scenario library and the identification performance measures remain missing.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): Structural estimability is genuinely critical, and C2, C3, C6, C9, and C12 are technically defensible. C4 is sloppy: scalar rank and nullity give dimensions, but the orientation of the row or null space determines which particular contrasts are estimable. C1 is true only for a functional lying wholly in a likelihood-null direction; a generally non-estimable contrast can contain a data-informed row-space projection plus a prior-determined null-space projection. C7 is also too absolute: bias, RMSE, and coverage can reveal poor behavior for selected simulation truths, but they cannot certify structural identification or whether a method should abstain. A smallest singular value is informative only after specifying weighting and parameter scaling, and prior-to-posterior contraction is a useful diagnostic rather than a proof of identification. At cpaic 9d150e9, the blanket title is already stale: the package implements target-dependent augmented row-space screening, labels results as exact, first-order screen, or not identified, suppresses nonidentified estimates, provides prior-sensitivity refits, and tests several structural scenarios. It does not yet provide the proposed canonical five-class simulation library or the full performance-measure suite. Literature-existence claims C5 and C8 were not adjudicated.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I read Petropoulou et al. 2023 in full. Estimability in component networks is neither unstudied nor unimplemented: the paper states ‘we describe an algorithm to identify inestimable interactions in the supplement as only estimable interactions should be considered in interaction CNMA models’, and in the Cochrane application reports ‘The network has eleven combinations of two interventions, however, only ten 2-way interactions are estimable’, with specific cross-subnetwork contrasts reported as inestimable in the simulated and applied disconnected networks. I could not retrieve the full text (paywalled), so I rely on title and venue only and make no claim about its exact content..

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text: DIA-13 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Statement
Quantitative bias analysis for unanchored PAIC has not been evaluated over a design crossing bias mechanisms with the primary data-generating factors. The leading recent method paper, Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates plus deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed marginal means of unmeasured confounders, and runs no simulation study of the proposed method, relying instead on prior results for standard unanchored STC and on a case study. The cells that would be decisive are the ones nobody runs: the truth outside the elicited range, cancelling biases, a misspecified bias model, non-confounding biases acting jointly with omitted-variable bias, and correlated sensitivity parameters. A complete Cartesian factorial is not mathematically required; the scenario set should be chosen by estimand, plausible mechanisms and the interactions that could change the conclusion.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Why it is open
QBA papers typically demonstrate a single bias mechanism in a single scenario to show that a correction works, which cannot reveal how the correction behaves when several biases act at once or when the bias model itself is wrong. Crossing bias mechanisms with the primary factors multiplies the design size, so authors avoid it unless a shared simulation platform exists. The scientifically decisive cells, where the truth lies outside the elicited range, where biases cancel, or where the bias model is misspecified, are precisely the cells a proponent has no incentive to run.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates with deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed means of unmeasured confounders, demonstrated on a case study with no simulation study of the proposed method; the state of practice the entry describes.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build a QBA simulation design that crosses bias count, bias type, measurement status of the unmeasured variable, dependence structure, elicitation correctness and bias-model correctness with the primary population and outcome factors, selecting cells by which interactions could change the decision rather than by exhaustive crossing. Include cells where the truth lies outside the elicited range, where multiple biases cancel, and where selection, index-date, outcome-misclassification and censoring bias act jointly with omitted-variable bias. Treat correlated sensitivity parameters as a factor wherever the QBA is probabilistic or its joint sensitivity set is dependence-sensitive.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Quantitative bias analysis for unanchored PAIC has never been evaluated over a factorial design crossing the primary data-generating mechanisms with explicit bias mechanisms: one, two or five omitted variables of varying type; U measured in source IPD but unreported in target AgD versus unmeasured in both; prognostic-only, treatment-modifying, component-modifying and time-varying U; varying source-target imbalance and U-X dependence; correct versus misspecified target prevalence, outcome association and interaction; true sensitivity parameters inside versus outside the elicited range; deterministic versus probabilistic QBA; independent versus correlated sensitivity parameters; selection, index-date, outcome-misclassification and censoring bias separately and jointly; component drift; reinforcing versus cancelling biases; correct versus misspecified bias models; and target-population versus comparator-trial-population QBA.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors judged the claim open, and the literature auditor sourced the state of practice to Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), which conducts no simulation of its proposed method. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed the prescription: no complete Cartesian factorial is mathematically required, and correlated sensitivity parameters matter for probabilistic QBA or dependence-sensitive joint sensitivity sets rather than for a deterministic analysis whose joint support is held fixed.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I retrieved the leading recent QBA-for-unanchored-PAIC paper, Ren, Ren, Welton & Strong 2025 in Research Synthesis Methods, which proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates plus deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed marginal means of unmeasured confounders. No simulation study was conducted for the proposed method; the authors instead lean on prior simulation properties of standard unanchored STC and demonstrate on a case study. A companion strand, flexible QBA for subject-level ITC under proportional-hazards violation, is likewise method development with case-study demonstration. That is direct positive evidence for the entry’s claim that QBA in this setting varies one mechanism at a time at most and has never been crossed factorially with the primary data-generating factors. The decisive cells named by the entry (truth outside the elicited range, cancelling biases, misspecified bias model, joint non-confounding biases, correlated sensitivity parameters) appear nowhere in what I retrieved.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The proposed stress tests are technically well motivated. C2 tests elicitation failure rather than merely correction under oracle inputs; C3 correctly separates reinforcing from canceling biases; C4 distinguishes partial measurement, where source associations can be estimated, from complete nonmeasurement; C5 separates mechanisms with different identifying assumptions; and C6 distinguishes estimands defined in different target populations. C7 applies specifically to probabilistic QBA or dependence-sensitive joint sensitivity sets: correlation can materially change the distribution of combined bias, but it need not change a deterministic analysis whose joint support is held fixed. A complete Cartesian factorial is not mathematically required for every QBA method; scenarios should be chosen according to the estimand, plausible mechanisms, and interactions that could alter conclusions. The assertion about how existing studies vary factors is a literature-coverage claim and was not assessed. This is primarily a method-validation roadmap rather than a uniformly critical omission in each applied analysis.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text: DIA-15 Overstated High priority Emerging

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Statement
Two of the five measures the entry calls unreported already exist. Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected when it truly holds, rising from 3.5 percent to 18.8 percent with increasing heterogeneity, plus correct-model selection rates, which is false-synergy selection under another name; Mao et al. 2025 (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w) gives a variance-based leave-one-out contribution measure for component networks; and cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package not on CRAN, exports fitted-analysis bridge fragility and edge influence diagnostics. What is reported nowhere is bias under deliberately corrupted component coding, rank reversal as a performance measure, and sensitivity calibration, meaning whether a sensitivity interval covers the truth at the true drift. Two framings also need adjusting: false-synergy selection is a conventional null selection rate (type I error, family-wise error or false discovery), and component-effect error is meaningful only for identified parameters, so rank-deficient designs must score estimable row-space contrasts rather than arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Why it is open
Coding a treatment into components is a human data-preparation step, so its error propagates in ways only a simulation with deliberately corrupted coding can quantify, and no such simulation is standard. Sensitivity calibration is repeated-sampling coverage evaluated under a specified true drift rather than under the reference model, so it cannot be read off any currently reported quantity and has to be reported separately from nominal coverage. Rank reversal is an error only relative to a fixed target population and decision estimand, since a genuine population-dependent reversal is not a failure, and that conditioning is exactly what current reporting omits.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected when it holds and the rate at which the wrong interaction model is selected, which is the false-synergy selection probability the entry says is unreported.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis
Provides a quantified bridge-contribution and fragility measure for component networks based on variance inflation when each direct comparison is removed.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Implements a fitted-analysis tipping-point measure for cross-subnetwork main-effect drift, explicitly excluding interaction drift, and per-edge influence weights that can identify an adjusted IPD edge contributing nothing to the requested contrast. It does not provide false-selection rates, coding-error operating characteristics, or standardized Monte Carlo calibration.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Bring the measures that already exist into routine use rather than reinventing them: report the additivity-rejection and interaction-selection error rates computed in component simulation studies, and the leave-one-out contribution measure, as standard outputs for component and disconnected-network methods. Add the three that do not exist: robustness under an explicitly specified component-miscoding mechanism, ranking or decision loss for a fixed target estimand, and repeated-sampling coverage under a specified true sensitivity violation reported alongside reference-model coverage. Score error on estimable row-space contrasts and predictions, and extend the existing fitted-analysis fragility and influence diagnostics to interaction drift and to methods beyond the single package that implements them.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Bias under component coding error, rank reversal, and sensitivity calibration at the true drift are not reported performance measures in component and disconnected-network simulation studies; false-synergy selection and bridge contribution have already been operationalized, as model-selection error rates and as variance-based leave-one-out contribution respectively.
The source titled this. “False synergy, coding error, and bridge fragility are never scored” The title says false synergy and bridge fragility are never scored, but the audit found both already operationalized as model-selection error rates and leave-one-out contribution.
The source said. “Component and network simulations do not report the performance measures that would expose their characteristic failures: component-effect and component-interaction error, bridge contribution and fragility, rank reversal, the probability of selecting a false synergy, bias under component coding error, and sensitivity calibration, meaning whether a sensitivity interval covers the truth at the true drift.”
What was wrong with it. The source said false-synergy selection probability and bridge contribution and fragility are not reported; the literature auditor found both already operationalized, as additivity-rejection and model-selection error rates (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) and as a variance-based leave-one-out contribution algorithm (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w), and GPT-5.6 Sol found bridge_fragility() and edge_influence() implemented in cpaic at commit 9d150e9. Three of the five measures survive as genuinely unreported.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Two of the five claims are contradicted by papers I read. False-synergy selection IS reported: Petropoulou et al. 2023 report, for scenarios where additivity truly holds, ‘The percentage of networks rejecting the additivity assumption increases from 3.5% to 18.8% with increasing [heterogeneity]’, and give correct-model selection rates (69.3% and 65.2% for no and low heterogeneity, under 50% for moderate). Rejecting additivity when additivity holds is precisely the probability of concluding a synergy exists when it does not. Bridge contribution and fragility are also quantified: Mao et al. 2025 give a variance-based leave-one-out contribution algorithm for CNMA that measures how excluding each direct comparison inflates component-effect variance and flags comparisons whose removal destroys identifiability. The remaining three claims survive: I found no reporting of bias under deliberately corrupted component coding, no rank-reversal performance measure in this literature, and nothing on sensitivity calibration at the true drift. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected and the rate at which the wrong interaction model is selected, i.e. the false-synergy selection probability.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w: Provides a quantified bridge-contribution/fragility measure for component networks based on variance inflation on removal of each direct comparison..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 and C2 are uncited literature-absence assertions and are outside this technical audit. The methodological framing is nevertheless too broad. False-synergy selection probability is a conventional null selection rate, type I error, family-wise error rate, or false discovery measure. Raw component-effect or interaction error is meaningful only for identified parameters; in rank-deficient designs, simulations must score estimable row-space contrasts or predictions rather than arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients. Rank reversal is an error only relative to a fixed target population and decision estimand; a true population-dependent reversal is not a failure. C5 is repeated-sampling coverage evaluated under a specified true drift, not a fundamentally different probability concept from coverage, although it should be reported separately from reference-model coverage. At 9d150e9, cpaic already exports bridge_fragility() and edge_influence(), partly addressing C4 at the fitted-analysis level. They do not provide false-selection rates, coding-error operating characteristics, or standardized Monte Carlo calibration. The asserted High severity is justified only when interaction selection, ranking, or a cross-gap decision is actually part of the analysis. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Implements a fitted-analysis tipping-point measure for cross-subnetwork main-effect drift, while explicitly excluding interaction drift.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Implements per-edge influence weights for a requested contrast and can identify an adjusted IPD edge that contributes nothing to that contrast..

text: DIA-17 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Statement
No study masks selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset down to aggregate data and scores PAIC estimates against the full-IPD target-standardized analysis, and PAIC validation concentrates on relative effects rather than on the absolute arm-level predictions a transport model actually makes; the closest multi-IPD study, Phillippo et al. 2022 (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), validates through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency and modifier relaxation, with no held-out trial and no predicted-versus-observed arm check. Real-data benchmarking against randomized evidence does exist as one-off case studies, which the source does not acknowledge: Signorovitch et al. 2023 (doi:10.1080/09546634.2023.2169574) compares previously published guselkumab MAIC estimates against the subsequently completed ECLIPSE and IXORA-R head-to-head trials. The benchmark is a prespecified reference analysis carrying its own uncertainty rather than known truth, and it must match the estimand: a marginal PAIC estimate needs a marginal target-standardized comparator while conditional STC or conditional ML-NMR output needs a conditional one, a distinction that is material on non-collapsible scales.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Why it is open
Both designs require multi-trial IPD, which sits with sponsors and consortia rather than with methodologists, and data-sharing agreements rarely permit the repeated re-analysis a validation study needs. Population-shift validation additionally requires an identified absolute-risk transport model, compatible outcome definitions and follow-up, adequate overlap and preferably a shared arm for calibration, a rarer configuration than it appears. Masked-IPD validation is uniquely capable of embarrassing a method, so incentives run against it and the real-data checks that exist are sponsor-authored one-offs rather than standing benchmarks with reusable protocols.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Establish standing IPD-masking benchmarks on shared multi-trial datasets with a fixed protocol: mask selected trials to aggregate data, run the comparator method set, and report discrepancy from a prespecified full-IPD analysis of the same estimand, marginal for marginal methods and conditional for conditional ones, with uncertainty in both estimates carried through, alongside decision agreement. Where trial pairs with IPD from distinct populations and a shared arm exist, transport in both directions and compare uncertainty-aware predicted arm outcomes with observed ones, treating a failed arm-level prediction as evidence against the transport model. Report arm-level calibration as a routine validation output rather than relative-effect agreement alone.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The two real-data designs with an unambiguous benchmark are not standard practice: IPD masking, in which selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset are reduced to aggregate data and the PAIC estimate is compared with the full-IPD target-standardized analysis it is supposed to approximate; and population-shift validation, in which transport between IPD populations is checked by comparing predicted with observed absolute arm outcomes as well as contrasts.”
What was wrong with it. The source called masked IPD the one design with an unambiguous benchmark and did not mention that MAIC estimates have already been checked against subsequent head-to-head trials (Signorovitch et al. 2023, doi:10.1080/09546634.2023.2169574). GPT-5.6 Sol added that a full-IPD benchmark is a prespecified reference analysis with its own sampling uncertainty and must be marginal or conditional to match the estimand of the method being scored.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is sound only if ‘known target’ means a prespecified reference analysis, not known causal truth. A full-IPD estimate remains finite-sample uncertain and may depend on its outcome and transport models. C3 must be estimand-specific. Marginal target standardization is the appropriate comparator for a marginal PAIC estimand, but conditional STC or cML-NMR output requires a corresponding conditional benchmark. This distinction is material on non-collapsible scales. The cpaic source confirms that cstc() is conditional and cmaic() is marginal, while cML-NMR’s current effect path is conditional rather than marginally standardized. C4 requires more than two IPD populations: absolute arm prediction needs an identified baseline-risk model, compatible outcomes and follow-up, positivity, and cross-trial transportability of absolute risks; a shared arm can provide calibration. Observed arm outcomes are noisy benchmarks and should be compared using uncertainty-aware predictions. C6 is correct because common baseline-risk errors can cancel in a contrast. C2 and C5 are literature-practice assertions outside this audit. The validation agenda remains valuable, but its benchmark is neither universal nor unambiguous.

Literature and prior-art check

I found no study that masks selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset down to aggregate data and scores PAIC estimates against the full-IPD target-standardized analysis, so the core claim holds. Two caveats. First, real-data benchmarking of PAIC against randomized evidence does exist and the entry does not acknowledge it: Signorovitch et al. 2023 compared previously published guselkumab MAIC estimates against the subsequently completed ECLIPSE and IXORA-R head-to-head trials on PASI 90 risk differences (14.4% in ECLIPSE vs 9.4% in the MAIC at week 48; 0.0% vs 0.7% at week 24). Second, the population-shift design is not entirely unexercised: Phillippo et al. 2022 fit ML-NMR to a plaque psoriasis network with IPD from several trials and produce absolute target-population predictions, but explicitly do not hold out a trial or compare predicted with observed absolute arm outcomes, which confirms the entry’s arm-level calibration claim. title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text: DIS-01 Confirmed open Very high priority Established

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Statement
In a connected network the relative effect between two treatments is identified through a path of randomized contrasts; when no such path exists the cross-subnetwork contrast lies outside the row space of the design and is absent from the randomized likelihood, so no amount of additional within-component data supplies it. Any finite estimate of that contrast comes from structure the analyst imposes: a proper prior, an equality restriction, a component or class model, external evidence, or a bridging trial. Goring et al. 2016 describe the setting and the standard fix of inserting a distribution for the unknown contrast, and Pedder et al. 2021 state that comparisons between disconnected treatments are not possible without strong assumptions. Unanchored MAIC and STC sit in this class; their requirement is conditional exchangeability of absolute potential outcomes across studies together with positivity, consistency, and correct outcome modeling, which Phillippo et al. 2018 describe as much stronger assumptions widely regarded as infeasible.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Why it is open
The missing quantity is a structural property of the evidence graph rather than a sampling limitation: the cross-component contrast lies in a null direction of the design, so within-component precision can grow without ever touching it. Removing the anchor removes the structure that made cross-trial differences cancel, so the analysis must reconstruct an absolute-outcome comparison from studies never designed to be compared. Once any linking structure is added, Bayesian and frequentist software returns a finite estimate with an interval that reads to a decision maker exactly like an identified result, and posterior connectedness is not likelihood identification. Reporting guidance for population-adjusted comparisons now exists (Ishak et al. 2025), so this is not a total absence of standards, but that framework is scoped to population adjustment and does not require a disconnected-network result to name the structure that supplied the cross-gap contrast.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Precede every disconnected-network result with an explicit statement that the randomized evidence identifies effects only within each connected component and that the cross-component comparison is identified only after imposing the stated bridge assumptions. Report the linking structure as part of the estimand definition rather than as a modeling footnote, and extend the existing population-adjustment reporting framework so it covers which parameter carries a disconnected gap. Drop the goal of a single algorithm combining five named linking devices: that combination is unbuilt only because nobody has proposed it, and the useful work is making whichever bridge is used auditable.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “In a connected network the relative effect between two treatments is identified through a path of randomized contrasts; when no such path exists the cross-subnetwork contrast is not merely imprecise but absent from the randomized likelihood. Any finite estimate of that contrast is supplied entirely by structure the analyst imposes, which is why unanchored MAIC and STC and other disconnected-network methods inherit strong no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions.”
What was wrong with it. The source asserted the identification claim without attribution; the literature auditor supplied the canonical sources, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1204 (Goring et al. 2016), doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315 (Pedder et al. 2021), and doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740 (Phillippo et al. 2018), so the claim is now sourced. GPT-5.6 Sol replaced the loose no-unmeasured-confounding wording with the assumption unanchored comparisons actually require, and neither auditor could establish the entry’s further claims that disconnected aggregate-data methods are still niche or that no algorithm combines five named linking devices, so both are dropped.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, so I retrieved the canonical sources myself. Goring et al. 2016 (Res Synth Methods) frames disconnected networks exactly as the entry does and states the standard fix is to insert a distribution for the unknown contrast. Pedder et al. 2021 states outright that comparisons between disconnected treatments are not possible without strong assumptions. Phillippo et al. 2018 supplies the unanchored-MAIC/STC claim verbatim. The structural non-identification claim is correct and cannot be solved by any paper, so open is right. Caveats: two claims are absence claims I cannot verify by finding nothing, namely that disconnected aggregate-data methods are ‘still niche in practice’ and that ‘no network-connecting algorithm currently combines’ five named devices. The second is trivially true only because nobody has proposed that particular five-way combination; it should not be read as a research gap of consequence. The entry should cite Goring 2016, which is the reference a disconnected-networks reader will expect first. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1204: Sources the unsourced identification claims and is the canonical missing citation for this entry. Cites 10.1177/0272989X17725740: Sources the claim that unanchored MAIC and STC inherit much stronger (no-unmeasured-confounding style) assumptions. Cites 10.1177/0272989X20983315: Sources the claim that a cross-gap contrast requires structure beyond the randomized evidence.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C2-C6 are correct for a standard contrast-based NMA after fixing a common estimand and the usual consistency and transport assumptions. With an edge-incidence design, a disconnected graph has component-specific shift directions that leave the randomized likelihood unchanged; a cross-component contrast is outside the design row space. Additional within-component data cannot remove that null direction. A proper prior, equality restriction, component or class model, external evidence, or bridging trial can produce a finite estimate, but posterior connectedness is not likelihood identification. C7 is directionally correct, although the precise requirement for unanchored MAIC or STC is conditional exchangeability of absolute potential outcomes across studies, together with positivity, consistency, and correct modeling, rather than generic treatment-confounding language. C8-C9 and C1 are practice, universal-absence, or sourcing claims that cannot be established under this technical-only audit. Identification disclosure is decision-critical; the proposed five-way algorithm is a roadmap item.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text: DIS-03 Not supported High priority Promising

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Statement
Arm-based baseline-synthesis, reference-prediction, and aggregate-level matching models link disconnected subnetworks through a baseline-outcome structure, allowing disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies to be included. An observed control-arm risk depends on prognosis, endpoint definition, follow-up, ascertainment, care context, and calendar time, so it is not intrinsically exchangeable across designs or components. Thom et al. 2022 measured what this costs: disconnected-treatment bias ran from -0.16 to 0.392 for aggregate-level matching and from -0.102 to 0.40 for reference prediction, with coverage of 0.30 to 0.82 and 0.64 to 0.94 respectively, and they recommend reference prediction on coverage grounds. Beliveau et al. 2017 is not the cautionary result the source made it: across the two disconnected datasets it examined it found the use of random baseline treatment effects appropriate, while warning that the normality and exchangeability assumptions could be inappropriate in datasets it did not observe.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Why it is open
Where a single baseline parameter both carries the cross-gap bridge and absorbs study-level nuisance variation, nothing inside a disconnected graph separates the two roles, so a difference in endpoint definition can be absorbed as a difference in prognosis and propagated into the relative effect. Observed baseline heterogeneity and design associations can be examined, but no such check reaches the cross-gap counterfactual, which is exactly what the bridge supplies, and regression to the mean and measurement error in the baseline term add distortion invisible in the fitted output. Thom et al. 2022 show the residual bias and undercoverage are material rather than theoretical, and better relative coverage for reference prediction in one simulation program is a conditional preference under stated assumptions, not evidence that disconnected networks are solved.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Beliveau et al. 2017
asks how dangerous random baseline treatment effects are in disconnected networks and finds their use appropriate for the two datasets considered, with an explicit caveat about datasets it did not observe


Thom et al. 2022
extends baseline-effect and aggregate-level matching to disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies, and quantifies the residual bias and undercoverage of both by simulation

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use separate baseline distributions for connected, disconnected, and single-arm evidence, and use commensurate rather than fully exchangeable baseline priors so the bridge is down-weighted when source and target baselines conflict. Condition reference prediction on design covariates where the relevant covariates are measured, overlap, and can be modeled correctly, since the improvement depends on those conditions rather than being automatic, and calibrate with negative controls that detect design-driven baseline differences. Report an explicit posterior decomposition of how much the baseline bridge moves each treatment contrast, and treat reference prediction as a conditional method rather than a solution to disconnection.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Verification

Verdict. Not supported. No accessible source substantiates the claim as stated.
The source said. “Arm-based baseline-synthesis, reference-prediction, and aggregate-level matching models link disconnected subnetworks through a baseline-outcome structure, allowing disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies to be included. Baseline risk is not a universal bridge: it mixes prognosis with outcome definition, ascertainment, follow-up, supportive care, and calendar time, and simulations show cross-disconnected estimates can still be materially biased.”
What was wrong with it. The source’s gloss on Beliveau et al. 2017, its severity line, and the associated claim all inverted the paper’s finding; the literature auditor quoted doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256 saying that for the two datasets considered the use of random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks was appropriate. GPT-5.6 Sol added that not every implementation forces one baseline parameter to carry both nuisance variation and the whole bridge, and that observed baseline heterogeneity and its association with design features can be partly assessed, so the untestability narrows to the missing cross-gap counterfactual.

Literature and prior-art check

open / misattributed. I read the Beliveau et al. 2017 abstract in full. The title is a question and the paper’s answer is largely reassuring, not cautionary: ‘For the 2 datasets considered, we found that the use of random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks was appropriate.’ The entry’s prior_work gloss (‘shows random baseline treatment effects can be dangerous’), the severity line, and claim 1 all invert the paper’s finding. The authors do add a hedge about other datasets, which is the defensible version. This is the kind of error the people who wrote the paper will notice immediately. Everything attributed to Thom et al. 2022 checks out exactly: disconnected-treatment bias -0.16 to 0.392 (ALM) and -0.102 to 0.40 (reference prediction), coverage 0.30-0.82 versus 0.64-0.94, and ‘Reference prediction has greater coverage and may be recommended overall.’ The substantive problem (baseline risk mixes prognosis with ascertainment and design era) remains open; only the attribution needs fixing.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The technical core of C2-C9 and C13 is sound. An observed control-arm risk depends on prognosis, endpoint definition, follow-up, ascertainment, care context, and calendar time, so it is not intrinsically exchangeable across designs or components. A baseline bridge requires an appropriate arm-level outcome model plus explicit exchangeability or regression assumptions, and aggregate relationships do not identify individual-level transportability. The report nevertheless overgeneralizes. Not every implementation makes one baseline parameter carry both nuisance variation and the entire bridge; separate distributions, design covariates, measurement-error models, and partial pooling are possible. Observed baseline heterogeneity and design associations can be assessed, although such checks cannot validate the missing cross-gap counterfactual. Conditioning on design covariates is helpful only with measured relevant covariates, overlap, and a correctly specified model. C14-C15 are universal current-method absence claims, while C1 and C10-C12 are paper-attribution claims; none is established by the permitted technical and source-code lens. The issue is high priority only when baseline structure materially carries the decision contrast.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R6:counter-quote-uncontested

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text: DIS-05 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Statement
Hierarchical class models group treatments into classes and borrow strength across them, and can stabilize sparse or disconnected evidence where a network is disconnected at the treatment level but connected at the class level, as Perren et al. 2026 state in their practical guide and four-step model-selection algorithm. Class definitions are contestable and can hide genuine between-treatment heterogeneity. Observed class members can inform and sometimes challenge the hierarchy: Perren et al. assess it by comparing model fit statistics and between-study and between-treatment standard deviations, and advise looking for alternative methods when the class assumption is not supported. What cannot be validated is extrapolation of that learned relationship to a treatment whose cross-gap effect has no independent randomized identification.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Why it is open
The class mean and variance supply the cross-gap information, so a treatment on the far side of the gap is assigned an effect largely by its class membership rather than by evidence about it. The class partition is an analyst input, several plausible partitions are compatible with the same fit statistics, and a class variance driven small imposes similarity the data never demonstrated, with the resulting shrinkage read as precision. Model selection that optimizes fit inside the observed evidence does not test whether borrowing extrapolates to a held-out treatment, and leave-one-treatment-out validation works only when the held-out effect remains independently identifiable after deletion, which is exactly what fails across a gap.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Perren et al. 2026
publishes a practical class-effects guide and four-step model-selection algorithm, states that class effect models can estimate relative effects in networks disconnected at the treatment level but connected at the class level, and documents the implementation of class effects in multinma

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Let clinically prespecified classes constrain the candidate structures and use transparent algorithmic comparison and sensitivity analysis to choose among them, rather than treating either alone as sufficient. Extend the assessment step in Perren et al. toward held-out validation wherever a treatment can be deleted from a connected part of a network and its effect still identified, since that is the only setting in which class borrowing can be scored against something it did not see. Use structured heterogeneity with class-specific variance components, robust priors, and multivariate random effects so similarity is estimated rather than imposed, and report how much of the target contrast the class bridge contributed through shrinkage.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Class-effect bridges rest on untestable class exchangeability” The title calls class exchangeability untestable, but the audit found observed class members can inform and challenge the hierarchy through fit and variance comparisons.
The source said. “Hierarchical class models group treatments into classes, borrow strength across them, and can stabilize sparse or disconnected evidence under exchangeability within classes and a correctly specified class variance; a practical class-effects guide with a model-selection algorithm was published in 2026. Class definitions are contestable, may hide genuine heterogeneity, and class exchangeability cannot be tested from the disconnected data.”
What was wrong with it. The source said class exchangeability cannot be tested from the disconnected data; GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed this to the extrapolation, since with several observed treatments per class the data can inform class means, between-treatment variance, outliers, and the relative fit of candidate hierarchies, and since class variance is normally estimated with uncertainty rather than fixed at a supposedly correct value. The literature auditor confirmed doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887 and noted that leave-one-treatment-out validation, class-outlier probability, and the preference for clinical over algorithmic class definition are the catalog’s own proposals rather than findings of that paper; class effects also already ship in multinma 0.8.0.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I read the Perren et al. 2026 open-access text. The citation is accurate: it is a practical guide with a four-step model-selection algorithm, and it does claim disconnected-network utility: ‘In some cases, class effect models can also facilitate the estimation of relative effects in evidence networks that are disconnected at the treatment level, as long as they are connected at the class level.’ Two caveats. First, the entry’s claim that class exchangeability ‘cannot be tested from the disconnected evidence itself’ is the entry’s own inference, not Perren’s; Perren instead offers assessment by comparing model fit statistics and between-study/between-treatment standard deviations, and warns that ‘if the network is disconnected at the treatment level but a class model assumption is not supported, we may need to look for alternative methods’. Second, the paper does not prescribe algorithmic versus clinical class definition, so claim 9 is the entry’s recommendation, not a finding. Neither leave-one-treatment-out validation nor a class-outlier probability appears in Perren. Class effects shipped in multinma 0.8.0, which the entry does not note. Cites 10.1177/0272989X251389887: Confirms the citation and supplies the disconnected-network caveat the entry paraphrases; also documents implementation of class effects in multinma.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2, C4, C6, and C7 are broadly correct: hierarchical class models borrow through a distributional similarity assumption, and poorly justified classes can hide genuine treatment heterogeneity. C3 is too absolute. With several observed treatments per class, the data can inform class means, between-treatment variance, outliers, and relative fit of candidate hierarchies. What remains untestable is extrapolation of that learned relationship to the particular treatment or cross-gap contrast lacking independent identification. C5 is imprecise because class variance may be estimated with uncertainty rather than fixed at a supposedly correct value. C8 works only when the held-out treatment effect remains independently identifiable after deletion; otherwise the validation target is unavailable. C9 is overly categorical: clinical prespecification should constrain the candidate structures, but transparent algorithmic comparison and sensitivity analysis can supplement it. C1 is a publication-attribution claim outside this lens. The residual transport problem remains open and important when class borrowing determines the decision.
