title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text: DIS-07 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Statement
Real-world or historical controls can bridge a disconnected gap, but doing so replaces randomization-only identification with cross-design exchangeability, transportability, consistency, and positivity assumptions. If residual design bias is left unmodeled, reported intervals omit an important source of uncertainty; the false precision follows from that omission rather than arising automatically. Most of the design-bias layer the source proposed is already built: Hussein et al. 2023 nest studies within designs with an additional, optionally class-specific bias parameter for observational studies and report that uncertainty around effect estimates increased once design differences were modeled; Schmitz et al. 2018 bridged two disconnected myeloma networks with single-arm observational data and propagated bridge uncertainty by analyzing the space of possible matches; a 2022 rheumatoid arthritis study bridged first- and second-line networks using registry data with target-trial emulation; and robust mixture priors for down-weighting external information have been standard since Schmidli et al. 2014. What remains is calibration: where no overlapping randomized and observational contrasts, validation data, negative controls, or external calibration inform the bias, treatment effect and residual design bias are not separately identified.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Why it is open
The external control supplies the missing arm, so any difference between the observational source and the randomized trials that still affects the outcome after adjustment loads directly onto the cross-gap contrast. A synthesis likelihood that treats the external control as another randomized arm shrinks the interval while leaving that residual bias unmodeled. Where no design overlaps both evidence types and no validation or negative-control data exist, the treatment effect and the residual design bias are not separately identified, and there is no accepted way to elicit or calibrate the bias parameter that the published hierarchical models require as an input.

What it contributes

Schmitz et al. 2018
bridges a genuinely disconnected myeloma network with single-arm observational data and incorporates bridge uncertainty by analyzing the space of possible matches


Bridging disconnected networks of first and second lines of biologic therapies in rheumatoid arthritis with registry data (2022)

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use the published design-bias machinery rather than rebuilding it: fit hierarchical models with design-level bias parameters, use robust mixture priors to down-weight external evidence and react to prior-data conflict, and keep the randomized and observational likelihoods separate. Direct new work at the calibration problem that remains: elicitation protocols and empirical calibration evidence for how large residual design bias is in a given disease area and era, and estimation of it wherever overlapping randomized and observational contrasts, validation samples, or negative controls exist. Report the sensitivity of the cross-gap contrast to that bias parameter alongside the point estimate, since separating likelihoods or emulating a target trial does not by itself remove residual bias.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Real-world or historical controls can create a bridge across a disconnected gap, but doing so converts the problem into one of cross-design causal synthesis. Combining randomized and nonrandomized evidence without an explicit design-bias layer often produces false precision.”
What was wrong with it. The source listed the design-bias layer, robust priors, cross-design estimators, and target-trial emulation as directions to build; the literature auditor found each already published, at doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01925-5, doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7, doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2022.06.011, and doi:10.1111/biom.12242. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed two overstatements: only residual differences affecting the outcome after valid adjustment load onto the contrast, not all confounding, selection, and measurement differences, and design bias is not invariably unidentified, since overlapping randomized and observational comparisons, validation samples, negative controls, or external calibration can inform it.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty and the entry’s proposed direction is largely already published. Hussein et al. 2023 (BMC Med Res Methodol) build exactly the design-bias layer the entry asks for: hierarchical NMA models nesting studies within designs with an additional bias parameter for observational studies, optionally class-specific, and they report that uncertainty around effect estimates increased once design differences were modelled, which is the entry’s false-precision claim demonstrated. Schmitz et al. 2018 bridged two genuinely disconnected myeloma networks with single-arm observational studies and propagated bridge uncertainty by analysing the space of possible matches. Bujkiewicz et al. 2022 bridged disconnected first- and second-line networks using registry data with target-trial emulation, which the entry lists as a future direction. Robust mixture priors for down-weighting external information are standard since Schmidli et al. 2014. What genuinely remains open is calibration and elicitation of design-bias parameters, which are not identified from the data. The entry overstates novelty by presenting existing methods as directions. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01925-5: Implements the explicit design-bias layer the entry proposes, and shows the widened uncertainty relative to naive pooling. Cites 10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7: External-control bridging of a real disconnected network with explicit propagation of bridge-choice uncertainty. Cites 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2022.06.011: Target-trial emulation as a bridge is already implemented, not merely a proposal. Cites 10.1111/biom.12242: The robust/down-weighting prior for external controls the entry proposes is an established, validated construction.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is correct: once an external or historical control carries the missing comparison, identification rests on cross-design exchangeability, transportability, consistency, and positivity rather than randomization alone. C2 is directionally correct but its frequency word often is empirical, and false precision is conditional rather than automatic. The problem occurs when nominal uncertainty conditions on an unjustified no-residual-bias assumption. The why-open text overstates that all design differences load onto the contrast; only residual differences affecting the outcome after valid adjustment do so. Design bias is not invariably unidentified or necessarily elicited. It may be estimated or partially informed by overlapping randomized and observational comparisons, validation samples, negative controls, or external calibration. Without such information, however, treatment effect and residual design bias are not separately identified. The strategies in C3 are useful conditional tools, but separating likelihoods, down-weighting, or target-trial emulation alone does not remove residual bias. The residual identification problem remains open and decision-critical when the external control materially carries the comparison.

title: Structured elicitation is not applied to the cross-gap contrast
text: DIS-09 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Structured elicitation is not applied to the cross-gap contrast
text:
Statement
When the likelihood does not identify a cross-gap contrast, an explicitly justified prior can supply external identifying information under the Bayesian model, though it does not create likelihood identification; Goring et al. 2016 already describe inserting a distribution for the unknown treatment effect as the recommended approach for disconnected networks. Structured elicitation is likewise codified rather than missing: the NIHR reference protocol of Bojke, Soares and Claxton covers expert selection, level of elicitation, fitting, and pooling, and the STEER resources operationalize it for health care decision making. Software defaults are modeling conventions that may dominate a flat likelihood direction; calling a hidden default prior undocumented expert judgment overstates it, since a default need not represent anyone’s elicited belief. What is not standard is applying either apparatus to the cross-gap quantity itself, and reporting prior-only alongside posterior estimates so a reader can see how much of the answer is prior.

title: Structured elicitation is not applied to the cross-gap contrast
text:
Why it is open
In a weakly identified disconnected model the prior determines the flat direction of the likelihood, so the number a reader sees can be mostly prior, and without a prior-only estimate beside the posterior there is no way to tell how much. The elicitation protocols that exist were built for health-economic parameters rather than for cross-gap treatment contrasts, which are harder to phrase in clinically interpretable terms and harder to check against an expert’s experience. Prior-data conflict diagnostics are also ill-posed for a parameter with no likelihood contribution across the gap, since there is nothing for the prior to conflict with.

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text: DIS-11 Partially addressed Very high priority Established

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Statement
Predictive criteria computed on observed within-subnetwork units compare models but cannot establish the correctness of an unobserved cross-gap extrapolation, and leave-one-out cross-validation will still return a winner when every candidate shares a false bridge assumption. The qualifier matters: predictive checks can falsify observable restrictions, and validation using external cross-gap evidence or synthetic deletion of a link from a connected network does have leverage. Population comparison is a useful screening diagnostic for bridges that require population exchangeability, but it is computed over reported covariates while the bridge requires exchangeability with respect to every variable creating cross-study outcome differences, so it cannot rule out unmeasured prognostic or design differences; it is not logically required for component, class, or mechanistic bridges. Both checks are shipping alongside disconnected-network fits: multinma pull request #68 lists LOO-PSIS cross-validation and compare_populations() under testing.

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Why it is open
Predictive scores measure fit to observed data while the bridge governs an extrapolation to a contrast that is unobserved by construction, so an ordinary within-subnetwork leave-one-out score has no leverage on it, and a ranking reads as validation to a user who does not check what was held out. The prediction unit is usually left implicit in software output, so reported criteria may not answer a consistent question across models, and grouped validation at the study or subnetwork level, which would come closer to the cross-gap question, is unimplemented in the tools the auditors inspected. A favorable similarity table over reported covariates is easy to produce and looks like evidence, so it is presented as justification even for bridges whose assumption is not about population overlap at all.

Declare the prediction unit explicitly (participant, arm, study, or subnetwork), implement leave-one-study and leave-one-subnetwork validation matched to the cross-gap question, and keep ordinary predictive criteria labeled as model comparison. Where a connected network can be thinned into a disconnected one, use synthetic bridge deletion as the validation with actual leverage, and use external cross-gap evidence where any exists. title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text: DIS-13 Confirmed open Very high priority Speculative Tractability 2/5

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Statement
Using several imperfect bridges at once is a reasonable response to bridge-choice uncertainty, but the aggregation rule is the problem: if candidate bridges induce the same observed-data distribution within the components and differ only across the unobserved gap, the data cannot update weights for cross-gap correctness. Weights can still be estimated against an observed predictive objective; that objective simply need not track cross-gap accuracy. Two of the listed constructions are established rather than novel: a mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states is the robust meta-analytic-predictive prior of Schmidli et al. 2014, and ensembling over a bridge’s admissible configurations was done in a real disconnected network by Schmitz et al. 2018, who propagated uncertainty by analyzing the space of possible matches. What has not been done is averaging across distinct bridge families in a disconnected network, where the weights are unidentified.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Why it is open
Ensemble weights are learned from fit inside the connected components while the quantity at stake is a functional of the extrapolation across the gap, and nothing in the data-generating structure forces the two to agree, so a bridge that fits the observed subnetworks best can extrapolate worst. Model averaging cannot bear on any assumption every member shares, so an ensemble whose families all assume, say, population exchangeability inherits that assumption intact while looking like a hedge. Averaging across families is also incoherent when the members target different estimands, and none of these constructions has been developed or validated for a disconnected network; the catalog’s own portfolio rates the direction at tractability 2 of 5 because validation is difficult.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Schmidli et al. 2014
establishes the two- and three-component mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states, so that construction is validated prior art rather than a new direction


Schmitz et al. 2018
ensembles over the admissible configurations of a single bridge in a genuinely disconnected network by analyzing the space of possible matches

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing constructions rather than inventing them: robust mixture priors and match-space ensembling already work within a bridge, and the open step is extending them across families with weights that are declared rather than estimated, or with bridge-specific bias parameters shrunk toward zero. Score any proposal on synthetic bridge-deletion experiments, where a connected network is thinned so the cross-gap answer is known, since that is the only setting where ensemble weights can be checked against extrapolation accuracy. Never treat model averaging as validation: pair it with structural sensitivity analysis over the assumptions the members share, and report intersection or union bounds so disagreement between bridges is visible rather than absorbed into a single interval.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Multi-bridge ensembles need weights that cannot be learned” The title says the weights cannot be learned at all, but the audit noted weights can be estimated against an observed predictive objective that simply need not track cross-gap accuracy.
The source said. “A novel direction is to use several imperfect bridges simultaneously without pretending any one is certainly valid, via Bayesian model averaging over bridge families, stacking on leave-one-study or synthetic bridge-deletion prediction, robust Bayes with neighborhoods around each bridge, intersection or union bounds, a mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states, or bridge-specific bias parameters shrunk toward zero. Predictive performance within observed subnetworks may not identify which bridge extrapolates correctly across the gap, so the aggregation rule itself is not identified.”
What was wrong with it. The source described mixture priors, robust Bayes, and bridge ensembles as undeveloped; the literature auditor identified doi:10.1111/biom.12242 and doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7 as existing validated constructions, so the novelty claim narrows to averaging across distinct bridge families. GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the claim that averaging narrows intervals relative to any single model, which is false in general because a mixture variance contains both within-model and between-model components, and noted that a single model can include an explicit bridge-discrepancy term, so selecting one model does not always understate uncertainty.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The central claim, that ensemble weights learned inside connected components need not identify which bridge extrapolates across a gap, is correct and I found nothing that solves it. But two of the listed constructions are presented as novel when they are established methods in adjacent literatures, and the entry should say so. A ‘mixture prior containing commensurate, partially commensurate, and noncommensurate states’ is the robust meta-analytic-predictive prior of Schmidli et al. 2014, a validated construction with a large downstream literature on external and historical controls; robust Bayes over neighbourhoods likewise. Ensembling over a bridge’s admissible configurations has already been done in a real disconnected network: Schmitz et al. 2018 propagate uncertainty by analysing the space of possible matches. So the accurate framing is not that these constructions are undeveloped, but that they have never been developed for averaging across distinct bridge families in a disconnected network, where the weights are unidentified. Claim 5 is self-referential to the source report and unauditable. Cites 10.1111/biom.12242: Shows the proposed commensurate-to-noncommensurate mixture prior is an established validated construction, not a new direction. Cites 10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7: Prior instance of ensembling over admissible bridge configurations in a genuinely disconnected network.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C6 captures the real problem when candidate bridges are observationally equivalent on the observed subnetworks and differ only in their cross-gap extrapolations. Otherwise, ensemble weights can be learned for an observed-data predictive objective, although that objective need not track cross-gap accuracy. C1 is not universal because a single model can explicitly include bridge discrepancy or conservative bounds. The claim that averaging narrows intervals relative to any single model is mathematically false in general: mixture variance contains both within-model and between-model components and may increase or decrease interval width relative to particular members. C3-C4 are coherent constructions, but they do not solve the relevance of the weighting objective. C2 is a literature-status claim outside this audit, while C5 is confirmed only as a self-description of the local report.

text:
Statement
Decision-linked threshold analysis is not missing. Phillippo et al. 2018 derive bias-adjustment thresholds giving the smallest changes to the data that change a treatment decision in fixed and random-effects NMA, released as the CRAN package nmathresh, and the cpaic development package maps uniform box-bounded component main-effect drift to any scalar link-scale decision threshold, which for a one-dimensional monotone economic model can already represent a reimbursement tipping point. Two extensions are genuinely absent: perturbing a cross-gap bridge parameter in a disconnected network rather than an observed data point, and propagating a multidimensional cross-gap identified set through costs, QALYs, survival extrapolation, and competing decisions to incremental net benefit. cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub and is not installable from CRAN, so its part of this capability is not available to a general user.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Why it is open
The existing threshold machinery perturbs observed evidence in a connected network, so it has no notion of a bridge parameter carrying a gap, and the fragility calculation that does perturb a bridge is limited to a uniform box bound on component main effects and to a scalar threshold on the link scale. Mapping a drift set into a reimbursement decision needs the economic model as well as the synthesis model, so it crosses the boundary between synthesis software and decision-analytic software and neither side currently owns the interface. Until that interface exists, a bound on the effect scale cannot be translated into a statement about whether the recommendation is robust, except in the special case where net benefit is monotone in a single contrast.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the interface rather than the primitive: extend decision-invariant threshold analysis so the perturbed quantity is a bridge parameter in a disconnected network, and extend the existing per-component fragility calculation from a scalar link-scale threshold to a full net-benefit boundary. Propagate multidimensional identified sets through the health-economic model and report the smallest cross-gap assumption violation that flips the reimbursement decision, alongside superiority and noninferiority thresholds. Where net benefit is monotone in a single contrast, document that the existing scalar-threshold tools already answer the question, so effort goes to the cases they do not cover.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Decision-invariant threshold analysis (Phillippo et al. 2018, R package nmathresh) already reports the smallest change to observed evidence that flips a treatment recommendation in a connected NMA, but it has not been extended to perturbations of a cross-gap bridge parameter in a disconnected network, nor propagated through a cost-effectiveness model to a net-benefit or reimbursement threshold.
The source titled this. “Cross-gap bounds are not linked to decision thresholds” The title says bounds are not linked to decision thresholds, but decision-invariant threshold analysis is on CRAN and component-drift fragility already maps to a decision threshold.
The source said. “The research opportunity flagged by the report is to connect partial-identification bounds for cross-gap contrasts to decision thresholds and net benefit, producing the smallest assumption violation that changes reimbursement.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no current method reports the smallest cross-gap assumption violation that would change a reimbursement decision and that bounds are not linked to decision thresholds; both auditors judged this too strong. The literature auditor cited doi:10.1111/rssa.12341 and the nmathresh package, and GPT-5.6 Sol found that cpaic’s bridge_fragility() already computes the smallest per-component drift that moves the contrast to a user-supplied decision threshold. What survives is the net-benefit and reimbursement propagation, not an absence of all decision-linking machinery.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Claim 1, that no current method reports the smallest assumption violation that would change a decision, is contradicted as written. Phillippo, Dias, Ades, Didelez and Welton (JRSS-A 2018) derive decision-invariant bias-adjustment thresholds that give exactly ‘the smallest changes to the data that result in a change of treatment decision’, for individual studies or aggregate contrasts, in fixed and random-effects NMA, with an accompanying R package; nmathresh is on CRAN and its stated purpose is ‘the calculation and presentation of decision-invariant bias adjustment thresholds and intervals for Network Meta-Analysis’. What is genuinely missing is the two extensions the entry actually needs: the perturbed quantity being a bridge parameter in a disconnected network rather than an observed data point, and the decision being net benefit at a cost-effectiveness threshold rather than the treatment recommendation from the synthesis. Stated that way the problem is real and well posed. Stated as ‘no current method’, it will be read as unfamiliarity with a well-known Bristol method by the same group whose software the catalog audits elsewhere. Cites 10.1111/rssa.12341: Provides the decision-linked smallest-violation quantity the entry claims does not exist, for connected NMA. Cites cran:nmathresh: Released implementation of decision-invariant thresholds, showing this is available software rather than a research direction.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is too absolute. At the requested cpaic snapshot, the exported bridge_fragility() function computes d* = |D - tau| / sum|m_c| per posterior draw for box-bounded cross-subnetwork component drift and accepts any finite scalar link-scale decision threshold. Mathematically, the drift set produces the interval [D - d sum|m_c|, D + d sum|m_c|], so this is exactly the smallest violation whose bound reaches tau. For a one-dimensional monotone economic model whose net-benefit boundary can be translated into tau, it can already represent a reimbursement tipping point. C2 is therefore false regarding decision thresholds, although it remains true regarding general net benefit: cpaic does not propagate multidimensional identified sets through costs, QALYs, survival extrapolation, or competing decisions. The remaining work is an economic-model interface, not an absence of all decision-linking machinery. Very-high severity is conditional on the reimbursement decision actually being bridge-sensitive. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: bridge_fragility() implements the exact tipping violation for uniform per-component main-effect drift relative to a user-supplied scalar decision threshold; it does not implement general net-benefit propagation..

Decision path

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text: EST-01 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Statement
Applied ITC and PAIC practice still defaults the target population to whichever aggregate-data trial reported enough baseline covariates, and reported effects are rarely labeled with the population they refer to. The normative half of the source’s Direction A is not new: NICE DSU TSD18 (Phillippo et al. 2018, doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) has required since 2016 that the target population be stated explicitly and that population-adjusted effects be generated for it, and it names a cohort or registry population relevant to the decision as the appropriate external source. The machinery is not missing either: multilevel network meta-regression estimates every contrast in a network in one externally supplied target population (Phillippo et al. 2020, doi:10.1111/rssa.12579; doi:10.1002/sim.8759), and multinma implements it through relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects(), each of which accepts an arbitrary target via newdata. What survives is the gap between that requirement and practice, together with the substantive judgment of which target to name, which no statistical criterion settles.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Why it is open
The requirement exists but nothing enforces it at the point where the target is actually chosen, so the estimator’s target is still fixed by which trial reported enough baseline variables, and no diagnostic run on the source analysis can flag a target that was never declared. Transporting a whole network to one external population needs IPD for at least one study and a covariate law for the target, so the capability that exists in ML-NMR is unavailable in exactly the aggregate-only networks where the default is most damaging. Choosing among candidate target sources is a policy judgment no statistical criterion settles, and falling back to an overlap population restores comparability only if the whole network shares one declared overlap estimand rather than a different overlap per pair. Because a single unlabeled symbol denotes both the estimated and the required quantity, the substitution leaves no trace for a reviewer to challenge.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2018, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD18)
Requires that the target population for any treatment comparison be stated explicitly and that population-adjusted relative effects be generated for that target, and names a cohort or registry population relevant to the clinical decision as the appropriate source, which is unlikely to match the aggregate-data trial population. It supplies the normative half of Direction A a decade before this agenda; it does not make the declaration a field anyone checks outside NICE submissions.


Phillippo, Dias, Elsada, Ades and Welton 2020, Multilevel network meta-regression for population-adjusted treatment comparisons, JRSS-A
Defines the one-stage individual-level regression that fits aggregate data by integration and produces population-adjusted contrasts for a specified target population across a whole network, which is the machinery the entry described as nonexistent. It requires IPD from at least one study.


Phillippo, Dias, Ades, Belger, Brnabic, Schacht, Saure, Kadziola and Welton 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study, Statistics in Medicine
Simulation evidence that ML-NMR extends to larger treatment networks and produces estimates in any target population, unlike pairwise MAIC and STC.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (R package)
Implements ML-NMR, with relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() all accepting newdata describing an arbitrary target population’s covariate distribution, so estimating every network contrast in one declared target is available software rather than a proposal.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not rebuild the declaration rule or the network estimator, since both exist. The work is to make the declared target binding: carry the TSD18 requirement into journal and submission templates, label every reported contrast with its population, and treat target-specific prediction from a network model as the default output rather than an option. Where the full decision target lacks covariate support, change the estimand to one common overlap population for the whole network, and use several targets as sensitivity analysis rather than in place of a primary decision target. The measurable question is whether an enforced declaration changes what appears in submissions, not whether the method exists.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Although NICE DSU TSD18 has required since 2016 that the target population be explicitly stated, and although ML-NMR/multinma can estimate every network contrast in one externally supplied target population, applied ITC and PAIC practice still defaults the target to whichever aggregate-data trial reported enough covariates, and reported effects are rarely labelled with the population they refer to.
The source said. “Population-adjusted analyses adjust to whichever aggregate-data trial population happens to be reportable, while the decision concerns a different population, and the reported effect carries no label identifying the population it refers to. The report’s Direction A instead requires every relevant contrast to be estimated in one externally defined target population P*, chosen from a named source such as a jurisdictional registry, the eligible treatment population, a pooled trial-eligible population, a standardized reference population, or an overlap population where the full target is unsupported.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated both explicit target declaration and one-target network estimation as absent; the literature auditor found both already in place, in Recommendation 6 of NICE DSU TSD18 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) and in ML-NMR as implemented in multinma (https://cran.r-project.org/package=multinma). GPT-5.6 Sol added that the target need not come from an external data source, that an overlap target is acceptable only as one common network estimand rather than pair by pair, and that reporting several targets is sensitivity analysis rather than a substitute for naming a primary decision target.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Phillippo et al. 2018 Med Decis Making (the peer-reviewed NICE DSU TSD18). Its Recommendation 6 reads: ‘The target population for any treatment comparison must be explicitly stated, and population-adjusted estimates of the relative treatment effects must be generated for this target population.’ It also already names the external source the entry asks for: ‘the target population should be a cohort or registry study population relevant to the clinical decision, which is unlikely to match the population of the [AgD] trial.’ The practice half of the entry survives (Phillippo 2019 NICE review; Serret-Larmande 2023 found 3/133 PAIC articles reported all key methodological aspects). What does not survive is ‘there is no standard machinery for … transporting every contrast in a network to it at once’: ML-NMR does exactly that, and multinma implements relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() with a newdata target population. The claim that the report ‘names exactly five candidate sources’ is self-referential and not externally checkable. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Already mandates explicit target-population declaration for NICE submissions and names registry/cohort populations as the appropriate external source, i.e. the normative half of Direction A predates this agenda by a decade.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.8759: Establishes ML-NMR as machinery that transports all contrasts of a network into a single declared target population.. Cites cran:multinma: Software implementation: relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() all accept newdata describing an arbitrary target population’s covariate distribution..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 describes conventional pairwise anchored MAIC/STC, not ITC or PAIC generally; C2 and C6 are prevalence or adoption claims that this technical audit cannot establish. C3 is a second transport only when a population-indexed effect is reused in another population; a genuinely invariant conditional parameter is different. A coherent multi-treatment decision normally needs a common decision target, but C4 is too absolute: the target need not come from an external data source, and some decisions legitimately require several populations. C5’s count of five is textually true but methodologically vacuous. C7 is acceptable only as an explicit change to a common network overlap estimand; pair-specific overlap targets destroy contrast comparability. C8 is useful sensitivity analysis, not a substitute for choosing a primary decision target. Target declaration and common-target network standardization already have methodological and software machinery, so the technical problem is partly solved; data support and disciplined use remain. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Already requires an explicit target population and effects generated for that target, resolving the claim that no target-declaration machinery exists.. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Provides one-stage network machinery for population-adjusted contrasts in a specified target population.. Cites cran:multinma: Implements target-specific prediction and marginal-effect calculations for a network, so the capability is not absent..

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text: EST-03 Not supported Very high priority Promising

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text:
Statement
Odds ratios and hazard ratios can vary across populations even without confounding, so the shared effect modifier assumption alone does not make a marginal effect portable to an arbitrary population. The result is not new and does not belong to the citation the source gave it: Remiro-Azocar (doi:10.1002/sim.10111) established the stronger result that under non-collapsibility even purely prognostic variables shift the marginal effect, Phillippo et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/sim.8965) had already noted that marginal effects are less transportable than population-average conditional ones, and Chandler and Ishak (arxiv:2602.17041) restate it inside an explicit two-step transportability framing for PAIC. Collapsibility is also not the same as transportability: a risk difference or an RMST difference marginalizes cleanly but still varies across populations when effects are heterogeneous, and a standardized risk is a target-specific absolute quantity rather than a treatment-effect scale.

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text:
Why it is open
Non-collapsibility is a property of the effect measure rather than a bias, so it cannot be removed by better adjustment, better models or larger samples. An assumption about effect modification of the conditional contrast does not license moving the marginal contrast, because the marginal effect depends on the covariate distribution it is averaged over, and under non-collapsibility even purely prognostic variables move it. What remains open is propagation rather than theory: the formal results are published and target-specific standardization is implemented, but reporting conventions and HTA submission scales still carry marginal odds ratios and hazard ratios without a population index. Because the same number is valid in its own population and invalid in the target, no diagnostic run on the source analysis reveals the error.

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Remiro-Azocar 2024, Transportability of model-based estimands in evidence synthesis, Statistics in Medicine 43(22):4217-4249
Establishes that for non-collapsible measures purely prognostic variables that are not determinants of treatment response can modify marginal effects even under individual-level treatment effect homogeneity, which is why an assumption about effect modifiers cannot suffice for portability. This is the work that establishes the entry’s central result.


Phillippo, Dias, Ades and Welton 2021, Target estimands for efficient decision making: Response to comments on Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study, Statistics in Medicine
States that marginal population-average treatment effects depend more strongly on the population of interest than population-average conditional effects and are less generalizable as a result, foreshadowing the formal result by three years.


Chandler and Ishak 2026, Reframing Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons as a Transportability Problem
Restates that the shared effect modifier assumption alone does not guarantee direct transportability of marginal effects, inside an explicit two-step transportability framing for PAIC. It restates rather than establishes the result.


Jiang et al. 2025, A critical assessment of matching-adjusted indirect comparisons in relation to target populations, Research Synthesis Methods
Documents the population dependence of MAIC results in relation to target populations.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (R package)
Implements target-population marginal-effect calculation, with marginal_effects() defaulting to a risk difference, so the standardization step is available and the collapsible default is already in software.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
Distinguishes a conditional profile contrast from a marginal population-standardized effect in its documentation, stating that the returned value is the conditional contrast at the covariate profile rather than the marginal effect standardized over a population. The labeling is correct; the marginal path is absent.

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Index every marginal estimand by the population it is defined in and standardize explicitly to a named target covariate law before any decision use, rather than assuming scale invariance. Directly collapsible contrasts make that standardization easier, so prefer them where the decision permits, but do not present them as empirically constant across populations, since the target still has to be declared. The concrete work is in outputs rather than derivations: get the population index into reporting templates and into packages that do not yet separate a conditional profile contrast from a population-standardized marginal effect, as in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not installable from CRAN, where at commit 9d150e9 the cML-NMR path returns only the conditional contrast at a covariate profile.

title: Non-collapsible marginal effects are not portable across populations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Not supported. No accessible source substantiates the claim as stated.
The source said. “Odds ratios and hazard ratios can vary across populations even in the absence of confounding, so a marginal effect estimated in one population is not automatically transportable to another. The shared-effect-modifier assumption, routinely invoked to justify population adjustment, does not by itself make non-collapsible marginal effects portable to an arbitrary population.”
What was wrong with it. The source credited Chandler and Ishak (arxiv:2602.17041) with establishing that shared effect modification does not make non-collapsible marginal effects portable; the literature auditor found the result established two years earlier by Remiro-Azocar (doi:10.1002/sim.10111) and foreshadowed by Phillippo et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/sim.8965), and found the claim that it has not reached software defaults false, since multinma’s marginal_effects() defaults to a risk difference. GPT-5.6 Sol separately struck the equation of collapsibility with portability and the treatment of a standardized risk as an effect scale.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): Chandler & Ishak 2026 does say what is attributed (‘SEMA alone does not guarantee direct transportability of marginal treatment effects’; non-collapsible marginal effects ‘are not directly transportable, even when SEMA holds’), so claims 1-3, 5 and 6 hold. Claim 4 does not: Chandler & Ishak are not the work that establishes this. Remiro-Azocar, Statistics in Medicine 43(22):4217-4249 (2024) establishes a strictly stronger result two years earlier - for non-collapsible measures even purely prognostic variables that are not determinants of treatment response modify marginal effects - which is exactly why an assumption about effect modifiers cannot suffice. Earlier still, Phillippo, Dias, Ades & Welton (Stat Med 2021) wrote that marginal effects ‘depend more strongly on the population of interest than the population-average conditional treatment effects, and are less generalizable/transportable as a result’. The why_open assertion that the result ‘has not propagated into guidance, software defaults’ is also wrong at the software level: multinma’s marginal_effects() defaults to mtype = ‘difference’, a collapsible absolute scale. Status stays open because these are formalizations of an unfixable property. codex dissented (overstated): C1-C3 are mathematically correct: a marginal odds ratio or hazard-ratio projection can change with baseline risk, prognostic covariate distribution, or follow-up composition despite no confounding and a stable conditional treatment parameter. C4 is a priority-attribution claim outside this assigned technical lens; the result is an established consequence of non-collapsibility, not something that can be credited from technical truth alone. C5 is sloppy: risk differences and RMST differences are collapsible linear contrasts, but collapsibility neither guarantees transportability under effect modification nor makes them universally preferable; a standardized risk is target-specific and is not itself a treatment-effect scale. C6 should require a named target population, and numerical standardization needs a target covariate or outcome law, but the abstract marginal estimand need not encode one particular covariate representation. Target-specific standardization is established and implemented, so the management problem is partly solved; no population-free marginal OR or HR exists.

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text: EST-05 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text:
Statement
No journal or HTA template requires an analysis to declare all four of target population, target estimand, effect scale, and whether the result is marginal or conditional; the marginal versus conditional element in particular is nowhere mandated. Two of the four are already required for NICE submissions: NICE DSU TSD18 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) requires the target population to be stated explicitly and requires indirect comparisons to be carried out on the linear predictor scale. A published PAIC framework also codifies definition of the comparison as an estimand as its first element (Ishak et al. 2025, doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1), and Phillippo et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2) give recommendations for reporting marginal and conditional estimands in the decision target population, so what is missing is a single enforcement point rather than a standard to enforce. Population-superscripted notation likewise already appears in the methods literature, including TSD18; what has not happened is its adoption in applied reports.

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text:
Why it is open
The requirements that exist are scattered across a technical support document, a framework paper and a recommendations paper, so there is no one field where a reviewer checks all four and no error signal when one is missing; the marginal versus conditional element has recommendations behind it but no template that demands it. Writing the declaration forces the analyst to fix the target population before seeing the data, which conflicts with the current practice of choosing the adjustment set from whatever the comparator publication reported. Because nothing pushes the population into the name of the estimand in applied reports, two numerically different quantities are published under one label and inherited unlabeled by appraisal templates and economic models. The mismatch changes the number rather than breaking the analysis, so nothing forces the field to correct itself.

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2018, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD18)
Requires the target population to be stated explicitly and requires indirect comparisons to be carried out on the linear predictor scale with the usual link functions, covering two of the four declaration elements for NICE submissions, and uses population-indexed estimand notation. It does not require a marginal versus conditional declaration.


Ishak et al. 2025, A Framework for Reliable, Transparent, and Reproducible Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons, PharmacoEconomics
Six-element PAIC reporting and risk-of-bias framework whose first element is definition of the comparison of interest in terms of an estimand. It is a published framework rather than a mandated field in journal or submission templates, and it does not impose population-indexed notation.


Phillippo, Remiro-Azocar, Heath, Baio, Dias, Ades and Welton 2025, Effect modification and non-collapsibility together may lead to conflicting treatment decisions, Research Synthesis Methods
Provides published recommendations for declaring and jointly reporting marginal and conditional estimands in the decision target population, the element TSD18 does not cover.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
Requires a target profile for effect-modified cML-NMR output and prints the result as a conditional effect at that profile, stating that relative effects from a model with effect modifiers are population-specific. Partial enforcement of the declaration inside one unreleased package.

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Assemble the declaration from the pieces that exist rather than writing a new standard: TSD18 fixes target population and scale, Ishak et al. 2025 supply a PAIC framework whose first element is estimand definition, and Phillippo et al. 2025 supply the marginal versus conditional recommendation, so the work is binding them into one mandatory field in analysis plans, journal templates and submission templates. Require every reported contrast to identify its population, by superscript or by an equally explicit structured field, since the point is unambiguous identification rather than one notation. Forbid silent reinterpretation of a conditional effect as a marginal one, or of a comparator-trial effect as a decision-target effect, and treat software that already enforces part of this, such as cpaic requiring a target profile for effect-modified cML-NMR output, as a pattern to generalize rather than as a finished solution; cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub and is not installable from CRAN.

title: Nothing requires declaring whether a result is marginal or conditional
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No journal or HTA template requires a four-part declaration; in particular nothing requires an analysis to state whether its result is marginal or conditional, even though NICE DSU TSD18 has required an explicit target population and a pre-specified linear-predictor scale since 2016, and population-superscripted notation already exists in the methods literature without being adopted in applied reports.
The source titled this. “No required estimand declaration or population-indexed notation” The title says population-indexed notation is missing, but the audit found it already used in TSD 18 and the methods literature; only applied adoption is absent.
The source said. “Nothing in the publication or submission pipeline requires an analysis to declare its target population, target estimand, effect scale, and whether the result is marginal or conditional, so the literature continues to tolerate analyses that switch interpretations without admitting it. The report also requires population-indexed notation of the form Delta_AB^{P2} versus Delta_AB^{P*}, and asserts that a report should never call both quantities simply the treatment effect.”
What was wrong with it. The claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced, and both auditors judged it overstated: the literature auditor found that NICE DSU TSD18 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) already requires an explicit target population and a pre-specified linear-predictor scale and already uses population-indexed notation, and that Phillippo et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2) supplies the marginal versus conditional recommendations TSD18 does not cover. A PAIC reporting and risk-of-bias framework established elsewhere in this audit, Ishak et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1), makes definition of the comparison as an estimand its first element. GPT-5.6 Sol added that population-superscripted notation is a useful convention rather than a mathematical necessity, since explicit prose or structured fields identify the population equally well.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Also SOURCE-A-UNSOURCED. Reading the full text of Phillippo et al. 2018 Med Decis Making (the published NICE DSU TSD18) contradicts the framing that ‘nothing in the publication or submission pipeline requires an analysis to declare its target population … [and] effect scale’. Recommendation 6 requires the target population to be explicitly stated; Recommendation 5 requires the scale: ‘Indirect comparisons should be carried out on the linear predictor scale, with the same link functions that are usually employed for those outcomes.’ TSD18 is the reference document for NICE submissions, so an enforcement point exists for two of the four declaration elements. That same paper already uses population-indexed notation of exactly the requested form, writing estimands with a population superscript and stating the transport relation between two populations P and Q, so ‘no established standard uses source-target notation’ is too strong for the methodological literature even if true of applied reports. What genuinely remains undeclared and unenforced is the marginal-versus-conditional element; Phillippo et al. 2025 RSM is the closest thing to a normative recommendation there. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Supplies an existing enforcement point for two of the four declaration elements (target population, effect scale) and already uses population-indexed estimand notation.. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2: Provides published recommendations for declaring and jointly reporting marginal and conditional estimands in the decision target population, the element TSD18 does not cover..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is a placeholder. C2, C3, C5, C6, C9, and C10 are claims about current practice, prevalence, or standards that cannot be established from technical correctness alone. C4 is a sound minimum declaration, although a full estimand also needs outcome, treatment conditions, time horizon, and handling of intercurrent events where relevant. C7 is useful notation, not a mathematical necessity; equally explicit prose or structured fields can identify the population. C8 is a sound communication rule unless the quantities have been shown to coincide and that fact is stated. The absolute statement that nothing in the pipeline requires target or scale declaration is false, and cpaic itself requires a target for effect-modified cML-NMR output and labels it as conditional. Existing guidance and package behavior partly solve declaration; universal four-part enforcement and routine source-target notation remain operational issues. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Requires explicit target-population declaration and specifies the synthesis scale, covering two of the proposed four fields.. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2: Supplies an explicit framework for distinguishing and reporting marginal and conditional estimands.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Requires a target profile for effect-modified cML-NMR and prints the result as a conditional effect at that profile..

title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
text:
Statement
Reported target-population means and standard deviations are estimates, and standard PAIC estimators condition on them as fixed inputs, so the reported interval omits that variability whenever the inference is to a superpopulation rather than to the realized finite target sample. The first of the four uncertainty sources the source bundles together has been solved, though outside the ITC literature: Sheng, Sun and Huang (arxiv:2603.02474) give asymptotic normality and a variance estimator for an entropy-balancing transport estimator, which is MAIC-equivalent, that accounts for uncertainty in covariate summaries, and Chen, Chen and Yu (doi:10.1002/sim.70358) construct resampling-based perturbation intervals for a target effect estimated from summary-level target information. The other three sources are not sampling error and do not belong in the same interval: uncertainty in reconstructed correlations is model uncertainty, inclusion-criteria ambiguity is estimand ambiguity, and secular change is a transport bias over time. The claim that no software propagates target-moment uncertainty was verified only for cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not installable from CRAN, where at commit 9d150e9 cmaic() bootstraps IPD patients while holding target means and standard deviations fixed.

title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
text:
Why it is open
Conditioning on published summaries as if exact omits variability from the reported interval in a way no convergence diagnostic reveals, and the fix is not a bootstrap of the source IPD, which carries no information about how the target summaries were estimated. Propagating that uncertainty needs target microdata, a sampling design, or at least the covariance or influence information behind the published summaries, which aggregate publications rarely provide. Two of the four listed sources have no conventional variance representation at all, so they need declared alternative estimands or explicit bias models rather than a wider interval. The solutions that do exist sit in the transportability literature and have not been carried into PAIC estimators or packages, which still take reported moments as given.

title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Sheng, Sun and Huang 2026, Transportable inference using target population summary statistics under covariate shift
Establishes asymptotic normality for the entropy balancing estimator, which is MAIC-equivalent, and proposes a variance estimator that accounts for uncertainty in covariate summaries, plus a second method handling covariate shift and summary uncertainty together. It is framed as transportability rather than PAIC and has not been carried into ITC software.


Chen, Chen and Yu 2026, Confidence Interval Construction for Causally Generalized Estimates With Target Sample Summary Information, Statistics in Medicine 45(1-2):e70358
Proposes a resampling-based perturbation method for constructing confidence intervals for an estimated target average treatment effect using summary-level target information with entropy balancing weights.


Gao, Heath and Baio 2025, Regression augmented weighting adjustment for indirect comparisons in health decision modelling (G-MAIC), Research Synthesis Methods
Uses Bayesian bootstrap to propagate the uncertainty of population-adjusted estimates, but treats the reported comparator summaries as fixed balancing targets, so it addresses uncertainty from the matching process rather than sampling error in the target moments.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
At commit 9d150e9, cmaic() holds target means and standard deviations fixed while bootstrapping only IPD patients, cstc() centers on fixed target means, and cmlnmr() builds fixed integration points from aggregate means, standard deviations and a supplied or borrowed correlation. This confirms the conditioning behavior in one unreleased package rather than across all PAIC software.

title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing target-summary variance results into PAIC rather than deriving them again: the entropy-balancing variance estimator and the perturbation interval both apply to MAIC-equivalent weighting, so the work is validation under PAIC conditions and implementation in packages that currently hold target moments fixed. A Bayesian formulation placing a distribution over the target covariate law is a reasonable complement, but its posterior is identified only through the target data and the chosen law or prior, so that prior has to be stated rather than absorbed. Handle inclusion-criteria ambiguity and secular drift as declared alternative estimands or explicit bias models with sensitivity ranges, not as extra variance in one interval. Uncertainty in reconstructed correlations remains the genuinely unaddressed component and is the natural next target.

title: Reported target moments are treated as known constants
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Reported target-population means and standard deviations are estimates, not known constants, yet standard PAIC estimators condition on them as fixed inputs. Direction B holds that a joint model should propagate sampling uncertainty in target moments, uncertainty in reconstructed correlations, ambiguity in target inclusion criteria, and secular change between the trial and current practice.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated all four uncertainty sources as unaddressed; the literature auditor found the first already solved for MAIC-equivalent estimators (arxiv:2603.02474; doi:10.1002/sim.70358) and noted that G-MAIC (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10021) propagates uncertainty by Bayesian bootstrap of the IPD only, leaving the target summaries fixed. GPT-5.6 Sol judged the entry overstated for treating the moments as necessarily random when the estimand may condition on the realized finite target, for bundling estimand ambiguity and secular drift with sampling variance, and for a universal software negative that source code confirms only for cpaic.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is correct for superpopulation inference from a finite target sample, but not when the estimand deliberately conditions on the realized finite target population and its exact summaries. C2 is an empirical ecosystem claim; source code confirms it for cpaic. At 9d150e9, cmaic() holds target means and SDs fixed while bootstrapping only IPD patients, cstc() centers on fixed target means, and cmlnmr() constructs fixed integration points from aggregate means, SDs, and a supplied or borrowed correlation. C3 improperly bundles sampling uncertainty, reconstructed-law model uncertainty, estimand ambiguity, and temporal transport bias. Inclusion criteria and secular change need explicit alternative estimands, scenarios, or bias models, not automatic addition to one interval. C4 is possible but posterior uncertainty is identified only through the target data and chosen law or prior. C5 requires target microdata, a sampling design, or at least the covariance or influence information for the reported summaries; bootstrapping source IPD alone cannot do it. C6 is an unsupported universal software negative, although it is true of cpaic. Frequentist methods already address target-summary sampling uncertainty, so only the broader structural components remain open. The priority is very high only when the target sample is small, the effect is sensitive to its law, or the decision changes.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The descriptive half checks out. G-MAIC (Gao, Heath & Baio, Res Synth Methods 2025) uses the reported comparator summaries as fixed balancing targets and propagates uncertainty only by Bayesian bootstrap of the IPD; Chandler & Proskorovsky’s 108-scenario MAIC variance study (Res Synth Methods 2024) compares conventional, ESS-rescaled, sandwich and bootstrap estimators, all of which address uncertainty from the matching process, none the sampling error in the target moments; maicplus matches weighted moments to reported moments taken as given. But the first of the four listed uncertainty sources has been solved outside the ITC literature, using estimators that are equivalent to MAIC. Sheng, Sun & Huang (arXiv:2603.02474, March 2026) apply entropy balancing to transportability and ‘propose a variance estimator to account for uncertainty in covariate summaries’, then give a second method handling covariate shift and summary uncertainty simultaneously; Chen, Chen & Yu (Stat Med 45(1-2):e70358, 2026) give a resampling-perturbation confidence interval for a target ATE estimated from target summary-level information. The other three sources (reconstructed correlations, inclusion-criteria ambiguity, secular drift) remain genuinely unaddressed. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.70358: Constructs confidence intervals for a target-population effect when only summary-level target information is available, using entropy balancing weights..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

C1 is correct for superpopulation inference from a finite target sample, but not when the estimand deliberately conditions on the realized finite target population and its exact summaries. C2 is an empirical ecosystem claim; source code confirms it for cpaic. At 9d150e9, cmaic() holds target means and SDs fixed while bootstrapping only IPD patients, cstc() centers on fixed target means, and cmlnmr() constructs fixed integration points from aggregate means, SDs, and a supplied or borrowed correlation. Inclusion criteria and secular change need explicit alternative estimands, scenarios, or bias models, not automatic addition to one interval. C4 is possible but posterior uncertainty is identified only through the target data and chosen law or prior. C5 requires target microdata, a sampling design, or at least the covariance or influence information for the reported summaries; bootstrapping source IPD alone cannot do it. C6 is an unsupported universal software negative, although it is true of cpaic. Frequentist methods already address target-summary sampling uncertainty, so only the broader structural components remain open. The priority is very high only when the target sample is small, the effect is sensitive to its law, or the decision changes. title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text: EST-09 Partially addressed High priority Emerging

title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text:
Statement
Reporting a single pooled effect hides population dependence, scale dependence and identification fragility, and the source’s response is a ladder of estimands whose divergence is read as informative. The lower rungs are already obtainable from one fitted model: multinma returns study-specific conditional effects, population-average marginal effects and predictions in an arbitrary target through newdata, and Phillippo et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2) recommend comparing conditional and marginal estimates in the decision target population, calling multilevel network meta-regression the only population-adjustment method able to produce both in any target. An overlap-population rung has a dedicated method in arbitrated indirect comparisons (arxiv:2510.18071). What does not exist is the top rung and the packaging: no software produces partially identified bounds under unmeasured effect modification as routine PAIC output, and there is no accepted convention for reading divergence between rungs.

title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text:
Why it is open
A single number conflates population dependence, scale dependence and identification fragility, and none of the three can be recovered from it afterwards. The rungs that exist are not assembled: they come from different functions, papers and packages, and no output presents them together with each one labeled by its population, so the comparison Phillippo et al. recommend is not what the reader of a submission actually sees. The partially identified rung needs bias-function machinery that is not integrated with PAIC estimators, and bounds are informative only when a defensible sensitivity model and range are specified, otherwise they are vacuous. There is also no convention for how a committee should read divergence between rungs, so an analyst who reports one invites the charge of indecisiveness, which removes the incentive to produce it.

title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo, Remiro-Azocar, Heath, Baio, Dias, Ades and Welton 2025, Effect modification and non-collapsibility together may lead to conflicting treatment decisions, Research Synthesis Methods
Establishes that multilevel network meta-regression can deliver conditional and marginal estimands in any decision target population from one model, which covers the lower rungs jointly, and supplies the published justification for reading their divergence rather than treating it as failure.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (R package)
Implements relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() from a single fitted model, each targetable at an arbitrary population through newdata, so the conditional, trial-population marginal and target-population marginal rungs are already computable together.


Fang and He 2026, Arbitrated Indirect Treatment Comparisons
Supplies the overlap-population rung as a dedicated method that fixes a single common overlap target.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
At commit 9d150e9 its namespace exposes no ladder, overlap-target or partial-identification bound interface, and cML-NMR lacks marginal standardization, so cSTC and cMAIC supply separate conditional and marginal analyses rather than an integrated ladder.

title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Assemble rather than invent: wire the conditional, trial-population marginal, target-population marginal and overlap rungs into one labeled output built on the estimators that already produce them. Fix the number and content of rungs to the decision at hand rather than to a list of five, since marginal effects in each trial population multiply with the network and the rungs are different kinds of object. Develop the partial-identification rung as declared sensitivity models with defensible ranges, and report model and overlap diagnostics alongside each rung so divergence can be attributed to population dependence rather than to misspecification or positivity failure. In cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not installable from CRAN, none of this is exposed at commit 9d150e9, so the ladder is a concrete build there rather than a research question.

title: No convention for reading divergence between estimand rungs
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “No estimand ladder: analyses report a single pooled effect” The title says there is no estimand ladder, but the lower rungs are already obtainable from a single multinma fit and an overlap-population method exists.
The source said. “Direction C proposes that each analysis estimate a ladder of estimands rather than one effect: a conditional effect at a clinically interpretable profile, marginal effects in each trial population, the marginal effect in the policy target, an overlap-population effect, and partially identified bounds under plausible unmeasured effect modification. Divergence between rungs is treated as scientifically informative rather than as analytic failure.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no standard workflow or software computes the rungs jointly; the literature auditor found the first three obtainable from a single multinma fit and the fourth addressed by arbitrated indirect comparisons (arxiv:2510.18071), and found the justification for treating divergence as informative already published in Phillippo et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2). GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the count of exactly five rungs, noted that divergence can also come from misspecification, positivity failure or numerical error, and held that partial-identification bounds are informative only under a specified sensitivity model rather than as routine output.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I found no published or implemented five-rung estimand ladder, so the packaged proposal is genuinely new. But the why_open claim that ‘no standard workflow or software computes the rungs jointly’ is too strong for the first three rungs. From one fitted multinma model, relative_effects() returns study-population-specific (conditional) effects, marginal_effects() returns population-average marginal effects on difference, ratio or link scales, and both accept newdata for an arbitrary policy target - and Phillippo et al. (Res Synth Methods 2025) both recommend comparing conditional and marginal estimates in the decision target population and state that ‘multilevel network meta-regression is the only population-adjustment method capable of producing both conditional and marginal estimates, in any decision target population’. That same paper also supplies the missing justification for the entry’s claim that divergence between rungs is informative rather than a defect. Rung 4 has a dedicated method (overlap-population targeting, arXiv:2510.18071). Rung 5 is closest to open: Ren et al. (Res Synth Methods 2025) give quantitative bias analysis with code for unmeasured confounding in unanchored PAIC, but that is sensitivity analysis, not partial identification, and does not restore identification. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.2: Establishes ML-NMR as able to deliver conditional and marginal estimands in any decision target population from one model, i.e. rungs 1-3 jointly, and recommends reading their divergence.. Cites cran:multinma: Implements relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() from a single fitted model, each targetable at an arbitrary population via newdata..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 has no basis for exactly five rungs: “marginal effect in each trial population” generates as many estimands as there are trial populations, and a conditional profile effect, population-marginal effects, an overlap effect, and a partial-identification set are different kinds of objects. C2 is conditional: divergence can reveal population dependence or non-collapsibility when every rung is correctly defined and estimated, but it can also reflect model misspecification, positivity failure, or numerical error. C3 is generally right under effect heterogeneity or non-collapsibility, although a single effect explicitly labeled for the decision target is not intrinsically defective. C4 is false as a routine claim: informative bounds require a specified sensitivity model, defensible ranges for unmeasured modification, adequate target information, and support; otherwise bounds may be vacuous. At cpaic 9d150e9, NAMESPACE exposes no ladder, overlap-target, or partial-identification-bound API, and cML-NMR explicitly lacks marginal standardization; cSTC and cMAIC instead provide separate conditional and marginal analyses. Thus the integrated ladder remains open in cpaic. C5 is supported for cpaic but unverifiable as a universal statement about all ITC/PAIC software under this audit’s no-literature constraint.

Decision path
