title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text: EST-11 Overstated High priority Emerging

title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text:
Statement
No published PAIC simulation crosses a full menu of target-population choices with correct versus incorrect second-stage transport and with uncertainty in the reported target moments, and a simulation that defines truth by the estimator’s own implicit target makes target-mismatch error invisible. The blanket version of the claim is false: Chandler and Ishak’s ML-UMR simulation (arxiv:2606.20341) treats the target population as a design factor over index and comparator populations, crosses it with effect-modification strength, overlap and covariate dependence including a misspecified between-population correlation, uses two effect measures, and scores bias and coverage against true marginal effects computed externally from simulated populations of ten million. The count of eight factors is also not defensible as exact or orthogonal, since target choice, overlap and distributional difference cannot always be varied independently, and dimensions such as network geometry, baseline risk and censoring are equally material.

title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text:
Why it is open
What has not been mapped is the interaction between a full menu of target choices, including pooled, registry and overlap populations, and the correctness of the second-stage transport; no study varies uncertainty in the reported target moments at all. Judging bias against an externally declared decision estimand presupposes the target-declaration discipline the field does not enforce, so simulations keep inheriting the estimator’s implicit target as truth, and an estimator that answers the wrong question scores as unbiased. The full crossed design is large and expensive to summarize, and because comparative simulations are the main evidence used to recommend methods, the metric propagates directly into method-selection guidance.

title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler and Ishak 2026, Anchors Away: Navigating Unanchored Indirect Comparisons with Multilevel Unanchored Meta-Regression (ML-UMR)
Runs a 24-scenario factorial simulation at 500 replications that treats the target population as a design factor over index and comparator populations, crosses effect modification, population imbalance and covariate dependence including a misspecified between-population correlation, uses two effect scales, and computes true marginal effects externally from populations of ten million rather than from any estimator’s implicit target. It does not vary a five-level target menu, second-stage transport correctness, or target-moment uncertainty.

title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing design rather than start one: Chandler and Ishak’s simulation already varies the target population and defines truth externally, so the increment is a wider target menu including pooled, registry and overlap populations, a correct versus incorrect second-stage transport factor, and target-moment uncertainty, run as a coherent fractional-factorial design rather than a full crossing of eight nominally independent factors. Separate the effect-modification factor into functional form and whether modification is shared or treatment-specific, instead of treating four levels as mutually exclusive. Report bias, RMSE and coverage against the declared decision estimand for every method, and report each estimator’s error for its own native estimand separately, so target-mismatch error and estimation error can be read apart.

title: No simulation crosses target choice with second-stage transport error
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No published PAIC simulation crosses a full menu of target-population choices with second-stage transport correctness and target-moment uncertainty, although at least one 2026 study (Chandler & Ishak’s ML-UMR simulation) does treat target population as a design factor, uses two effect measures, and scores bias and coverage against an externally defined target estimand rather than the estimator’s implicit target.
The source titled this. “No factorial simulation of target choice, judged against the target” The title says no factorial simulation of target choice exists, but a 2026 ML-UMR simulation treats target population as a design factor and scores against externally computed truth.
The source said. “Section 5.4 specifies a target-population simulation program crossing eight factors (target choice; effect measure; effect-modification structure; prognostic effect strength; overlap; covariate-distribution difference; target-moment uncertainty; and correct versus incorrect second-stage transport), and no such crossed study is reported as existing. Its principal outcome should be bias relative to the declared target estimand, not bias relative to whichever population the estimator implicitly targets.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated that no crossed study exists and that existing PAIC simulations judge bias against the estimator’s implicit target; the literature auditor falsified the blanket version with Chandler and Ishak’s ML-UMR simulation (arxiv:2606.20341), which varies the target population as a design factor and evaluates against externally computed true marginal effects. GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the fixed count of eight factors as neither exhaustive nor orthogonal and abstained on how much published simulation coverage exists, holding that question outside a technical audit’s reach.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The two blanket negative claims are falsified by a 2026 preprint from the same authors the neighbouring EST entries already cite. Chandler & Ishak’s ML-UMR paper (arXiv:2606.20341, 18 June 2026) runs a factorial simulation that treats the target population as a design factor - the methods section states ‘For a target population P in {index, comparator}’ and reports bias and coverage in both - and defines truth externally rather than by any estimator’s implicit target: ‘True marginal treatment effects were computed for each scenario using large simulated populations (N = 10,000,000) to approximate the data-generating distributions’, on two effect scales (log odds ratio and log risk ratio). Its Table C.1 crosses effect modification (none / weak / strong), population imbalance (moderate / high overlap), covariate dependence including a misspecified between-population correlation, and sample size, for 24 scenarios at 500 replications. So target choice has been crossed with effect measure, effect-modification structure and overlap. What survives is narrower: no study crosses a five-level target choice (IPD trial, AgD trial, pooled, registry, overlap) with correct-versus-incorrect second-stage transport, and no study varies target-moment uncertainty. Cites arxiv:2606.20341: Demonstrates a PAIC simulation that varies the target population as a design factor, crosses it with effect-modification strength, overlap and covariate dependence, uses two effect measures, and evaluates bias against externally computed true marginal effects..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

abstain / overstated. C1 is not defensible as “exactly eight.” The dimensions are sensible but neither exhaustive nor orthogonal: nonlinear effect modification can also be shared or treatment-specific, and target choice, overlap, and distributional difference cannot always be varied independently. Other potentially material dimensions include network geometry, sample size, baseline risk, censoring, measurement error, and outcome-model misspecification. C4 and C5 are useful simulation dimensions when defined coherently. C6 should separate functional form from whether modification is shared or treatment-specific rather than treating them as four mutually exclusive levels. C7 is correct for decision-focused method comparison, although native-estimand estimation error should be reported separately from target-mismatch error. C9 follows directly: an estimator unbiased for θ(P) has bias θ(P)-θ(Q) for decision target Q. C10 is correct because precision conditional on an estimand cannot validate that estimand’s policy relevance. C2, C3, and C8 are claims about published simulation coverage, explicitly outside this audit’s lens and unsupported by cited works here; therefore the open-status vote is an abstention rather than an inference from absence.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text: EVB-02 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Statement
Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can materially change an indirect comparison by changing which studies, populations and contrasts are represented, and this is demonstrated rather than hypothetical: a multiverse of 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone reported a Janus effect (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3), and a multiverse over all possible antidepressant networks found 172 of 231 pairwise comparisons showing opposite effects between the 1st and 99th percentiles (Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848). What remains open is that multiverse reporting is not required or routinely performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible. Selection changes how relevant the assembled evidence is to an externally defined target population; it does not by itself define the target estimand.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Why it is open
The evidence set is assembled by the party that reports the result, and every downstream analysis conditions on the assembled network, so no covariate adjustment recovers the comparisons that were excluded. The tools to expose this now exist and their published applications show inclusion choices can flip the direction of an estimate, but nothing obliges a sponsor submission to report one, and the demonstrations to date sit in the general synthesis literature rather than in HTA practice. An undefined multiverse over all defensible networks also reintroduces analyst discretion and multiplicity, so the missing piece is a transparent rule for what counts as defensible rather than the technique itself.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Vinatier et al. 2024, BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine
Multiverse analysis covering all possible network meta-analyses over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step.


Palpacuer et al. 2019, BMC Medicine
Enumerates 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone by varying eligibility criteria and analytic model, showing that inclusion decisions alone can reverse the direction of the comparison.


Guelimi et al. 2025, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Quantifies how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change network meta-analysis conclusions in psoriasis; shows sensitivity over alternative networks is operational.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The multiverse machinery exists and the work is to require and discipline it rather than to invent it: specify transparent rules for which alternative evidence sets are defensible, then report the estimate across them as a matter of course. Protocol-first feasibility assessment that fixes eligibility before results are known addresses the outcome-aware part of the problem that a multiverse cannot, since a multiverse run after the fact still starts from a chosen frame. Applying target-trial emulation to the construction of the evidence set rather than to a single analysis remains unevidenced; the literature auditor could not verify any published instance and Grok also left it open.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Multiverse analysis over the assembled evidence set has been demonstrated for indirect comparisons and for network meta-analysis and shows that inclusion decisions can flip the direction of the estimate; what remains open is that it is not routinely required or performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible.
The source said. “Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can induce a favorable network or a favorable target population before any modeling begins, and only one of the defensible networks is ever shown.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented multiverse analysis over defensible networks as an emerging direction and said alternative networks are never reported; the literature auditor found two published multiverses of exactly that object (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3; Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848), with a third for inclusion criteria in psoriasis (Guelimi et al. 2025, doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6). GPT-5.6 Sol separately rejected the conflation of the population represented by the selected studies with an externally defined target population, and struck the universal claims that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are never shown.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): The claim that eligibility and comparator choices can favor a network or target population before modeling, and that only one defensible network is typically shown, remains faithful for HTA/ITC practice. Recent work does, however, implement the multiverse response for treatment/network assembly in evidence synthesis, so the problem is not open as if no method existed. Vinatier et al. (2024) ran a multiverse covering all possible NMAs on different treatment combinations in antidepressants and showed large vibration of effects, especially for indirect comparisons. Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I retrieved two published multiverse analyses of exactly the object this entry proposes as future work, both in indirect comparison settings. Palpacuer 2019 BMC Medicine enumerated 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene vs naltrexone by varying eligibility (condition, abstinence, sex, comorbidity, psychological support, dose, duration, outcome, publication status, risk of bias) and analytic model, and reported a ‘Janus effect’. Vinatier 2024 BMJ EBM ran the multiverse over network composition itself: all possible NMAs over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients. Claim 1 and claim 2 are therefore not merely plausible but empirically demonstrated. Claim 4, however, is written as if multiverse analysis over defensible networks were a promising future direction (‘Emerging’ maturity); it has been executed at scale and published in general medical journals. The why_open sentence ‘Defensible alternative networks usually exist and are never reported’ is contradicted by these two papers. Claim 3 (target-trial emulation applied to evidence-set construction) I could not verify; the only candidate I found was in an obscure venue I will not cite. Cites doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848: Executes the entry’s proposed direction: a multiverse over all defensible network compositions, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step.. Cites doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3: Demonstrates claims 1 and 2 for an indirect comparison specifically, varying eligibility criteria that define both the network and the target population..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Evidence-set selection can materially change network connectivity, available contrasts, precision, and conclusions, so C1 and the underlying robustness problem are valid. C2 conflates the population represented by the selected studies with the externally defined target population; study selection changes evidential relevance to a target but should not itself define the target estimand. Target-trial principles can help prespecify eligibility and estimand attributes, but calling evidence-set assembly target-trial emulation does not recover excluded information or identify selection effects. C4 is a reasonable sensitivity strategy if defensible networks are specified by transparent rules, although an undefined multiverse of all defensible networks invites further researcher discretion and multiplicity. The assertions that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are usually or never reported are unsupported universal claims. This can be critical when eligibility was selected after results were known, but it is not automatically a modeling failure in every ITC.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The claim that eligibility and comparator choices can favor a network or target population before modeling, and that only one defensible network is typically shown, remains faithful for HTA/ITC practice. Recent work does, however, implement the multiverse response for treatment/network assembly in evidence synthesis, so the problem is not open as if no method existed. Vinatier et al. (2024) ran a multiverse covering all possible NMAs on different treatment combinations in antidepressants and showed large vibration of effects, especially for indirect comparisons. Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks. Cites doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848: Demonstrates multiverse/all-possible-NMA analysis over treatment selection and shows large vibration of effects; partially resolves the proposed multiverse response to selective network assembly (C4) for treatment inclusion.. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6: Shows inclusion criteria and methodological choices alter NMA conclusions; supports that assembly decisions matter before modeling (C1) and that sensitivity over alternative networks is operational..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text: EVB-04 Unverifiable Very high priority Speculative

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Statement
Methods for choosing the next data collection by expected decision value exist and are mature: conditional trial design sizes and configures a new trial against an existing network (Salanti et al. 2018, doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2; Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014, pmid:25225031), and expected value of sample information has practical tutorials and worked prioritization examples (doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292; doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-092158). Neither has been applied to deciding which individual patient dataset to acquire for a population-adjusted comparison, nor to sizing and allocating a bridging trial that would connect two disconnected subnetworks. Whether acquisition in ITC practice is in fact opportunistic is undocumented: no auditor found a survey of it.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Why it is open
The general machinery is decision-theoretic and only produces an answer once the decision, utility, costs, access probability, model uncertainty and target population are specified; for a population-adjusted comparison none of these is currently packaged as an input to acquisition. The value of an additional IPD study depends on the target population, the bridge in use and the decision threshold, and no published formulation ties those to a request for a specific dataset. For disconnected networks the harder version, choosing which bridge treatment to run and how to allocate sample across the gap, was not found by any auditor. What is open is the ITC-specific operational formulation and its robustness, not the existence of a principled criterion.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Salanti et al. 2018, Trials
Four-step framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial that updates an existing network while minimizing required sample size, allowing the new trial to omit some interventions and still contribute direct and indirect evidence.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014, Biometrical Journal
Derives conditional power of a network meta-analysis to inform the design of future trials; earliest of the conditional trial design papers and establishes that sample size can be computed conditional on the existing network.


Heath et al. 2022, Medical Decision Making
Practical guidance and recommendations for four model-based methods of computing expected value of sample information efficiently; shows the machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature and tutorialized.


Glynn et al. 2025, BMJ Open (DiaDeM)
Worked example of value-of-information analysis used to prioritize which data to collect, showing the acquisition-as-decision-object framing is present in the wider literature.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing value-of-information and conditional trial design machinery to the ITC setting rather than build new criteria: specify the decision, utility, costs, access probability and target population, then rank candidate IPD acquisitions by expected decision value. Extend conditional trial design from adding a trial to a connected network to the disconnected case, where the objects of choice are the bridge treatment, the sample size and the allocation across the gap. Establishing whether current acquisition is opportunistic requires a survey of practice, which no auditor could find, so that claim should be tested before it is used to justify the programme.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “Data acquisition is opportunistic rather than decision-driven” The title asserts that acquisition is opportunistic, which the audit recorded as undocumented since no survey of ITC practice was found.
The source said. “Decisions about which individual patient dataset to obtain, or which bridging trial to run, are made opportunistically rather than by any principled criterion linking the acquisition to the decision it would improve.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no formal object exists to quantify what a dataset would contribute and listed bridging-trial design as a research direction; conditional trial design for networks has been published since 2014 (pmid:25225031; doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2) and EVSI tooling is mature (doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292), as the literature auditor documented and GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed on decision-theoretic grounds. Grok agreed the ITC-specific application is absent but read the entry as supported, so the disagreement here is over framing rather than over what exists.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): Claim 3 is the weak point. Salanti et al. 2018 Trials present a four-step conditional trial design framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial updating an existing network while minimizing required sample size, explicitly allowing the new trial to omit some interventions while still contributing direct and indirect evidence. Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014 Biometrical Journal derive conditional power of an NMA to inform future trial design; Nikolakopoulou 2019 Trials surveys methodologists on it; Siontis 2022 F1000Research applies conditional sample size calculation. Designing the next trial from an existing network is an established literature, not a proposed research direction. What I could not find in any retrieved source is the specific case the entry names: sizing and allocating a bridging trial across the gap between disconnected subnetworks. Claim 2 is similarly half-built: EVSI machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature (Heath 2022 MDM, Vervaart 2023/2024 MDM, Glynn 2025 BMJ Open), but I found no application to choosing which IPD to acquire for an ITC. Claim 1 concerns current practice and I found no survey of it; Clayton 2017 Trials reports only 6% of trialists using VOI, which is adjacent but a different population.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Claim 3 is the weak point. Salanti et al. 2018 Trials present a four-step conditional trial design framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial updating an existing network while minimizing required sample size, explicitly allowing the new trial to omit some interventions while still contributing direct and indirect evidence. Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014 Biometrical Journal derive conditional power of an NMA to inform future trial design; Nikolakopoulou 2019 Trials surveys methodologists on it; Siontis 2022 F1000Research applies conditional sample size calculation. Designing the next trial from an existing network is an established literature, not a proposed research direction. What I could not find in any retrieved source is the specific case the entry names: sizing and allocating a bridging trial across the gap between disconnected subnetworks. Claim 2 is similarly half-built: EVSI machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature (Heath 2022 MDM, Vervaart 2023/2024 MDM, Glynn 2025 BMJ Open), but I found no application to choosing which IPD to acquire for an ITC. Claim 1 concerns current practice and I found no survey of it; Clayton 2017 Trials reports only 6% of trialists using VOI, which is adjacent but a different population. Cites doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2: Directly contradicts the framing of claim 3 as a proposed direction: optimal design of the next trial given an existing network is published methodology with worked examples.. Cites pmid:25225031: Earliest of the conditional-trial-design papers; establishes that sample size for a future trial can be computed conditional on the existing network.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292: Confirms claim 2’s machinery exists and is tutorialized; the ITC-specific application of choosing which IPD to acquire is what remains unbuilt.. Cites doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-092158: Recent worked example of VOI used to prioritise which data to collect, showing the acquisition-as-decision-object framing is not absent from the literature generally..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 and C3 are technically valid research directions: expected-utility or value-of-information criteria can rank candidate IPD acquisitions, and optimal-design criteria can choose bridge treatments, sample size, and allocation. The central empirical claim C1, that current decisions are generally opportunistic, is unsupported here. The literal statement that no formal object exists is false because decision theory already supplies such objects once the decision, utility, costs, predictive model, access probability, and relevant uncertainties are specified. What remains open is an ITC-specific operational formulation and its robustness, not the existence of a principled criterion. This is generally a roadmap and resource-allocation issue rather than a universal threat to identification or decision-grade validity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Search assumed VOI and optimal design had already made IPD acquisition decision-driven. General value-of-information methods for HTA research prioritization and study design are mature (ISPOR VOI task force reports; Jackson et al. reviews of VOI in policy models; EVPI/EVPPI/EVSI tooling). That infrastructure means C2 is a defensible direction rather than science fiction. However, no retrieved 2020–2026 paper or software release implements a standard, decision-linked criterion for which IPD dataset to request for PAIC/ITC, or optimal sample allocation of a bridging trial across a gap between disconnected subnetworks, as a routine acquisition object. Dose-response and other NMA extensions discuss reconnecting disconnected networks when common agents exist; that is model-based reconnection, not VOI-guided bridge-trial design. No CRAN/GitHub signal for multinma/maicplus/netmeta/outstandR closed this acquisition gap. C1 (opportunistic access in practice) remains descriptive and unfalsified by a competing formal acquisition framework. Queries: VOI/EVSI IPD meta-analysis; VOI network meta research prioritization; optimal bridge trial disconnected NMA; active IPD acquisition strategy. Vote open with moderate-low confidence because VOI is adjacent and may be applied without being published as ITC-specific method.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text: HET-01 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Statement
Cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy and care pathway are properties of the trial rather than of the patient, so baseline covariate balancing in MAIC or STC cannot remove them, and a standard PAIC output does not separate residual protocol difference from residual patient-mix imbalance. Known design features are not beyond the reach of every estimator: they can enter study-level meta-regression, estimand or measurement models, and bias models, provided the network supplies enough cross-study variation to identify them. What stays nonidentifiable is the latent part and the split between design difference and patient mix. The bias-adjustment machinery the source proposes as new is mature: elicited, design-stratified priors for internal and external bias were published in Turner et al. 2009 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x), and threshold analysis quantifies how much study-level bias would have to be present to change a network’s recommendation (Phillippo et al. 2018, doi:10.1111/rssa.12341); neither has been ported to the population-adjusted setting.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Why it is open
The offending quantities have no patient-level distribution, so a weight that equalizes age and biomarker status leaves an imaging schedule or a rescue-therapy rule untouched, and separating the latent part of a design difference from residual patient-mix imbalance is not identified without further information or assumptions. Where a design feature is recorded and varies across enough studies it can be modeled, but PAIC networks are usually too small for that variation to exist, and these features are written up as narrative study characteristics rather than as variables. Adherence is a further complication because it is post-randomization: balancing baseline predictors can equalize it incidentally, while adjusting for it directly can change the estimand. Once baselines are balanced the analysis looks comparable, which makes the residue easy to overlook, and how much it matters is not established, since severity turns on whether the difference changes the estimand or the treatment as implemented.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Turner, Spiegelhalter, Smith and Thompson, 2009, Bias modelling in evidence synthesis, JRSS-A 172:21-47
Constructs prior distributions from elicited opinion to represent internal bias (lack of rigour) and external bias (lack of relevance) in each study and performs a bias-adjusted meta-analysis; this is the hierarchical bias model with design-stratified priors that the source lists as a new direction.


Phillippo et al., 2018, Sensitivity of treatment recommendations to bias in network meta-analysis
Threshold analysis: quantifies how much study-level bias would have to be present before a network’s treatment recommendation changes, giving existing machinery for the design-feature direction the source proposes.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing bias-adjustment apparatus rather than build it. Turner et al.’s elicited, design-stratified bias priors and Phillippo et al.’s threshold analysis are both defined for aggregate-data meta-analysis and NMA; what is missing is their combination with a weighting or standardization step and with an explicit target population. Design-feature meta-regression stays a reasonable route where the network holds enough studies to identify a study-level coefficient, and that replication, not the modeling, is the binding constraint. Negative-control endpoints are worth trying as a residual-heterogeneity signal, but there is no use of them in this field to build on, and a negative control can at best flag residual incompatibility; it cannot attribute that incompatibility to patient mix rather than to trial design.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy and care pathway are properties of the trial, not the patient, so baseline covariate balancing cannot remove them and standard PAIC output does not distinguish them from residual patient-mix imbalance. Bayesian bias-adjustment models with elicited, design-stratified priors exist and are well developed for meta-analysis and NMA (Turner et al. 2009), but have not been ported to the population-adjusted setting.
The source said. “Population adjustment balances baseline patient covariates, but cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy, and care pathway are properties of the trial rather than of the patient and remain once balancing is complete. Nothing in a standard PAIC output distinguishes residual patient-mix imbalance from residual protocol difference.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented hierarchical bias models with design-stratified priors as an emerging response and cited nothing; the literature auditor found them a seventeen-year-old evidence-synthesis literature, so the entry is now sourced to Turner et al. 2009 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x) and Phillippo et al. 2018 (doi:10.1111/rssa.12341) and the gap is their absence from PAIC, not from the literature. The same auditor could verify neither the claim that reviews find these sources under-handled in ITC and PAIC work nor any literature at all on negative-control endpoints in this field, and the code auditor struck the source’s assertion that these features cannot enter the estimator even when known.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. Retrieved Turner, Spiegelhalter, Smith & Thompson (2009), JRSS-A 172:21-47: ‘We present simple methods of allowing for differences in rigour (or lack of internal bias) and relevance (or lack of external bias) in evidence synthesis… Using elicited opinion, we construct prior distributions to represent the biases in each study and perform a bias-adjusted meta-analysis.’ Hierarchical bias models with design-stratified elicited priors are therefore a 17-year-old, mature evidence-synthesis literature, extended by Phillippo et al. (2018) threshold analysis and by the 2025 RoB NMA tool. Presenting them as an emerging idea is the overstatement. The core identification problem is genuinely open: design and conduct features have no patient-level distribution, so no weighting or standardization estimator can separate residual protocol difference from residual patient-mix imbalance; this is structurally untestable, so no paper can solve it. Two sub-claims fail verification. I found no review asserting that design and conduct heterogeneity is specifically under-handled in ITC/PAIC; the reviews I retrieved (Phillippo 2019 NICE TAs, Freitag 2023, van Beekhuizen 2025 EUnetHTA) concern covariate/effect-modifier selection and overall ITC suitability. And I found no literature at all on negative-control endpoints in ITC/PAIC, so that absence claim is unverifiable. Cites doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x: Supplies the real reference for the entry’s unsourced ‘Bayesian hierarchical bias models and design-stratified bias priors’ direction. It already exists for evidence synthesis; the gap is its absence from PAIC, not its absence from the literature.. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12341: Existing quantitative machinery for asking how much study-level bias would have to be present to change a network’s treatment recommendation; a real prior-art anchor for the ‘design-feature’ direction..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The core limitation is real, but several claims exceed it. C2 and C4 are correct for baseline-only MAIC and STC: patient reweighting cannot change endpoint definitions, follow-up, rescue rules, care delivery, or latent study-level features. C3 is generally but not logically true because balancing complete baseline predictors could incidentally balance adherence; adherence itself is postrandomization, and direct adjustment may change the estimand or introduce bias. The statement that known design features cannot enter an estimator is false: they can enter study-level meta-regression, measurement or estimand models, and bias models when replication and identifying assumptions permit. Negative controls can signal residual incompatibility only under valid negative-control assumptions and cannot by themselves attribute it to patient mix versus trial design. C5 through C7 are prevalence or current-use claims with no cited source and are unverifiable in this offline technical audit. C8 is plausible but limited by study-level confounding and sparse replication. Very high severity is justified when the differences change the estimand or treatment implementation, not automatically for every conduct difference.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text: HET-03 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Statement
Network models in current software default to a single between-study heterogeneity variance shared across the whole network, adopted for estimability rather than for plausibility: multinma’s tau is one network-wide scalar, as is the common tau recorded by cMLNMR in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN. The structured alternatives are not open research. Thorlund et al. 2013 (pmid:23311298) state the problem and build and compare four replacements for the homogeneous-variance assumption, empirically derived heterogeneity priors exist for 80 settings (Turner et al. 2015, doi:10.1002/sim.6381) and weakly informative ones for the very-few-studies case (Rover et al. 2021, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475), and class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes ship in multinma via class_sd since 0.8.0 (Perren et al. 2025, doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887), although that is a within-class treatment standard deviation rather than tau. What has not been done is establishing how large a network must be before the competing variance structures are distinguishable, and no structure indexes heterogeneity by target population; nor is the direction of the error fixed, since a shared variance can overstate uncertainty in a sparse stratum as readily as understate it, depending on which strata are more heterogeneous.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Why it is open
Networks rarely contain enough studies per class or component to estimate separate variances, so a separate-variance model is often only nominally identified and its posterior is driven by the prior rather than by the data. Model comparison statistics have little power to distinguish competing variance structures at realistic network sizes, and no one has established the size at which they become distinguishable, so the default is neither tested nor visibly violated. Component-specific variances need further assumptions about the covariance among component deviations, and any structured alternative must keep the random-effects covariance positive semidefinite, which is why the existing proposals have not displaced the default in software. Population-indexed heterogeneity has no implementation at all: the software parameter is a single network-wide scalar, so the question of whether tau should differ by target population cannot currently be asked.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Thorlund, Thabane and Mills, 2013, Modelling heterogeneity variances in multiple treatment comparison meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology 13:2
States the entry’s problem (the homogeneous variance assumption is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates, so credible intervals may lose nominal coverage and rank probabilities may be distorted) and builds and compares four alternatives: exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, and two informative variance-prior schemes.


Turner et al., 2015, Predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity and simple methods for their application in Bayesian meta-analysis
Derives empirically based predictive distributions for heterogeneity in 80 settings defined by outcome and comparison type, usable directly as heterogeneity priors; this is the robust-prior component the source lists as needed.


Rover et al., 2021, On weakly informative prior distributions for the heterogeneity parameter in Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis
Guidance on heterogeneity priors when very few studies contribute, which is the sparse-stratum case the entry names.


Perren, Pedder, Welton and Phillippo, 2025, Network Meta-Analysis with Class Effects: A Practical Guide and Model Selection Algorithm
Class-specific variance components with sharing of the standard deviation across groups of classes when a class has too few treatments to estimate its own, implemented in multinma as class_sd since 0.8.0, plus a model selection algorithm; note this is a within-class treatment standard deviation, not the between-study heterogeneity variance.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The modeling work is largely done, so the useful contributions are evaluation and porting rather than invention. Run the distinguishability simulation the field lacks: how many studies per class or component are needed before exchangeable, consistency-constrained and separate-variance structures can be told apart, so a default can be defended or abandoned on the basis of network size rather than convention. Carry the existing structures and the empirically derived heterogeneity priors into population-adjusted network models, where the heterogeneity parameter is still a single scalar, and report prior sensitivity rather than claiming any prior is universally robust. The genuinely new case is heterogeneity indexed by target population, which none of the existing work addresses.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Network models default to one common between-study heterogeneity variance even when the network spans treatment classes, components, and populations for which a shared value is implausible. The default is adopted for estimability rather than for plausibility.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented structured heterogeneity models and robust heterogeneity priors as work still to be developed; the literature auditor found them published and evaluated years ago (Thorlund et al. 2013, pmid:23311298; Turner et al. 2015, doi:10.1002/sim.6381; Rover et al. 2021, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475; class-specific variances in multinma since 0.8.0, doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887), so the residual gap is adoption plus the population-indexed case. The two auditors split on whether the entry is open or partly solved, and the code auditor added that ‘often unrealistic’ is an unsupported prevalence claim and that a shared variance does not automatically understate uncertainty where a new treatment sits; the entry is published at the weaker claim.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): Retrieved Thorlund, Thabane & Mills (2013), BMC Med Res Methodol 13:2, which is the entry’s problem and much of its proposed direction, already executed. Verbatim: ‘Random-effects MTCs have commonly modeled heterogeneity under the assumption that the between-trial variance for all involved treatment comparisons are equal… The homogeneous variance assumption, however, is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates. Consequently 95% credible intervals may not retain nominal coverage, and treatment rank probabilities may become distorted.’ They build and compare four alternatives (exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, two informative variance-prior schemes) and conclude ‘All four approaches should be viable candidates for replacing or supplementing the conventional homogeneous variance MTC model.’ The ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ claim is likewise delivered rather than open: Turner et al. (2015) empirical predictive distributions for tau, Rover et al. (2021) weakly informative heterogeneity priors, Lilienthal et al. (2024) empirical HTA priors. Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes are implemented in multinma 0.8.0+ via class_sd, though that is the within-class treatment SD, not between-study tau; multinma’s tau remains a single network-wide scalar, so the software-default half stands. Genuinely open: population-indexed heterogeneity, and the distinguishability simulation (Thorlund used two illustrative datasets).

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Retrieved Thorlund, Thabane & Mills (2013), BMC Med Res Methodol 13:2, which is the entry’s problem and much of its proposed direction, already executed. Verbatim: ‘Random-effects MTCs have commonly modeled heterogeneity under the assumption that the between-trial variance for all involved treatment comparisons are equal… The homogeneous variance assumption, however, is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates. Consequently 95% credible intervals may not retain nominal coverage, and treatment rank probabilities may become distorted.’ They build and compare four alternatives (exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, two informative variance-prior schemes) and conclude ‘All four approaches should be viable candidates for replacing or supplementing the conventional homogeneous variance MTC model.’ The ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ claim is likewise delivered rather than open: Turner et al. (2015) empirical predictive distributions for tau, Rover et al. (2021) weakly informative heterogeneity priors, Lilienthal et al. (2024) empirical HTA priors. Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes are implemented in multinma 0.8.0+ via class_sd, though that is the within-class treatment SD, not between-study tau; multinma’s tau remains a single network-wide scalar, so the software-default half stands. Genuinely open: population-indexed heterogeneity, and the distinguishability simulation (Thorlund used two illustrative datasets). Cites pmid:23311298: Already states the problem and supplies four evaluated alternatives to a single shared heterogeneity variance.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.6381: Supplies empirically derived heterogeneity priors for 80 settings, the ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ the entry lists as needed.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475: Guidance on robust heterogeneity priors when very few studies contribute, the sparse-stratum case the entry names.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887: Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes, implemented in multinma (class_sd argument, since 0.8.0), plus a model-selection algorithm..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 is technically plausible but context-dependent; the word often is an unsupported prevalence claim. A common heterogeneity variance can be implausible across distinct classes or populations, but it can either understate or overstate uncertainty depending on which strata are more heterogeneous. Understatement near a new treatment is not automatic. C2 is a valid modeling direction only if the resulting random-effects covariance is positive semidefinite and the network supplies enough replication. Component-specific variances also require assumptions about covariance among component deviations. In sparse strata, separate variances may be practically unidentified and dominated by priors. C3 is too categorical: proper regularization, hierarchical pooling, and prior-sensitivity analysis are advisable, but there is no universally robust prior that is always required. At cpaic 9d150e9, cMLNMR explicitly records a single common tau. It offers half-normal and half-Student-t priors but no class-specific or component-specific heterogeneity structure, so the core package limitation remains open. This is a potentially material sensitivity issue, not automatically a high-severity defect in every network.

title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
text: IDN-01 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
text:
Statement
Transitivity, consistency and conditional constancy restrict counterfactual quantities that are never jointly observed, so they cannot be verified nonparametrically from the data and passing any check does not establish transportability. Prespecifiable screens nevertheless exist: Spineli et al. (doi:10.1002/sim.70068) compute dissimilarities between treatment comparisons from study-level characteristics and cluster them to locate hot spots of potential intransitivity, backed by the tracenma database of 217 network datasets assembled to develop exactly this methodology, and Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162) assess conditional constancy through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency, though only in sufficiently large networks. What survives is narrower than the source claimed: each screen tests one observable implication, a calibrated failure is evidence against at least one assumption without saying which, and no catalogue states which implications a population-adjusted comparison should prespecify or what action a failure triggers.

title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
text:
Why it is open
The restriction is on treatment contrasts in study and population cells that are never jointly observed, so no function of the observed data has power against every violation, and covariate balance or model fit can look excellent under severe residual confounding. The screens that exist do not close this. The dissimilarity and clustering approach works on reported study-level characteristics and returns a semi-objective judgment rather than a verdict, and in 209 real networks a likely intransitivity prevailed in all of them while statistical tests were feasible in only 61 percent and often disagreed with the dissimilarity reading. For population-adjusted comparisons the residual-heterogeneity route needs a network large enough to support it, which is not the setting where conditional constancy does the most identifying work.

title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The screening step no longer needs inventing, so the work is calibration and prespecification: characterize the operating characteristics of the dissimilarity and clustering screen against the tracenma datasets, and fix in advance which implications are checked, on what scale, and what a failure obliges the analyst to do. Around it, assemble the falsification devices that population adjustment still lacks, including held-out-trial contrast prediction, bridge deletion, negative controls, transported versus observed control-arm comparison, cross-trial interaction replication, and transport checks separated by calendar time, geography and setting. Report all of them with an explicit statement that passing does not establish transportability, and where falsification is impossible attach an explicit bias function to the restriction instead of asserting it.

title: Transitivity and conditional constancy cannot be tested in-sample
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Standard ITC requires transitivity, consistency and a sensible effect scale, and PAIC adds conditional constancy of relative effects, yet these assumptions cannot be fully tested from the observed data. Research should therefore be redirected from impossible assumption tests towards prespecified falsification opportunities, accepting that success does not prove transportability while failure is highly informative.”
What was wrong with it. The source carried no citations and asserted both that there is no agreed catalogue of which implications to check or how to prespecify them and that a failed check is highly informative. The literature auditor sourced the practice claims (doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03322-1, doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02436-7) and found a prespecifiable transitivity screen already published (doi:10.1002/sim.70068, with cran:tracenma), so the entry is now sourced; the source-code auditor cut ‘highly informative’ back to evidence against at least one unidentified assumption, since a failure can equally reflect sampling variation, support failure, outcome-version differences or an invalid control.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Retrieved Spineli et al. 2024 (BMC Med, 721 NMAs) and Spineli 2024 (BMC Med Res Methodol, 209 networks), which supply exactly the empirical backing this unsourced entry lacks: transitivity is mostly evaluated statistically rather than conceptually (40% vs 12% pre-PRISMA-NMA; 54% vs 11% post), consistency evaluation is the single most-used device (34% -> 47%), and likely intransitivity ‘prevailed in all datasets’. Phillippo et al. 2023 independently states that conditional constancy ‘may be assessed by checking for residual heterogeneity and inconsistency’ only ‘in sufficiently large networks’. The core claim (the restriction is on counterfactuals never jointly observed, so no in-sample test has power against every violation) is unsolvable by construction and stays open. Caveat: why_open asserts ‘no agreed catalogue of which implications are worth checking, how to prespecify them’. That is now materially narrowed. Spineli et al. 2025 (Stat Med) give a prespecifiable dissimilarity-plus-clustering transitivity screen with empirically derived thresholds, backed by the public tracenma CRAN database (217 NMA datasets) built expressly to develop such methodology. The entry cites none of this and should. Cites 10.1186/s12916-024-03322-1: Sources the unsourced claims that transitivity is poorly examined in practice and that NMA diagnostics lean on after-the-fact inconsistency. Cites 10.1186/s12874-024-02436-7: Empirical evidence that intransitivity is common and that statistical tests are a poor device for assessing it. Cites 10.1002/sim.70068: Provides a prespecifiable, quantitative transitivity screen (dissimilarity matrices plus hierarchical clustering) that narrows the entry’s claim that no catalogue or prespecification procedure exists. Cites cran:tracenma: A public benchmark database of 217 NMA datasets with extracted study-level candidate effect modifiers, built specifically to develop transitivity methodology.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central nonidentification point is correct: observed data cannot verify equality of counterfactual treatment contrasts across unobserved study-treatment cells, and balance or model fit cannot rule out residual bias. However, C6 is a false scientific-versus-statistical dichotomy because these are formal statistical restrictions informed by science, sometimes with testable implications. C13 is materially too strong: a failed held-out prediction or negative control may reflect sampling variation, heterogeneity, support failure, outcome-version differences, model misspecification, or an invalid negative control. It is not automatically highly informative about transitivity. C14 additionally requires that withholding the trial preserve identification and that prediction and observation target the same population-specific estimand. C15 requires a valid negative control sharing the relevant bias pathway. C8-C10 are empirical literature claims outside this audit lens.

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text: IDN-03 Confirmed open Very high priority Established

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text:
Statement
Anchored versus unanchored is a primary identification distinction: Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) state that unanchored comparisons make much stronger assumptions that are widely regarded as infeasible, and NICE DSU TSD 18 calls the requirement that all effect modifiers and prognostic factors be accounted for largely impossible to meet. It is not the only axis that matters, because MAIC, STC and ML-NMR still differ in estimand, model dependence, extrapolation and uncertainty, and anchored adjustment is not modifier-only on a non-collapsible scale, where shifting the distribution of a purely prognostic covariate moves the marginal odds ratio even with a constant conditional odds ratio and no interaction. What is unresolved is completeness: unanchored identification needs a measured set sufficient to block the study-selection paths for absolute potential outcomes, that set is fixed by a scientific claim rather than by the data, and no accepted procedure demonstrates that a proposed set is complete. ML-UMR (arXiv:2606.20341) extends unanchored comparison beyond the pairwise case and makes its assumptions explicit for sensitivity testing, which is an estimation and reporting advance rather than a completeness result.

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text:
Why it is open
With a common comparator, randomization still identifies the within-trial contrast and the analyst is fixing an imbalance in modifiers of that contrast; once the anchor is gone, study membership and treatment are inseparable and every cross-study difference in absolute outcomes loads onto the treatment effect. That is a change in what must be known rather than in how well it is estimated, so no choice of estimator recovers it and larger samples do not help. Because the required set is a claim about what drives cross-study outcome differences, any proposed list is an argument rather than a result, and method debates conducted at the estimator level let an analysis lose the anchor with no corresponding change in what is reported or how the result is labeled.

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2018, Medical Decision Making
sets out population-adjustment methods for HTA and distinguishes anchored from unanchored comparisons according to whether a common comparator arm is used, stating that unanchored comparisons make much stronger assumptions that are widely regarded as infeasible


NICE DSU Technical Support Document 18: Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Submissions to NICE

Chandler and Ishak 2026, Anchors Away: Navigating Unanchored Indirect Comparisons with Multilevel Unanchored Meta-Regression (ML-UMR), arXiv:2606.20341

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Make anchored versus unanchored the primary axis for guidance, reporting and appraisal, and route unanchored analyses into a transportability frame with explicit residual-confounding analysis instead of treating them as a variant of the same estimator family. State the required adjustment set as a causal restriction attached to the declared estimand and effect scale, separating modifiers of the randomized contrast from the prognostic drivers of cross-study outcome differences, and say where non-collapsibility makes prognostic standardization necessary even in the anchored case. Treat completeness as a target for quantitative bias analysis, partial identification, negative controls, proximal methods and hidden-truth calibration, and allow no strong causal reading of an unanchored comparison without one of these or an explicit statement that the result is exploratory.

title: No procedure shows an unanchored adjustment set is complete
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Anchored versus unanchored is the decisive identification split” The title calls the anchored versus unanchored split decisive, but the audit found it is not the only axis that matters and that anchored adjustment is not modifier-only on a non-collapsible scale.
The source said. “The decisive methodological fault line is anchored versus unanchored, not MAIC versus STC versus ML-NMR: an anchored PAIC needs only effect modifiers of the within-study randomized contrast, whereas an unanchored PAIC needs every prognostic factor and every effect modifier that explains cross-study outcome differences. The asymmetry is widely stated but not operationalized, because no procedure exists for enumerating or defending the completeness of the unanchored adjustment set.”
What was wrong with it. The source framed the split as decisive against the choice among MAIC, STC and ML-NMR and said anchored comparisons need only effect modifiers; the source-code auditor rejected both, since the estimators differ in estimand and extrapolation and non-collapsible marginal estimands can require prognostic standardization. The completeness claim held up, and this previously unattributed entry is now sourced to Phillippo et al. 2018 and NICE DSU TSD 18, whose own text asserts the gap, with ML-UMR (arXiv:2606.20341) named as the nearest recent work.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Retrieved the Phillippo et al. 2018 abstract verbatim; it carries the entry’s central asymmetry claim word for word: ‘We distinguish between anchored and unanchored comparisons according to whether a common comparator arm is used or not. Unanchored comparisons make much stronger assumptions, which are widely regarded as infeasible.’ NICE DSU TSD 18 states that an unanchored MAIC or STC ‘effectively assumes that absolute outcomes can be predicted from the covariates; that is, it assumes that all effect modifiers and prognostic factors are accounted for. This assumption is very strong, and largely considered impossible to meet’ (retrieved via search of the TSD text, not the PDF directly, hence confidence 0.8 not higher). That guidance sentence is itself the source assertion that licenses the entry’s ‘no accepted procedure for demonstrating completeness’ claim, so it is not an unverifiable absence claim. Nothing I found resolves the identification problem. The most recent relevant method, ML-UMR (arXiv 2606.20341, Chandler and Ishak, June 2026), extends unanchored comparison beyond the pairwise case and makes assumptions explicit for sensitivity testing; that is an estimation and reporting advance, not a completeness result, and the entry does not cite it.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Anchoring is a major identification distinction, but C2 creates a false choice: MAIC, STC, and ML-NMR still differ in estimand, model dependence, extrapolation, and uncertainty. C3 is valid only for suitable conditional or collapsible relative-effect estimands under conditional constancy and support. On non-collapsible marginal scales, a purely prognostic covariate can matter without a conditional interaction. For example, a logistic model with constant conditional OR 3 and no treatment-covariate interaction gives marginal ORs 1.958 and 2.581 when Pr(X=1) changes from 0.1 to 0.9. C4 is therefore too reassuring: randomization identifies within-trial effects, not their transport, and network connectivity alone supplies neither overlap nor transitivity. Unanchored identification requires a sufficient set blocking study-selection paths for the relevant potential outcomes, not literally every prognostic variable. QBA characterizes sensitivity but does not itself license a causal interpretation. Claims about what NICE documents say are outside this technical audit.

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text: IDN-05 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text:
Statement
A published, software-implemented check on the shared effect modifier assumption already exists: Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162) split the common class interaction into treatment-specific interactions one covariate at a time and compare posteriors and model fit, inside a single nine-study network and with no second IPD trial, and multinma implements the hierarchical relaxation this entry proposed through nma(class_interactions = c(‘common’, ‘exchangeable’, ‘independent’)). The check has low and uncharacterized power, which its authors concede, no calibration threshold and no agreed stability metric, and it is least feasible in the small, IPD-poor networks where the assumption does the most identifying work. The restriction is also not the universal mechanism that makes anchored adjustment work; it becomes an identifying restriction in particular class, component and sparse ML-NMR parameterizations, and hierarchical pooling regularizes weak information rather than creating identification.

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text:
Why it is open
Interaction terms are estimated far less precisely than main effects, so the existing check can pass on intervals wide enough to accommodate almost any drift, while apparent discrepancies can come from non-collapsibility, differing covariate ranges or different outcome definitions instead of genuine modifier drift. Nothing states how much interaction stability is enough, so comparing posteriors and model fit returns a judgment rather than a calibrated verdict. The networks where the restriction carries the most identifying weight are the ones with the least data to relax it, and treatment-specific interactions are rarely estimable where one arm contributes only aggregate summaries.

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis, Medical Decision Making
assesses population-adjustment assumptions inside a nine-study network: splits the common class interaction into treatment-specific interactions one covariate at a time, checks conditional constancy through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency in sufficiently large networks, and reports that the shared-interaction restriction was required to identify the model where a treatment was informed only by aggregate data

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The estimator and the diagnostic exist, so the work is characterization: establish the power of the split-interaction check across network sizes and IPD availability, define a stability metric reporting how far interactions can drift before conclusions move rather than a binary verdict, and set a calibration threshold. Use estimated between-trial interaction drift to set priors or sensitivity envelopes on modifier drift, and report how conclusions move as the restriction is relaxed from common to exchangeable to independent, which multinma already supports. Where mechanistic pharmacology or biomarker evidence exists, use it to inform the shrinkage prior instead of defaulting to a common interaction.

title: The shared effect modifier check has low and uncalibrated power
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. A published, software-implemented check on the shared effect modifier assumption exists (split the common class interaction into treatment-specific interactions and compare posteriors and model fit, as in Phillippo et al. 2023 with multinma’s class_interactions argument), but it has low and uncharacterized power, no calibration threshold, and no agreed stability metric, and it is infeasible in the small, IPD-poor networks where the assumption does the most identifying work.
The source titled this. “Shared effect modification is assumed rather than estimated or tested” The title says shared effect modification is never estimated or tested, but a published within-network check exists and its hierarchical relaxation ships in multinma.
The source said. “Population adjustment commonly assumes that a covariate modifies the effects of different treatments in the same way, although the same modifier may act differently on different treatments. The only empirical check on offer, testing whether modifier interactions estimated in one IPD trial predict the treatment-effect heterogeneity observed in another, is not standardized and is rarely feasible.”
What was wrong with it. The source called cross-trial replication with two IPD trials the only empirical check on offer and proposed hierarchical shrinkage of treatment-specific interactions as future work. Both auditors found the check published in 2023 as a within-network procedure needing no second IPD trial (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162) and the shrinkage already shipped in multinma’s class_interactions argument, so what remains open is power, calibration and a stability metric rather than the method itself.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Phillippo et al. 2023 (Med Decis Making), which the entry does not cite, and it directly contradicts the statement’s ‘only empirical check on offer’. They assess the shared effect modifier assumption inside a single 9-study network with no second IPD trial, by splitting the common class interaction into treatment-specific interactions one covariate at a time and comparing posteriors and DIC, and they report a result (weak evidence against sharing for weight). The entry’s own proposed direction, hierarchical shrinkage of treatment-specific interactions, is already released software: multinma’s nma() takes class_interactions = c(“common”, “exchangeable”, “independent”) (verified in man/nma.Rd), so exchangeable within-class interactions are fittable today. What remains genuinely open is exactly what Phillippo et al. concede: ‘It is likely that this approach to assessing the shared effect modifier assumption has low power, particularly when data are lacking.’ Power, calibration, a stability metric rather than a binary verdict, and the data conditions under which the check is informative are unresolved. So the problem is real but the framing overstates the void by roughly one decade and one R package. Cites 10.1177/0272989X221117162: Provides and applies a standardized within-network empirical check on the shared effect modifier assumption, not requiring two IPD trials. Cites cran:multinma: Implements common, exchangeable (hierarchically shrunk) and independent treatment-class effect-modifier interactions, i.e. the entry’s proposed direction.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 and C2 are correct: treatment-specific modification can differ, and shared conditional interactions do not make marginal odds or hazard ratios population-invariant. Hierarchical pooling is a coherent relaxation but regularizes weak information rather than creating identification. The shared-interaction restriction is not the universal mechanism that makes anchored PAIC work; an anchored analysis targeting the comparator-trial population can transport the IPD trial contrast and subtract the contrast observed in the target trial without assuming identical interactions for every treatment. Shared interactions become identifying restrictions in particular class, component, or sparse ML-NMR parameterizations. The proposed two-trial replication is also not the only empirical check and does not invariably require two complete IPD datasets: treatment-specific interactions can be compared within a mixed network, and sufficiently detailed subgroup aggregate data may support a limited check. Existing within-network relaxation and model comparison partially address the problem; power, calibration, and prior sensitivity remain open. Cites 10.1177/0272989X221117162: Demonstrates a within-network empirical assessment of shared effect modification by relaxing common interactions to treatment-specific interactions and comparing the resulting models, so cross-trial replication using two IPD trials is not the only available check..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)
