title: Reference QBA software and a minimum reporting standard
text:
Statement
QBA for unanchored PAIC is done with bespoke per-submission scripts and no validated reference package with a benchmark suite and model manifest exists; the nearest artefact the literature auditor found is the analysis code accompanying Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), a repository with a simulated dataset. Parts of the proposed object are already built: cpaic (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9, an unreleased development package on GitHub, not installable from CRAN) exports estimability labels, effective sample size and weight diagnostics, edge influence, integration-error diagnostics, prior sensitivity and bridge fragility, but no qba(), net-benefit, tipping-surface, partial-identification, benchmark-suite or model-manifest interface. The reporting side is also partly occupied, since Ishak et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) publish a PAIC framework covering estimand definition, method and adjustment-variable selection, application, risk-of-bias assessment and comprehensive reporting, and Leahy et al. 2023 (doi:10.1017/S0266462323002702) already require transparent parameter sourcing and code and data sharing, so what no guideline covers is sensitivity-parameter provenance, dependence among bias parameters, feasibility surfaces and failed fits.

title: Reference QBA software and a minimum reporting standard
text:
Why it is open
Bespoke scripting means results cannot be reproduced, compared across submissions or checked by a reviewer, and without a benchmark suite there is no way to establish that an implementation is correct, so software correctness is currently taken on trust. A reference API must expose objects that existing PAIC packages have no representation for, including nonidentified sensitivity parameters, feasibility maps, decision-reversal surfaces and partial-identification bounds, so several checklist items require output that does not yet exist. No reporting guideline covers sensitivity-parameter provenance, dependence assumptions among bias parameters, feasibility surfaces or failed fits, so a reviewer has no standard against which to judge a submitted sensitivity analysis, and the proposed checklist has been neither validated nor adopted by any appraisal body. Economic models consume absolute arm-level survival and event probabilities, so a bias scenario can leave the relative effect plausible while implying arm outcomes no clinician would accept, and reporting only the contrast hides that.

title: Reference QBA software and a minimum reporting standard
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Leahy et al. 2023, International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
Covers part of the proposed reporting standard: transparent input sourcing, a-priori specification, sharing of all code and data used to inform and conduct QBA analyses with the respective HTA bodies, elicitation and early engagement.


Ishak, Chandler, Liu and Klijn 2025, A Framework for Reliable, Transparent, and Reproducible Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons, PharmacoEconomics 43:691-710
Published PAIC framework covering six elements: estimand definition, PAIC method selection, adjustment-variable selection, application of the adjustment method, risk-of-bias assessment and comprehensive reporting. Occupies part of the reporting-standard space the entry said was empty; does not cover sensitivity-parameter provenance, dependence among bias parameters, feasibility surfaces or failed fits.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
Supplies several proposed ingredients: estimability labels, a per-study weight panel (effective sample size, weight-entropy efficiency, coefficient of variation, largest normalized weight, mass in the top 5% of weights), edge influence, integration-error diagnostics, prior sensitivity and bridge fragility. It exports no qba(), net-benefit, tipping-surface, partial-identification, benchmark-suite or model-manifest interface, and its cMAIC returns within-study contrasts rather than bias-adjusted absolute arm outcomes.


Ren et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
The nearest artefact to reference QBA software the literature auditor located: analysis code with a simulated dataset accompanying the paper, rather than a validated package with a benchmark suite or model manifest.

title: Reference QBA software and a minimum reporting standard
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Assemble the reference API from the diagnostics that already exist rather than specifying it from scratch, and release it so a reader can install and check it: make the sensitivity specification, the mode of analysis and the decision threshold explicit arguments, and have the returned object report the estimand and effect scale, identified versus sensitivity-specified quantities, provenance, feasible versus unsupported scenarios and decision-reversal surfaces, invoking effective sample size, partial-identification bounds, dependence, dominance and cancellation only where they are defined for the analysis at hand. Pair it with a benchmark suite and a model manifest, and embed the checklist items in the output so compliance is a by-product of running the analysis. Extend the published PAIC reporting framework with the QBA-specific items it does not cover rather than proposing a rival checklist, and report bias-adjusted absolute arm outcomes wherever the estimator produces them, using clinical implausibility of implied arm outcomes as grounds for excluding scenarios.

title: Reference QBA software and a minimum reporting standard
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “QBA for unanchored PAIC is done with bespoke per-submission scripts and there is no validated reference package, benchmark suite or model manifest. The report proposes a fourteen-item minimum reporting checklist covering target population and exact estimand, causal diagram and bias mechanism, classification of each sensitivity variable, every parameter with scale, range or distribution and evidence source, dependence assumptions, interpretation mode, models used, support and feasibility diagnostics throughout the sensitivity region, all uncertainty layers and failed fits, decision thresholds, the proportion of the region leading to each decision, code, seeds, source data and elicitation materials, bias-adjusted absolute arm outcomes, and a statement of what QBA does not prove.”
What was wrong with it. The literature auditor found the claim that no ITC or PAIC reporting guideline exists overstated, because Ishak et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) already publish a PAIC risk-of-bias and reporting framework, so the claim narrows to the QBA-specific items it does not cover, and the requirement to share code and data is already in Leahy et al. 2023 (doi:10.1017/S0266462323002702). It does not, as far as I can establish from the abstract, cover sensitivity-parameter provenance, dependence among bias parameters, feasibility surfaces or failed fits, so the narrow version of claim 9 survives, but the sweeping version does not. Claims 2 to 6, 8, 10 and 11 are specifications for a future object and are internally coherent. codex dissented (overstated): C1’s field-wide absence cannot be established from source code or under the instructed non-literature lens. C5 applies to a probabilistic joint specification; a deterministic grid has constraints or allowed combinations but no correlations to report. C6 should require diagnostics where they vary and apply, not mechanically at every point. C9 is overstated because the cited Leahy guidance already covers transparent parameter sourcing and code/data disclosure, even if it does not supply this PAIC-specific checklist. title: No package unifies PAIC, transport, estimands and reporting
text: SFW-01 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: No package unifies PAIC, transport, estimands and reporting
text:
Statement
Existing packages already cover substantial and overlapping subsets of this agenda, but no mature, widely adopted package covers the whole capability list and none supplies a shared field-wide specification and reporting workflow. outstandR 2.0.0 (CRAN, 10 June 2026) unifies MAIC, STC and parametric G-computation behind one API with an explicit outcome-model and balance-model split; maicChecks 0.3.0 supplies dedicated MAIC feasibility and overlap diagnostics implementing Glimm and Yau (doi:10.1002/pst.2210); and cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not installable from CRAN, spans disconnected component bridging, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, marginal and conditional estimands, multiple outcome families and overlap, ESS, prior and bridge diagnostics at commit 9d150e9. What no single package supplies is doubly robust transport, integrated missing-data modeling, a coherent quantitative bias analysis object and regulatory reporting in one workflow. Defaults, diagnostics and output conventions still differ across packages, so the estimand and target are re-specified informally at every hand-off.

title: No package unifies PAIC, transport, estimands and reporting
text:
Why it is open
Each package grew around one methodological tradition, and the abstractions those traditions use for population, evidence structure and estimand are incompatible, so unification is not a matter of adding features to any one of them. The partial unification that exists stays inside a tradition: outstandR unifies the pairwise PAIC estimator families, maicChecks covers feasibility and overlap, cpaic covers the component and disconnected case, and none of them shares a representation of IPD plus aggregate data plus a target population on which a common diagnostic or reporting layer could sit. Defaults encode different implicit estimands, so two packages can answer the same question differently without either being wrong by its own conventions. The integration layer is unglamorous maintenance work that no funder, maintainer or academic incentive currently owns.

title: No package unifies PAIC, transport, estimands and reporting
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




outstandR 2.0.0 (CRAN, published 10 Jun 2026)
unifies MAIC, STC and parametric G-computation behind one API with an explicit outcome-model and balance-model split and a diagnostics vignette; partial unification across the PAIC estimator families, but pairwise and without transport, quantitative bias analysis or regulatory reporting layers


maicChecks 0.3.0 (CRAN; Yau, Glimm and Deng)
dedicated MAIC feasibility and overlap diagnostic package listed in the CRAN CausalInference task view; supplies the built-in overlap diagnostics the source said few ITC packages have


Glimm and Yau 2022
introduces multivariate data analysis methods for assessing whether MAIC is appropriate for a given set of baseline characteristics, comparing the matched variables between the aggregate-data study and the IPD study; the method maicChecks implements

spans disconnected component bridging, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, marginal and conditional estimands, component structure, multiple outcome families and overlap, ESS, prior and bridge diagnostics, and ships public known-truth data with cross-package equivalence tests; lacks doubly robust transport, integrated missing-data analysis, marginal standardization for cML-NMR, a quantitative bias analysis object and regulatory ledgers

title: No package unifies PAIC, transport, estimands and reporting
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not start from an empty platform. outstandR 2.0.0 already separates outcome model from balance model in a single API and says in its release notes that the split is meant to accommodate doubly robust methods, maicChecks already implements the feasibility and overlap layer, and cpaic already covers the component and disconnected case. The work is defining the shared data model for IPD, aggregate data and target populations that lets those pieces interoperate, then adding the capabilities none of them has: doubly robust transport, missing-data modeling, a quantitative bias analysis object and regulatory reporting. Pair that with a common reference API and cross-package gold-standard tests built out from the known-truth fixtures and equivalence tests cpaic already carries.

Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “ITC and PAIC capability is scattered across packages with inconsistent defaults, diagnostics and output conventions, and no mature, widely adopted open package natively unifies target-population definition, connected and disconnected evidence, marginal and conditional estimands, doubly robust transport, component structure, complex outcomes, missing data, sensitivity analysis, overlap diagnostics and regulatory reporting. The report states this is an inference from reviewed package scopes and issue trackers, not a formal theorem.”
What was wrong with it. The source was unattributed and claimed both that few ITC packages carry built-in PAIC diagnostics or overlap visualization and that no public validation datasets or cross-package gold-standard tests exist; the literature auditor supplied maicChecks 0.3.0 (cran:maicChecks, implementing doi:10.1002/pst.2210) and outstandR 2.0.0, and GPT-5.6 Sol found public known-truth fixtures and cross-package equivalence tests in cpaic at commit 9d150e9. The conjunctive gap across the full capability list survives, those two supporting claims do not, and the entry is now sourced.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): At cpaic commit 9d150e9, the package already spans disconnected component bridging, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, marginal and conditional estimands, component structure, multiple outcome families, and overlap, ESS, prior, and bridge diagnostics. It still lacks doubly robust transport, integrated missing-data analysis, marginal standardization for cML-NMR, a coherent QBA object, and regulatory ledgers, so the complete platform gap remains open. C2-C3 are defensible only as conjunctions covering the entire feature list. C4, C6, C10, C11, and C15 are proportionate. C7 is vague; C8 is an interoperability claim rather than a statistical result; C9 is false as an absolute because cpaic includes public known-truth data and cross-package equivalence tests; and C12-C14 are unsupported superlatives. The decision-grade concern is failure to declare estimands, targets, assumptions, and diagnostics, not the absence of one omnibus package.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, so nothing to check for fidelity; I hunted prior art instead. The conjunctive negative (one package covering target definition + disconnected evidence + marginal/conditional estimands + DR transport + components + complex outcomes + missing data + QBA + overlap + regulatory reporting) survives: I found no candidate. But two supporting claims are weaker than stated. outstandR 2.0.0 (CRAN, 2026-06-10) already unifies MAIC, STC and parametric G-computation behind one API with an explicit outcome_model/balance_model split and a diagnostics vignette, i.e. partial unification across PAIC families. And ‘few ITC packages have built-in PAIC diagnostics, overlap visualisation’ overlooks maicChecks 0.3.0 (Yau, Glimm, Deng; CRAN, CausalInference task view), a dedicated MAIC feasibility/overlap diagnostic package implementing Glimm & Yau (2022). Neither appears anywhere in the SFW landscape. ‘No public validation datasets exist’ is a negative I cannot verify and is partly countered by the public simulation studies cited under SFW-04.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, the package already spans disconnected component bridging, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, marginal and conditional estimands, component structure, multiple outcome families, and overlap, ESS, prior, and bridge diagnostics. It still lacks doubly robust transport, integrated missing-data analysis, marginal standardization for cML-NMR, a coherent QBA object, and regulatory ledgers, so the complete platform gap remains open. C2-C3 are defensible only as conjunctions covering the entire feature list. C4, C6, C10, C11, and C15 are proportionate. C7 is vague; C8 is an interoperability claim rather than a statistical result; C9 is false as an absolute because cpaic includes public known-truth data and cross-package equivalence tests; and C12-C14 are unsupported superlatives. The decision-grade concern is failure to declare estimands, targets, assumptions, and diagnostics, not the absence of one omnibus package.

Decision path

text: SFW-03 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: No minimum validation standard for ITC and PAIC packages
text:
Statement
The report specifies ten items every methodological ITC/PAIC package should contain, and the literature auditor confirmed the list is exactly ten and matches the source at section 16.5 item for item. The requirements are sound but scale with a package’s model surface rather than applying uniformly: simulation-based calibration applies to Bayesian generative implementations rather than thin wrappers around already validated engines, and the multi-arm, separation, correlation-matrix and Stan toolchain items apply only where those features or dependencies exist. No package is documented as meeting the whole bar, but parts of it are met in practice: the literature auditor found multinma runs continuous integration and ships 13 test files reproducing published NICE TSD and paper examples, with no visible simulation-based calibration, non-estimability assertion or model card, and GPT-5.6 Sol found analytic estimability, deliberate non-estimability, multi-arm and cross-package equivalence tests in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN.

title: No minimum validation standard for ITC and PAIC packages
text:
Why it is open
Statistical packages in this field are usually validated by reproducing a published example, which exercises the happy path, so the failure modes that matter (non-estimable contrasts, degenerate overlap, invalid target moments, ill-conditioned correlation matrices) go mostly untested; the exceptions the audit found are one package’s example suite and one unreleased development package. Several listed items have no standard tooling: there is no convention for asserting that a package refuses to produce a data-driven estimate for a non-estimable contrast, and model cards for statistical software are not an established artifact. Continuous integration across evolving Stan and R toolchains is a recurring maintenance cost few academic packages sustain and no funder pays for. Nothing yet says which items apply to which kind of package, so a maintainer cannot tell what compliance would even mean.

multinma 0.9.1 (CRAN, published 16 Apr 2026)
runs GitHub Actions continuous integration (R-CMD-check, HTML5, rhub, test coverage) and carries 34 testthat files of which 13 reproduce published NICE TSD and paper examples; the literature auditor found no simulation-based calibration, non-estimability assertion or model card, which is the pattern this entry describes

title: No minimum validation standard for ITC and PAIC packages
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Publish the bar as a conditional standard: name the items that apply to every methodological package (analytic special cases, non-estimability behavior, equivalence tests where models coincide, deliberate failure tests) and the items that apply only when the corresponding feature or dependency exists (multi-arm covariance, Bayesian calibration, toolchain matrices). Build the shared tooling the conditional items need, and specify tolerances and inferential invariants for versioned expected outputs so they do not turn into brittle snapshots. Start from the partial implementations that exist rather than from nothing: multinma’s continuous integration and published-example suite for the reproduction half, cpaic’s analytic estimability and cross-package equivalence tests for the correctness half.

title: No minimum validation standard for ITC and PAIC packages
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The report specifies ten items every methodological ITC/PAIC package should contain: analytic unit tests for special cases; simulation-based calibration for Bayesian models; numerical equivalence tests against established software where models coincide; tests that non-estimable contrasts return no data-driven estimate; tests for multi-arm covariance; deliberate failure tests for separation, poor overlap, invalid target moments and non-positive-definite correlations; reproducible vignettes with tracked simulation code; model cards recording estimand, target, priors, integration and assumptions; versioned expected outputs; and continuous integration across R and Stan/toolchain versions. No package in the field is documented as meeting this bar.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol judged the universal framing overstated: several of the ten items are conditional on a package having the relevant model feature or dependency, model cards are desirable rather than a condition for mathematical correctness, and versioned expected outputs become brittle unless stochastic tolerances and inferential invariants are specified. The claim that no package meets the bar also needs qualifying, since the auditors found multinma’s continuous integration and published-example suite and cpaic’s analytic, non-estimability and cross-package equivalence tests already meeting parts of it.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I retrieved section 16.5 of the source document (lines 2309-2322). It contains exactly ten numbered items and they match the ten claims_to_check one for one, in order, including ‘simulation-based calibration for Bayesian models’, ‘tests that non-estimable contrasts return no data-driven estimate’, ‘model cards recording estimand, target, priors, integration, and assumptions’ and ‘continuous integration across R and Stan/toolchain versions’. The ‘exactly ten items’ claim is exact. On the empirical claim that no package meets the bar, I inspected the strongest candidate: multinma has GitHub Actions for R-CMD-check, R-CMD-check-HTML5, rhub and test-coverage, and 34 testthat files of which 13 are test-example_*.R reproductions of published NICE TSD and paper examples. That is CI plus published-example reproduction, with no visible simulation-based calibration, non-estimability assertion or model card, which is precisely the pattern the entry describes. Claims 1-10 are normative and not falsifiable by literature.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C11 is correct: the report enumerates exactly ten items. Analytic special-case tests, equivalence tests where models coincide, non-estimability tests, covariance tests, and deliberate failure tests are sound requirements when applicable. The universal wording is too strong. Simulation-based calibration applies to Bayesian generative implementations, not necessarily thin wrappers around already validated engines. Multi-arm, separation, correlation-matrix, and Stan-version requirements apply only when those features or dependencies exist. Reproducible examples and model cards are highly desirable, but their exact artifact form is not a condition for mathematical correctness. Versioned outputs can also become brittle unless stochastic tolerances and inferential invariants are specified. CI should cover declared supported toolchains rather than every R and Stan version. This is an important software-quality agenda, but not every item is independently critical for every decision-grade package.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text: SFW-05 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text:
Statement
Generic quantitative bias analysis packages implement algebraic confounding, misclassification or selection analyses, and survival tools such as survSens address adjacent observational settings, but none provides a coherent PAIC object holding the source, comparator and decision targets together with all three adjustment families, omitted-variable and target-distribution bias, outcome, measurement and censoring bias, overlap and ESS surfaces, multiple-bias simulation, target-standardized survival and RMST, bridge drift and machine-readable reporting. The one direct implementation, QBA-UM-STC, is supplementary research code for Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), tied to unanchored STC, with no licence, test suite or interface contract. The gap is in built-in abstractions and workflows rather than in method: transport-specific sensitivity analysis has been developed, including Nguyen et al. 2017 (doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1001) on bias functions for effect modifiers not observed in the target and Dahabreh et al. 2026 (doi:10.1002/sim.70083) on global sensitivity analysis for extending inferences, and generic bias algebra can be adapted to encode target-distribution bias even though no package represents it natively.

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text:
Why it is open
A PAIC bias-analysis object has to carry the estimand, the source and target populations, the adjustment method and the bridge at the same time, and no existing software abstraction represents that combination, so the published transport sensitivity methods have no implementation route into a PAIC workflow. Research scripts accompanying a paper encode that paper’s data structures and assumptions and carry no tests, versioning or interface contract, so another analysis cannot reuse them. Because the one implementation is tied to STC, the same bias model cannot be applied to unanchored MAIC or ML-UMR without a rewrite, so sensitivity analysis for unanchored PAIC is done ad hoc if at all. A sensitivity tool also cannot resolve an identification problem, so the object has to make the unidentified assumption visible rather than dissolve it.

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025 (QBA-UM-STC repository)
supplementary research code implementing quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured or unreported covariates in limited-aggregate-data unanchored STC, with deterministic and probabilistic scenario analysis and graphical output; no licence, tests or interface contract, and it is STC-specific


Ren, Ren, Welton and Strong 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons, Res Synth Methods 16(3):509-527
the paper the QBA-UM-STC code accompanies; proposes simulation of unreported comparator covariates with deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analysis for unanchored STC, demonstrated on a case study


survSens (CRAN)
sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding in observational survival and competing-risks studies; an adjacent observational setting rather than a transport or PAIC setting


Nguyen et al. 2017
sensitivity analysis for generalizing trial results using bias functions, covering effect modifiers not observed in the target population; shows transport-specific sensitivity methodology exists even though no package implements it as a PAIC object


Dahabreh et al. 2026
global sensitivity analysis framework for studies extending inferences from a trial to a target population; further transport-specific methodology available to a PAIC bias-analysis implementation

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the reference package around a coherent object holding source, comparator and decision targets, all three adjustment families, and the bias, overlap, drift and reporting layers, implementing the transport sensitivity methods that already exist, such as bias functions and global sensitivity analysis, rather than inventing new ones. Generalize QBA-UM-STC from unanchored STC to a common interface covering MAIC and ML-UMR, and give it the licence, tests, versioning and automated validation that research code lacks. Design the output so the bias model, sensitivity-parameter provenance, support failures and decision consequences cannot be omitted, and do not settle for wrapping E-values.

title: No coherent QBA software object for population-adjusted comparison
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The report states the QBA software gap is more severe than the estimator gap: generic QBA packages implement algebraic confounding, misclassification or selection analyses and survival packages such as survSens address adjacent observational settings, but none provides a coherent PAIC object combining explicit source, comparator and decision targets, MAIC plus STC/g-computation plus ML-UMR, omitted-variable and target-distribution QBA, outcome, measurement and censoring bias, overlap and ESS surfaces, multiple-bias simulation, target-standardized survival and RMST, bridge drift for disconnected and component networks, economic-decision propagation and machine-readable reporting. The only direct implementation, QBA-UM-STC, is supplementary research code for one paper.”
What was wrong with it. The entry’s premise that existing bias-analysis tools were built for observational epidemiology and not for transport is too strong at method level: the literature auditor named Nguyen et al. 2017 (doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1001) and Dahabreh et al. 2026 (doi:10.1002/sim.70083) on sensitivity analysis for transport and for effect modifiers unobserved in the target, and GPT-5.6 Sol added that generic bias algebra can be adapted to transport even though no package represents it natively. The unverifiable priority claim that QBA-UM-STC is the first such public implementation has been dropped, and its paper is now cited (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13).

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Both citations check out. The QBA-UM-STC repository (created 2025-02-10, last pushed 2025-02-11, two items, no licence) states ‘This provides supplementary R code for the paper, Ren S, Ren S, Welton NJ, Strong M…’, confirming research-code status; the paper is Res Synth Methods 16(3):509-527, doi 10.1017/rsm.2025.13, and its abstract confirms STC-specificity and unmeasured/unreported covariates. survSens is correctly characterised: its CRAN description is confounding sensitivity analysis in observational survival/competing-risks studies. The coherent-object gap is real and, per calibration, a sensitivity-analysis tool cannot resolve an identification problem anyway. Two caveats. ‘First public implementation’ is a priority claim neither the paper nor the repo makes. And the why_open assertion that existing QBA tools were built for observational epidemiology ‘not for transport’ is too strong at method level: the catalog’s own reference folder holds Nguyen (2017, 2018) on sensitivity analysis for effect modifiers not observed in the target population and Dahabreh (2026) on global sensitivity analysis for studies extending inferences.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The proposed coherent object is technically well motivated because PAIC sensitivity analysis must jointly track the estimand, source and target populations, support, adjustment method, bridge assumptions, and bias-parameter provenance. C4 and C6-C8 are proportionate. C3 is correct only as a statement about built-in abstractions and workflows: generic QBA algebra can be adapted to encode transport or target-distribution bias, even if existing generic packages do not represent it natively. C1 is a subjective comparison of two software gaps, and C2 is an exhaustive package-landscape assertion rather than a mathematical conclusion. C9 is a priority or novelty claim outside this audit lens. Under the no-web constraint, C10-C13 could not be independently audited against the QBA-UM-STC source tree. The high severity is justified when an unanchored decision-grade analysis lacks defensible sensitivity analysis, but absence of a unified software object is itself primarily a roadmap and reproducibility problem.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: multinma lacks partial IPD, missing data and a data-informed bridge
text: SFW-07 Overstated Very high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: multinma lacks partial IPD, missing data and a data-informed bridge
text:
Statement
Open multinma issues include missing data (#67), mixed aggregate and individual data within one study (#58), mixed likelihoods (#42) and the interpretation and ranking of some time-to-event auxiliary parameters (#52), and data-informed baseline connections for disconnected networks existed only as unmerged pull request #68 at inspection. Baseline-risk adjustment and marginal effects in external target populations are not open needs: the former is a released feature announced in the 0.9.0 release notes through the new .mu regression variable following TSD3, and the latter was confirmed implemented by the maintainer when closing issue #59 on 11 December 2025, documented in the plaque psoriasis vignette with the method published as Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162). Released multinma will also fit a disconnected network; what it lacks is a data-informed bridge, because cross-component relative effects are then determined entirely by priors. The remaining substantive gaps are partial IPD within a study, missing-data modeling inside the integration step, broader mixed-likelihood structures and released support for data-informed disconnected bridges.

title: multinma lacks partial IPD, missing data and a data-informed bridge
text:
Why it is open
The data model still assumes a study is either IPD or aggregate and that studies share a likelihood family, so a partially individual study or a network mixing binary and survival outcomes has no representation in the object. Missing covariate data interacts with the integration step, because the covariate distribution being integrated over is itself partly unobserved, which makes it a modeling problem rather than preprocessing. For disconnected evidence the software already returns an answer, which is the harder problem: nothing in the returned object separates a prior-driven cross-component contrast from a data-informed one, and the baseline-connection work that would supply the data-informed bridge sits in an unmerged branch. The steep learning curve keeps the user base small, which slows the feedback that would settle the remaining interface questions.

title: multinma lacks partial IPD, missing data and a data-informed bridge
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the data model to represent partially individual studies, mixed likelihoods across a network and missing covariate or outcome data inside the integration step, and implement missing data as a modeling layer rather than a preprocessing step. Complete and merge the baseline-connection work in PR #68 so disconnected networks can be bridged with data-informed rather than purely prior-driven cross-component effects, and make the prior-driven versus data-driven contribution visible in the returned object so a prior-dominated estimate does not look like any other. title: multinma lacks partial IPD, missing data and a data-informed bridge
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Open multinma issues include missing data (#67), mixed aggregate and individual data within one study (#58), mixed likelihoods (#42) and the interpretation and ranking of some time-to-event auxiliary parameters (#52), and disconnected-network support existed only as unmerged pull request #68 at inspection. Baseline-risk adjustment and marginal effects in external target populations are implemented in the released package (0.9.0/0.9.1), the former announced in NEWS and the latter confirmed by the maintainer when closing issue #59, although issue #35 was left open in the tracker.
The source titled this. “multinma data model omits partial IPD, missing data and disconnection” The title says the data model omits disconnection, but released multinma does fit disconnected networks; what it lacks is a data-informed baseline bridge.
The source said. “Open multinma issues include missing data, mixed aggregate and individual data within one study, mixed likelihoods, baseline-risk adjustment, marginal effects in external populations, and interpretation and ranking of some time-to-event parameters, while disconnected-network support existed only as unmerged pull request #68 at inspection. The most mature open Bayesian NMA/ML-NMR platform therefore had no released support for disconnected evidence at the audit date.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors found the entry stale in the same two places: baseline-risk adjustment shipped in 0.9.0 (release notes, .mu regression variable, PR #36, with issue #35 left open in the tracker only because it was never closed) and marginal effects in an external target population were already implemented when the maintainer closed issue #59, so listing them as open needs was wrong. GPT-5.6 Sol also found the claim of no released disconnected-network support literally false, since released multinma fits disconnected networks with prior-driven cross-component effects and what PR #68 adds is the data-informed baseline connection; the claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Two of the enumerated gaps are shipped features in the very release the entry cites. (1) Baseline-risk adjustment: multinma NEWS for 0.9.0 (CRAN 2026-04-13, superseded by 0.9.1 on 2026-04-16) announces regression on baseline risk via the new .mu variable, done on the estimated intercept per TSD3, with a Certolizumab vignette. Issue #35 is open only because it was never closed; the maintainer wrote in-thread that the fix was in PR #36. (2) Marginal effects in external populations: issue #59 ‘Marginal effects in an external target population’ is CLOSED (2025-12-11) with the maintainer answering that it is already implemented via baseline_type=‘response’ and baseline_level=‘aggregate’, demonstrated in the plaque psoriasis vignette, method in Phillippo et al. 2022. The remaining claims verify: #67 missing data, #58 mixed AgD/IPD in one study, #42 mixed likelihoods, #52 ranking of TTE auxiliary parameters are all open, and PR #68 (opened 2026-07-07) is unmerged with no disconnected-network entry anywhere in NEWS. Cites cran:multinma: Baseline-risk adjustment, listed by the entry as an open need, is a released feature.. Cites https://github.com/dmphillippo/multinma/issues/59: Marginal effects in external target populations, listed by the entry as an open issue, is an implemented and documented feature; the issue is closed.. Cites 10.1177/0272989X221117162: The published method behind multinma’s external-target-population intercept solution, cited by the maintainer when closing issue #59..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2, C3, and the released limitations underlying C5 are supported: missing data are not modeled internally, duplicate study labels across IPD and aggregate sources are rejected, and outcome-family combinations are restricted. C4 is stale because version 0.9.1 supports baseline-risk regression. C7-C8 are supported by the unmerged PR #68 branch. C9 is literally false: released multinma will fit disconnected networks, but cross-component relative effects are entirely prior-driven rather than identified through a data-informed bridge. C12 is only partly current because external-population marginal effects and baseline-risk adjustment are already implemented; time-to-event interpretation or ranking questions may remain. C6 incorrectly treats mixed likelihoods as equivalent to multivariate outcomes. C10-C11 are supported by the release source, while C13-C14 are unquantified superlatives. The remaining substantive gap is released support for data-informed disconnected bridges, partial IPD within a study, missing-data models, and broader mixed-likelihood structures. Cites dmphillippo/multinma@4fe8a6e9977b7ba6ef93822dda43b617b256587a: Resolves the claimed absence of baseline-risk adjustment and external-target marginal effects, and documents that disconnected networks can be fitted with cross-component effects determined by priors.. Cites dmphillippo/multinma@47863128c1f6aa012c754babc82e1c30d4b746d1: Partially implements baseline connections for disconnected networks and mixed-study handling, but was not merged into the inspected release or development ancestry..

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text: SFW-09 Confirmed open High priority Established Implementation-specific

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text:
Statement
maicplus 0.1.2 (CRAN, 21 February 2025) restricts its public analysis APIs to binary and time-to-event endpoints, offering odds ratio, risk difference or risk ratio for binary data and hazard ratio for survival, with open issues requesting continuous and count outcomes (#209, #96), further time-to-event effect measures (#51) and a time-dependent Cox model (#95). Risk ratio is fitted with a weighted binomial model with a log link, with warnings suppressed and no explicit convergence guard, and issue #200 reports problems with it, so the numerical concern is credible. This is a package scope gap rather than a field gap: continuous-outcome MAIC is available elsewhere in the ecosystem, for example the Shiny-MAIC application (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1709), which offers anchored and unanchored MAIC across different covariate and outcome types with bootstrap and robust variance estimators. The gaps bind only when an analysis needs one of the missing outcomes or estimands.

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text:
Why it is open
The estimation and variance machinery was built around binary and time-to-event endpoints, so the weighted variance, bootstrap and reporting paths all assume those outcome types and adding a link function is not sufficient. Effect measures that are not a single coefficient, such as anything derived from the weighted survival curve, change the object being bootstrapped rather than only the summary reported. The risk-ratio path is a weighted binomial fit with a log link and no convergence guard, so instability there is a numerical problem in existing code rather than a missing feature. None of this blocks an analysis whose outcome the package already supports, which is why the gaps persist in an actively maintained package.

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




maicplus 0.1.2 (CRAN, published 21 Feb 2025)
provides a maintained MAIC workflow with anchored and unanchored binary and survival analyses plus weighting and reporting utilities across seven vignettes; public analysis APIs are limited to binary (odds ratio, risk difference, risk ratio) and time-to-event (hazard ratio) endpoints


hta-pharma/maicplus (GitHub)
development repository whose open issues were examined in the audit, including #209 and #96 on continuous and count data, #200 on risk ratio for binary outcomes, #51 on further time-to-event effect measures and #95 on a time-dependent Cox model


Shiny-MAIC application

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Add continuous and count outcome paths with variance and reporting machinery matched to each outcome type rather than retrofitted onto the binary and survival paths, porting what already works in other MAIC implementations instead of deriving it again. Add an explicit convergence guard and diagnostics to the weighted log-link binomial fit behind the risk ratio rather than suppressing warnings. Specify which further time-to-event effect measures are actually wanted, since the underlying issue asks for more measures rather than for non-proportional-hazards measures specifically, and add the requested time-dependent Cox path.

title: maicplus supports only binary and time-to-event endpoints
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “maicplus lacks continuous, count and non-proportional-hazards outcomes” The title names non-proportional-hazards outcomes as a documented gap, but the audit found the underlying issue asks for more time-to-event effect measures and mentions neither NPH nor RMST.
The source said. “maicplus, the maintained CRAN MAIC workflow supporting anchored and unanchored binary and survival analyses, has open needs for continuous and count outcomes, risk-ratio convergence, non-proportional-hazards effect measures and time-dependent Cox models.”
What was wrong with it. Two of the source’s labels were stronger than the tracker text the literature auditor checked: risk-ratio convergence rests on an issue titled only issues with RR for binary (#200), and non-proportional-hazards effect measures maps to #51, add more effect measure for time to event, which mentions neither non-proportional hazards nor RMST. The auditor also found continuous-outcome MAIC available elsewhere (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1709), and GPT-5.6 Sol judged the general high severity inflated because these gaps matter only for analyses needing those outcomes.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Retrieved all 23 open maicplus issues. Confirmed open: #209 ‘add support for continuous and count data’ (2026-05-18), #96 ‘add continuous endpoint’, #200 ‘issues with RR for binary’, #95 ‘add time dependent cox model’. CRAN confirms 0.1.2 published 2025-02-21 and a scope of time-to-event and binary endpoints, anchored and unanchored, across seven vignettes. Two claims are paraphrases stronger than the tracker text: ‘risk-ratio convergence’ rests on an issue titled only ‘issues with RR for binary’, and ‘non-proportional-hazards effect measures’ maps to #51 ‘add more effect measure for time to event’, which does not mention non-PH or RMST. Context worth adding rather than a defect: continuous-outcome MAIC is available elsewhere in the ecosystem, so this is a maicplus gap and not a field gap.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. maicplus 0.1.2 restricts its public analysis APIs to binary and time-to-event endpoints, with OR, RD, or RR for binary data and HR for survival data. It lacks continuous and count paths, inferential non-proportional-hazards measures such as RMST contrasts, and time-dependent Cox models. RR uses a weighted binomial model with a log link, suppressed warnings, and no explicit convergence guard, so the numerical concern is credible. These are material only when the analysis requires those outcomes or estimands, making the asserted general high severity somewhat inflated. The v0.1.2 tag is dated 21 February 2025 and supports anchored and unanchored binary and survival analyses.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text: SFW-11 Overstated Medium priority Established Implementation-specific

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text:
Statement
Archived and explicitly deprecated MAIC packages are poor foundations for a new reference workflow: CRAN archived maic on 22 July 2025 because email to the maintainer was undeliverable, leaving only versions 0.1.2 to 0.1.4 with the last dated 27 April 2022, and the Roche MAIC README states the package is no longer developed and recommends maicplus. That is a reason to migrate with a documented mapping rather than a reason to call historical analyses unverifiable, since source archives, dependency locks and containers can preserve them. BUGSnet has never been on CRAN, so installation still depends on GitHub plus JAGS, and it carries many long-open issues, several dating from 2019, but it is not without releases: the repository has five version tags through v1.1.2 on 22 June 2024. It has no native PAIC layer, so its reporting-oriented graphics sit outside the population-adjustment workflow.

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text:
Why it is open
Published analyses built on archived packages cannot be reinstalled from CRAN and drift out of compatibility as dependencies move, so reproducing them needs a preserved environment most submissions never captured; the record degrades quietly rather than becoming impossible. Migration to a maintained successor is not a drop-in substitution because defaults, diagnostics and outputs differ, and no migration mapping or behavioral comparison has been published. BUGSnet’s weaker signals, meaning no CRAN path and issues open since 2019 despite a 2024 release, make adoption for new work a bet on maintainer capacity. Its strength is exactly the reporting-oriented output the field says it needs, so decay there removes the capability that is scarcest.

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




heorltd/maic
early MAIC workflow package; CRAN archived it on 22 July 2025 because email to the maintainer was undeliverable, and the archive holds only 0.1.2 to 0.1.4 with the last dated 27 April 2022


Roche/MAIC
Roche MAIC package whose README carries the deprecation notice and the recommendation to use maicplus instead


BUGSnet (GitHub)
accessible, feature-rich Bayesian NMA workflow with reporting-oriented graphics and survival examples; never on CRAN, so installation depends on GitHub plus JAGS, and it has no native PAIC layer


BUGSnet releases (GitHub)
five tagged releases, v1.0.3 (2019) through v1.1.2 on 22 June 2024, contradicting the entry’s claim that the repository has no releases

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Publish a migration path and behavioral mapping from the archived and deprecated MAIC packages to maicplus, so historical analyses can be re-expressed rather than only reinstalled, and record the environment (dependency locks or containers) needed to re-run the originals rather than declaring them lost. For BUGSnet, either restore a maintained, versioned release path so its reporting outputs stay reproducible or port those graphics into a maintained package. Check maintenance and installation status before adopting any of these tools for new work, judging by release tags and issue age rather than by a binary maintained-or-not label.

title: Archived MAIC packages leave no maintained CRAN installation path
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. The BUGSnet GitHub repository shows many long-open issues, several dating from 2019, and no release since v1.1.2 on 22 June 2024; it has never been on CRAN, so installation still depends on GitHub plus JAGS rather than a maintained CRAN path.
The source titled this. “Archived and unmaintained ITC packages break reproducibility” The title says archived packages break reproducibility, which the audit rejected since preserved source, dependency locks and containers keep historical analyses reproducible.
The source said. “Legacy MAIC tooling is no longer viable: the maic package was archived on CRAN in July 2025 and Roche states its MAIC package is no longer developed, recommending maicplus instead, so those installs belong in reproducibility archaeology rather than in a new reference workflow. BUGSnet, which is feature-rich and reporting-oriented, shows weaker maintenance signals, with long-open issues, no releases and a GitHub plus JAGS installation path rather than a maintained CRAN path.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors rejected the claim that BUGSnet has no releases: the repository carries five tagged releases through v1.1.2 on 22 June 2024, and GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed Version: 1.1.2 in the source at audrey-b/BUGSnet@46102ef. That matters because the whole maintenance-decay argument rests on those signals; GPT-5.6 Sol also rejected the stronger reproducibility claim, since archived software remains reproducible with preserved environments, and the claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced to the CRAN archive notice and the Roche README.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. Three of four claim clusters verify exactly. CRAN states maic was ‘Archived on 2025-07-22 as email to the maintainer is undeliverable’, so July 2025 is right, and the archive holds only 0.1.2-0.1.4 (last 2022-04-27). The Roche/MAIC README carries the deprecation and the maicplus recommendation verbatim. BUGSnet is genuinely absent from CRAN (404), so the GitHub plus JAGS install path holds, and long-open issues are real: over 30 open issues, many filed in 2019. But ‘no releases’ is false. The repository has five tagged releases, the most recent BUGSnet v1.1.2 on 2024-06-22, which is a weaker maintenance signal than active packages but not the absence of releases. Since the whole BUGSnet-decay argument rests on maintenance signals, getting one of the two signals wrong matters.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is an empty placeholder. Archival and explicit deprecation are sound reasons not to choose the legacy MAIC packages for a new reference workflow, and a migration mapping remains useful. They increase reproducibility fragility but do not make historical analyses inherently unverifiable when source archives, dependency locks, or containers exist. BUGSnet upstream uses a GitHub and JAGS installation path, includes extensive NMA graphics and survival material, and has no native PAIC layer. The categorical claim of no releases is not supported by its source history: it has five version tags and a v1.1.2 DESCRIPTION. Offline evidence cannot determine whether separate GitHub Release objects exist or establish comparative maintainer capacity.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text: SFW-13 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Implementation-specific

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text:
Statement
cpaic and mlumr are young single-maintainer research packages on GitHub, neither released to CRAN and neither installable from it, that need independent benchmarking and external validation of the strong structural and unanchored assumptions they rely on. At commit 9d150e9 cpaic implements every capability the source listed, namely estimability, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, edge influence, bridge fragility and binary, continuous, count and time-to-event outcomes, along with estimability, influence, fragility, prior, MCMC and model-comparison diagnostics; what it still lacks is marginal standardization on the cML-NMR path, which returns a conditional profile contrast. mlumr is at version 0.2.0 and remains limited to one pairwise IPD-versus-aggregate contrast, but it already supports arbitrary target populations by Bayesian g-computation, prior sensitivity, MCMC and integration diagnostics, model comparison, several outcome families and worked case-study vignettes, and it is adapted from multinma concepts rather than running on multinma. Readers should also know that both packages are authored by this catalog’s own byline holder, which is why independent replication matters more here than usual.

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text:
Why it is open
Component PAIC rests on component additivity and bridge assumptions the evidence generally cannot check, and unanchored comparison requires conditional exchangeability of absolute outcomes given adjusted covariates, which is untestable from the data at hand; software can make these assumptions explicit but cannot test them. Being first integrated implementations, there is no second implementation to compare against, so numerical equivalence testing is largely unavailable and validation depends on case studies and independent replication that do not exist yet. Extending unanchored work beyond two treatments means deciding how unanchored links compose across a network, which is a methodological question rather than an implementation task. Single-maintainer packages written by the same person who wrote the agenda have no independent user base to generate the validation evidence.

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




cpaic 0.1.0, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
integrates component-PAIC estimability, cMAIC, cSTC and cML-NMR with edge influence, bridge fragility and binary, continuous, count and time-to-event outcomes, plus estimability, influence, fragility, prior, MCMC and model-comparison diagnostics; the cML-NMR path returns a conditional profile contrast rather than a marginal standardized effect


mlumr 0.2.0, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit b2e24ce
implements Bayesian multilevel unanchored meta-regression with STC and naive comparators, transporting treatment effects and absolute outcomes to an arbitrary target population by Bayesian g-computation, with automatic MCMC diagnostics, prior sensitivity, model comparison, several outcome families and worked case-study vignettes; still limited to one pairwise IPD-versus-aggregate contrast, and adapted from multinma concepts rather than running on multinma

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The construction work is largely done, so the priority is external evidence: independent benchmarking against the adversarial suite proposed elsewhere in this catalog, replication by someone unconnected to the packages, and quantitative bias analysis attached to every unanchored estimate. The concrete remaining build in cpaic is marginal standardization on the cML-NMR path, which currently returns a conditional profile contrast; in mlumr it is extension beyond one pairwise contrast, which requires first settling how unanchored links compose across a network. Both should state the structural and unanchored assumptions they rely on in their own output, and neither should be described as installable from CRAN, because they are not.

title: cpaic and mlumr are unreleased and independently unvalidated
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “cpaic and mlumr are early-stage with no external validation” The title calls both packages early-stage, which the audit found stale since each already implements its listed capabilities and diagnostics.
The source said. “The two packages implementing the newest PAIC methods are early-stage GitHub development packages: cpaic 0.1.0, described as the first integrated component-PAIC platform known to this review, covering estimability, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, edge influence, bridge fragility and multiple outcomes; and mlumr, implementing Bayesian unanchored ML-UMR plus STC and naive comparators on multinma machinery. Both lack mature external validation, rely on strong structural or unanchored assumptions, and leave marginal standardization, complex-data modules, wider treatment scope, diagnostics and HTA case studies open.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol found the immaturity claims stale in two places: at commit 9d150e9 cpaic implements all the listed capabilities plus extensive diagnostics, and mlumr 0.2.0 already provides target-population standardization, diagnostics, prior sensitivity, model comparison and worked examples, so the claim that it still needs target and diagnostic development no longer holds, and mlumr is adapted from multinma concepts rather than built on multinma machinery. The literature auditor confirmed both repositories, flagged first and most promising as unverifiable priority claims, and disclosed that both packages are authored by the catalog’s own byline holder; the claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced to the repositories.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is an empty placeholder. At the specified cpaic commit, every named capability is exported and implemented, including estimability, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, edge influence, bridge fragility, and multiple outcome families. Strong additivity, bridge, and unanchored assumptions and the absence of mature independent validation remain legitimate concerns. The cML-NMR path still returns a conditional profile contrast rather than a marginal standardized effect. Conversely, cpaic already has substantial estimability, influence, fragility, prior, MCMC, and model-comparison diagnostics. mlumr 0.2.0 remains limited to one pairwise IPD-versus-AgD contrast, but it already supports arbitrary target populations by g-computation, prior sensitivity, MCMC and integration diagnostics, model comparison, several outcome families, and worked case-study vignettes. It is adapted from multinma concepts rather than using multinma as its runtime engine. Claims that it still lacks target and diagnostic development are stale; ‘first’ and ‘most promising’ are novelty or subjective claims outside this audit lens.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Both repositories exist and match their descriptions: cpaic DESCRIPTION is version 0.1.0, extends cNMA to PAIC via netmeta and maicplus with anchored STC/MAIC/ML-NMR and binary, continuous, count and time-to-event outcomes; mlumr was created 2026-03-10. Source line 2253 matches the mlumr row verbatim. The immaturity claims are true by construction: cpaic was created 2026-06-26, weeks before the audit date, neither package has releases or a second maintainer. Searching PubMed for component NMA crossed with MAIC, population-adjusted or ML-NMR returns nothing relevant, so the ‘first integrated component-PAIC platform’ claim is not contradicted, but it is a priority claim I cannot verify. Two things a reader would want disclosed. Both packages are authored by the catalog’s own byline holder (cpaic DESCRIPTION lists Ahmad Sofi-Mahmudi as sole aut/cre), and mlumr is simultaneously rated ‘the most promising early-stage package for unanchored work’. Also, Wigle & Beliveau (2022) use ‘unanchored’ for a weaker CNMA additivity assumption, a terminology collision worth avoiding.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is an empty placeholder. At the specified cpaic commit, every named capability is exported and implemented, including estimability, cMAIC, cSTC, cML-NMR, edge influence, bridge fragility, and multiple outcome families. Strong additivity, bridge, and unanchored assumptions and the absence of mature independent validation remain legitimate concerns. The cML-NMR path still returns a conditional profile contrast rather than a marginal standardized effect. Conversely, cpaic already has substantial estimability, influence, fragility, prior, MCMC, and model-comparison diagnostics. mlumr 0.2.0 remains limited to one pairwise IPD-versus-AgD contrast, but it already supports arbitrary target populations by g-computation, prior sensitivity, MCMC and integration diagnostics, model comparison, several outcome families, and worked case-study vignettes. It is adapted from multinma concepts rather than using multinma as its runtime engine. Claims that it still lacks target and diagnostic development are stale; ‘first’ and ‘most promising’ are novelty or subjective claims outside this audit lens. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements the named component-PAIC methods and multiple outcome families, while leaving the cML-NMR marginal standardization gap open.. Cites choxos/mlumr@b2e24ceed0edf166fd10f985c38b5784c7f08056: Provides arbitrary-target g-computation, diagnostics, sensitivity analysis, model comparison, and worked examples; wider treatment-network scope remains open..

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text: SFW-15 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text:
Statement
netmeta 3.6-1 (CRAN, 20 June 2026) and gemtc 1.1-1 (CRAN, 26 March 2026) are mature NMA platforms carrying machinery the PAIC agenda needs: component NMA, rare-event methods, inconsistency assessment, node splitting, evidence flow, rankings, disconnected combination networks through discomb, and standard reporting. Neither is a native population-transport platform, because their analysis surfaces are study-level contrasts, arm summaries and study-level meta-regression with no representation of an IPD covariate distribution, a target population or a weighting step, so target standardization, component PAIC and IPD plus aggregate synthesis require external or new methods. Both auditors judged this supported: no function in the netmeta index or NAMESPACE references individual patient data or a target population. This is a package-scope and interoperability boundary rather than a defect, and it becomes decision-critical only when effect modification makes a declared target-population estimand necessary.

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text:
Why it is open
Both packages are defined over contrasts among studies with no representation of a target covariate distribution, so there is no place in the object for individual patient data, a target population or a weighting step, and adding transport would mean a different data model rather than an extra argument. Component NMA in netmeta therefore delivers component effects that are not indexed by a population, which is exactly the gap component PAIC exists to close, and gemtc’s inconsistency machinery is reachable only after population adjustment has happened elsewhere. Bridging the two would require an agreed intermediate representation that does not exist, so analysts re-specify the target population outside the model at the hand-off, which is where estimand definitions get lost. When effect modification is absent the boundary costs nothing, which is why it persists without pressure to close it.

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




netmeta 3.6-1 (CRAN, published 20 Jun 2026)
provides mature frequentist NMA with component NMA (netcomb), rare-event methods (netmetabin), inconsistency and evidence-flow tools (netsplit, netheat, netimpact), rankings and connectivity checks; no function references individual patient data or a target population


guido-s/netmeta (GitHub)
development repository for netmeta, including discomb, additive network meta-analysis for combinations of treatments in disconnected networks, implemented over study-level contrasts rather than IPD covariate distributions


gemtc 1.1-1 (CRAN, published 26 Mar 2026)
provides mature Bayesian JAGS-based NMA with node splitting, heterogeneity and inconsistency assessment and standard reporting; no native PAIC or population-transport layer, so transportability and target-population estimation are external tasks for its users

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not expect population adjustment from these packages. Make their rare-event, inconsistency, node-splitting and disconnected-network machinery interoperable with PAIC tooling through a shared intermediate representation, so transport and IPD plus aggregate synthesis can reuse mature backends and the target-population specification travels explicitly across the tool boundary instead of being duplicated by hand. Prioritize that interoperability work for the cases where a declared target-population estimand is necessary, since that is where the hand-off currently loses the estimand.

title: netmeta and gemtc carry no target-population representation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Every checkable claim verifies. CRAN gives netmeta 3.6-1 published 2026-06-20 and gemtc 1.1-1 published 2026-03-26, so both are active in 2026. The netmeta function index confirms discomb, described verbatim as ‘Additive network meta-analysis for combinations of treatments (disconnected networks)’, alongside netcomb (component NMA), netmetabin (binary/rare-event methods), netsplit, netheat, netimpact, netrank and netconnection. No function in that index references individual patient data or a target population, which is exactly the entry’s point: these packages are defined over study-level contrasts with no slot for a target covariate distribution. I found no evidence of any population-transport layer in either package, and the entry’s recommendation not to expect one is the correct reading of their data models.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported. The listed capability boundary is technically correct. netmeta’s NAMESPACE exports netcomb, discomb, netmetabin, netsplit, netheat, netimpact, netrank, and netconnection; R/discomb.R implements additive component NMA for disconnected networks. Its native analysis surface uses study-level contrasts, arm summaries, and study-level meta-regression, not IPD covariate distributions, population weighting, target standardization, or joint IPD-plus-AgD transport. Thus C2-C3 and C5-C7 hold. C9-C11 also correctly distinguish gemtc’s Bayesian JAGS NMA, node-splitting, heterogeneity, and inconsistency machinery from PAIC or external-target transport. C1 is a provenance flag rather than a statistical claim. Under the no-web constraint, C4 and C8 are accepted from the supplied CRAN metadata rather than independently rechecked. This is an interoperability and package-scope gap, not a defect in either NMA package; it becomes decision-critical only when effect modification makes a declared target-population estimand necessary.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R12:supported
